Summary: Gopher App - Complete Order Process Bug
Description: When a Standard Gopher marks a request as Completed, the request moves to Pending Confirmation status in the Active tab. The Gopher is currently stuck on this screen and cannot navigate to the Available tab to browse or accept new requests. This is a bug — once a request is marked Completed, the one-request-at-a-time restriction should lift and the Gopher should be free to accept new work. The only cap is that a Gopher may not accept a new request if they already have 2 Confirmation Pending requests outstanding. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Standard Gopher who has just marked a request as Completed, ## 🎯 I want to be able to navigate to the Available tab and accept a new request while my previous request is awaiting Requestor confirmation, ## ✅ So that I can continue working efficiently without being forced to wait for confirmation before taking on new requests. ## 💡 Context / Background * Standard Gophers are restricted to one active request at a time while a request is In Progress. * Once a Gopher marks a request as Completed, the request status changes to Pending Confirmation — awaiting the Requestor’s confirmation. * At this point the Gopher’s active work is done. The one-request restriction should no longer apply, and the Gopher should be free to browse and accept new available requests. * Currently the app keeps the Gopher on the Pending Confirmation screen and blocks access to the Available tab entirely. * A cap applies: if the Gopher already has **2 Confirmation Pending requests** outstanding, they may not accept a third until at least one resolves. ## ❌ Current Behavior * After marking a request as Completed, the Gopher is stuck on the Pending Confirmation screen * The Gopher cannot navigate to the Available tab to view or accept new requests * The one-request-at-a-time restriction incorrectly persists even after the Gopher has completed their work ## ✅ Expected Behavior * Once a Gopher marks a request as Completed, the one-request-at-a-time restriction is lifted * The Gopher can navigate to the Available tab, browse available requests, and accept a new one * The Pending Confirmation request remains visible in the Active tab while the Gopher works on the new request * If the Gopher has **2 Confirmation Pending requests** outstanding, they are blocked from accepting a new request until at least one resolves ## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce 1. Log in as a Standard Gopher and accept a request. 2. Update the request to In Progress, then mark it as Completed. 3. Observe the request changes to Pending Confirmation in the Active tab. 4. Attempt to navigate to the Available tab. 5. Observe the Gopher is stuck on the Pending Confirmation screen and cannot view available requests. ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Gopher can access Available tab after marking a request Completed * **Given** a Standard Gopher has marked a request as Completed * **When** the request enters Pending Confirmation status * **Then** the Gopher can navigate to the Available tab * **And** available requests are visible and selectable ### Scenario 2 – Gopher can accept a new request while one is Pending Confirmation * **Given** a Standard Gopher has 1 Pending Confirmation request * **When** the Gopher navigates to the Available tab and selects a new request * **Then** the Gopher can successfully accept the new request * **And** the Pending Confirmation request remains visible in the Active tab ### Scenario 3 – Gopher is blocked from accepting a new request when 2 are Pending Confirmation * **Given** a Standard Gopher already has 2 Confirmation Pending requests outstanding * **When** the Gopher attempts to accept a new request * **Then** the Gopher is blocked from accepting the new request * **And** they must wait until at least one Pending Confirmation resolves before accepting again ### Scenario 4 – One-request restriction still applies while a request is In Progress * **Given** a Standard Gopher has a request that is In Progress (not yet Completed) * **When** the Gopher attempts to accept another request * **Then** the one-request restriction applies and they cannot accept a new request ## ⚙️ Business Rules * The one-request-at-a-time restriction applies only while a request is In Progress. * Once a request is marked Completed (status: Pending Confirmation), the restriction lifts and the Gopher may browse and accept new requests. * A Standard Gopher may have a maximum of 2 Confirmation Pending requests at any time. If 2 are pending, they cannot accept a new request until at least one resolves. * Pending Confirmation requests must remain visible in the Active tab while the Gopher works on a new request. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * The restriction logic must check request status (In Progress vs. Pending Confirmation) rather than simply checking whether any active request exists. * The Available tab must become accessible as soon as the request transitions to Pending Confirmation. * The 2 Confirmation Pending cap must be enforced on the backend to prevent race conditions. * This logic applies to Standard Gophers only — confirm whether different rules apply to other Gopher tiers. ## 🧪 QA Notes * Mark a request as Completed — confirm the Gopher can navigate to the Available tab and see available requests. * With 1 Pending Confirmation request, accept a new request — confirm it is accepted successfully and the Pending Confirmation request remains in the Active tab. * With 2 Pending Confirmation requests, attempt to accept a third — confirm the Gopher is blocked. * Resolve one Pending Confirmation — confirm the Gopher can now accept a new request. * Confirm the one-request restriction still applies while a request is In Progress. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher App - Auto-Repost Workflow When Gopher Cancels an Active Request
Description: When a Gopher cancels an active request, the Requestor must be immediately presented with three clear options: Assign New Gopher, Edit Request, or Cancel Request. The appropriate flow must be triggered based on the Requestor’s selection, the original order must be closed, the Gopher’s cancellation must be logged, and any reposted or edited request must receive a new Order #. If the Requestor takes no action within 15 minutes, the request automatically cancels. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Requestor whose Gopher has cancelled an active request, ## 🎯 I want to be immediately presented with clear options to reassign, edit, or cancel my request, ## ✅ So that I can quickly recover from a Gopher cancellation without losing my request details or experiencing unnecessary friction. ## 💡 Context / Background * When a Gopher cancels an active request, the Requestor currently has no streamlined recovery path. * The Requestor receives a banner notification when their Gopher cancels. * The app should immediately present a modal with three options so the Requestor can act quickly. * Payment handling must ensure the Requestor does not experience a new authorization charge if the request is reassigned — internally the order is cancelled, but Stripe should treat it as a reassignment, not a new transaction. * If the Requestor takes no action within 15 minutes, the request automatically cancels. * An admin-level repost capability is also required in the Admin Panel under Orders, so the support team can step in and repost on the Requestor’s behalf when needed. ## 🗒️ The Three Options ### 1. Assign New Gopher * System automatically reposts the request with all original details and terms unchanged * A new Order # is generated and the request returns to the marketplace for Gopher selection * No changes to the request are permitted during this flow * Original order is closed and the cancelling Gopher is logged with a cancellation ### 2. Edit Request * Requestor is taken to the original Request Details page with all previous inputs pre-filled and editable * Pre-filled fields include cost of items, payment to Gopher, details, notes, and any other original inputs * After editing, the updated request is posted under a new Order # * Original order is closed and the cancelling Gopher is logged with a cancellation ### 3. Cancel Request * Requestor is shown the standard Gopher rating screen so they can rate the Gopher who cancelled * No repost occurs * Original order is closed and the cancelling Gopher is logged with a cancellation ## ❌ Current Behavior * When a Gopher cancels, the Requestor receives a banner notification but has no structured recovery options in the app * The Requestor must manually cancel and recreate the request themselves * No automatic repost, pre-fill, or rating flow is triggered * Admin panel has no ability to repost a cancelled order on the Requestor’s behalf ## ✅ Expected Behavior * When a Gopher cancels, the Requestor is immediately shown a modal with three options: Assign New Gopher, Edit Request, Cancel Request * Each option triggers the correct flow as defined above * Regardless of which option is chosen, the original Order # is closed and the cancelling Gopher is logged with a cancellation * Any reposted or edited request receives a new Order # * If the Requestor takes no action within 15 minutes, the request automatically cancels * Stripe does not re-authorize payment when a request is reassigned via Assign New Gopher or Edit Request * Admin panel includes a repost option on Orders so support staff can repost on the Requestor’s behalf ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Gopher cancellation triggers the recovery modal * **Given** a Gopher cancels an active request * **When** the cancellation is confirmed * **Then** the Requestor immediately receives a banner notification and is shown a modal with three options: Assign New Gopher, Edit Request, Cancel Request ### Scenario 2 – Assign New Gopher reposts with original details * **Given** the Requestor selects Assign New Gopher * **When** the action is confirmed * **Then** the request is automatically reposted with all original details unchanged * **And** a new Order # is generated and the request is live in the marketplace * **And** the original order is closed and the Gopher’s cancellation is logged * **And** no new Stripe authorization is triggered ### Scenario 3 – Edit Request pre-fills original details for editing * **Given** the Requestor selects Edit Request * **When** the edit page loads * **Then** the Requestor is taken to the original Request Details page with all previous inputs pre-filled and editable * **When** the Requestor submits the edited request * **Then** a new Order # is generated and the request is posted * **And** the original order is closed and the Gopher’s cancellation is logged ### Scenario 4 – Cancel Request shows rating screen * **Given** the Requestor selects Cancel Request * **When** the selection is confirmed * **Then** the standard Gopher rating screen is displayed * **And** no repost occurs * **And** the original order is closed and the Gopher’s cancellation is logged ### Scenario 5 – Auto-cancel after 15 minutes of inaction * **Given** the Requestor has been shown the recovery modal * **When** 15 minutes pass without any selection * **Then** the request is automatically cancelled * **And** the original order is closed and the Gopher’s cancellation is logged ### Scenario 6 – Admin can repost a cancelled order on the Requestor’s behalf * **Given** an admin navigates to a cancelled order in the Admin Panel * **When** the admin selects the repost option * **Then** the request is reposted with original details under a new Order # * **And** the action is logged against the original order ## ⚙️ Business Rules * The original Order # must always be closed when a Gopher cancels, regardless of which recovery option the Requestor selects. * The cancelling Gopher must always be logged with a cancellation against the original Order #. * Any reposted or edited request always receives a new Order #. * Stripe must not trigger a new payment authorization when the Requestor selects Assign New Gopher or Edit Request — the payment is internally treated as a reassignment. * If the Requestor takes no action within 15 minutes of the modal appearing, the request auto-cancels. * This workflow applies to both instant (Need ASAP) and scheduled requests. * The rating screen must pull the correct Gopher ID of the cancelling Gopher. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Requires a new "repost with same terms" function tied to the Assign New Gopher flow. * Backend must finalize and close the original order before creating a new one. * Coordinate with Stripe on payment reassignment logic to avoid re-authorization on the Requestor’s card. * Push notifications must fire correctly for all three flows. * Wallet/held funds must be handled appropriately during order close and repost. * Backend must log: original Order #, new Order # (where applicable), Gopher who cancelled, and timestamp of cancellation. * Admin panel Orders section requires a repost action so support staff can act on behalf of the Requestor. * Figma UI/UX reference: https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=4902-2963 * Figma banner notification reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=49-14197 ## 🧪 QA Notes * Test Gopher cancellation — confirm Requestor immediately receives banner notification and recovery modal. * Test Assign New Gopher — confirm request reposts with identical details, new Order # is generated, original order is closed, and Gopher cancellation is logged. * Test Edit Request — confirm pre-fill is accurate, edited request posts under a new Order #, and original order is closed. * Test Cancel Request — confirm rating screen appears with correct Gopher, no repost occurs, and original order is closed. * Test 15-minute auto-cancel — confirm request cancels automatically with no action taken. * Verify no new Stripe authorization is triggered when Assign New Gopher or Edit Request is used. * Test admin panel repost on a cancelled order — confirm new Order # is created and action is logged. * Test across both instant (Need ASAP) and scheduled request types. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher App - Stripe - Account - Payment Account - Additional User Info Required For Security
Description: > 🔧 **DEV-READY HANDOFF — groomed & unparked 2026-07-02 (John Newbury).** This block is the authoritative spec; where it conflicts with the original body below, this block wins. All prior open questions are resolved — no developer decisions remain. Full handoff doc: `docs/handoff/G40-11-card-verification.md`. ## 🎯 Goal Every new card added must collect five verifiable fields **incl. billing address**, pass name/address to Stripe for **AVS + Radar**, require an **SMS OTP** to the account phone before the card is saved, and **log the verification event** so we have evidence to appeal chargeback disputes. ## ✅ Resolved decisions (were open questions) | # | Decision | Answer | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | Status (was parked pending Stripe Connect R&D, Shaun 2024‑09) | **Unparked — build it.** | | 2 | In-scope surfaces | **Native Gopher Request app + Gopher Request (web) + Gopher Connect (business).** Gopher Deals **out of scope.** | | 3 | OTP on card add | **Required on EVERY card add** (even though phone is already OTP-verified at signup). No skip. | | 4 | Dispute evidence | **Log each card-add verification event** for chargeback appeals (see below). | | 5 | Prototype UI | **Do not build UI in the prototype** (payments fenced off); use existing prototype screens as visual reference only. | ## 💳 Required fields (all mandatory — Submit disabled until all valid) Full Name · Card Number · Expiration Date · CVC · **Billing Address (street, city, state, ZIP)**. ## 🔐 Stripe + OTP * Tokenize via Stripe; **raw PAN never stored on Gopher servers.** * Pass name + billing address in `billing_details` → enables AVS + Radar and retains dispute evidence. Enable AVS/CVC checks + Radar rules in Dashboard. * Modern equivalent of the 2024 `CardElement` note is **Payment Element + SetupIntent** — dev's engineering call; either is fine as long as `billing_details` is populated and AVS/Radar active. * After submit, send **6-digit SMS OTP** to the **account phone** (reuse existing signup OTP provider/Twilio). Card not saved until verified. **Expiry 5 min, resend once.** Wrong/expired → not saved, retry/resend offered. ## 🧾 Dispute audit log (NEW — John's requirement) Persist an auditable, retained record on every card-add attempt: account/user id + Stripe payment-method id (brand/last4); UTC timestamp; phone OTP sent to (masked/hashed per policy) + OTP outcome (sent/verified/failed/expired/resent); IP + device/user-agent; Stripe **AVS result, CVC result, Radar score/outcome**. Dedicated retained table (survives card edit/removal); retention ≥ chargeback dispute window (\~120+ days — confirm vs. Stripe/network timelines). ## ✅ Acceptance criteria 1. Submit disabled until all five fields (incl. billing address) valid. 2. On submit, SMS OTP sent to account phone; card not saved pre-verification. 3. Correct OTP → card saved & usable. 4. Incorrect/expired OTP → not saved; resend (once)/retry offered. 5. Name + billing address present on Stripe payment method object (AVS + Radar). 6. **Dispute audit record written for every card-add attempt** with fields above. 7. Holds on native Request app (iOS+Android), Request web, and Connect. ## 🖼️ Prototype reference (visual only — do NOT edit these files) * `Final/gopher-request.html` — add-payment modal `ensureModal()`/`__openAddPaymentModal` (\~L10792–10937; ids `payName/payNum/payExp/payCvc/paySave/payErr`) — collects Name/Num/Exp/CVC only, **no billing address, no OTP** (add both). Reusable signup phone-OTP: `rqSuPhoneOtpBtn` / `rqOtpLabel` (\~L16316). * `Final/gopher-connect.html` — same modal (\~L9468) + signup phone-OTP (\~L7290); street/city/state address pattern (\~L7097) to mirror for the billing block. * Figma card entry screens 1 & 2 (links in original body below). --- ## 📜 Original ticket (2024 — retained for context) The current payment method entry flow does not collect enough identifying information to verify that a card or payment method genuinely belongs to the user adding it. This creates exposure to fraud and chargebacks. The payment entry flow must be updated to require additional user information that Stripe can use for verification, fraud scoring, and chargeback dispute evidence. **As a** Gopher App user adding a payment method, **I want** to be required to provide verifiable identifying information when adding a card, **so that** the platform can confirm the payment method is legitimate and reduce fraud/chargeback risk. * Figma – Card entry screen 1: https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=5945-10274 * Figma – Card entry screen 2: https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=5945-10275 * Stripe chargeback prevention: https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/prevention * Stripe Radar: https://docs.stripe.com/radar _(The original detailed acceptance criteria, business rules, and QA notes from 2024 are superseded by the DEV-READY HANDOFF block above and the full handoff doc_ `docs/handoff/G40-11-card-verification.md`.)

Summary: Gopher Go - Stripe - Payout Account Confirmation
Description: Some users are being redirected to Stripes website (via mobile browser) to “fix” their payout account. Stripe is asking for their business website which is irrelevant for payouts. The integration between GopherGo and Stripe needs to be re-examined to cleaned up to prevent confusion. ‌ ### **As a** Gopher Go user setting up or confirming my **payout account**, ### **I want** a clear and accurate verification process that does **not** redirect me to irrelevant Stripe business setup pages, ### **So that** I can complete my payout verification smoothly without confusion or unnecessary steps. ‌ ### **💡 Context / Background** ‌ * Some Gopher Go users are being **redirected to Stripe’s website via the mobile browser** when attempting to confirm or “fix” their payout account. * Stripe is then asking the user for a **business website**, which is irrelevant for Gopher payouts and causes confusion. * This indicates that the current Stripe integration may be using an **incorrect onboarding or account-type flow**, likely one meant for businesses instead of individuals. * The payout account flow needs to be **re-examined and cleaned up** to ensure the correct Stripe verification path is used and no unnecessary fields or redirects are shown. ‌ ### **✅ Acceptance Criteria (Given / When / Then)** ‌ **Scenario 1 – Correct verification flow** * **Given** a user attempts to verify or update their payout account in Gopher Go, * **When** Stripe requires additional information, * **Then** the user must be taken to the **correct Stripe payout onboarding flow** (individual payouts), * **And** must **not** be redirected to business onboarding or asked for business-specific information. ‌ **Scenario 2 – No external unnecessary redirects** * **Given** a user taps “Fix” or “Verify” payout account, * **When** the integration logic triggers Stripe verification, * **Then** the user should **not** be redirected to an irrelevant mobile browser page. ‌ **Scenario 3 – Appropriate Stripe requirements only** * **Given** Stripe requests are valid, * **When** the user provides required information, * **Then** only relevant fields (e.g., identity verification, tax information, personal details) should be shown — **NOT business-only fields** such as “business website.” ‌ **Scenario 4 – Clear messaging inside Gopher Go** * **Given** verification is required, * **When** the user starts verification, * **Then** the UI should clearly indicate that Stripe is verifying their payout identity, not setting up a business account. ‌ ### **⚙️ Business Rules** ‌ * Gophers must be set up as **individual payouts** (or the correct Stripe account type for the application). * Gopher Go must map users to the **correct Stripe account object**, preventing business-account flows. * No business onboarding steps (website, EIN, company info) should ever appear unless the user is intentionally registered as a business. * Only relevant Stripe fields should be presented. * Integration must prevent unnecessary redirections to mobile browsers unless absolutely required. ‌ ### **🧠 Dependencies / Notes** ‌ * Investigate Gopher Go’s Stripe integration flow: * Check the account type being created (e.g., custom, express, standard). * Confirm whether Gophers use the correct capabilities (e.g., transfers). * Ensure correct onboarding link is generated (Stripe account link type). * Review account linkage logic to ensure existing payout accounts are reused, not recreated incorrectly. * Validate that no legacy or deprecated onboarding types are being used. * QA should test multiple payout scenarios (new user, returning user, restricted user). ‌ ### **🧪 QA Notes:** ‌ * Attempt to reproduce issue on iOS and Android. * Confirm user is never redirected to a browser asking for business information. * Test: * New payout account setup * Fixing a restricted payout account * Updating existing payout details * Verify correct Stripe onboarding link is used each time. * Confirm that payout verification screen is appropriate for an **individual**, not a business.

Summary: Gopher Go - Account - Payout Account - Adding A Card - Incorrect Error Displayed
Description: When a Gopher enters their payout card, while Stripe is verifying the card, it is showing the payment error. This should say “Payout Account pending…” so the user is not confused. Also need to change the “Default Payment Card” to “Default Payout Card” ‌ ### **As a** Gopher Go user adding a **payout card**, ### **I want** the app to show the correct status message while Stripe verifies my card, ### **So that** I’m not confused by incorrect payment-related errors and I understand my payout setup is processing correctly. ‌ ### **💡 Context / Background** ‌ * When a Gopher enters their **payout card** in **Account → Payout Account**, Stripe begins verifying the card. * During this verification period, the app incorrectly displays a **payment error message**, which is misleading. * Instead, the message should inform the user that their **payout account is pending verification**. * Additionally, the label **“Default Payment Card”** on this screen should be updated to **“Default Payout Card.”** * These changes help clarify that the user is setting up a _payout_ method, not a _payment_ method. ‌ 📎 _Screenshot reference:_ ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=0af3403c-e93d-4d06-97d1-1b88e9b9f35f&&collection=&height=844&occurrenceKey=null&width=390&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) ‌ ### **✅ Acceptance Criteria (Given / When / Then)** ‌ **Scenario 1 – Correct pending message displayed** * **Given** a user adds a payout card in **Account → Payout Account**, * **When** Stripe Summary: Stripe - Active Request - 7 Day Max Payment Authorization Issue
Description: **UPDATE - This was not executed correctly. What is happening is the authorization IS expiring on Stripe's end after 7 days. (use Order # 59422 for reference) This is working on some orders and NOT with others. Seems to be happening more with “Services.”** **Simply put… a request authorization NEVER expires with a “pending” request. Once a request is accepted, the card authorization needs to be extended until the request is COMPLETED OR CANCELLED. Enter whatever logic is needed to comply with Stripe’s requirements.** **IF a cost adjustment is made, the new amount will follow the “authorization never expires” logic. If a request is disputed, it will follow the “authorization never expires” logic.** ‌ Stripe is only allowing an authorization for 7 days. We allow users to schedule 2 weeks out. Order 34747 cancelled a $1300+ authorization as a result. Request was still active. \*Need to ensure authorization is for the duration of the scheduled request and if connected to a gopher, it’s doesn’t ever expire. IF a request is rescheduled in the app, no matter what the date is (which is a max of 2 weeks) the authorization needs to align. ‌ EX: Stripe Notes for Order 34747 Authorization expired. It may take a few days for the money to reach the customer's bank account. View details Nov 15, 2024, 1:14 PM Payment authorized, but not yet capturedNov 8, 2024, 1:14 PM Payment startedNov 8, 2024, 12:18 PM ‌ The app will give the user an option to schedule out 2 weeks, as shown here, just the authorization will only last until 7 days later. This is unknown to the worker or the customer. The request will still stay live and function as normal, all the way up until 1) a cost adjustment is attempted or 2) a completed request update is attempted. It will then say “network error” ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=7fadb08f-aee1-4ad2-9c69-b3247c28418e&&collection=&height=2796&occurrenceKey=null&width=1290&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) ## **Jira Ticket: Extend Stripe Authorization Handling for Scheduled Requests** **Type:** Bug / Feature Gap **Priority:** High **Component:** Payments / Stripe Integration **Reporter:** John **Environment:** Production (iOS + Android + Backend) --- ### **Summary** Stripe only holds payment authorizations for **7 days**, but the Gopher app allows users to **schedule requests up to 14 days out**. As a result, authorizations are expiring before the scheduled service occurs, causing failures when workers or customers attempt cost adjustments or request completion. --- ### **Description** Users can currently schedule requests up to **two weeks in advance**. However, Stripe authorization windows expire after **7 days**, which is resulting in: * Authorizations expiring before the scheduled service date * Orders remaining active in the app without valid payment authorization * Workers and customers seeing “network error” when attempting: 1. Cost adjustments 2. Completing the request **Example Issue (Order #34747):** * Scheduled beyond the 7-day authorization window * $1300+ authorization expired * Stripe displayed: * _“Authorization expired. It may take a few days for the money to reach the customer's bank account.”_ * App still treated the request as active This issue is invisible to both the customer and the worker. --- ### **Business Impact** * High-value authorizations are failing silently * Workers complete services and cannot be paid * Customers assume payment is secured but it is not * Increased support overhead * Revenue loss due to inability to capture expired authorizations * Platform trust and reliability risks --- ### **Requirements** ✅ **1. Authorization must remain valid for the entire scheduled window (up to 14 days).** * If Stripe supports reauthorization or incremental authorization refreshes, implement it. * If not possible, implement a scheduled “authorization refresh” before expiration. ✅ **2. Once a request is connected to a Gopher (worker), authorization must never expire.** * Auto-renew authorization until the request is either completed or canceled. ✅ **3. If a request is rescheduled in the app (within the 2-week limit), authorization must automatically adjust to match the new date.** * Trigger a refresh if the date moves beyond the current authorization window. ✅ **4. Error handling & UX improvements** * Prevent “network error” by checking authorization validity before: * Cost adjustments * Request completion * Surface proper UI messaging when authorization lapses * Reattempt reauthorization in background --- ### **Acceptance Criteria** **AC1 — New requests scheduled ≤ 14 days in advance always have a valid authorization at time of service.** * Validation: Payment can be captured successfully on completion. **AC2 — If a request is connected to a worker, authorization is automatically extended/renewed until completion.** * No silent expiration. **AC3 — Rescheduling a request triggers a payment authorization refresh.** * Edge case: user changes date multiple times. **AC4 — No “network error” should occur due to expired authorization.** * If authorization is invalid, system performs refresh automatically. **AC5 — Admin dashboard logs must show authorization renewal events.** --- ### **Technical Notes / References** **Stripe Log Example (Order #34747):** * Nov 8, 2024: Payment authorized * Nov 15, 2024: Authorization expired * Stripe note: _“Authorization expired. It may take a few days for the money to reach the customer's bank account.”_ **Stripe Limitation:** * Standard authorization validity = 7 days * Extensions possible with manual reauthorization flow (Stripe API) * May require SetupIntents + delayed capture or recurring reauth via PaymentIntents --- ### **Suggested Implementation Path** 1. **Introduce background job** that checks pending/scheduled requests daily. 2. **If authorization expiration < 48 hours away**, create a new authorization. 3. **Update payment intent** to maintain coverage. 4. **Lock the job to worker assignment**—continue reauth until service is completed. 5. **On reschedule**, immediately call payment refresh flow. FLOW 1. Requestor creates a request (either Flexible - Next 2 weeks or Scheduled >7 days) 2. Request is accepted by a Gopher 3. The Gopher updates app to completed >7 days from the initial authorization. 4. Requestor receives the Confirm/Dispute alert and taps Confirmed and receives an error massage stating a payment error.

Summary: Gopher Go - Failed Instant Transfer Email and New Debit Card Entry Protocol
Description: When a Gopher completes an order and the payout deposit attempt fails due to an invalid debit card, the system must immediately notify the Gopher via push alert and in-app popup, send an automated email with payout failure details and instructions, and accurately reflect the failed payout status in the request history log. The "Payout Completed" status must only be recorded when a deposit is verified as successful. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher Go user who has just completed an order, ## 🎯 I want to be immediately notified if there was an issue with my debit card on file, ## ✅ So that I can correct the issue and receive my payout without unnecessary delays. ## 💡 Context / Background * When a debit card on file becomes invalid (expired or compromised), there is currently no proactive way to detect this until a payout attempt fails. * A payout failure is identified at the moment the Gopher completes an order and the deposit attempt is made. * The Gopher must be notified immediately and guided to update their debit card so the payout can be retried. * Once a new card is added, the retry sequence is: the new card is assigned to the existing payout balance on the next business day, and the deposit is received the following business day. * The request history log currently records "Payout Completed" regardless of whether the payout succeeded or failed — this must be corrected. ## ❌ Current Behavior * No push alert or in-app notification is sent when a payout fails * No automated email is sent to the Gopher to explain the failure or provide resolution steps * The request history logs "Payout Completed" even when the payout has failed * "Requestor Confirmed" and "Payout Completed" are being logged simultaneously, regardless of actual payout status * The Gopher has no in-app path to update their debit card when a failure occurs ## ✅ Expected Behavior * When a payout fails, the Gopher immediately receives a push alert and an in-app popup modal notifying them of the issue * Tapping the push alert or popup takes the Gopher directly to the debit card update screen * An automated email is sent from admin@gophergo.io to the Gopher with their name, last 4 digits of the failed card, the failed payout amount, and instructions on the retry sequence * The request history accurately reflects the failed payout with a timestamped PAYOUT FAILED entry and a prompt to add a new debit card * "Payout Completed" is only logged in the request history once the deposit is verified as successful * Once a new card is added and the deposit is confirmed, a timestamped "Payout Completed" entry is added to the request history ## 📧 Automated Email Template * **From:** admin@gophergo.io * **To:** Gopher’s email address on file * **Subject:** Payout error for order #\[Order #\] Hi \[First\] \[Last\], It appears Stripe is showing your card ending in \[last 4\] is no longer valid (typically this means the card is either expired or compromised). You’ll need to enter a new debit card to receive the transfer. The $\[amount\] will continue unsuccessfully attempting to deposit on this card until a new card is updated. The sequence works like this: * Once updated, the next business day the new card is assigned to the existing payout balance. * The following business day, the deposit is received on the new card. We know things happen, but to avoid payout delays, you’ll want to make sure you always have a valid debit card on file. It delays payouts to the point where Gopher, Inc can’t help speed up the process. Rest assured the money is yours — you’ll now just need to let Stripe and your bank run its course. Regards, Gopher Support Team ## 🗒️ Request History Log Behavior * On payout failure: `3/19/2024 08:05 PM: PAYOUT FAILED (Please add a new debit card)` * On payout success after card update: `3/20/2024 08:05 PM: Payout Completed` * "Payout Completed" must never be logged unless the deposit is verified as successful * "Requestor Confirmed" and "Payout Completed" must not be logged simultaneously — payout status must be verified independently ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Payout failure triggers push alert and in-app popup * **Given** a Gopher completes an order and the payout deposit attempt fails * **When** the failure is detected * **Then** the Gopher immediately receives a push alert and an in-app popup modal notifying them of the payout failure * **And** tapping the alert or popup navigates the Gopher directly to the debit card update screen ### Scenario 2 – Automated payout failure email is sent * **Given** a payout failure is detected * **When** the failure is logged * **Then** an automated email is sent from admin@gophergo.io to the Gopher’s email address * **And** the email includes the Gopher’s name, last 4 digits of the failed card, the failed payout amount, and the retry sequence instructions ### Scenario 3 – Request history shows PAYOUT FAILED when payout fails * **Given** a payout attempt has failed * **When** the Gopher views their request history * **Then** a timestamped PAYOUT FAILED entry is shown with a prompt to add a new debit card * **And** no "Payout Completed" entry is logged ### Scenario 4 – Payout Completed is only logged after verified deposit * **Given** a Gopher has updated their debit card and the deposit has been confirmed * **When** the payout is successfully deposited * **Then** a timestamped "Payout Completed" entry is added to the request history ### Scenario 5 – Requestor Confirmed and Payout Completed are not logged simultaneously * **Given** a Requestor confirms order completion * **When** the confirmation is recorded * **Then** "Requestor Confirmed" is logged * **And** "Payout Completed" is only logged separately once the deposit is independently verified ## ⚙️ Business Rules * Payout failure detection must trigger immediately upon a failed deposit attempt following order completion. * Both a push alert and an in-app popup modal must fire simultaneously on failure detection. * The automated payout failure email must be sent from admin@gophergo.io and must dynamically populate the Gopher’s name, card last 4, order number, and failed amount. * "Payout Completed" must never be logged in the request history unless a deposit is confirmed as successful. * "Requestor Confirmed" and "Payout Completed" are independent log events and must never be recorded simultaneously. * Retry sequence: new card assigned to payout balance on next business day; deposit received the following business day. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Stripe webhook or callback must be set up to detect failed instant transfer events and trigger the notification and email flows. * Email must dynamically pull: Gopher first/last name, card last 4, order number, and failed payout amount. * Push alert and popup must deep-link directly to the debit card update screen. * Request history payout status logic must be decoupled from Requestor confirmation — payout status must be driven by Stripe deposit confirmation only. * Figma assets reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=21-10645 * Figma debit card update screen reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=22-11093 ## 🧪 QA Notes * Simulate a payout failure on order completion — confirm push alert and in-app popup fire immediately. * Tap the push alert — confirm it navigates directly to the debit card update screen. * Tap the in-app popup — confirm it also navigates to the debit card update screen. * Verify the automated email is sent from admin@gophergo.io with correct dynamic fields: name, card last 4, order number, and failed amount. * Check request history after a failed payout — confirm PAYOUT FAILED entry appears with timestamp and no "Payout Completed" entry is logged. * Update the debit card and confirm the deposit — verify "Payout Completed" entry is added to request history with correct timestamp. * Confirm "Requestor Confirmed" and "Payout Completed" are never logged at the same time. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher App - Stripe - Cost Adjustment Error
Description: ### **As a** Gopher App customer submitting a request, ### **I want** the system to handle cost adjustments **within the pre-authorized 20% cushion** without triggering a new authorization, ### **So that** I am not charged twice or have my transaction declined due to insufficient funds when adjustments remain within the originally approved total. ‌ ### **💡Context / Background** ‌ * When a transaction is created, the system **pre-authorizes 20% more** than the original total (e.g., $100 → $120). * If a **Cost Adjustment** is later made — for example, the **Gopher Offer** amount increases from $100 → $115 — the system currently triggers **a second authorization** for $115. * This results in customers being temporarily charged twice ($120 + $115 = $235), which often causes **declined transactions** because of insufficient funds. * Adjustments that stay **within** the 20% pre-authorized cushion should **not create an additional authorization**; they should be processed under the original authorized amount. ‌ 📎 _Screenshots attached:_ 1️⃣ User notification **before submitting the request** ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=8f7332e9-6a9c-432a-a976-2a1c846667f0&&collection=&height=512&occurrenceKey=null&width=438&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) 2️⃣ User notification **after submitting via email** ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=7df4599a-b36f-48ff-94ab-3cbd9eccd980&&collection=&height=488&occurrenceKey=null&width=546&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) ‌ ### **✅ Acceptance Criteria (Given / When / Then)** ‌ **Scenario 1 – Adjustment within the 20% cushion** * **Given** a transaction is pre-authorized for the total amount + 20%, * **When** a cost adjustment increases the total but remains **≤ the pre-authorized limit**, * **Then** the system must **not create a new authorization**, and * **Then** the total should update inside the existing authorization. ‌ **Scenario 2 – Adjustment exceeding the 20% cushion (must confirm if this scenario is going to be worked here or separate)** * **Given** a transaction is pre-authorized for the total amount + 20%, * **When** a cost adjustment increases the total **beyond the pre-authorized limit**, * **Then** the system must **initiate a new authorization** for the additional amount beyond that limit. ‌ **Scenario 3 – Customer notification points** * **Given** the user is notified before and after submission, * **When** a cost adjustment occurs, * **Then** the app must display and email the **adjusted total only**, without performing a duplicate authorization if the new total stays within the authorized range. ‌ ### **⚙️ Business Rules** ‌ * The 20% cushion is calculated based on the **original total request amount**. * Any adjustment that remains within this cushion **must reuse the existing authorization**. * Only adjustments exceeding the cushion should trigger a **new authorization request** to Stripe. * Stripe integration must compare the **adjusted total vs. pre-authorized limit** before creating a new authorization. * Logs should reflect only **one authorization** for valid within-limit adjustments. ‌ ### **🔍 Example Calculations** ‌ **Example 1 – Within cushion** * Pre-authorization total: $100 → authorized $120 (20% increase) * Adjustment: $100 → $115 * Adjusted total $115 ≤ $120 → ✅ **No new authorization.** ‌ **Example 2 – Exceeds cushion** * Pre-authorization total: $100 → authorized $120 * Adjustment: $100 → $130 * Adjusted total $130 > $120 → ⚠️ **New authorization required.** ‌ ‌ **Example 3 – Full breakdown example** _Pre-authorization:_ * Cost of items: $100 * Gopher Offer: $20 * Gopher Fee: $0.99 * Age-Restricted Fee: $1.99 * Fees: $9.84 * **Total: $132.82 → Authorized for $159.38 (20% cushion)** _Adjustment:_ * Cost of items: $115 * Gopher Offer: $20 * Gopher Fee: $0.99 * Age-Restricted Fee: $1.99 * Fees: $11.04 * **New Total: $149.02 < $159.38 → No new authorization needed.** ‌ ### **🧠 Dependencies / Notes** ‌ * Applies to all **Stripe** transactions that include cost adjustments. * Review logic in backend payment authorization service and ensure consistent handling on client side. * Verify that user notification messages (pre-submit screen and confirmation email) reflect the **final adjusted total** only. ‌ ### **🧪 QA Notes** ‌ * Simulate multiple adjustment types (e.g., Gopher Offer, item cost, service fee). * Confirm Stripe logs show only one authorization for adjustments within cushion. * Verify both in-app and email notifications display the correct adjusted total. * Test with limited user balance scenarios to ensure decline logic works as expected.

Summary: Gopher App - Gophers Interested & Counter-Offer Distance Details Communicated To Requestor if >15 miles Requires Requestor Approval (combined with GA-309)
Description: ### **As a** Requestor submitting a service request in Gopher Go, ### **I want** to clearly understand when a Gopher requires my approval and see their distance immediately, ### **So that** I can take action without confusion and avoid requests expiring due to hidden or unclear steps. ‌ ## **🎯 Goal** Eliminate the hidden “Needs Attention” approval step in **First Available** requests and make Gopher distance + approval requirements immediately visible and actionable. ‌ ## **💡Context / Background** ‌ ### **🔁 Current Acceptance Logic (as designed)** ‌ **First Available** 1. Any Gopher **within 15 miles** who accepts is **automatically connected**. 2. Any Gopher **over 15 miles** who accepts requires **Requestor approval** (behaves like Select My Gopher). ‌ **Select My Gopher** * Any Gopher who accepts **always requires Requestor approval**. ‌ **Notify One of MY Gophers** 1. Any MY Gopher who accepts is **automatically connected**. 2. Summary: Both Apps - ALL In-App Messaging Notifications and Flow
Description: In-App Messaging not showing banner notifications or red-circle alert timely. User will not be aware of new message received in a relevant timeframe. The in-app messaging needs to behave EXACTLY like native cell phone texting. Including the thinking dots when a new message is coming in. Currently the user has to tap in the inbox every time they get a message. Ideally if the user is in that active messaging screen, we do not need to send push or banner alerts. ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=692e057e-b0e9-40fc-b827-027d7ad1b94e&&collection=&height=960&occurrenceKey=null&width=444&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) ## **Jira Ticket: In-App Messaging Alerts Not Updating / Missing Real-Time Behavior** **Type:** Bug / Feature Gap **Priority:** High **Component:** Messaging / Notifications **Reporter:** John **Environment:** Production (iOS + Android + Backend) --- ### **Summary** In-app messaging does **not** show timely banner notifications or red-circle unread indicators. Users are not aware when new messages arrive. Messaging behavior must mirror native SMS texting, including real-time typing indicators. --- ### **Description** Currently, in-app messages only update when the user manually **taps into the Inbox** or re-opens the conversation thread. This leads to: * No banner alerts when a new message arrives * Delayed or missing **red-circle unread indicators** * No real-time “typing dots” to show the other party is responding * Users receiving messages they are unaware of for long periods * Push notifications not firing consistently (or not firing when expected) **Impact:** Users—especially workers and customers coordinating job details—are missing messages in real time. This results in miscommunication, failed coordination, delays, cancellations, and support issues. --- ### **Business Impact** * Workers miss important customer messages before arriving * Customers think the worker is unresponsive * Increased cancellations and poor user experience * Messaging feels unreliable and “dead” * Direct negative impact on job completion rate and trust --- ### **Requirements** ✅ **1. Implement real-time banner notifications (in-app) for every new message.** * Should appear instantly, like iMessage or Android SMS alerts. * Should trigger even if the user is elsewhere in the app. ✅ **2. Add real-time red-circle badge updates on:** * Inbox icon * Individual conversation thread ✅ **3. Add typing indicators ("thinking dots") in the active conversation.** * Must show the other party is currently typing, identical to native texting. ✅ **4. If the user is already inside the active message thread, suppress push notifications.** * No need for banners if user is viewing that conversation * Still show typing indicator in real time ✅ **5. Messages must update instantly without requiring manual refresh or tapping the screen.** * Real-time WebSocket or push-based updates * Must not rely on user actions or page reloads --- ### **Acceptance Criteria** **AC1 — User receives immediate in-app banner when a new message arrives (unless inside that active chat).** **AC2 — Red unread indicator updates within < 1s of new message arriving.** **AC3 — Typing indicator (“…” animation) displays in real time for the other user.** **AC4 — If user is in conversation thread, no push/banner alerts are shown.** **AC5 — Message list updates in real time without requiring refresh, reload, or tapping Inbox.** **AC6 — No missed or delayed in-app message alerts under any scenario (foreground, background, switching screens, etc.).** --- ### **Technical Notes** * Implement WebSockets or improve existing socket reconnection logic. * Ensure backend emits messaging events instantly. * Add front-end listeners for: * `message_received` * `message_read` * `typing_started` * `typing_stopped` * Add throttling / debounce logic for typing events.

outline** does **not expand** when comments contain multiple lines or long text. * Instead, the text **protrudes outside the box**, creating readability and UI layout issues. * The comment area should Summary: Both Apps - Submitting A Request - Image Upload Failures & Keyboard Blocking Inputs During Request Creation
Description: ## **🧑‍💻 As a** Gopher App user (Requestor or Gopher), ## **🎯 I want** to upload images successfully and interact with form fields without UI obstructions, ## **✅ So that** I can complete requests and ratings without the app stalling or blocking my input. ‌ ## **💡 Context / Background** ‌ ### **Image Upload Issue** ‌ * Users are experiencing **silent failures** when uploading images during: * Request creation * Gopher Rating after job completion * After tapping **“Review my request”**, the app spins indefinitely with no feedback. * Common image formats are affected, especially on iOS: * HEIF / HEIC (default iPhone format) * PNG * JPG / JPEG * Live Photos often produce large or non-standard file structures that appear to be rejected. * The failure: * Is not communicated to the user * Blocks request submission entirely * Affects both sides of the marketplace Reference order [50278](https://admin.gophergo.io/booking/50278) ### **Keyboard Blocking Input Issue (Critical)** ‌ * The on-screen keyboard **obscures input fields inside modal views**. * Most notably affects the **address entry field** during request creation. * Users cannot see what they are typing, making it **impossible to complete the request**. * This issue was explicitly flagged by **John Newbury** as **critical and app-breaking**. * Likely solutions include increasing modal height or enabling scroll/keyboard-aware behavior. ‌ ## **❌ Current Behavior** ‌ * Image upload fails silently. * “Review my request” spins indefinitely. * Rating screen stalls after photo upload. * No error message or recovery path is provided. * Keyboard overlaps modal input fields, hiding user-entered text. ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=7f83c6fc-c125-497e-aa92-277421c5efb0&&collection=&height=1118&occurrenceKey=null&width=516&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) ‌ ## **✅ Expected Behavior** ‌ * Standard image formats are accepted or gracefully handled. * Users are informed immediately when an upload fails. * The request and rating flows never stall silently. * Modal input fields remain visible when the keyboard is open. ‌ ## **🔁 Steps to Reproduce** ‌ ### **Image Upload** ‌ 1. Open Gopher App (iOS or Android). 2. Create a new request. 3. Add a photo from camera or photo library. 4. Tap **“Review my request.”** 5. Observe infinite spinner with no feedback. ‌ **Also reproducible in:** * Completed request → Gopher Rating → add photo → same behavior. ‌ ### **Keyboard Blocking Input** ‌ 1. Start creating a request. 2. Open a modal requiring address input. 3. Focus the address field. 4. Keyboard opens and covers the input. 5. User cannot see what is being typed. ‌ ## **✅ Acceptance Criteria** ‌ ### **Scenario 1 – Accept standard image formats** * **Given** a user uploads an image during request creation or rating * **When** the image format is HEIF, HEIC, PNG, JPG/JPEG, WebP, or AVIF * **Then** the image is accepted and the flow continues normally ‌ ### **Scenario 2 – Handle oversized or unsupported images** * **Given** a user uploads an image that exceeds size limits or is unsupported * **When** validation fails * **Then** a clear, user-friendly error message is displayed * **And** the app does not stall or spin indefinitely ‌ ### **Scenario 3 – Prevent infinite spinner** * **Given** an image upload fails for any reason * **When** the user attempts to proceed * **Then** the request does not enter an infinite loading state ‌ ### **Scenario 4 – Rating screen image upload** * **Given** a Gopher uploads an image on the Rating screen * **When** the image is submitted * **Then** the upload succeeds or fails with clear feedback ‌ ### **Scenario 5 – Keyboard does not block modal inputs** * **Given** a user focuses an input field inside a modal * **When** the keyboard opens * **Then** the input field remains visible and usable ‌ ### **Scenario 6 – Address field visibility** * **Given** the address entry field is active * **When** the keyboard is displayed * **Then** the user can clearly see and verify the text they are typing ‌ ### **Scenario 7 – Logging and diagnostics** * **Given** an image upload fails * **When** the failure occurs * **Then** the system logs: * File type * File size * Failure reason ## **⚙️ Business Rules** ‌ * Image uploads must never fail silently. * The app must always provide user feedback on upload issues. * Keyboard behavior must not block form completion. * Applies to both **Request creation** and **Gopher Rating** flows. * No regression to existing request or rating functionality. ‌ ## **🧪 QA Notes** ‌ * Test on: * iOS (HEIC, Live Photos enabled) * Android (camera + gallery) * Verify no infinite spinners remain. * Validate modal behavior across screen sizes. * Confirm error messages are clear and actionable. * Verify backend logs capture upload failures.

Summary: Stripe - Request - New Payment Options For Requestors
Description: The Gopher App currently only supports debit and credit card payments. To reduce declined transactions, increase checkout conversion, and give Requestors more flexibility when their card balance is insufficient, additional payment methods must be added. All methods will be integrated through Stripe’s existing infrastructure using the Stripe Payment Element and Express Checkout Element, minimizing new engineering overhead while unlocking multiple wallets and payment platforms in a single integration. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Requestor placing a request on the Gopher App, ## 🎯 I want to be able to pay using my preferred payment method beyond just a debit or credit card, ## ✅ So that I can complete my request even if my card balance is insufficient, and choose the payment option most convenient for me. ## 💡 Context / Background * Card declines represent a direct loss of completed orders. Offering alternative payment methods reduces this friction and increases the likelihood of a successful transaction. * Digital wallets have surpassed credit cards as the most popular online checkout method in 2025, with 58% of online purchases projected to be made via alternative payment methods by 2028. * Stripe research shows that dynamically offering just one additional relevant payment method increases conversion by an average of 7.4%, with businesses expanding payment options seeing an average revenue boost of 12%. * 10% of US shoppers have abandoned a purchase solely because their preferred payment method was not available. * All target payment methods are supported natively through Stripe, meaning they can be enabled from the Stripe Dashboard with minimal additional code using the Payment Element and Express Checkout Element. * Adding alternative payment methods also reduces fraud risk by shifting payment authentication and liability to established third-party platforms. ## 💳 Payment Methods to Add ### Apple Pay * One-tap checkout using Face ID, Touch ID, or passcode — no card details re-entered * Automatically presented on iOS/Safari devices when enabled via Stripe Express Checkout Element * Card data is masked — Gopher Inc never sees the underlying card number, reducing fraud exposure * Stripe integration reference: https://stripe.com/payments/apple-pay ### Google Pay * One-tap checkout on Android and Chrome devices * Automatically presented on Android/Chrome when enabled via Stripe Express Checkout Element * Same tokenization and fraud protection benefits as Apple Pay * Stripe integration reference: https://stripe.com/payment-method/google-pay ### PayPal (includes Venmo access) * PayPal is one of the most trusted and widely used alternative payment methods in the US * Connecting PayPal through Stripe also unlocks Venmo access for users who have linked Venmo to their PayPal account * PayPal handles authentication and payment liability independently, reducing fraud risk for the platform * Note: PayPal via Stripe charges slightly higher processing fees than standard card payments — this should be factored into pricing expectations * Stripe integration reference: https://stripe.com/payment-method/paypal ### Cash App Pay * Popular among younger demographics and users without traditional banking relationships * Users authenticate and pay directly through the Cash App * Supported natively through Stripe with no separate merchant account required * Stripe integration reference: https://stripe.com/payments/cash-app-pay ### Venmo (Standalone) * Venmo is accessible via the PayPal Stripe integration (above) for users with linked accounts * For standalone Venmo support, integration is available through Braintree (PayPal’s payment platform) using iOS and Android SDKs * Important: Venmo must not be loaded in a WebView or iframe — must use Safari View Controller (iOS) or Chrome Custom Tabs (Android) * Venmo is US-only and requires a US-based business entity * Business transaction fee: 1.9% + $0.10 per transaction ## 📸 Card Scan to Register * Users must be able to take a photo of their debit or credit card to register it, rather than manually entering card details * Stripe’s mobile SDKs support card scanning natively via the Stripe iOS and Android SDKs * This feature reduces checkout friction and card entry errors on mobile ## ⚙️ Integration Approach & Best Practices * **Use Stripe’s Payment Element + Express Checkout Element** — a single integration that dynamically surfaces eligible payment methods based on the user’s device, location, and transaction context. No separate integrations needed for Apple Pay or Google Pay. * **Enable Dynamic Payment Methods** from the Stripe Dashboard — Stripe automatically orders payment methods by conversion probability. New methods can be turned on without code changes. * **Device-aware display** — Apple Pay should only appear on Apple devices; Google Pay on Android/Chrome. Stripe’s Express Checkout Element handles this detection automatically. * **Never handle raw card data server-side** — all payment data is tokenized through Stripe before it reaches Gopher’s servers, maintaining PCI DSS compliance. * **Use webhooks for payment status** — do not rely solely on client-side confirmation. Stripe webhooks must confirm payment success server-side before a request is submitted. * **Set user expectations on fees** — some payment methods (PayPal, Venmo, Cash App) carry slightly different processing fees. The UI must clearly communicate any cost differences to the Requestor before they confirm payment. * **Accordion layout** — with 4+ payment methods, use the accordion layout in the Payment Element for cleaner UX. Display the top 3–4 by default with a “More” option. * **Enable Stripe Link** — Stripe’s one-click checkout that saves and autofills payment and shipping details for returning users, further reducing friction. ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Requestor sees all available payment methods at checkout * **Given** a Requestor reaches the payment step * **When** the payment screen loads * **Then** all eligible payment methods are displayed based on the user’s device and location * **And** Apple Pay is shown on iOS devices, Google Pay on Android/Chrome devices ### Scenario 2 – Requestor can complete payment via each new payment method * **Given** a Requestor selects an alternative payment method (Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Cash App, or Venmo) * **When** they complete authentication with the chosen provider * **Then** the payment is processed and the request is submitted successfully ### Scenario 3 – Card scan registers a new card * **Given** a Requestor wants to add a new debit or credit card * **When** they tap the card scan option and capture their card with the camera * **Then** the card details are populated automatically and the card is registered to their account ### Scenario 4 – Fee differences are communicated before payment confirmation * **Given** a Requestor selects a payment method that carries a different processing fee * **When** the method is selected * **Then** any applicable cost adjustment is clearly shown before the Requestor confirms payment ## ⚙️ Business Rules * All payment methods must process through Stripe — no raw payment data is to be handled by Gopher’s servers. * Apple Pay must only be presented on Apple devices; Google Pay must only be presented on Android/Chrome. * Venmo must not be loaded in a WebView — must use Safari View Controller (iOS) or Chrome Custom Tabs (Android). * Any fee differences associated with a payment method must be disclosed to the Requestor before payment confirmation. * Payment success must be confirmed server-side via Stripe webhooks before a request is activated. * Card scan must tokenize data through Stripe SDKs — no raw card numbers stored on Gopher’s servers. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Implement Stripe’s Payment Element and Express Checkout Element using the iOS and Android SDKs for in-app payments. * Enable Dynamic Payment Methods in the Stripe Dashboard so new methods can be toggled on/off without code changes. * PayPal must be enabled through Stripe’s PayPal integration to also unlock Venmo for linked accounts. * For standalone Venmo, evaluate Braintree SDK integration (PayPal’s platform) as a complementary option. * Review and confirm processing fee structure for each new payment method with finance before go-live. * Card scan requires Stripe’s mobile SDK card scanning feature — confirm availability in current SDK version. * Configure Stripe webhooks to handle payment success, failure, and cancellation events for all new payment methods. * Evaluate enabling Stripe Link for one-click returning user checkout. * Figma UI reference: https://www.figma.com/design/H6THlatWvwT6ESI2j4MPTi/Final-Flows?node-id=1149-3711 ## 🧪 QA Notes * Test each payment method end-to-end: Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Cash App Pay, and Venmo — confirm successful payment and request submission. * Verify Apple Pay only appears on iOS devices and Google Pay only on Android/Chrome. * Test card scan — confirm card details are correctly populated and registered. * Simulate payment failures for each method — confirm graceful error handling and that the Requestor is returned to the payment screen to retry or select a different method. * Verify fee disclosures appear correctly for applicable payment methods before confirmation. * Confirm payment success is verified server-side via webhook before the request is activated. * Test Venmo flow — confirm it launches in Safari View Controller (iOS) or Chrome Custom Tabs (Android), not a WebView. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher App - Ratings Screen - Viewing Pic For Non Age-Restricted Request
Description: When a non-age-restricted request is completed, the Gopher must be taken through a photo upload screen before reaching the rating screen. Photos taken by the Gopher are shared with the Requestor on their confirmation screen for verification — particularly important for contactless deliveries. The rating screen must persist until completed, and if the Gopher has been selected as a Favorite, a congratulations modal must fire after rating. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher who has just completed a non-age-restricted request, ## 🎯 I want to optionally add completion photos and then be taken to the rating screen once the Requestor confirms, ## ✅ So that the Requestor can visually verify the completed delivery, confirmation is smooth, and the full post-completion flow resolves correctly including Favorite Gopher recognition. ## 💡 Context / Background * Age-restricted requests require mandatory in-person identity verification and follow a separate completion flow (covered in G40-192). * Non-age-restricted requests use this photo upload and rating flow instead. * The photo upload step allows Gophers to document completed deliveries, providing the Requestor with visual proof — especially valuable for contactless deliveries. * The Submit button must remain inactive until at least one photo is added or Skip is explicitly selected. * The rating screen must remain displayed until the Gopher completes the rating — it must not be dismissible. ## 🔀 Complete Flow ### Step 1 – Photo Upload Screen * Immediately after marking the request complete, the Gopher is taken to the photo upload screen * The Gopher can upload up to 3 photos * The Submit button remains inactive until at least one photo is added OR the Gopher taps Skip * Note: this photo step does NOT apply to age-restricted deliveries, which require mandatory in-person verification ### Step 2 – Photo Appears on Requestor’s Confirmation Screen * If one or more photos were added, they are displayed on the Requestor’s confirmation screen under a "View pic(s) of completed request" section * The Requestor can review the photo(s) before confirming the order * If Skip was selected, no photos are shown on the confirmation screen ### Step 3 – Requestor Confirms → Gopher Receives Banner Notification * Once the Requestor confirms the order, the Gopher receives a banner notification * Tapping the banner notification — or the current screen — transitions to the rating screen ### Step 4 – Rating Screen * The rating screen is shown and remains displayed until the Gopher completes the rating * The screen must not be dismissible until the rating is submitted ### Step 5 – Favorite Gopher Congratulations Modal * After the rating is submitted, if the Gopher has been selected as a Favorite Gopher by the Requestor, the standard congratulations modal is displayed * If the Gopher is not a Favorite, the modal is not shown ## ❌ Current Behavior * The photo upload screen and associated flow are not functioning as designed for non-age-restricted requests * Photos may not be correctly surfaced on the Requestor’s confirmation screen * The Submit button may not correctly gate on photo upload or Skip selection * The rating screen may not persist correctly until the rating is completed * The Favorite Gopher congratulations modal may not fire correctly after rating ## ✅ Expected Behavior * On non-age-restricted request completion, the Gopher is taken to the photo upload screen * Submit is inactive until a photo is added or Skip is tapped * Any added photos appear on the Requestor’s confirmation screen for review before confirmation * On Requestor confirmation, the Gopher receives a banner notification and is transitioned to the rating screen * The rating screen persists until the Gopher completes the rating * If the Gopher is a Favorite, the congratulations modal fires after the rating is submitted ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Submit is inactive until photo added or Skip selected * **Given** a Gopher is on the photo upload screen after completing a non-age-restricted request * **When** no photo has been added and Skip has not been tapped * **Then** the Submit button remains inactive ### Scenario 2 – Photos appear on Requestor confirmation screen * **Given** a Gopher has added one or more photos and submitted * **When** the Requestor views their confirmation screen * **Then** the photo(s) are displayed under "View pic(s) of completed request" * **And** the Requestor can review them before confirming ### Scenario 3 – No photos shown when Skip was selected * **Given** a Gopher tapped Skip on the photo upload screen * **When** the Requestor views their confirmation screen * **Then** no photo section is shown ### Scenario 4 – Gopher receives banner notification on Requestor confirmation * **Given** the Requestor has confirmed the order * **When** the confirmation is submitted * **Then** the Gopher receives a banner notification * **And** tapping the banner or the current screen transitions to the rating screen ### Scenario 5 – Rating screen persists until completed * **Given** the Gopher is on the rating screen * **When** the Gopher attempts to navigate away without completing the rating * **Then** the screen remains displayed and cannot be dismissed until the rating is submitted ### Scenario 6 – Favorite Gopher congratulations modal fires after rating * **Given** the Gopher has been selected as a Favorite by the Requestor * **When** the Gopher submits the rating * **Then** the congratulations modal is displayed ### Scenario 7 – No congratulations modal if Gopher is not a Favorite * **Given** the Gopher has not been selected as a Favorite * **When** the Gopher submits the rating * **Then** no congratulations modal is shown ## ⚙️ Business Rules * This photo upload and rating flow applies to non-age-restricted requests only. Age-restricted requests follow a separate completion flow (G40-192). * The Submit button on the photo upload screen must never activate unless at least one photo is added or Skip is tapped. * A maximum of 3 photos may be uploaded per completed request. * Photos submitted by the Gopher must always appear on the Requestor’s confirmation screen before confirmation is possible. * The rating screen must persist and remain non-dismissible until the Gopher submits their rating. * The Favorite Gopher congratulations modal must only fire if the Requestor has designated the Gopher as a Favorite. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * This flow is specific to non-age-restricted requests. Age-restricted completion flow is covered in G40-192. * The photo(s) must be stored and linked to the Order ID so they can be retrieved and displayed on the Requestor’s confirmation screen. * The Favorite Gopher status must be queryable at the time the rating is submitted to determine whether to show the congratulations modal. * Figma design reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=110-15858 ## 🧪 QA Notes * Complete a non-age-restricted request — confirm photo upload screen appears immediately. * Attempt to submit without adding a photo or tapping Skip — confirm Submit button remains inactive. * Add 1, 2, and 3 photos — confirm Submit activates and up to 3 photos can be uploaded. * Submit with photos — confirm photos appear on the Requestor’s confirmation screen under "View pic(s) of completed request". * Submit with Skip — confirm no photo section appears on the Requestor’s confirmation screen. * Requestor confirms the order — confirm the Gopher receives a banner notification. * Tap the banner notification — confirm transition to the rating screen. * Attempt to navigate away from the rating screen without submitting — confirm the screen persists. * Submit the rating as a Favorite Gopher — confirm the congratulations modal appears. * Submit the rating as a non-Favorite Gopher — confirm no congratulations modal appears. * Confirm this flow does not trigger for age-restricted requests. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher App - Expired Request - Do Not Let A Request Expire With Pending Offers - Send Final SMS
Description: > ✅ **GROOMED 2026-07-02 — spec locked with owner, no open questions.** The in-app **NEEDS ATTENTION** + accept/decline UI is _already largely built_ in the new front-end (`gopher-request.html`). The remaining work is the **backend deferred-expiration guard + final SMS** — see the comment for the code trace and where it lives. ## 🎯 Goal A request must **not expire while a Gopher has already accepted it** (pending requestor accept/decline) **or submitted a counter-offer.** Instead, prompt the requestor (final SMS + in-app NEEDS ATTENTION) and hold the request open for a **1-hour grace window**, so a valid offer isn't lost just because the requestor stepped away from their phone. _Why (real scenario):_ 1pm — requestor puts phone down → 2pm — worker accepts → 3pm — request would normally expire → 4pm — requestor returns. Without this feature the accepted offer is lost at 3pm. ## ⏲️ Normal expiration timers (a request “expires” = never accepted) | Request type | Expires after | | --- | --- | | First available | 1 hour | | Flexible | 24 hours / 1 week / 2 weeks (requestor's chosen window) | | Scheduled | the exact scheduled date/time | The deferral below applies to **all** of these triggers. ## 🔁 Behavior 1. **Defer on pending offer.** When a request reaches its expiration (any timer above) **AND** a Gopher has accepted (pending requestor action) **OR** a counter-offer is pending → do **not** expire. 2. **Final SMS.** Send **one** final SMS to the requestor — “you have a pending offer” + a deep link into the app. Respect SMS opt-out; never send duplicates. 3. **In-app NEEDS ATTENTION.** Opening the app shows a NEEDS ATTENTION alert / blocking prompt that disables other activity until addressed. Tapping **View Interested Workers** → the offer screen to **Accept** or **Decline**. 4. **1-hour grace.** The request is held open for **1 hour, measured from when the final SMS / NEEDS ATTENTION prompt is sent.** * **Accept** → request connects and proceeds to fulfillment as a standard accepted request. * **Decline** → request expires immediately (normal expired logic). * **No action within the 1 hour** → request expires (normal expired logic). ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria **S1 — Pending offer prevents expiration (all timer types).** Given a request of any type (first-available / flexible / scheduled) reaches its expiration with a Gopher acceptance or counter-offer pending, when the expiration logic runs, then the request must NOT expire. **S2 — Final SMS.** Given a request with a pending offer reaches expiration, then exactly one final SMS with an app deep link is sent to the requestor (respecting opt-out, no duplicates). **S3 — NEEDS ATTENTION shown.** Given the requestor opens the app, then a NEEDS ATTENTION alert is clearly displayed and routes to View Interested Workers → Accept/Decline. **S4 — Accept after expiry time.** Given the request had already reached its expiration time, when the requestor accepts the pending offer, then the request connects and proceeds to fulfillment. **S5 — Decline.** Given the deferred request, when the requestor declines, then the request expires immediately. **S6 — Grace lapse.** Given no action is taken, when 1 hour elapses from the final SMS/prompt, then the request expires (normal expired logic). **S7 — Scheduled-request regression (the QA failure).** Given a **scheduled** request whose exact date/time passes with a Gopher already accepted (the “I'll select my worker” case), when the scheduled time is reached, then the request must **defer, not expire** — this is the specific regression QA returned on 2026-01-15 (booking #466). ## ⚙️ Business Rules * A request cannot expire while there is a pending acceptance or counter-offer; expiry is deferred until the requestor accepts/declines or the 1-hour grace lapses. * The 1-hour grace is anchored to the **final SMS / NEEDS ATTENTION prompt**. * Applies to **all** request types and all expiration timers. * SMS respects opt-out and must not duplicate. Confirm no conflict with broadcast/reminder logic. ## 🎨 Design Figma (pop-up + NEEDS ATTENTION + Accept/Decline): https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=8821-8919 ## 🧪 QA Notes * Test single acceptance, multiple acceptances, and counter-offers — across first-available, flexible, and scheduled requests. * Re-verify the booking #466 scheduled-request case specifically. * Verify one and only one SMS is sent, and only when applicable. * Validate Accept vs Decline vs no-action-after-1-hour paths. iOS + Android.
