Summary: Both apps — render phone-sized layout on tablets (iPad + Android), scaled to width and locked to portrait, to fix distortion and unreachable navigation
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher or Requestor using either app (Gopher / Gopher Go) on a tablet, ## 🎯 I want the app to render in a usable, distortion-free portrait layout that fills my tablet's screen width, ## ✅ So that I can navigate, view request details, and complete every flow on my tablet without controls being unreachable, stretched, or cut off. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * Both apps currently render poorly on tablets — layouts intended for phone-sized viewports stretch, misalign, or leave navigation controls in unreachable positions when the OS supplies a larger viewport. * The fix is to **render the existing phone layout on tablets**, scaled to the tablet's full width in portrait orientation. This avoids building and maintaining a separate tablet UI while restoring usable navigation. * Vertical space is allowed to extend naturally — taller tablet aspect ratios will simply show more content or allow scrolling where appropriate. * This approach is conceptually similar to apps like CashApp that lock to phone-style layouts on tablets, but uses **scale-to-width** rather than centred-with-letterbox so the tablet's full screen width is used. --- ## 🚫 Current Behavior * On tablets (iPad and Android), layouts intended for phone viewports do not render correctly. * Symptoms reported include stretched or misaligned elements and navigation controls that are unreachable or distorted. * Net effect: users on tablets are unable to navigate the app reliably. --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior * On any supported tablet (iPad **and** Android tablets), the app renders the existing phone layout with the following adjustments: * **Width:** the layout is scaled to fill the tablet's full width. * **Height:** content flows naturally to the tablet's height. Where content is shorter than the viewport, the screen simply has unused vertical space at the bottom. Where content would exceed the viewport, the screen scrolls. * **Orientation:** the app is **locked to portrait** on tablets — landscape is not supported in this release. * All controls, navigation elements, and tappable areas remain reachable and functional. * No tablet-specific UI components are introduced — the existing phone components are reused. --- ## 📐 Approach Summary | Dimension | Behaviour | | --- | --- | | Layout source | Reuse existing phone layout (no tablet-specific UI) | | Width | Scale to the tablet's full screen width | | Height | Adapt to tablet height; scroll vertically if content exceeds viewport | | Orientation | Lock to portrait | | Platforms in scope | iPad (iPadOS) and Android tablets | | Apps in scope | Both — Gopher (Requestor) and Gopher Go | --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — iPad portrait rendering** * **Given** a user opens the app on an iPad in portrait orientation, * **When** the app loads, * **Then** the phone layout is rendered scaled to the iPad's full width, all controls are reachable, and no elements are stretched, distorted, or cut off. **Scenario 2 — Android tablet portrait rendering** * **Given** a user opens the app on an Android tablet in portrait orientation, * **When** the app loads, * **Then** the phone layout is rendered scaled to the tablet's full width, all controls are reachable, and no elements are stretched, distorted, or cut off. **Scenario 3 — Orientation lock** * **Given** the user is on a tablet (iPad or Android), * **When** the user rotates the device to landscape, * **Then** the app remains locked in portrait orientation — the layout does not rotate. **Scenario 4 — Tall viewport with shorter content** * **Given** a screen with content shorter than the tablet's viewport height, * **When** the user views that screen, * **Then** the content displays in full at the top with unused vertical space at the bottom — no stretching to fill the viewport. **Scenario 5 — Tall viewport with overflowing content** * **Given** a screen with content taller than the tablet's viewport height, * **When** the user views that screen, * **Then** the content is scrollable vertically and all elements are reachable. **Scenario 6 — Both apps covered** * **Given** the fix is shipped, * **When** a user opens Gopher (Requestor) on a tablet and a Gopher opens Gopher Go on a tablet, * **Then** both apps render correctly under the same rules. **Scenario 7 — Phone regression check** * **Given** the fix is shipped, * **When** the same builds are opened on phones, * **Then** phone layouts render identically to pre-change — no regression introduced by the tablet rendering changes. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * Tablets must always render in **portrait orientation**. Landscape is explicitly out of scope for this release. * The phone layout is the single source of truth for both phones and tablets — no tablet-specific component variants are introduced. * The layout must scale to use the tablet's **full screen width**, not a fixed maximum width. * Vertical layout is adaptive — short content does not stretch; long content scrolls. * All interactive elements (buttons, inputs, navigation, modals) must remain fully functional and reachable on every supported tablet form factor. * The fix applies uniformly to both Gopher and Gopher Go. --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * Scaling to width will also scale text and touch target sizes proportionally — confirm text wrapping, line heights, and any fixed-pixel constraints in components don't break at scaled-up sizes. * Modals, popovers, and bottom sheets should be tested specifically — these often have hardcoded dimensions that don't survive scale-to-width. * iPad split-view / Stage Manager and Android split-screen modes can hand the app a phone-width viewport at any moment — the layout should already work in that mode without special-casing. * The portrait lock should be set at the app/manifest level (`UISupportedInterfaceOrientations` on iOS, `screenOrientation` on Android), not per-screen. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Test on a representative range of tablets covering both narrow and wide tablet aspect ratios. Suggested matrix: * iPad mini, iPad (standard), iPad Pro 12.9" * Android tablets in both 16:10 and 4:3 aspect ratios * For each device, walk every primary flow end-to-end: sign-in, request creation, request acceptance, completion, profile, payout setup. * Verify orientation lock by attempting to rotate every screen. * Test a screen known to be short (e.g., a login screen) and a screen known to be long (e.g., an order details with multiple items) to confirm vertical handling. * Run the same builds on phones (iOS and Android) to confirm no regression. * Re-attach the original screenshot directly to this ticket (the existing `blob:` URL does not render for other users). --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * This is a UI-layer change with no backend impact — no API or data model work is required. * Landscape orientation and tablet-specific UI components (multi-column layouts, sidebars, etc.) are explicitly **out of scope** and can be considered in a future enhancement if tablet usage justifies the investment.

Summary: Gopher App - Account - Payment Account - Enter Debit/CC Error
Description: ### **As a** Gopher App user adding my debit or credit card information, ### **I want** to be able to easily tap and enter my card details in all required fields, including the **CVC code**, ### **So that** I can successfully save my payment method without frustration or input errors. ‌ ### **💡Context / Background** ‌ * Since the **June 2025 Apple iOS update**, users have reported issues when attempting to add a **debit or credit card** in the **Gopher App → Account → Payment Account** section. * The **tap area** for the card number and especially the **CVC input field** has become **extremely difficult or unresponsive** to interact with. * This prevents users from completing card entry, affecting their ability to add or update payment methods. ‌ ### **✅ Acceptance Criteria (Given / When / Then)** ‌ **Scenario 1 – Card input fields responsive** * **Given** the user navigates to **Account → Payment Account**, * **When** they tap on any debit or credit card input field (card number, expiry, CVC), * **Then** the input cursor should reliably activate in the selected field, * **And** the keyboard should appear immediately for text entry. ‌ **Scenario 2 – CVC input specifically** * **Given** the user attempts to tap into the **CVC field**, * **When** tapping anywhere within its visible area, * **Then** the tap target should register correctly, allowing input focus without repeated attempts. ‌ **Scenario 3 – Cross-device consistency** * **Given** the app is running on different devices and OS versions, * **When** users enter payment information, * and may relate to layout or framework compatibility (e.g., iOS tap target sizing). * Minimum tap area must comply with Apple’s accessibility guidelines (44x44pt). * No changes to payment processing logic — only UI responsiveness. * Ensure the fix maintains PCI compliance and secure entry behavior. ‌ ### **🔍 Example** | **Field** | **Current Behavior** | **Expected Behavior** | | --- | --- | --- | | Card number | Difficult to tap / activate | Tap reliably activates input cursor | | Expiration date | Occasionally responsive | Always responsive and easy to select | | CVC | Nearly impossible to engage | Fully tappable area, easy to enter CVC | ‌ ### **🧪 QA Notes:** ‌ * Test on multiple iPhone models and iOS versions (pre- and post–June ’25). * Confirm that all card fields (number, expiry, CVC) respond on first tap. * Validate keyboard pop-up timing and cursor positioning. * Ensure no new visual misalignments introduced by the fix.

Summary: Gopher Location Not Updating in Real Time During Active Requests
Description: **Type:** Bug / Functional Gap **Priority:** High **Component:** GPS / Location Services / Worker App **Reporter:** John **Environment:** Production (iOS + Android) --- ## **Summary** During active requests, the **Gopher location icon does not update or move in real time** on the customer’s map. This is caused by the Gopher app not running in the foreground and the device disabling GPS in the background. Real-time tracking is critical for request monitoring, ETA accuracy, and overall trust. --- ## **Description** When a request is marked **In Progress**, the requester expects to see the Gopher’s movement live on the map. However: * The Gopher icon remains frozen * No location updates occur unless the Gopher reopens the app * Many devices are disabling GPS when the app is in the background * Some Gophers fully close the app, eliminating location updates entirely This results in inaccurate ETAs, poor transparency, and negative user experience. --- ## **Business Impact** * Requesters believe Gophers are not moving, causing cancellations and support messages * Workers appear unreliable even though they are en route * Trust and transparency are compromised * Essential for deliveries, ride share–style jobs, and any location-based service * Impacts worker safety and accountability --- ## **Requirements** ✅ **1. Implement reliable background location updates for Gophers during any active request** * App must continue sending GPS updates even when minimized * Must comply with iOS/Android background location requirements ✅ **2. Add a persistent location-tracking state when a job is In Progress** * Backend must continue receiving updates at defined intervals * App should NOT rely on the user keeping the app open ✅ **3. Implement fallback logic if GPS is disabled** * If OS blocks GPS → show a “Location Paused” or similar state (optional) * Prompt Gopher to re-enable location permissions ✅ **4. Summary: Admin Panel / Gopher Go — Capture GPS and timestamp when a Gopher taps "Requestor not present" / "No-Show," matching the existing capture pattern used by other status updates (ref: order 38057)
Components: Gopher Admin Panel, Gopher Go App
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher admin reviewing request logs to investigate no-show disputes, ## 🎯 I want the Gopher's "Requestor not present" / "No-Show" action to capture the GPS location and timestamp — the same way other status updates already do — ## ✅ So that I have the evidence I need to fairly evaluate no-show situations (was the Gopher actually at the address? at what time?), instead of relying on the Gopher's word alone. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * During the completion cycle of a request, a Gopher can mark the Requestor as not present (the "No-Show" / "Requestor not present" action). * For every **other** status update in the completion flow, the app captures the Gopher's GPS coordinates and a server-side timestamp — these populate the order's activity log and are used for disputes, support, and pattern detection. * This one status update does **not** capture either field. That gap means we have no objective evidence of where or when the Gopher claimed the Requestor wasn't there, which is exactly the data needed when a no-show is disputed. * **Reference order for reproduction:** 38057. --- ## 🚫 Current Behavior * When a Gopher taps "Requestor not present" / "No-Show" during a request's completion cycle, the action is recorded but no GPS coordinates or timestamp are captured against that action in the order log. * Other status updates in the same flow do capture GPS + timestamp correctly, so the gap is specific to this one event. --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior * When the Gopher taps "Requestor not present" / "No-Show," the system captures: * **GPS coordinates** (latitude / longitude) of the Gopher at the moment of the tap. * **Server-side timestamp** of when the action was recorded. * Both fields are written to the order's activity log alongside the no-show event, in the same format as existing status-update entries. * The capture follows the **same pattern used by other status updates** — same location-permission handling, same fallback for stale / unavailable location (e.g., last-known + staleness flag), same persistence path. * The captured data is visible in the **Admin Panel request log** for the order, in the same way other status update timestamps and locations appear today. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — GPS and timestamp captured when no-show is tapped** * **Given** a Gopher is in the completion cycle of a request, * **When** they tap "Requestor not present" / "No-Show," * **Then** the order's activity log records the action with the Gopher's GPS coordinates and a server-side timestamp. **Scenario 2 — Data is visible in the Admin Panel request log** * **Given** a no-show event has been recorded for an order, * **When** an admin opens the order's request log in the Admin Panel, * **Then** the no-show entry displays its GPS coordinates and timestamp in the same format as other status update entries. **Scenario 3 — Capture pattern matches other status updates** * **Given** a side-by-side comparison of the no-show entry and other status-update entries on the same order, * **When** an admin inspects them, * **Then** the format and presence of GPS / timestamp data is consistent across all entries. **Scenario 4 — Stale or unavailable location handled the same way** * **Given** location services are unavailable, denied, or stale at the moment of the no-show tap, * **When** the action is recorded, * **Then** the same fallback used by other status updates is applied (e.g., last-known location + staleness flag, or null with a clear indicator) — the event itself is still recorded. **Scenario 5 — Reference order regression check** * **Given** the conditions of order 38057 are reproduced on a test order, * **When** the no-show action is triggered, * **Then** GPS and timestamp are captured (whereas on order 38057 today they are not). --- ## 📐 Business Rules * The no-show event must capture both **GPS coordinates** and a **server-side timestamp**. * Capture behaviour follows the same pattern as other status updates in the request completion flow — no special-case handling for this action. * The captured data appears in the Admin Panel request log alongside other status events. * This is the **Gopher Go** app (Gopher-side action); the data flows server-side into the shared order activity log visible in the Admin Panel. --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * The fix is almost certainly a small one: the existing status-update code path captures GPS + timestamp, and this one action's handler is missing that step. Find the handler for "Requestor not present" / "No-Show" and call the same capture helper used by sibling status updates. * Confirm the capture is server-side timestamp (not client clock) to prevent tampering or clock-drift issues. * Do not introduce a new schema for the no-show entry — reuse whatever activity-log row shape other status updates use. * No backend migration is required — historical no-show entries that were recorded without GPS/timestamp remain as-is. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Reproduce the bug against order 38057's flow on a test account: trigger a no-show event without the fix and confirm no GPS/timestamp is captured. * Apply the fix, trigger the same flow, and confirm GPS coordinates and timestamp are recorded in the activity log. * Open the Admin Panel request log and confirm the no-show entry shows its GPS and timestamp in the same format as other status update entries. * Disable location permission on the test device and trigger the no-show — confirm the action is still recorded with the same fallback that other status updates use. * Confirm no regression to any other status update's GPS/timestamp capture. * Test on both iOS and Android. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Depends on the existing status-update GPS/timestamp capture pattern being modifiable to cover this one missing event. * Out of scope: backfilling GPS/timestamp on historical no-show records (we don't have the location data; only going-forward events will have it). * Out of scope: any UI changes to the Gopher-facing no-show flow — the fix is purely in the data capture path. ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=external&localId=null&id=&&collection=&height=null&occurrenceKey=null&width=null&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=blob%3Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fmedia.staging.atl-paas.net%2F%3Ftype%3Dfile%26localId%3Dnull%26id%3Daeec6a5e-90ff-45d3-ab08-2862f9878ed9%26%26collection%3D%26height%3D408%26occurrenceKey%3Dnull%26width%3D253%26__contextId%3Dnull%26__displayType%3Dnull%26__external%3Dfalse%26__fileMimeType%3Dnull%26__fileName%3Dnull%26__fileSize%3Dnull%26__mediaTraceId%3Dnull%26url%3Dnull)

Summary: Gopher App - Completed Request Confirmation Screen Update
Description: Requestors can have multiple active requests running simultaneously. When a completion notification fires, the current confirmation screen does not specify which request was completed, leaving the Requestor unable to quickly identify it. A "Tap to view details" link must be added to the completion modal so the Requestor can immediately see which request has been completed. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Requestor who may have multiple active requests at the same time, ## 🎯 I want the completion confirmation screen to clearly identify which specific request has been completed, ## ✅ So that I am never confused about which of my requests was just finished and can quickly review the details. ## 💡 Context / Background * Some Requestors run multiple requests concurrently, making it ambiguous which request a generic completion notification refers to. * The current completion confirmation screen does not surface any request-specific identifying information. * A "Tap to view details" link must be added to the completion modal, taking the Requestor directly to the details of the completed request. ## ❌ Current Behavior * The completion confirmation screen does not specify which request has been completed * Requestors with multiple active requests have no way to quickly identify which one was just finished from the confirmation screen ## ✅ Expected Behavior * The completion confirmation modal includes a "Tap to view details" link * Tapping the link opens a modal or navigates the Requestor directly to the details of the specific request that was just completed * This behavior applies regardless of how many active requests the Requestor has ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Tap to view details link appears on completion modal * **Given** a Gopher marks a request as completed * **When** the completion confirmation modal is shown to the Requestor * **Then** a "Tap to view details" link is visible on the modal ### Scenario 2 – Tapping the link shows the correct completed request details * **Given** the Requestor taps "Tap to view details" on the completion modal * **When** the link is tapped * **Then** the details of the specific request that was just completed are displayed (including any pics) * **And** no other active requests are shown or confused with it ### Scenario 3 – Behavior is consistent for single and multiple active requests * **Given** a Requestor has one or more active requests * **When** any request is completed * **Then** the "Tap to view details" link always appears and always links to the correct completed request ## ⚙️ Business Rules * The "Tap to view details" link must always reference the specific Order # of the request that was just completed. * The link must appear on the completion modal for all Requestors, regardless of how many active requests they have. * Tapping the link must never navigate to a different request. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * The completion modal must pass the correct Order ID to the "Tap to view details" link at the time of completion. * Figma design reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=85-5288 ## 🧪 QA Notes * Test with a Requestor who has a single active request — confirm "Tap to view details" appears and links to the correct request. * Test with a Requestor who has multiple active requests — confirm the link identifies and displays only the completed request. * Verify the modal and link render correctly at the point of completion notification. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher App - Submitted Request - Gophers Interested, Bids or Counter Offers View - View Profile - Update Previous Job Views
Description: When a Requestor views a Gopher’s profile from the Gophers Interested, Bids, or Counter Offers screen, the previous jobs view must be updated to offer two viewing options: all previous jobs, and a filtered view showing only jobs matching the top-level category of the currently active request. The category-filtered view must dynamically reflect the relevant category and gracefully handle cases where the Gopher has no prior jobs in that category. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Requestor reviewing a Gopher’s profile from the Gophers Interested, Bids, or Counter Offers screen, ## 🎯 I want to be able to view all of a Gopher’s previous jobs or filter to only see jobs relevant to my current request category, ## ✅ So that I can quickly assess whether a Gopher has relevant experience for the type of request I am posting. ## 💡 Context / Background * When a Requestor taps View Profile on a Gopher from the Gophers Interested, Bids, or Counter Offers list, they can see the Gopher’s previous job history. * Currently the view shows all previous jobs without any filtering option. * Two viewing options must be available, with the full job history shown by default. * The category filter must use the top-level category of the currently broadcast request, mapping to one of four values: **Delivery**, **Need A Ride**, **Service**, or **Other** * Example: if the active request is Service → Home Service → Handyman, the filtered view label reads "View Previous Service Jobs Only" and shows only that Gopher’s past Service jobs. * If the Gopher has no prior jobs in the relevant category, an empty state message is displayed. ## 💼 Viewing Options * **View All Previous Jobs** — default view, shows the Gopher’s complete job history across all categories * **View Previous \[Category\] Jobs Only** — filtered view showing only jobs that match the top-level category of the currently broadcast request. The category label is dynamic and reflects one of: Delivery, Need A Ride, Service, or Other ## 🗒️ Dynamic Category Label Examples * Active request: Service → Home Service → Handyman → filter label: **View Previous Service Jobs Only** * Active request: Delivery → Convenience Store → filter label: **View Previous Delivery Jobs Only** * Active request: Need A Ride → filter label: **View Previous Need A Ride Jobs Only** * Active request: Other → filter label: **View Previous Other Jobs Only** ## ❌ Current Behavior * The View Profile screen displays all previous jobs with no filtering option * There is no way for a Requestor to quickly identify category-relevant experience for the Gopher they are considering ## ✅ Expected Behavior * The View Profile screen displays View All Previous Jobs by default * Below the default view, a second option reads "View Previous \[Category\] Jobs Only" with the category dynamically populated based on the active request * Tapping the category filter shows only jobs matching the top-level category of the active request * If the Gopher has no jobs in the relevant category, an empty state is shown: "No Previous \[Category\] Jobs" ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Default view shows all previous jobs * **Given** a Requestor taps View Profile on a Gopher from the Interested, Bids, or Counter Offers list * **When** the profile screen loads * **Then** all previous jobs are shown by default * **And** the "View Previous \[Category\] Jobs Only" option is visible below ### Scenario 2 – Category filter label reflects the active request’s top-level category * **Given** the active request is in the Service category * **When** the Requestor views a Gopher’s profile * **Then** the filter option reads "View Previous Service Jobs Only" ### Scenario 3 – Category filter shows only matching jobs * **Given** the Requestor taps "View Previous \[Category\] Jobs Only" * **When** the filtered view loads * **Then** only previous jobs matching the top-level category of the active request are displayed * **And** jobs from other categories are excluded ### Scenario 4 – Empty state when Gopher has no jobs in the relevant category * **Given** the Gopher has no previous jobs in the active request’s category * **When** the Requestor taps the category filter * **Then** an empty state message is displayed: "No Previous \[Category\] Jobs" ### Scenario 5 – Category label is correct across all four top-level categories * **Given** the active request belongs to any of the four top-level categories * **When** the Requestor views a Gopher’s profile * **Then** the filter label correctly reads Delivery, Need A Ride, Service, or Other respectively ## ⚙️ Business Rules * View All Previous Jobs is always the default view when the profile screen loads. * The category filter label must always map to one of the four top-level categories: **Delivery**, **Need A Ride**, **Service**, or **Other** — sub-categories are not used in the label. * The category is determined by the top-level category of the currently active/broadcast request, not the Gopher’s profile. * If a Gopher has no jobs in the relevant category, the empty state must be shown — no jobs from other categories should appear as a fallback. * This feature applies when viewing a profile from the Gophers Interested, Bids, and Counter Offers screens. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * The profile view must receive the top-level category of the active request at the time it is opened to dynamically populate the filter label and apply the correct filter. * Previous jobs must be tagged or queryable by top-level category on the backend. * Figma design reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=83-7733 ## 🧪 QA Notes * Test from a Service request — confirm filter label reads "View Previous Service Jobs Only" and shows only Service jobs. * Test from a Delivery request — confirm filter label reads "View Previous Delivery Jobs Only". * Test from a Need A Ride request — confirm filter label reads "View Previous Need A Ride Jobs Only". * Test from an Other request — confirm filter label reads "View Previous Other Jobs Only". * Test with a Gopher who has jobs in the relevant category — confirm only those jobs appear in the filtered view. * Test with a Gopher who has no jobs in the relevant category — confirm the empty state "No Previous \[Category\] Jobs" is shown. * Confirm View All Previous Jobs is always the default when the profile loads. * Test from Gophers Interested, Bids, and Counter Offers screens — confirm behavior is consistent across all three. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher Go - Active Request - SMS Message To Gopher Who Has Accepted A "Need ASAP" Request But Not Started After 10 min.
Description: When a Gopher accepts a "Need ASAP" request but fails to update the status to In Progress within 10 minutes, an automated SMS must be sent to prompt them to take action. If the request remains inactive after the SMS, push notification follow-ups must fire every 5 minutes until the Gopher updates the request to In Progress. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher who has accepted a Need ASAP request, ## 🎯 I want to be reminded if I have not started a request within 10 minutes of accepting it, ## ✅ So that I do not miss or delay a time-sensitive request and the Requestor receives timely service. ## 💡 Context / Background * "Need ASAP" requests are time-sensitive by nature — a Gopher who accepts but does not start creates a poor experience for the Requestor. * If a Gopher accepts a request but does not update the status to In Progress within 10 minutes, the system has no current mechanism to alert them. * An automated SMS is sent at the 10-minute mark as the primary alert, followed by push notification reminders at 5-minute intervals until the Gopher takes action. * This notification sequence applies only to Need ASAP requests, not scheduled requests. ## 📱 Notification Sequence * **T+10 minutes:** SMS sent to the Gopher * **T+15, T+20, T+25... (every 5 minutes):** Push notification follow-ups sent until the Gopher updates the request to In Progress * **Notifications stop** the moment the Gopher updates the request status to In Progress ## 💬 SMS Message Template Hi \[First Name\], Your Gopher request hasn’t had any activity since you accepted it. Please reach out to your customer ASAP and update the app to in-progress. Thanks! Gopher, Inc ## ❌ Current Behavior * No SMS or push notification is sent when a Gopher accepts a Need ASAP request but fails to start it within 10 minutes * There is no automated mechanism to prompt the Gopher to take action after acceptance ## ✅ Expected Behavior * 10 minutes after a Gopher accepts a Need ASAP request without updating to In Progress, an automated SMS is sent using the template above * Every 5 minutes after the initial SMS, a push notification follow-up is sent until the request is updated to In Progress * All notifications stop immediately when the Gopher updates the request status to In Progress ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – SMS fires at 10 minutes of inactivity after acceptance * **Given** a Gopher has accepted a Need ASAP request * **When** 10 minutes pass without the request being updated to In Progress * **Then** an automated SMS is sent to the Gopher using the defined message template ### Scenario 2 – Push notifications follow every 5 minutes after the SMS * **Given** the initial SMS has been sent and the request is still not updated to In Progress * **When** each 5-minute interval passes * **Then** a push notification reminder is sent to the Gopher ### Scenario 3 – All notifications stop when Gopher updates to In Progress * **Given** SMS and/or push notifications have been sent * **When** the Gopher updates the request status to In Progress * **Then** all scheduled notifications are cancelled immediately * **And** no further SMS or push notifications are sent for this request ### Scenario 4 – Notification sequence does not fire for scheduled requests * **Given** a Gopher has accepted a scheduled (non-Need ASAP) request * **When** 10 minutes pass without an In Progress update * **Then** no SMS or push notification is sent ## ⚙️ Business Rules * This notification sequence applies exclusively to Need ASAP requests. * The 10-minute timer starts from the moment the Gopher accepts the request, not from when the request was created. * The initial alert is an SMS; all follow-ups are push notifications at 5-minute intervals. * The notification sequence must stop immediately when the Gopher updates the request to In Progress. * The SMS must dynamically populate the Gopher’s first name. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * A background timer or job must be triggered on request acceptance for Need ASAP requests to track inactivity. * The timer and notification sequence must be cancelled immediately when the request status changes to In Progress. * SMS delivery requires an active SMS provider integration (e.g. Twilio or equivalent). * Push notification infrastructure must support scheduled/recurring notifications that can be cancelled on demand. ## 🧪 QA Notes * Accept a Need ASAP request and do not update to In Progress — confirm SMS arrives at exactly the 10-minute mark with correct Gopher name. * Continue waiting without updating — confirm push notifications arrive at 5-minute intervals after the SMS. * Update the request to In Progress at any point — confirm all pending notifications are cancelled and no further alerts fire. * Accept a scheduled request and wait 10+ minutes without updating — confirm no SMS or push notifications are sent. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher HQ Dashboard — replace Active Admin "Admin Panel" + embed Gopher iQ (Gopher Brain); plug into DB
Description: **This is a plug-in job, not a build.** A complete, working internal console — the **Gopher HQ Dashboard** — already exists and runs on **real production data**. It is intended to **completely replace the current Active Admin “Admin Panel,”** and it **embeds Gopher iQ — the “Gopher Brain.”** The developer’s job is to connect it to the production database + admin auth. No metrics or redesign work. **▶ Full developer handoff (red carpet):** `docs/handoff/G40-70-gopher-hq-dashboard.md` **▶ Artifact lives in:** `Documentation/Dashboard/` (built output: `output/Gopher_HQ_Dashboard.html`). ### What’s built * \~30 views across Operate / Grow / Platforms / Reports / Listen / Tools (orders, users, revenue, funnels, ops cadence, marketplace, moderation, financials, geo/DMA, retention). * Fed by the Gopher admin API via `gopher_pull.py` → `refresh.py` → `regen_*.py` → `build.py`. The `regen_*.py` transforms **are** the query spec (source table → metric block map is in the handoff). * Locked definitions: **GMV = delivered-only ≈ $1.23M**; `delivered` = finished. * **Gopher iQ (the Brain):** routing keyword vocab (8 categories, \~1,481 words), 182-entry FAQ, pill spec, and an **internal** moderation lexicon (11 policies / \~3,613 phrases). Real-time is the end state; automating the snapshot on a schedule is the fast first phase. 2. **Admin auth + retire the old Admin Panel** (real PII — auth is non-negotiable; owner-only for iQ + write-backs). 3. **Wire the write-backs:** moderation actions (`app_part4.js action()` BACKEND SEAM), iQ promote endpoint, pricing/promo. 4. Connect `moderation_rules.json` to the **G40-35** `POST /messages/precheck` (one moderation source of truth, not two). Automate the Invites CSV (last manual dataset). Everything — how it’s built, what it pulls from the DB, and how Gopher iQ is embedded — is documented in the handoff so implementation is turnkey.

Summary: Both apps — Cancellation push notification not firing for scheduled requests (should fire for all cancellations regardless of state, initiator, or proximity to scheduled time)
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher or Requestor whose scheduled request has been cancelled, ## 🎯 I want to receive a push notification at the moment of cancellation — the same way I do when an active request is cancelled — ## ✅ So that I'm immediately aware the request is no longer happening and can plan accordingly, instead of finding out only when I next open the app. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * Today, when an **active** request is cancelled (by Requestor, Gopher, or admin), both parties correctly receive a push notification. * When a **scheduled** request is cancelled, the push notification does **not** fire. The cancellation is processed and the order status updates, but neither party is alerted. * This is a clear inconsistency: cancellation notifications should not depend on whether the request was active vs. scheduled. --- ## 🚫 Current Behavior * Active request cancelled by any initiator (Requestor / Gopher / admin) → push notification fires to both parties. ✅ * **Scheduled** request cancelled by any initiator → push notification does **not** fire. ❌ --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior When a request is cancelled — **for any reason, whether active or scheduled, whether by Requestor, Gopher, or admin** — both users receive a push notification. The push notification format and content should match the existing active-request cancellation push (per the attached screenshots and Figma). ### Cancellation matrix (all should fire the push to both users) | Initiator | Request state | Push to Requestor | Push to Gopher | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Requestor | Active | ✅ Today | ✅ Today | | Requestor | Scheduled | ❌ Today → ✅ After fix | ❌ Today → ✅ After fix | | Gopher | Active | ✅ Today | ✅ Today | | Gopher | Scheduled | ❌ Today → ✅ After fix | ❌ Today → ✅ After fix | | Admin | Active | ✅ Today | ✅ Today | | Admin | Scheduled | ❌ Today → ✅ After fix | ❌ Today → ✅ After fix | --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — Requestor cancels a scheduled request** * **Given** a Requestor has a scheduled request matched with a Gopher, * **When** the Requestor cancels the request, * **Then** both the Requestor and the Gopher receive the cancellation push notification. **Scenario 2 — Gopher cancels a scheduled request** * **Given** a Gopher has accepted a scheduled request, * **When** the Gopher cancels the request, * **Then** both the Requestor and the Gopher receive the cancellation push notification. **Scenario 3 — Admin cancels a scheduled request** * **Given** a scheduled request exists, * **When** an admin cancels it from the Admin Panel, * **Then** both the Requestor and the Gopher receive the cancellation push notification. **Scenario 4 — Active-request push notifications are unchanged** * **Given** an active request is cancelled by any initiator, * **When** the cancellation processes, * **Then** both parties continue to receive the cancellation push notification as they do today — no regression. **Scenario 5 — Push notification content matches existing format** * **Given** a scheduled-request cancellation has occurred, * **When** the push notifications are dispatched, * **Then** their content and format match the existing active-request cancellation push (per the attached screenshots and linked Figma). **Scenario 6 — Both parties receive the push even if the cancellation happens shortly before the scheduled time** * **Given** a scheduled request whose scheduled time is within a few minutes of the cancellation moment, * **When** any party cancels it, * **Then** both push notifications fire normally — timing proximity to the scheduled time does not suppress the push. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * Cancellation push notifications must fire on **every** cancellation event, regardless of: * Who initiated (Requestor, Gopher, admin), * Whether the request was active or scheduled, * How close to the scheduled time the cancellation occurred. * **Both** the Requestor and Gopher must receive the push (one notification per party). * The push notification format and content match the existing active-cancellation push — no new design is introduced by this fix. --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * The fix is almost certainly localised: the cancellation handler probably has a code path for active requests that fires the push and a separate path for scheduled requests that doesn't. Find the scheduled-cancellation handler and add the same push-dispatch call used by the active path. * Confirm the push is fired **server-side** as part of the cancellation transaction — not from the client of the initiator. Otherwise, if the initiator's client crashes mid-flow, the counterparty silently misses the notification. * Reuse the existing push-notification template and dispatch helper used by the active-cancellation flow. Summary: Gopher App - Ratings - Add A MY Gopher issue
Description: After confirming an order on the ratings screen, even when the Gopher is already a MY Gopher, the box to recommend adding that Gopher as one of MY Gophers is unchecked. Very inconsistent performance here. ‌ ### **As a** Gopher App user rating a completed order, ### **I want** the “Add a MY Gopher” checkbox to remain correctly checked when the Gopher is **already part of my MY Gophers**, ### **So that** the post-order rating screen behaves consistently and doesn’t prompt me to add someone who’s already on my list. ‌ ### **💡 Context / Background** ‌ * After confirming an order, the user is taken to the **Ratings** screen. * Even when the Gopher is already saved as one of the user’s **MY Gophers**, the checkbox to “Add this Gopher as one of MY Gophers” sometimes appears **unchecked**. * This causes confusion and suggests the system does not recognize the existing relationship. * The issue occurs **intermittently** and results in **inconsistent behavior** between different sessions or users. ‌ ### **✅ Acceptance Criteria (Given / When / Then)** ‌ **Scenario 1 – Existing MY Gopher correctly recognized** * **Given** the user completes an order with a Gopher already on their MY Gophers list, * **When** the Ratings screen is displayed, * **Then** the “Add a MY Gopher” checkbox must appear **checked by default**. ‌ **Scenario 2 – New Gopher behavior unchanged** * **Given** the user completes an order with a Gopher **not yet** on their MY Gophers list, * **When** the Ratings screen appears, * **Then** the checkbox should be **unchecked by default**, allowing the user to opt-in manually. ‌ **Scenario 3 – Consistent logic across sessions** * **Given** any user completes multiple orders with the same Gopher, * **When** rating subsequent orders, * **Then** the checkbox state must remain consistent (checked if already a MY Gopher). ‌ ### **⚙️ Business Rules** ‌ * The checkbox should reflect the real-time database state of the Gopher–Requestor relationship. * When the user checks or unchecks the box, the backend should update the MY Gophers list accordingly. * No duplicate “Add” attempts should occur if the Gopher already exists in the list. * Applies to both **iOS** and **Android** apps. ‌ ### **🧠 Dependencies / Notes** ‌ * Review the logic linking the Ratings screen to the MY Gophers database table. * Confirm that user–Gopher relationship data is loaded before rendering the Ratings UI. * Verify caching or timing issues that may cause inconsistent state detection. * Test against multiple accounts and order histories to confirm fix reliability. ‌ ### **🧪 QA Notes:** ‌ * Test completing orders with both existing and new Gophers. * Verify checkbox state accurately reflects real relationship status. * Confirm behavior across multiple consecutive orders. * Ensure the MY Gopher list updates correctly when toggled manually. * Validate on both Android and iOS builds.

Summary: Gopher App - Dispute Protocol Update
Description: ### **As a** Requestor or Gopher involved in a dispute, ### **I want** a structured dispute resolution window before escalation, ### **So that** both parties have a fair opportunity to resolve the issue functionally (e.g., via cost adjustment) before the dispute is escalated and locked. ‌ ## **🎯 Goal** ‌ Prevent premature escalation of disputes that blocks resolution by introducing a **24-hour waiting period** before a Requestor can select **“Unable to resolve.”** ‌ ## **💡 Context / Background** ‌ Currently, the dispute flow works as follows: * A dispute is initiated by the Requestor. * The Requestor and Gopher are expected to work toward a resolution, often via **cost adjustment**. * If no agreement is reached, the Requestor can select **“Unable to resolve.”** * Selecting **“Unable to resolve” immediately disables the Gopher’s ability to make a cost adjustment.** ‌ ### **❌ Current Problems** ‌ * There is **no time limitation** between: * Initiating a dispute, and * Selecting “Unable to resolve.” * A Requestor can select “Unable to resolve” immediately, even before the Gopher has a reasonable chance to respond. * Once “Unable to resolve” is selected: * The dispute becomes **irreversible** * Gopher, Inc. **cannot intervene or assist** * The Gopher loses the ability to resolve the issue functionally This results in: * Premature escalations * Unresolved disputes * Poor experience for both Requestors and Gophers ‌ ## **🛠️ Proposed Update to Dispute Protocol** ‌ ### **1️⃣ 24-Hour Lock on “Unable to Resolve”** ‌ * After a dispute is initiated: * The **“Unable to resolve”** option must be **disabled for 24 hours** * During this window: * The Gopher can still propose a cost adjustment * Both parties can communicate toward resolution ### **2️⃣ Admin Override Capability** ‌ * Gopher, Inc. must be able to: * **Manually override** the 24-hour timer from the Admin Panel * Escalate or close disputes early when appropriate (fraud, abuse, edge cases) * This doesn’t imply a new development feature within the admin panel: such as new tabs, no new designs, no new views. * It is about granting the admin the option to intervene in the dispute, just like the requestor would do. ‌ ### **3️⃣ Admin Notification** ‌ * When a dispute is created: * Send an alert email to [**admin@gophergo.io**](mailto:admin@gophergo.io) * The Gopher already receives an email with next steps and should continue to do so. ‌ ## **✅ Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin Format)** ‌ * **Scenario: Lock “Unable to resolve” immediately after dispute creation** * **Given** a dispute has just been created * **When** the Requestor views dispute resolution options * **Then** the “Unable to resolve” option is disabled for 24 hours * **Scenario: Allow cost adjustments during the lock period** * **Given** a dispute is within the 24-hour lock window * **When** the Gopher attempts to submit a cost adjustment * **Then** the cost adjustment is allowed * **Scenario: Enable “Unable to resolve” after 24 hours** * **Given** 24 hours have passed since the dispute was initiated * **When** the Requestor views dispute options * **Then** the “Unable to resolve” option is enabled * **Scenario: Prevent escalation before lock expires** * **Given** a dispute is less than 24 hours old * **When** the Requestor attempts to select “Unable to resolve” * **Then** the system prevents the action and indicates escalation is not yet available * **Scenario: Admin intervenes during lock period** * **Given** a dispute is within the 24-hour lock period * **When** an admin intervenes the dispute via the Admin Panel * **Then** the dispute can be escalated or resolved immediately * **Scenario: Send admin notification on dispute creation** * **Given** a dispute is created * **When** the dispute is saved * **Then** an email notification is sent to [admin@gophergo.io](mailto:admin@gophergo.io) * **Scenario: Preserve dispute flow after escalation** * **Given** the Requestor selects “Unable to resolve” after the lock expires * **When** the dispute is escalated * **Then** the Gopher can no longer submit cost adjustments * **Scenario: No regression in existing dispute behavior** * **Given** a dispute follows the standard flow * **When** no escalation occurs * **Then** all existing dispute functionality continues to work as expected ## **⚙️ Business Rules** ‌ * Disputes must allow a **reasonable resolution window** before escalation. * “Unable to resolve” should only be available after the lock period unless overridden by admin. * Cost adjustments must remain available until escalation occurs. * Admin intervention is required for exceptional cases. * Applies to all disputes initiated within the Gopher App ecosystem. ‌ ## **🔍 Example** ‌ | **Action** | **Current Behavior** | **Expected Behavior** | | --- | --- | --- | | Dispute created | “Unable to resolve” immediately available | Locked for 24 hours | | Gopher response | Often blocked | Always allowed initially | | Admin assistance | Not possible | Admin override available | ‌ ## **🧠 Dependencies / Notes** ‌ * Requires backend timer tracking per dispute. * Admin Panel must expose: * Dispute start time * Override control * Ensure UI clearly communicates: * Remaining lock time * When escalation becomes available * Email notifications must not spam (one per dispute creation). ‌ ## **🧪 QA Notes** ‌ * Test dispute initiation and timing logic. * Verify “Unable to resolve” is disabled/enabled at correct times. * Confirm cost adjustment remains available during lock period. * Validate admin override functionality. * Ensure admin and Gopher emails are sent correctly.

Summary: Gopher Go - Update Request - Cost Adjustment Issue - Gopher Should Not Be Able To Complete Request With Pending Cost Adjustment
Description: A Gopher should not be able to Complete a request with a pending cost adjustment. Need a pop-up to notify the Gopher the cost adjustment must be canceled and/or approved by the requestor before completing. <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=3602-8519&t=utIWFv6qWpNT39hi-4</custom> ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=20dee813-867e-4c79-9847-faa446ba9b08&&collection=&height=852&occurrenceKey=null&width=393&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) ‌ Currently we do not have a way for the Gopher to cancel the pending cost adjustment. Need to update the cost adjustment button to cancel cost adjustment once a cost adjustment is submitted. <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-1">https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=3754-53070&t=H1sHR2BsrIrIzIG1-4</custom> ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=0567a098-6937-499a-a647-5c539399692b&&collection=&height=1115&occurrenceKey=null&width=393&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) ‌ # **Jira Ticket: Block Completion When Cost Adjustment Is Pending + Add “Cancel Cost Adjustment”** **Type:** Bug + UX/Workflow Enhancement **Priority:** High **Component(s):** Worker App (Requests), Payments / Cost Adjustments, Backend **Reporter:** John **Environment:** Production (iOS + Android + Backend) --- ## **Summary** A Gopher can currently **complete** a request even when a **cost adjustment is pending**, which causes mismatched totals, capture errors, and support issues. We must **block completion** while a cost adjustment is pending and show a modal instructing the Gopher that the adjustment must be **approved by the Requestor or canceled** before completion. Also add a way for the Gopher to **cancel** a pending cost adjustment. --- ## **User Stories** * **As a Gopher,** I should be prevented from completing a request if my cost adjustment is pending, and I should see clear instructions on what to do next. * **As a Gopher,** I need a one-tap option to **cancel** my pending cost adjustment so I can proceed to completion. * **As a Requestor,** I need to **approve/decline** cost adjustments before the job can be completed. --- ## **References (Figma)** * **Block completion modal (pending adjustment):** [https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=3602-8519&t=utIWFv6qWpNT39hi-4](https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=3602-8519&t=utIWFv6qWpNT39hi-4) * **Cancel cost adjustment button/state:** [https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=3754-53070&t=H1sHR2BsrIrIzIG1-4](https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=3754-53070&t=H1sHR2BsrIrIzIG1-4) --- ## **Requirements** ### 1) Block Completion When Adjustment Pending * If `cost_adjustment_status = PENDING`, **disable/guard** the **Complete Request** action. * Tapping **Complete** shows modal per Figma: indicates the adjustment must be **approved by Requestor** or **canceled**by Gopher. * This rule must be enforced **server-side** to prevent race conditions / spoofed clients. ### 2) Add “Cancel Cost Adjustment” Action * Once a cost adjustment is submitted (PENDING), the **Cost Adjustment** button converts to **“Cancel Cost Adjustment.”** * Tapping it shows a confirmation → sets status to **CANCELED**, restores pre-adjustment totals, and re-enables completion. ### 3) State Machine (Backend) * `NONE` → user can submit adjustment → `PENDING` * `PENDING` → Requestor action → `APPROVED` or `DECLINED` * `PENDING` → Gopher cancels → `CANCELED` * **Completion only allowed when:** `NONE`, `DECLINED`, `CANCELED`, or `APPROVED` (with updated totals applied). ### 4) Notifications & UX * Requestor receives standard approval prompt on submission (unchanged). * If Gopher cancels the pending adjustment: * Requestor is notified that the adjustment was canceled (optional). * Worker sees toast/snackbar: “Cost adjustment canceled.” * Any attempt to complete while pending shows the Figma modal (no silent failures). ### 5) Logging & Audit * Capture events: submit adjustment, cancel adjustment, approve/decline, attempt-to-complete-while-pending. * Include timestamps, user IDs, request ID, previous/updated totals. --- ## **Acceptance Criteria** **AC1 — Blocked Completion:** Attempting to complete with `PENDING` adjustment shows the specified modal and **does not** complete. **AC2 — Cancel Action Visible:** After submitting an adjustment, the cost adjustment UI swaps to **“Cancel Cost Adjustment.”** **AC3 — Cancel Works:** Confirming cancel sets status to **CANCELED**, restores totals, and enables completion. **AC4 — Server Guardrail:** Direct API calls to complete while `PENDING` return a 409/422 with a clear error. **AC5 — Post-Approval Completion:** If Requestor approves, totals update; completion succeeds without additional error. **AC6 — Analytics/Audit:** All state changes and blocked attempts are logged and visible to Admin. --- ## **Technical Notes** * **Backend** * Add/validate `cost_adjustment_status` on the Request model. * Gate `/complete` endpoint on non-PENDING states. * Add `/cost-adjustments/cancel` endpoint (idempotent). * Recalculate totals on APPROVED and on CANCELED (revert). * Emit events for UI updates (SSE/WebSocket, if applicable). * **Mobile (iOS/Android)** * Update request detail header/buttons to reflect state: * Normal → **Submit Cost Adjustment** * Pending → **Cancel Cost Adjustment**; **Complete** triggers modal * Implement modal exactly per Figma. * Refresh state after approve/decline/cancel (socket or polling). * **QA Scenarios** 1. Submit adjustment → try to complete → see modal; completion blocked. 2. Submit adjustment → cancel → completion succeeds. 3. Submit adjustment → Requestor approves → totals update → completion succeeds. 4. Submit adjustment → Requestor declines → completion allowed with original totals. 5. API call to complete while pending → receives error; no state change. 6. Rapid taps / offline: ensure idempotency and consistent state. --- ## **Out of Scope** * Changes to approval UX for Requestor (beyond existing flows). * Multiple concurrent adjustments (assume single pending at a time).

Summary: Gopher App - Warn user of potential duplicate before submitting a new request
Description: > ✅ **GROOMED + PROTOTYPE BUILT 2026-07-02.** The duplicate-warning modal is now **implemented in the new front-end** (`gopher-request.html`) following the repo's “build the UX, tag the BACKEND SEAM” convention. Summary: Both apps — Allow Gopher to reschedule an active request (Accepted through In Progress) with Requestor approval and Stripe authorization handling
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher who has accepted a request but needs to change the agreed-upon time before completion, ## 🎯 I want to propose a new date/time to the Requestor for their approval, ## ✅ So that the request can continue under terms that work for both parties — rather than being cancelled and re-requested from scratch. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * Gophers and Requestors occasionally need to shift the time of an already-accepted request (Gopher schedule conflict, Requestor change of plans, weather, etc.). * Today, the only option is to cancel and have the Requestor re-submit the request, which loses the existing match, the rating history of the engagement, and the captured payment authorization. * This ticket adds a **reschedule-with-approval** flow that preserves the existing match and order record. * After approval, the request **behaves exactly like the current rescheduled-request feature** — it falls back into the Gopher's scheduled tab on Home and updates the Requestor's Home Screen as a scheduled request. * The **Stripe payment authorization** is the highest-risk dependency — Stripe auths have a hard expiry (typically 7 days, up to \~30 on some cards), so the rule below handles three time-delta cases explicitly. --- ## 🔍 Scope * **Platform:** Both apps (Gopher Go for the Gopher proposing, Gopher Request for the Requestor approving). * **Initiator:** Gopher only. * **Eligibility window:** at any active state from **Accepted** through to (but not including) **Completed** or **Cancelled**. This includes **In Progress** — a Gopher mid-job can request a reschedule if needed. * **Approver:** the Requestor on the order. --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior ### Gopher-side propose flow 1. From an active request on Gopher Go, the Gopher selects **Reschedule** and picks a new date/time. 2. The Gopher confirms the proposed time. The request enters a **Reschedule Pending** sub-state — the underlying order status is unchanged at this point. 3. The Requestor is notified. ### Requestor-side approve / decline flow 1. Requestor receives a notification (push + in-app banner) with the proposed new time, including an Approve / Decline action. 2. **On Approve:** * The order's scheduled date/time is updated to the proposed value. * The order returns to a **scheduled** state and **falls back into the Gopher's scheduled tab on the Home Screen** (per current rescheduled-request feature behaviour). * The Requestor's Home Screen reflects the order as a scheduled request at the new time. * The Stripe payment authorization is handled per the rules below. * Both parties receive a confirmation notification. 3. **On Decline:** * The order remains at its original time and active state. * The Reschedule Pending sub-state is cleared. * Both parties receive a notification that the reschedule was not accepted. ### Approval window and timeout * The Requestor has **4 hours** to respond, with a **reminder push at 1 hour remaining**. * If the Requestor does not respond within 4 hours, the Reschedule Pending state expires automatically: * Treated as a decline — original time stands. * Both parties receive a notification that the reschedule request expired. ### Stripe payment authorization handling This is the highest-risk part of the ticket and is broken into three time-delta cases: | Case | Condition | Handling | | --- | --- | --- | | **A. New time within existing auth window** | Proposed time falls within the original Stripe authorization's expiry window. | No Stripe action required; the existing auth covers the new time. | | **B. New time past existing auth window but extendable** | Proposed time falls past the existing auth expiry, but the auth supports incremental authorization / extension. | Call Stripe to extend the existing authorization to cover the new time. | | **C. New time past existing auth window, not extendable** | Proposed time falls past the existing auth expiry and extension is not supported, OR Stripe rejects the extension. | Release the existing authorization and capture a new authorization on the card on file at the moment of Requestor approval. If the new capture fails (declined / expired card / insufficient funds), the reschedule is **rejected** and the order returns to its original time. The Requestor is notified that their card did not authorize, with a path to update their payment method and try again. | In all three cases, the Stripe step happens at the moment of Requestor approval — not at the moment the Gopher proposes. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — Propose reschedule from Accepted state** * **Given** an order is in Accepted state with a Gopher matched, * **When** the Gopher proposes a new date/time and confirms, * **Then** the order enters Reschedule Pending and the Requestor receives an approve/decline notification. **Scenario 2 — Propose reschedule from In Progress state** * **Given** an order is In Progress, * **When** the Gopher proposes a new date/time, * **Then** the same Reschedule Pending flow runs and the Requestor receives the approval notification — the order remains visibly In Progress until approval is resolved. **Scenario 3 — Requestor approves — within existing Stripe auth window** * **Given** a Reschedule Pending order with a proposed time within the original Stripe authorization window, * **When** the Requestor approves, * **Then** the order's scheduled time updates to the proposed value, the order returns to scheduled state in both Home Screens, and no Stripe action is required. **Scenario 4 — Requestor approves — Stripe extension succeeds** * **Given** a Reschedule Pending order whose proposed time exceeds the original Stripe auth window but supports extension, * **When** the Requestor approves, * **Then** Stripe extends the auth, the order's scheduled time updates, and both Home Screens reflect the new time. **Scenario 5 — Requestor approves — Stripe extension not supported, recapture succeeds** * **Given** a Reschedule Pending order whose proposed time exceeds the auth window and extension is not supported, * **When** the Requestor approves and Stripe successfully captures a new authorization on the card on file, * **Then** the original authorization is released, the new auth replaces it, and the reschedule completes. **Scenario 6 — Requestor approves — new Stripe capture fails** * **Given** a Reschedule Pending order requires a new capture and the card declines, * **When** the Requestor's approval triggers the Stripe call, * **Then** the reschedule is rejected, the order returns to its original time and state, the existing auth remains intact, and the Requestor is notified that their card did not authorize with a path to update their payment method. **Scenario 7 — Requestor declines** * **Given** a Reschedule Pending order, * **When** the Requestor taps Decline, * **Then** the order returns to its original time and state, the Reschedule Pending sub-state is cleared, and both parties receive notifications that the reschedule was declined. **Scenario 8 — Approval window expires without response** * **Given** a Reschedule Pending order and 4 hours have elapsed without a Requestor response, * **When** the timeout fires, * **Then** the order returns to its original time and state, and both parties receive expiration notifications. **Scenario 9 — Reminder fires at 1 hour remaining** * **Given** a Reschedule Pending order with 3 hours elapsed since the Gopher's proposal, * **When** the reminder job runs, * **Then** the Requestor receives a reminder push notification. **Scenario 10 — Reschedule not available outside the active lifecycle** * **Given** an order that is Completed or Cancelled, * **When** the Gopher views the order, * **Then** the Reschedule action is not available. **Scenario 11 — Post-approval behaviour matches existing rescheduled-request feature** * **Given** a reschedule is approved, * **When** both parties view their Home Screens, * **Then** the order appears in the Gopher's scheduled tab and on the Requestor's Home Screen as a scheduled request — indistinguishable from a normally-scheduled request, per the existing rescheduled-request feature. **Scenario 12 — Only Gopher can initiate** * **Given** an active order, * **When** the Requestor views their order details, * **Then** they do not have a Reschedule action — only Gophers can propose reschedules. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * **Initiator:** Gopher only. Requestors cannot initiate a reschedule in this release. * **Eligibility:** any active state from Accepted through to (but not including) Completed or Cancelled. Includes In Progress. * **Approval:** the Requestor must explicitly approve via the in-app notification. Back-channel chat agreement does not constitute approval. * **Approval window:** 4 hours from proposal, with a reminder at 1 hour remaining. No response = decline. * **Stripe authorization:** the order's payment authorization must cover the new time at the moment of approval. The three handling cases (A / B / C in the table above) define the rule. * **If recapture fails:** the reschedule is rejected and the order reverts to its original time and state. * **Decline behaviour:** order returns to original time and state. The reschedule attempt does not cancel the order. * **Post-approval state:** the order matches the existing rescheduled-request feature's behaviour exactly — scheduled tab on Gopher Home, scheduled request on Requestor Home Screen. * Only one Reschedule Pending state can exist on an order at a time. If a pending reschedule already exists, the Gopher cannot propose another until the current one is resolved. * The Stripe step runs at the moment of Requestor approval, not at the moment of Gopher proposal. --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * The state machine needs a new **Reschedule Pending** sub-state that overlays on top of the existing order state (Accepted / In Progress / etc.). The base state should not change during Pending so the order remains visibly active. * Treat the pending reschedule as a separate record (`pending_reschedule_id`, `proposed_time`, `expires_at`, `created_by`) attached to the order — don't try to overload existing scheduled-time fields until approval lands. * The 4-hour timeout and 1-hour reminder need either scheduled jobs or per-record scheduled tasks. Either approach is fine; the simpler one is a periodic sweep job that checks `pending_reschedule.expires_at <= now()` and fires the appropriate notification. * The Stripe handling should be encapsulated in a single service function that takes the order + proposed time and returns `auth_ok` / `auth_failed`. Keep the three-case logic in one place so it's testable. * Recommend deploying behind a feature flag — this touches state machine, payments, and dual-party UX simultaneously, so a flag for quick rollback is cheap insurance. * If a Gopher is mid-In-Progress (e.g., already picked up items) and reschedules, the existing rescheduled-request feature's handling of partial progress should govern. This ticket does not attempt to define a separate partial-progress flow. * Confirm Stripe API capability for incremental authorization on the card brands you accept — not all cards support it. If a card brand never supports extension, Case B effectively never fires for that brand and the logic falls through to Case C. --- ## 🎨 Design Reference * **Figma:** https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=6503-4701 --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Reproduce every Scenario above end-to-end — each one corresponds to a real production state combination. * Set up Stripe test cards with each of the three cases: an auth that can be extended, an auth that cannot, and a card that declines on capture. Confirm the right path is taken in each. * Test the timeout and reminder by manipulating `expires_at` on the pending record. * Test that proposing a reschedule on an order already in Reschedule Pending state is prevented. * Test the In Progress case end-to-end: a Gopher mid-job proposes, Requestor approves, the order returns to scheduled tab without losing rating history or audit trail. * Test feature flag rollback — disabling the flag should hide the Reschedule action without breaking existing orders. * Test on both iOS and Android, both apps. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Depends on the existing **rescheduled-request feature** being available as the post-approval state target — this ticket reuses that handling, not reimplements it. * Depends on Stripe's incremental-authorization API for Case B. If not supported in your account configuration, Case B effectively falls through to Case C. * Depends on the push-notification infrastructure for the 1-hour reminder. * Out of scope: a Requestor-initiated reschedule flow. If desired in future, that's a separate ticket — the symmetry is straightforward but the approval direction reverses. * Out of scope: bulk / recurring reschedule (e.g., "move this every-week order forward by a day").
