Summary: Gopher Go — Two-strike cancellation fee for unapproved Gopher cancellations, with admin oversight, 5-star rehabilitation, and Stripe negative-balance withholding
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher operations team protecting Requestors from unilateral Gopher cancellations while remaining fair to Gophers who occasionally need to cancel, ## 🎯 I want a two-strike cancellation fee system with Requestor input, admin oversight, performance-based rehabilitation, and Stripe withholding for unpaid balances, ## ✅ So that repeat offenders are financially accountable, well-behaved Gophers receive grace, and bad actors cannot evade fees by deleting and re-creating accounts. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * A Gopher cancellation after acceptance — especially without Requestor agreement — imposes a real cost on the Requestor (lost time, replanning, payment authorization tied up). Without consequence, repeat offenders erode the platform's reliability. * This system gives the Requestor a voice (Agreed vs Not Agreed), gives the Gopher a two-strike grace before any fee can apply, gives admin three-way oversight (Approve Cancel Fee / No Cancel Fee / Excused), and routes unpaid fees through Stripe as a negative balance offset against future payouts. * A **performance-based rehabilitation** path lets reformed Gophers clear past strikes by stringing together 50 consecutive 5-star completions without another unexcused cancellation. * Anti-evasion: a Gopher cannot delete their account while carrying a negative balance, and reaching a Stripe balance of **$-10 or lower** triggers auto-deactivation. --- ## 🔑 Definitions | Term | Meaning | | --- | --- | | **Agreed Upon** | Requestor selected "Agreed" on the cancellation prompt. No rating, no fee, done. | | **Not Agreed Upon** | Requestor selected "Not Agreed" OR did not respond within 6 hours OR deleted their account during the prompt window. | | **Unexcused cancellation** | Any cancellation that ended up Not Agreed Upon, regardless of admin's final disposition. | | **No Cancel Fee strike** | Admin disposition: the cancellation was unexcused but no fee was applied this time. Counts toward the 2-strike threshold for triggering a fee. | | **Approved Cancel Fee** | Admin disposition: $5 cancellation fee assessed against the Gopher. Recorded as a negative balance on the Gopher's Stripe account. | | **Excused** | Admin disposition: the cancellation is forgiven entirely. Does NOT count toward the 2-strike threshold. | | **Rehabilitation** | 50 consecutive 5-star-rated completed requests with no intervening unexcused cancellation. Erases all prior No Cancel Fee strikes and Approved Cancel Fee strike records (but does not refund any already-applied negative balance). | --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior ### Step 1 — Gopher cancels * Gopher cancels an active request (after the standard cancellation-comment flow from elsewhere in the spec). * Requestor receives a notification prompting them to mark the cancellation **Agreed** or **Not Agreed**. ### Step 2 — Requestor response window (6 hours) * The Requestor has **6 hours** to respond. * **If Agreed:** no rating, no fee, done. Process ends. * **If Not Agreed:** proceed to Step 3 immediately. * **If no response within 6 hours:** treated as Not Agreed Upon. Proceed to Step 3 at the 6-hour mark. * **If Requestor deletes their account before responding:** treated as Not Agreed Upon. Proceed to Step 3. ### Step 3 — Admin review (48 hours from when Step 3 starts) * An email is sent to **admin@gophergo.io** with a link to choose Approve Cancel Fee / No Cancel Fee / Excused for this specific cancellation. * The same three actions are available as buttons on the order in the Admin Panel. * The Gopher receives an **initial email** notifying them their cancellation is under review. * **Admin's choices and their gating:** * **No Cancel Fee** — always available. Logs a strike, applies no fee. * **Excused** — always available. Logs nothing toward strikes, applies no fee. * **Approve Cancel Fee** — only available if the Gopher already has ≥ 2 prior No Cancel Fee strikes on their record. Otherwise this option is disabled. * **If admin does not respond within 48 hours, default applies:** * If the Gopher has ≥ 2 prior No Cancel Fee strikes → default to **Approve Cancel Fee** ($-5 applied). * If the Gopher has < 2 prior No Cancel Fee strikes → default to **No Cancel Fee** (strike logged, no fee). ### Step 4 — Outcome and notifications * The Gopher receives a **follow-up email** with one of three messages corresponding to the outcome: * **Approve Cancel Fee** → "You have been assessed a $5 cancellation fee." * **No Cancel Fee** → "The cancellation was unexcused, but you have NOT been assessed a fee this time." * **Excused** → "The cancellation was excused." * The Gopher's strike record and Stripe balance are updated per the outcome. ### Step 5 — Auto-deactivation check * After applying the outcome, check the Gopher's standing: * If the Gopher's Stripe balance has reached **$-10 or lower**, **auto-deactivate** the Gopher's account. Balance is the **sole trigger** — a running count of Approved Cancel Fees is **not** used, because payouts offset the balance and rehabilitation erases strike records, so a strike count and the balance diverge over time. * Auto-deactivation follows the existing admin-deactivation flow (G40-225 — also auto-rejects the Stripe account). ### Step 6 — Rehabilitation tracking (ongoing) * The system maintains a rolling counter of **5-star completed requests since the Gopher's last unexcused cancellation**. * When this counter reaches **50**, all prior No Cancel Fee strikes AND Approved Cancel Fee strike records are **erased** — the Gopher returns to a clean record. * Any new unexcused cancellation **resets** the counter back to 0. * Rehabilitation erases the **strike records**, not any **already-applied negative balance**. A Gopher with a $-5 balance who rehabilitates still owes $5; it will simply be offset against the next payout. --- ## 💳 Stripe Negative-Balance Mechanics * Gophers do not carry a balance — all payouts are instant. So a fee cannot be debited proactively. * Approved Cancel Fees are recorded as a **negative balance** on the Gopher's Stripe account (e.g., $-5). * The next payout offsets the negative balance before reaching the Gopher (e.g., a $20 job pays $15 with the $-5 retained). * A Gopher with any negative balance **cannot delete their account** — the delete flow is blocked with a message explaining the balance must be resolved first. * This is critical: deleting the account would wipe the Stripe data and let the Gopher re-create a fresh account, evading the fee. Blocking the delete preserves accountability. * The auto-deactivation at a **$-10-or-lower** balance terminates the Gopher's ability to take new work. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — Requestor selects Agreed** * **Given** a Gopher cancels a request and the Requestor receives the Agreed/Not Agreed prompt, * **When** the Requestor selects Agreed within 6 hours, * **Then** no rating, no fee, and no admin review fires. The flow ends. **Scenario 2 — Requestor selects Not Agreed** * **Given** the Requestor receives the prompt, * **When** the Requestor selects Not Agreed within 6 hours, * **Then** admin review starts immediately and the 48-hour admin window begins. **Scenario 3 — Requestor does not respond within 6 hours** * **Given** the Requestor has not responded 6 hours after the prompt was sent, * **When** the 6-hour timer expires, * **Then** the cancellation is treated as Not Agreed Upon and admin review starts at the 6-hour mark. **Scenario 4 — Requestor deletes account during the prompt window** * **Given** the Requestor's account is deleted after the prompt is sent but before they respond, * **When** the deletion is detected, * **Then** the cancellation is treated as Not Agreed Upon and admin review starts. **Scenario 5 — First and second unexcused cancellations cannot incur a fee** * **Given** a Gopher with 0 or 1 prior No Cancel Fee strikes has an unexcused cancellation, * **When** the admin review screen loads, * **Then** the Approve Cancel Fee button is disabled — admin can only select No Cancel Fee or Excused. **Scenario 6 — Third unexcused cancellation enables the fee** * **Given** a Gopher with ≥ 2 prior No Cancel Fee strikes has an unexcused cancellation, * **When** the admin review screen loads, * **Then** all three actions (Approve Cancel Fee / No Cancel Fee / Excused) are available. **Scenario 7 — Admin timeout, Gopher has < 2 priors** * **Given** an admin review is open and the Gopher has < 2 prior No Cancel Fee strikes, * **When** 48 hours elapse without admin response, * **Then** the outcome defaults to No Cancel Fee. **Scenario 8 — Admin timeout, Gopher has ≥ 2 priors** * **Given** an admin review is open and the Gopher has ≥ 2 prior No Cancel Fee strikes, * **When** 48 hours elapse without admin response, * **Then** the outcome defaults to Approve Cancel Fee — $-5 is applied to the Gopher's Stripe balance. **Scenario 9 — Excused outcome does not count toward strikes** * **Given** an admin selects Excused, * **When** the outcome is recorded, * **Then** the Gopher's prior strike count is unchanged, no fee is applied, and the Gopher receives the "excused" follow-up email. **Scenario 10 — Negative balance offsets next payout** * **Given** a Gopher has a $-5 Stripe balance, * **When** the Gopher completes a $20 job and is paid out, * **Then** the Gopher receives $15 and the balance returns to $0. **Scenario 11 — Negative balance blocks account deletion** * **Given** a Gopher has any negative Stripe balance, * **When** the Gopher attempts to delete their account, * **Then** the deletion is blocked with a message explaining the negative balance must be resolved first. **Scenario 12 — Auto-deactivation at balance ≤ $-10** * **Given** applying an Approved Cancel Fee brings the Gopher's Stripe balance to **$-10 or lower**, * **When** the outcome is applied, * **Then** the Gopher's account is auto-deactivated via the standard admin-deactivation flow (G40-225), which also auto-rejects the Stripe account. **Scenario 13 — Rehabilitation erases prior strikes** * **Given** a Gopher with prior No Cancel Fee or Approved Cancel Fee strikes, * **When** the Gopher accumulates 50 consecutive 5-star-rated completed requests with no intervening unexcused cancellation, * **Then** all prior strike records are erased and the Gopher returns to a clean record. Any existing negative balance remains until offset by future payouts. **Scenario 14 — Rehabilitation counter resets on a new unexcused cancellation** * **Given** a Gopher has accumulated 30 5-star completions toward rehabilitation, * **When** the Gopher has a new unexcused cancellation, * **Then** the rehabilitation counter resets to 0. **Scenario 15 — Admin email and admin-panel button both available** * **Given** an admin review fires, * **When** an admin opens either the admin@gophergo.io email or the order detail view in the Admin Panel, * **Then** both surfaces present the same three actions (Approve Cancel Fee / No Cancel Fee / Excused) and resolve to the same outcome record. **Scenario 16 — Gopher receives initial and follow-up emails** * **Given** an admin review has fired, * **When** the review opens and later resolves, * **Then** the Gopher receives an initial email (cancellation is under review) and a follow-up email matching the final outcome (assessed / not assessed / excused). --- ## 📐 Business Rules * The Requestor has **6 hours** to respond to the Agreed/Not Agreed prompt. No response defaults to Not Agreed. * Admin has **48 hours** to act, measured from the moment the cancellation becomes Not Agreed. * A cancellation fee is **$5**. There is no current path to vary this amount per cancellation. * The fee can only be applied if the Gopher already has **≥ 2 prior No Cancel Fee strikes**. The first two unexcused cancellations are grace strikes. * **Three admin dispositions:** Approve Cancel Fee (applies $5), No Cancel Fee (logs strike, no fee), Excused (no strike, no fee). * **Default at admin timeout:** Approve Cancel Fee if ≥ 2 priors; No Cancel Fee otherwise. * **Rehabilitation:** 50 consecutive 5-star-rated completed requests without an intervening unexcused cancellation erases ALL prior strike records (both No Cancel Fee and Approved Cancel Fee). Already-applied negative balance is not refunded. * **Rehabilitation counter resets** to 0 on any new unexcused cancellation. * A Gopher with any negative Stripe balance **cannot delete their account**. * **Auto-deactivation** when the Gopher's Stripe balance reaches **$-10 or lower**. This is the **sole trigger** — not a count of Approved Cancel Fee strikes; the two diverge once payouts offset the balance or rehabilitation erases strike records. Triggers the standard admin-deactivation flow (G40-225), which also auto-rejects the Stripe account. * The Gopher receives an **initial** email when review starts and a **follow-up** email when it resolves. * The admin can take the action from either the **email link** or the **Admin Panel order view button** — both surface the same actions. * This system interacts with **G40-42** (Requestor rating after Gopher cancellation): when the Requestor selects Agreed, NO rating screen fires AND no fee. The rating screen only fires per G40-42's existing triggers when Not Agreed (or default-to-Not-Agreed) results in admin review. --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * A dedicated table for cancellation review records is recommended: `cancellation_id`, `order_id`, `gopher_id`, `requestor_response` (agreed / not_agreed / timeout / requestor_deleted), `admin_disposition` (approve_fee / no_fee / excused / null), `created_at`, `requestor_responded_at`, `admin_resolved_at`, `auto_resolved`. The `auto_resolved` flag captures both the 6-hour Requestor timeout and the 48-hour admin timeout. * The 6-hour and 48-hour timers should run as a single scheduled-sweep job that evaluates `created_at` and `requestor_responded_at` against `now()`. Avoid per-record scheduled tasks where possible. * The Stripe negative-balance handling needs API integration: write a service that records a $-5 ledger entry on the connected account at the moment of Approve Cancel Fee disposition, and have the payout flow consult this ledger before computing the payout amount. * The rehabilitation counter is a single integer on the Gopher record: increment on each 5-star completion, reset on each new unexcused cancellation, and check for the 50 threshold on each increment. * The negative-balance check at account deletion must run server-side; client-side hiding alone is insufficient. * Recommend a feature flag covering the entire mechanism so it can be rolled back if anomalies appear in early production. * Coordinate with **G40-42** (rating after Gopher cancellation) and **G40-225** (Stripe auto-rejection on deactivation). This ticket extends both of those. * The two admin paths (email link, Admin Panel button) should resolve to the same backend endpoint so behaviour is identical regardless of how admin dispositions. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Cover every acceptance criterion end-to-end, including the timing-sensitive ones (6-hour Requestor timeout, 48-hour admin timeout) by manipulating timestamps on the cancellation record. * Verify the Approve Cancel Fee button is correctly disabled on the admin review screen when the Gopher has 0 or 1 priors. * Verify the timeout default switches correctly based on prior strike count. * Verify Stripe negative balance is recorded and offset against the next payout. * Verify account deletion is blocked with any negative balance and unblocked once the balance returns to $0. * Verify auto-deactivation triggers exactly when the Stripe balance reaches $-10 or lower, and runs through the same flow as admin-initiated deactivation (G40-225), including auto-rejecting the Stripe account. * Verify the rehabilitation flow: 50 consecutive 5-star completions with no intervening unexcused cancellation erases all strike records. * Verify the rehabilitation counter resets to 0 on any new unexcused cancellation. * Verify both admin surfaces (email link + Admin Panel button) post to the same endpoint and produce identical outcomes. * Test on both iOS and Android for any Gopher-facing prompts. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Depends on **G40-225** (auto-reject Stripe account on Gopher deactivation) for the auto-deactivation step. * Depends on **G40-42** (Requestor rating after Gopher cancellation) for the rating screen interaction — specifically, this ticket's "Agreed" outcome must suppress the rating screen. * Depends on the existing **5-star rating capture** flow being able to feed the rehabilitation counter. * Depends on Stripe Connect account negative-balance ledger functionality. * Out of scope: variable fee amounts per cancellation, refund of the negative balance after rehabilitation, and Requestor-initiated cancellation fee flow.

Summary: Gopher Go — Send a 1-hour nudge SMS (with push fallback) to a Gopher whose accepted "Need ASAP" delivery is still not completed and has no recent two-way communication
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher operations team monitoring "Need ASAP" deliveries, ## 🎯 I want to nudge any Gopher whose accepted "Need ASAP" delivery is still not completed 1 hour after acceptance, when there's no recent two-way communication with the Requestor, ## ✅ So that deliveries that have stalled without explanation are surfaced to the Gopher proactively, and Requestors are protected from extended silence on a request they explicitly marked as urgent. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * A "Need ASAP" delivery is a request the Requestor explicitly flagged as urgent. The platform's reliability promise on these is the highest, so an hour of unresolved silence is a meaningful signal that the Gopher needs a nudge. * The nudge is **only sent when the silence is real** — if both parties are actively talking in the in-app chat, the nudge would be noise and is suppressed. * This is a Gopher-facing intervention; the Requestor does not see this SMS. --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior ### Trigger * **1 hour from the moment the Gopher accepted** the request, measured server-side. * The order is still in an active, **not yet completed** state. * The order is a **"Need ASAP" Delivery** — scheduled deliveries and other request types are out of scope. ### Skip conditions (any one suppresses the nudge) * The order has already been **completed** or **cancelled** at the moment the 1-hour job evaluates it. * Both parties have **active two-way communication** in the in-app chat for this order — defined as at least one in-app message sent by EACH party within the last 30 minutes. * The order is not a "Need ASAP" Delivery (scheduled deliveries, ride requests, services, etc.). ### Delivery channel * Primary: **SMS** to the Gopher's verified mobile number. * Fallback: if SMS is unavailable (no verified number, opt-out, delivery failure), send the equivalent as a **push notification** with the same intent but abbreviated for push length. * The nudge is sent **once per order** — no follow-up reminders at 90 min, 2 hours, etc. --- ## 📨 SMS Copy Hi \[Gopher first name\], Your Gopher Delivery request has reached the 1 hour mark. Because this was a "Need ASAP" request, please make sure you're updating your progress accurately and have communicated with your Requestor regarding your ETA. It is very important to contact your customer ASAP with an update. If you have already spoken with the customer and agreed on a delayed delivery, please disregard. Thank You, Gopher Support Team **Push fallback (abbreviated):** > Your "Need ASAP" delivery has reached the 1-hour mark. Please update your progress and contact the customer ASAP. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — Nudge fires at 1 hour for a stalled Need ASAP delivery** * **Given** a Gopher has accepted a Need ASAP delivery and 1 hour has elapsed since acceptance, * **And** the order is not yet completed or cancelled, * **And** the two parties have not exchanged messages from EACH side within the last 30 minutes, * **When** the 1-hour evaluation job runs, * **Then** the SMS is sent to the Gopher's verified mobile number using the copy above. **Scenario 2 — Active conversation suppresses the nudge** * **Given** the Gopher and the Requestor have each sent at least one in-app message on the order in the last 30 minutes, * **When** the 1-hour job evaluates, * **Then** no SMS or push is sent. **Scenario 3 — One-sided conversation does NOT count** * **Given** the Gopher has sent messages in the last 30 minutes but the Requestor has not (or vice versa), * **When** the 1-hour job evaluates, * **Then** the SMS is still sent — a one-sided thread does not count as two-way communication. **Scenario 4 — Stale conversation does NOT count** * **Given** the Gopher and Requestor exchanged messages earlier but neither has messaged within the last 30 minutes, * **When** the 1-hour job evaluates, * **Then** the SMS is still sent. **Scenario 5 — Completed before 1 hour skips the nudge** * **Given** the order completed before the 1-hour mark, * **When** the 1-hour job evaluates, * **Then** no SMS or push is sent. **Scenario 6 — Cancelled before 1 hour skips the nudge** * **Given** the order was cancelled before the 1-hour mark, * **When** the 1-hour job evaluates, * **Then** no SMS or push is sent. **Scenario 7 — Non-Need-ASAP request never triggers** * **Given** an accepted Delivery that is NOT marked Need ASAP (e.g., a scheduled delivery), * **When** 1 hour elapses, * **Then** no SMS or push is sent. **Scenario 8 — Push fallback when SMS unavailable** * **Given** the Gopher does not have a verified SMS number (or SMS delivery failed / opted out), * **When** the 1-hour job fires the nudge, * **Then** the abbreviated push notification is sent instead. **Scenario 9 — One nudge per order maximum** * **Given** the SMS has already been sent for this order, * **When** the job evaluates again later, * **Then** no additional nudge is sent. The nudge is one-shot per order. **Scenario 10 — Gopher first name correctly populated** * **Given** the SMS is dispatched, * **When** the Gopher reads it, * **Then** "\[Gopher first name\]" is replaced with the Gopher's first name from profile — not a literal placeholder, not "Name". --- ## 📐 Business Rules * The nudge fires only for **Need ASAP Delivery** request types. Other request types are out of scope. * The 1-hour timer anchors to **Gopher acceptance**, server-side. * The order must be in an **active, not-yet-completed, not-yet-cancelled** state at the moment of evaluation. * The skip rule for two-way communication requires **at least one message from EACH party within the past 30 minutes**. One-sided or stale conversations do not count. * The nudge is sent **once per order** — no follow-up reminders in this release. * Primary channel is **SMS**; fallback is **push notification** with abbreviated copy if SMS is not available. * The Requestor is not notified by this rule. This is a Gopher-side intervention only. --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * The 1-hour timer should run as a scheduled-sweep job that evaluates orders with `accepted_at <= now() - 1 hour AND status IN (active, in_progress) AND request_type = need_it_now_delivery AND nudge_sent_at IS NULL`. A periodic sweep is simpler than per-order scheduled tasks. * The two-way communication check should query the order's message thread for at least one message from each party with `created_at >= now() - 30 minutes`. Index the message table on `(order_id, sender_role, created_at)` to keep this fast. * Set `nudge_sent_at` on the order record at the moment the SMS or push is dispatched to guarantee one-shot behaviour. * For SMS, reuse the existing Twilio / SMS provider integration — don't introduce a new sender for this surface. * For push fallback, reuse the existing push infrastructure used elsewhere in the app. * Recommend deploying behind a feature flag so the nudge can be toggled off quickly if false-positive rates are unexpectedly high. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Accept a Need ASAP delivery on a test account, wait 1 hour without any messaging activity, and confirm the SMS is sent. * Repeat with two-way messaging activity in the last 30 minutes — confirm no SMS. * Repeat with one-sided messaging in the last 30 minutes — confirm SMS is still sent. * Repeat with two-way messaging earlier than 30 minutes ago — confirm SMS is still sent. * Complete the order before 1 hour — confirm no SMS. * Cancel the order before 1 hour — confirm no SMS. * Accept a non-Need-ASAP delivery (e.g., scheduled) and wait 1 hour — confirm no SMS. * Trigger the job a second time on the same order — confirm only one SMS was sent total. * Test the push fallback by simulating an unavailable SMS number. * Verify the Gopher's actual first name appears in the SMS — not a literal "Name" or "\[Gopher first name\]" placeholder. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Depends on the existing SMS provider integration (Twilio or equivalent) being usable for outbound nudges. * Depends on the existing push-notification infrastructure for the fallback path. * Depends on the order record having `accepted_at`, `status`, and `request_type` queryable, and the message thread being queryable by sender and timestamp. * Out of scope: escalation reminders at 90 minutes / 2 hours, Requestor-side notifications, and any auto-cancellation or re-broadcasting if the Gopher continues to be unresponsive after the nudge. Those would each be separate tickets.

Summary: Gopher Request — Extend TrustShield™ to give $1 off Ride Sharing requests, and send a targeted conversion email to non-TrustShield Requestors after Ride Sharing completions
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher product / marketing team, ## 🎯 I want to extend the existing TrustShield™ discount to cover Ride Sharing requests (in addition to age-restricted delivery), and send a targeted post-ride email to Requestors who don't have TrustShield to convert them, ## ✅ So that TrustShield holders get a tangible discount on a second high-frequency request type, and non-TrustShield Ride Sharing users see what they could be saving and are nudged toward signing up. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * TrustShield™ today provides discounts for age-restricted delivery requests. This ticket adds **Ride Sharing** as a second eligible category, with a flat **$1 discount per Ride Sharing request** for TrustShield holders. * Separately, the ticket introduces a **new completed-request email template specifically for Ride Sharing** — but the email is **only sent to Requestors who do NOT have TrustShield**. It's a conversion nudge: "Here's what you would have saved with TrustShield." * The discount mechanic mirrors the existing TrustShield age-restricted-delivery discount: same code path, **Gopher payout is preserved in full**, the platform absorbs the $1. * The discount **can stack** with promo code redemptions on the same Ride Sharing request — additive, in the same way other promo discounts combine today. --- ## 📝 Two Deliverables (within this ticket) | # | Type | Change | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | Feature | **TrustShield Ride Sharing discount** — TrustShield holders get $1 off every Ride Sharing request. Mirrors existing age-restricted-delivery mechanic. | | 2 | Feature | **Targeted Ride Sharing post-completion email** — sent only to Requestors who completed a Ride Sharing request AND do NOT have TrustShield. Marketing conversion play. | --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior ### Item 1 — TrustShield $1 off Ride Sharing * When a TrustShield-holding Requestor submits a **Ride Sharing** request, a $1 discount is applied to their checkout / final cost. * The Gopher's payout is **not reduced** — the platform absorbs the $1, matching how the existing age-restricted TrustShield discount works. * The discount applies at the same point in the flow that the existing TrustShield age-restricted-delivery discount applies (price calculation / display / billing). * **Stacking:** the $1 discount stacks additively with any promo code the Requestor redeems on the same request. The order of application doesn't matter mathematically; both reduce the Requestor's cost without affecting the Gopher's payout. ### Item 2 — Targeted post-ride email for non-TrustShield Requestors * After a **Ride Sharing** request is completed by a Requestor who does **NOT** have TrustShield, the system sends the new completed-request email template (per the linked Figma). * Requestors who **do** have TrustShield receive the existing completed-request email (or whatever standard email goes to TrustShield holders today) — they don't receive this new template. * The email is sent in addition to whatever existing post-completion notifications fire — it's a category- and audience-specific marketing nudge, not a replacement for transactional confirmation. * The email's purpose is to surface what TrustShield would have saved on this ride and drive sign-ups. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — TrustShield holder gets $1 off a Ride Sharing request** * **Given** a Requestor has active TrustShield™, * **When** they submit a Ride Sharing request and the price is calculated, * **Then** a $1 discount is applied to their checkout total, visible in the price breakdown. **Scenario 2 — Non-TrustShield Requestor sees no discount** * **Given** a Requestor does NOT have TrustShield™, * **When** they submit a Ride Sharing request, * **Then** no $1 discount is applied to their checkout total. **Scenario 3 — Gopher payout is unchanged by the discount** * **Given** a TrustShield-holding Requestor's Ride Sharing request is completed, * **When** the Gopher is paid out, * **Then** the Gopher receives the full payout amount they would have received if there had been no discount — the platform absorbs the $1. **Scenario 4 — Discount stacks with promo code** * **Given** a TrustShield holder redeems a $2 promo code on a $20 Ride Sharing request, * **When** the price is calculated, * **Then** both discounts apply additively: Requestor pays $17 ($20 − $1 TrustShield − $2 promo). The Gopher's payout is still calculated against $20. **Scenario 5 — Discount is Ride Sharing only** * **Given** a TrustShield holder submits a Delivery request that is NOT age-restricted, * **When** the price is calculated, * **Then** no TrustShield discount applies (the existing rule covering only age-restricted delivery is unchanged). **Scenario 6 — Existing age-restricted TrustShield discount remains intact** * **Given** a TrustShield holder submits an age-restricted Delivery request, * **When** the price is calculated, * **Then** the existing TrustShield discount on age-restricted delivery still applies as it does today — no regression introduced by this ticket. **Scenario 7 — Non-TrustShield Ride Sharing completion sends the new email** * **Given** a Requestor without TrustShield completes a Ride Sharing request, * **When** the post-completion flow runs, * **Then** the new completed-request email template (per the Figma) is sent to that Requestor. **Scenario 8 — TrustShield holder Ride Sharing completion does NOT send the new email** * **Given** a Requestor with TrustShield completes a Ride Sharing request, * **When** the post-completion flow runs, * **Then** they receive their normal completion email, NOT the new template — the new template is specifically for non-TrustShield holders. **Scenario 9 — Non-Ride-Sharing completions do not trigger the new email** * **Given** a Requestor without TrustShield completes a Delivery or Service request, * **When** the post-completion flow runs, * **Then** they do NOT receive the new Ride-Sharing-specific template — it's scoped to Ride Sharing completions only. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * The TrustShield Ride Sharing discount is a flat **$1** off, applied per request. * The discount is available **only** to active TrustShield holders. * The discount applies **only** to Ride Sharing requests. Other categories continue under their existing rules (age-restricted delivery still has its own TrustShield discount per existing logic; other categories have no TrustShield discount). * **Gopher payout is preserved in full** — the platform absorbs the discount. Same accounting treatment as the existing age-restricted TrustShield discount. * The discount **stacks additively** with promo code redemptions on the same request. * The new Ride-Sharing completed-request email template is sent **only to non-TrustShield Requestors** who completed a Ride Sharing request. TrustShield holders receive their normal completion email. * The new email is **scoped to Ride Sharing only** — it does not fire for Delivery, Service, or other request types. * This ticket affects the **Gopher Request** app (Requestor experience). Gopher Go is not directly touched, though the underlying payout calculation must of course remain consistent. --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * The discount logic should reuse the existing TrustShield discount path — ideally a single function / service that takes (request type, TrustShield status) and returns the discount amount. Adding Ride Sharing to this lookup is the lowest-risk change. * The Gopher-payout-preservation must be enforced at the same layer where the existing age-restricted discount is enforced. If that's a ledger entry recording the platform's subsidy, do the same for Ride Sharing. * The post-completion email selection should be guarded by an explicit `IF (request_type == Ride Sharing) AND NOT (requestor.has_trustshield)` check, evaluated at the moment the post-completion email job dispatches. * The new email template should pull the original Ride Sharing fare and (optionally) display "You could have saved $1 with TrustShield" with a CTA. Final copy is per the Figma. * Recommend wrapping the whole feature in a feature flag so it can be rolled back independently. * Coordinate with **G40-96** (Promo Code admin tool overhaul) — the stacking behaviour between TrustShield and promo codes should be tested specifically against the existing and new promo code types defined there. --- ## 🎨 Design Reference * **Figma (Ride Sharing completed-request email):** https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=161-1214 --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Set up two test Requestor accounts: one with TrustShield active, one without. * Submit a Ride Sharing request from the TrustShield account — confirm $1 discount appears in the price breakdown and Gopher payout is unchanged. * Submit a Ride Sharing request from the non-TrustShield account — confirm no discount and confirm the new email template fires on completion. * Submit a Ride Sharing request from the TrustShield account, redeem a promo code, complete it — confirm both discounts apply additively, Gopher payout still on the full original amount. * Submit an age-restricted Delivery request from the TrustShield account — confirm existing age-restricted discount still applies (regression check). * Submit a non-Ride-Sharing request from either account — confirm the new email template does NOT fire. * Confirm the new email template renders correctly per the Figma on both desktop and mobile email clients. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Depends on the existing TrustShield discount mechanism being extensible to a new request type (Ride Sharing). * Depends on the existing post-completion email infrastructure supporting per-request-type and per-Requestor-attribute template selection. * Coordinates with **G40-96** (Promo Code overhaul) for stacking behaviour. * Out of scope: discounts on Ride Sharing other than the flat $1 (e.g., percentage-off, fare-based scaling). If desired in future, a separate ticket. * Out of scope: equivalent conversion emails for Delivery, Service, or other categories. This ticket is Ride Sharing only — if the pattern is successful, additional categories can be added in follow-ups.

Summary: Gopher Go — Scheduled Request — "Add to Calendar" trigger to the worker's native phone calendar
Description: ## Goal Give workers a one-tap **“Add to Calendar”** link on a **scheduled order** that hands the order’s **title, date, and time** to their **native phone calendar**. The OS creates the event; the worker keeps or edits it. **Gopher Go is only the trigger** — after the hand-off it’s entirely between the user and their device. (This replaces the earlier “add a calendar page” framing — no in-app calendar page is needed.) ## Rules (John, 2026-07-02) * **Only scheduled orders.** A **“flexible”** order counts as a scheduled order. * **Flexible defaulting:** the calendar event defaults to the flexible window — **24 hours / 7 days / 2 weeks**. Because the worker views it in their own native calendar, they can change the date/time to whatever they want; that is **not** Gopher Go’s concern. * No post-hand-off tracking or logic — Gopher Go simply triggers the calendar. ## Placement rule (John, 2026-07-03) — critical * The button **only exists after the order is accepted**, in the **request details** of the scheduled order, **directly above the Start button** (its historical placement). * It must **never** appear before acceptance — a Gopher who hasn’t accepted isn’t connected to the request and can’t schedule it. ASAP/now orders never reach this scheduled-detail state, so the button is inherently scheduled-only. **▶ Full developer handoff:** `docs/handoff/G40-86-add-to-calendar.md` ## ✅ Done (front-end placement) — `_prototypes/Go/gopher-go-purchase-delivery-figma.html` Built in John’s **real design screens** — the file that owns the accepted-job lifecycle (active → detail → update). New frame **“Scheduled order (accepted · pre-start)”**, reusing existing tokens/components (topbar, navy pay-hero, block cards, kv rows, `.pill` ● Scheduled, `.btn` system) — no makeshift markup. * Post-accept surface: header pill **● Scheduled**, hero **“pays on completion”** — only reachable after accepting. * The **foot is stacked**: outlined **Add to Calendar** sits **directly above** the green **Start job →** — the placement John specified. * **Flexible** counts as scheduled and gets the same button (defaults to 24h / 7d / 2w, editable in the native calendar). Rule noted; no separate flexible frame drawn. **Cleanup:** the earlier misplaced build in the reference-only concept file `gopher-go-worker.html` (button on the **pre-accept** browse job-detail, where Pass/Accept live) was **fully reverted** — CSS, markup, handler, and `.ics` util removed; 0 remnants. That placement was a logic bug (a Gopher could schedule a request they aren’t connected to) and lived in a file the manifest marks reference-only. ## 🔧 To build (developer / native) * **Wire to the real accepted scheduled-order detail** (this frame is the placement reference — above Start, post-accept, scheduled/flexible only, never ASAP). * **Use the order’s real structured datetime**, not a display label — pass the scheduled date/time (and flexible tier) straight into the calendar-event builder. * **Build the** `.ics` / native hand-off: standard VEVENT (title, date/time + duration, location = on-site/pickup→drop-off, description) → open on device (cross-platform `.ics`, or iOS `EKEventStore` / Android `Intent.ACTION_INSERT`). * **Flexible window source:** read the order’s flexible tier (24h / 7d / 2w); default the start from it with an “adjust in your calendar” note. ## Acceptance criteria 1. On an **accepted scheduled** order (flexible counts), an **Add to Calendar** action is available in the request details, **above the Start button**; **never** before acceptance and **never** on ASAP/now orders. 2. Tapping it opens the worker’s **native calendar** with the order’s **title, date, and time** pre-filled. 3. **Flexible** orders default to the **24h / 7d / 2w** window and remain fully editable in the native calendar. 4. Gopher Go performs **no** further action after the hand-off.

Summary: Gopher App - Updating A Submitted Request - Send Another Email to User and Update Active Admin Anytime there is an update.
Description: > 🔧 **DEV MAP — see pinned comment (updated 2026-07-02 after owner review).** The updated-confirmation **email is consolidated into G40-305** (rebranded email program: template `request-updated-2026.ejs` / dispatcher type 36). The Figma board I first cited was tagged **G40-197, which is CANCELLED — ignore it**; source of truth is **G40-305** + `Documentation/SMS:Emails/`. **G40-88 now owns:** (1) the **admin order-log cost-delta** at `update.js:708`, and (2) making the requestor self-edit endpoint `update.js:52 exports.update_v2` fire the consolidated G40-305 email. Full step-by-step in the comment. Linked ↔ G40-305. --- When a Requestor updates a submitted request, the system currently only sends the original order confirmation email and logs a generic "Order Updated" entry in the admin panel. To prevent disputes — particularly around financial changes — an updated order confirmation email must be sent to the Requestor on every update, and the admin order log must capture the specific details of what changed, including any cost adjustments. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Requestor who has updated a submitted request, ## 🎯 I want to receive an updated order confirmation email reflecting the changes I made, ## ✅ So that I always have an accurate, up-to-date record of my order — especially when financial details have changed — and disputes can be avoided. ## 💡 Context / Background * Currently, a confirmation email titled "Gopher order confirmation #\[Order#\]" is sent when a request is first submitted. * When a Requestor later updates their request, no new email is sent — leaving the Requestor with an outdated confirmation and no record of the changes. * Updates frequently involve financial changes (e.g. total cost adjustments), which can lead to confusion and disputes if not documented. * The admin order log currently records a generic "Order Updated" entry with no detail on what changed. This must be updated to include specific change information, including cost deltas. ## 🗒️ Admin Order Log Format **Current (incorrect):** * 2025-02-07 04:56 PM — Order Created (Delivery-Convenience Store) * 2025-02-07 05:01 PM — Order Updated (Delivery-Convenience Store) **Required (correct):** * 2025-02-07 04:56 PM — Order Created (Delivery-Convenience Store) * 2025-02-07 05:01 PM — Order Updated (Delivery-Convenience Store) Total Cost from $43.23 to $54.32 ## 📧 Updated Confirmation Email (now via G40-305) * **Trigger:** Any update to a submitted request (requestor self-edit via `update_v2`). * **Email:** the consolidated G40-305 request-updated email (type 36, `request-updated-2026.ejs`). Copy/subject may branch by trigger — finalize with G40-305. * **Content:** Full updated order details reflecting all current request information, including any revised financials. ## ✅ Expected Behavior * Every time a Requestor updates a submitted request, the consolidated updated-request email (G40-305) is sent to the Requestor. * The admin order log entry for an update includes specific change details, including any cost adjustments showing the previous and new total. ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 – Updated-request email is sent on every request update.** Given a Requestor updates a submitted request, when the update is saved, then the consolidated G40-305 request-updated email is sent to the Requestor and reflects the full updated order details. **Scenario 2 – Admin order log captures change details including cost adjustments.** Given a Requestor updates a submitted request with a cost change, when saved, then the admin order log records the update with the specific change detail (previous and new total cost); format: Order Updated (\[Category\]) Total Cost from $\[old\] to $\[new\]. **Scenario 3 – Admin order log captures non-financial updates.** Given a Requestor updates without changing cost, when saved, then the log records the relevant change details AND the updated email is still sent. **Scenario 4 – Multiple updates each trigger a new email and log entry.** Given a Requestor updates the same request more than once, when each update is saved, then a new email is sent for each, and a new timestamped log entry is added for each (never overwriting). ## ⚙️ Business Rules * The updated-request email must be sent on every request update (via the consolidated G40-305 email). * The admin order log must record the specific details of each update, including previous and new total cost when financials change. * Each update must produce a separate, timestamped log entry — updates must never overwrite previous log entries. * This applies to all request types and categories. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * **Email work is consolidated into G40-305** — G40-88 only needs to add the requestor self-edit (`update_v2`) as a trigger site for the type-36 email. The admin order-log cost-delta enrichment is G40-88's own work. * The admin order log update logic must compare previous and new field values to generate the change detail string, including cost deltas. * Source of truth: G40-305 + `Documentation/SMS:Emails/` (`request-updated-2026.ejs`, `impl-request-updated-trigger.md`). ## 🧪 QA Notes * Update a request — confirm the consolidated request-updated email is sent with the correct updated details. * Update with a cost change — confirm the admin log entry shows previous and new total cost. * Update without a cost change — confirm the email is still sent and the log entry reflects the relevant change. * Update the same request multiple times — confirm a new email and a new log entry are generated for each. * Test across multiple request categories.

Summary: Gopher Request — Hide deactivated Gophers from all Requestors' MY Gopher lists and recent conversations (preserve underlying data; restore on reactivation)
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Requestor on the Gopher Request app, ## 🎯 I want deactivated Gophers to be removed from my MY Gopher list and recent in-app conversations, ## ✅ So that I don't attempt to re-engage a Gopher who has been deactivated for cause, and the platform's deactivation decision is consistently reflected across the Requestor experience. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * A Gopher account is deactivated when an admin bans the account for cause (per G40-143, G40-225). After deactivation, the Gopher cannot accept new requests. * Today, even after deactivation, the Gopher can still appear in Requestors' **MY Gopher (favorites)** lists and in **recent in-app messaging conversations**, creating dead-end re-engagement attempts and a degraded experience. * This ticket extends the deactivation flow to clean up those Requestor-facing surfaces. * **Hide, don't delete** — the underlying favorite relationship and message thread data must be preserved for audit, dispute, and potential reactivation. --- ## 🔍 Surface Scope | Surface | Action on deactivation | | --- | --- | | **MY Gopher list (favorites)** | Hide from the Requestor's view. The favorite record is preserved on the server. | | **Recent / Active in-app conversations list** | Hide the deactivated Gopher's thread from the list. | | **Existing message thread data** | Preserved on the server. The thread is no longer surfaced in the UI but the underlying data is retained for audit and dispute purposes. | | **Order history** | Untouched. Completed orders with the Gopher remain in Requestor history with the Gopher's name visible — it's a factual business record. | | **Existing ratings the Requestor left** | Untouched. Factual records of past interactions. | --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior ### On deactivation * The deactivated Gopher is **hidden** from every Requestor's MY Gopher list across the platform. * The deactivated Gopher's conversation thread is **hidden** from every Requestor's recent / active conversations list. * Underlying records (favorite relationships, message threads) are **preserved** on the server. The change is UI-level only. * Order history and prior ratings remain visible — these are factual business records and are not touched by this rule. ### On admin reactivation (if it happens later) * The deactivated Gopher is **restored** to every Requestor's MY Gopher list where they previously appeared. * The conversation thread is **restored** to the recent conversations list. * Because the underlying data was preserved on deactivation, restoration is a simple un-hide — no rebuild of relationships needed. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — Deactivated Gopher removed from MY Gopher lists** * **Given** a Gopher is on multiple Requestors' MY Gopher lists, * **When** the Gopher is deactivated by an admin, * **Then** the Gopher is no longer visible on any of those Requestors' MY Gopher lists. **Scenario 2 — Deactivated Gopher's conversations hidden from recent list** * **Given** a Gopher has active or recent in-app conversations with multiple Requestors, * **When** the Gopher is deactivated, * **Then** each Requestor's recent / active conversations list no longer shows the deactivated Gopher's thread. **Scenario 3 — Underlying favorite relationship is preserved** * **Given** a Gopher has been deactivated and removed from a Requestor's MY Gopher list, * **When** the underlying data is inspected, * **Then** the favorite relationship record still exists on the server — only the UI surfacing is suppressed. **Scenario 4 — Underlying message thread is preserved** * **Given** a Gopher has been deactivated, * **When** the underlying message thread is inspected, * **Then** the full message history is still present on the server, available for audit / dispute access. **Scenario 5 — Order history is untouched** * **Given** a Requestor has completed orders with a now-deactivated Gopher, * **When** the Requestor opens their order history, * **Then** the orders are still visible with the Gopher's name displayed as recorded at the time of the order. **Scenario 6 — Existing ratings are untouched** * **Given** a Requestor previously rated the Gopher who is now deactivated, * **When** the Requestor views any surface that displays those ratings, * **Then** the ratings remain visible exactly as before. **Scenario 7 — Reactivation restores MY Gopher and conversation visibility** * **Given** a previously deactivated Gopher is reactivated by an admin, * **When** the reactivation is applied, * **Then** the Gopher is restored to every Requestor's MY Gopher list where they previously appeared, and the conversation thread is restored to the recent conversations list. **Scenario 8 — Reactivation does not over-restore** * **Given** a Gopher was never on a particular Requestor's MY Gopher list before deactivation, * **When** the Gopher is reactivated, * **Then** they do not appear on that Requestor's MY Gopher list now — reactivation restores prior state, not new state. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * Removal is **UI suppression only** — the favorite-relationship record and message thread data are preserved on the server. * Both surfaces (MY Gopher list and recent in-app conversations) are affected uniformly. * Order history and prior ratings are explicitly out of scope — they remain visible with the Gopher's name as recorded. * Reactivation restores both surfaces to their pre-deactivation state automatically (no admin or Requestor action needed beyond the reactivation itself). * This rule applies to the **Gopher Request** app where MY Gopher lists exist. The Gopher Go app is not directly affected (Gophers don't have a "MY Requestor" equivalent). * The removal must take effect as part of the deactivation transaction — not eventually-consistent. A Requestor opening MY Gopher right after the deactivation must not see the deactivated Gopher. --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * The cleanest pattern is a `deactivated_at` (or equivalent) timestamp on the Gopher record, and a query filter that excludes Gophers with a non-null `deactivated_at` from MY Gopher and recent-conversation surface queries. Reactivation simply nulls the timestamp. * This approach gives free reactivation handling (no need for a separate restore step) and preserves all underlying data automatically. * Avoid deleting rows from any favorite-list or message-thread table to satisfy this ticket. The point of hide-only is preserving audit and dispute capability. * Confirm any cached / denormalised counts (e.g., "You have 12 favorites") update correctly on both deactivation and reactivation. Stale counts are the most likely follow-up bug. * Coordinate with **G40-225** (Stripe rejection on deactivation) and **G40-143** (anti-evasion identity check) — these all run on the same deactivation event and should be triggered from a single handler. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Set up a test Gopher who appears on multiple test Requestors' MY Gopher lists and has active conversations with each. * Deactivate the Gopher — confirm they immediately disappear from every Requestor's MY Gopher list and recent conversations list. * Inspect the underlying data — confirm the favorite relationships and message threads still exist on the server. * Open one of the Requestor's order history — confirm the Gopher's prior orders still display with their name. * Open one of the Requestor's ratings — confirm the rating is still visible. * Reactivate the Gopher (admin override) — confirm they are restored to each Requestor's MY Gopher list and recent conversations. * Confirm reactivation does NOT add the Gopher to MY Gopher for any Requestor who never had them as a favorite before. * Test on both iOS and Android. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Depends on the admin deactivation event being a single point in the system that other rules (G40-225, G40-143, this ticket) can hook into. * Out of scope: notifying the Requestor that one of their favorited Gophers was deactivated. The UI change is silent in this release; if a follow-up notification is desired, that's a separate ticket. * Out of scope: any equivalent rule on the Gopher Go side — Gophers do not have a "MY Requestor" list, so there's no symmetric work needed.

Summary: Gopher Go — Show full Requestor name and unblurred profile picture (skip anonymisation) when a request is sent to a MY Gopher
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher on the Requestor's MY Gopher list who has been notified of one of their requests, ## 🎯 I want to see the Requestor's full name and unblurred profile picture ## ✅ So that I can immediately recognise that this is from someone who has already chosen me as a trusted Gopher — and respond accordingly, without the friction of the standard anonymisation that applies to general broadcasts. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * Today, when a Gopher receives a broadcast for a submitted request, the Requestor's profile picture is blurred and their name is anonymised. This protects Requestor privacy when the recipient Gopher has no established relationship with them. * That protection is unnecessary friction when the Requestor has already explicitly added the recipient Gopher to their **MY Gopher** list — a trust relationship already exists. * This ticket adds a check: if the recipient Gopher is on the Requestor's MY Gopher list, **skip the anonymisation** entirely and show the full name and unblurred profile picture. * Anonymisation continues to apply for all other recipients on the same broadcast. --- ## 🔍 Display Matrix | Recipient Gopher's relationship to Requestor | Profile picture | Name | | --- | --- | --- | | **On Requestor's MY Gopher list** | Full, unblurred | Full name | | Not on Requestor's MY Gopher list | Blurred (existing behaviour) | Anonymised (existing behaviour) | The rule is evaluated **per recipient** — a single broadcast can simultaneously show full identity to MY Gopher recipients and anonymised identity to all others. --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior ### Surfaces in scope The rule applies to **every pre-acceptance surface** that currently shows an anonymised Requestor identity to recipient Gophers, including: * The push / SMS notification preview when a broadcast goes out. * The in-app broadcast preview / request list card. * The request details view shown before the Gopher accepts. Wherever the existing system applies anonymisation, the new rule replaces it with full identity when the recipient is on the Requestor's MY Gopher list. ### Post-acceptance behaviour (unchanged) * After a Gopher accepts the request, the Requestor's identity is already revealed to that Gopher per existing behaviour. This ticket does not change post-acceptance display. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — MY Gopher sees the full Requestor identity** * **Given** a Requestor has Gopher A on their MY Gopher list, * **When** the Requestor submits a request and Gopher A receives the broadcast, * **Then** Gopher A sees the Requestor's full name and unblurred profile picture on every pre-acceptance surface (push notification, broadcast preview, request details). **Scenario 2 — Non-MY-Gopher recipient still sees anonymised identity** * **Given** a Requestor's broadcast is sent to Gopher B, who is NOT on the Requestor's MY Gopher list, * **When** Gopher B receives the broadcast, * **Then** Gopher B sees the Requestor's blurred profile picture and anonymised name per existing behaviour. **Scenario 3 — Mixed broadcast (some recipients are MY Gopher, some are not)** * **Given** a single broadcast goes to Gopher A (on the Requestor's MY Gopher list) and Gopher B (not on the list), * **When** both Gophers receive the broadcast, * **Then** Gopher A sees the full Requestor identity and Gopher B sees the anonymised version — the same broadcast renders differently per recipient. **Scenario 4 — Rule applies to every pre-acceptance surface** * **Given** Gopher A is on the Requestor's MY Gopher list and receives a broadcast, * **When** Gopher A opens the push notification, then the in-app broadcast preview, then the request details view, * **Then** the Requestor's full identity is shown on all three surfaces — the rule is applied uniformly. **Scenario 5 — Removing a Gopher from MY Gopher reverts to anonymised** * **Given** Gopher A was on the Requestor's MY Gopher list but has just been removed before the broadcast was sent, * **When** Gopher A receives a subsequent broadcast, * **Then** Gopher A sees the standard anonymised display. **Scenario 6 — Post-acceptance display is unchanged** * **Given** any recipient Gopher accepts the request, * **When** the post-acceptance views render, * **Then** the Requestor's full identity is shown per existing post-acceptance behaviour — this ticket does not change that path. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * The rule is evaluated **per recipient** at the moment the broadcast is rendered for that Gopher. A single broadcast can produce different views for different recipients. * The check is: "is recipient Gopher on the Requestor's MY Gopher list at the moment of broadcast send?" If yes, full identity; if no, existing anonymisation. * The rule applies to **every pre-acceptance surface** that currently anonymises the Requestor. * Post-acceptance display is unchanged — the Requestor's identity is already revealed to the accepting Gopher per existing behaviour. * The rule applies on **Gopher Go** only — the Requestor app does not display the Gopher-side broadcast preview. --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * The anonymisation logic likely lives in a single place today (a serialiser or view-model for the broadcast payload). Adding the MY Gopher check there is the lowest-risk place to make this change, so it applies uniformly to every surface fed by that serialiser. * If the anonymisation is applied independently at each surface, the change should be made in each of those code paths — and a refactor to centralise it should be considered as a follow-up. * The MY Gopher membership check should run server-side at broadcast-send time, not client-side. A client-side check would require sending the Requestor's full identity to every recipient and conditionally rendering it, which leaks data. * Recommend wrapping the change in the existing broadcast feature flag (if any) so it can be rolled back independently. --- ## 🎨 Design Reference * **Figma:** https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=5412-8407 --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Add a test Gopher to a test Requestor's MY Gopher list. Submit a request that broadcasts to both that Gopher and at least one non-MY-Gopher. * Confirm the MY Gopher recipient sees the full Requestor name and unblurred profile picture on push, broadcast preview, and request details. * Confirm the non-MY-Gopher recipient sees the existing anonymised display on the same surfaces. * Remove the Gopher from MY Gopher and trigger a new broadcast — confirm the anonymised display now applies to them. * Verify on both iOS and Android. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Depends on the MY Gopher list being queryable from the broadcast-send logic. If MY Gopher membership lives in a separate service, that lookup needs to be in the broadcast hot path. * Out of scope: deactivated Gophers. Per the deactivation flow (G40-89 / G40-225), deactivated Gophers do not receive broadcasts, so the question of how to display the Requestor's identity to them does not arise. * Out of scope: any analogous "unblur for trusted Requestor" mechanism going the other direction — the Gopher's identity is shown differently in different contexts but is not anonymised by the same mechanism. ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=external&localId=null&id=&&collection=&height=null&occurrenceKey=null&width=null&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=blob%3Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fmedia.staging.atl-paas.net%2F%3Ftype%3Dfile%26localId%3Dnull%26id%3D24cfed5f-3ccf-4afd-abb4-b2f42b3584fc%26%26collection%3D%26height%3D1270%26occurrenceKey%3Dnull%26width%3D393%26__contextId%3Dnull%26__displayType%3Dnull%26__external%3Dfalse%26__fileMimeType%3Dnull%26__fileName%3Dnull%26__fileSize%3Dnull%26__mediaTraceId%3Dnull%26url%3Dnull)

Summary: Gopher App - Pending Submitted Request - Any Activity Without A Response - Notifications - SMS Sent to engage with Activity. (Not applicable to Inbox messaging)
Description: > 🔧 **DEV-READY HANDOFF — groomed 2026-07-02 (John Newbury).** Backend investigated; root cause identified. This block is authoritative; original 2024 body retained below. No open questions remain. Full handoff: `docs/handoff/G40-92-requestor-sms-followup.md`. ## 🔎 Root cause (evidence from `gopher-backend-api` export) The symptom is **not** a flaky SMS queue. An SMS was only ever wired for **one** trigger (cost adjustment). The other events notify the requestor by **push only**, gated on a valid FCM token — so with no/expired token or notifications off, the requestor gets **nothing, no SMS fallback**. That reads as "intermittent." | Trigger | What the old code sends to requestor | File:line | | --- | --- | --- | | Bid submitted | **Push only**, gated on `fcm_token`. No SMS. | `order_bids.js:148` | | Counter-offer | **Push only**. No SMS. | `counter_offer.js:168` | | Cost adjustment | **SMS** (+push). The only real requestor SMS. | `cost_adjustment.js:196` | | Request accepted / "select my worker" | **Push only** to requestor. | `order_gophers.js` (accept path) | Also: `lib/sendSms.js:19` re-throws on any Twilio error and call sites are inline `await send_sms(...)` with **no local try/catch** → a transient Twilio failure throws mid-request and the SMS is silently lost (no retry/queue). Push sends are fire-and-forget (unawaited). No acknowledgment gating on the requestor path. (`middleware/OOA_notif.js` is the **gopher-broadcast**, a different direction — out of scope, noted to avoid confusion.) ## ✅ Resolved decisions (John, 2026-07-02) * **Target:** fix the **live backend now** (interim) **and** write the **new-build spec**. * **Go-forward triggers:** Bid · Counter-offer · Cost adjustment · **Request accepted** ("Suggest My Gopher" is **renamed** "I'll select my worker" — same behavior). * **Inbox (NEW):** once a request is **connected**, an unacknowledged **inbox message** also fires an SMS. **Reverses** the old "no SMS for inbox" rule. * Recipient: **requestor only** (gophers excluded — saves Twilio cost). * **One SMS max per unacknowledged message** (no duplicate for same message; none if already read). ## 🛠️ Interim fix (live backend) 1. Add the missing requestor SMS at **bid** (`order_bids.js:148`), **counter-offer** (`counter_offer.js:168`), and **accept/"select my worker"** (`order_gophers.js`) — mirror the cost-adjustment SMS. 2. **SMS must not depend on push** — send regardless of `fcm_token`; do not nest inside the `if (fcm_token)` block. 3. Wrap each `send_sms` in its own try/catch + retry/queue so a Twilio error is logged and never aborts the bid/accept/adjustment action. 4. **Acknowledgment suppression** — no SMS if the requestor already viewed/responded. 5. Log every attempt (outcome keyed to `order_id`+event) and alert on failures; cross-check Twilio logs. ## ✅ Acceptance criteria (go-forward) 1. Bid submitted → requestor SMS (even with no FCM token). 2. Counter-offer → requestor SMS. 3. Cost adjustment pending → requestor SMS. 4. Request accepted / "I'll select my worker" → requestor SMS. 5. Connected request: new unread inbox message → exactly one requestor SMS per message; none if already read; gophers never get inbox SMS. 6. No SMS for any already-acknowledged event. 7. Every send attempt logged with outcome; failures alert. 8. A Twilio failure never aborts the underlying action. 9. Holds on iOS + Android + web. --- ## 📜 Original ticket (2024 — retained for context) The platform is designed to send a follow-up SMS to a Requestor when key activity occurs on their pending request and they have not yet responded. This feature was reported firing intermittently. **Note:** the 2024 body listed triggers as bid / Suggest My Gopher / cost adjustment and said "not applicable to Inbox messaging" — both are **superseded** by the resolved decisions above (SMG → "I'll select my worker"; counter-offer + request-accepted added; inbox now fires SMS once connected). Original trigger events: Bid submitted · Suggest My Gopher accepted · Cost adjustment pending. Original business rules: SMS must fire reliably on every trigger; inbox excluded; no SMS if already acknowledged. Original QA: fire each trigger 5×+ to confirm consistent delivery; test iOS + Android.
