Summary: Admin Panel — New "Users by Location" targeted messaging tool with active-user eligibility floor, two-step send, per-channel opt-out respect, and per-send audit log
Description: ## Goal An HQ Dashboard admin tool to message **users filtered by location**, with an **active-user eligibility floor**, a **two-step send** (compose → confirm), **per-channel opt-out** respect, and a **per-send audit log**. **Surface:** Gopher HQ Dashboard (`Documentation/Dashboard/`), the console replacing Active Admin (G40-70). Builds on G40-103 (Users detail location fields). John is building the tool UI in the dashboard directly. **▶ Full zero-discovery spec:** `docs/handoff/G40-95-users-by-location-messaging.md` (targeting columns, opt-out sources, send flow, audit schema — all grounded in `gopher-backend-api`). ## Logic (grounded in live backend) * **Location targeting:** `addresses.state / city / zip_code` (+ `latitude/longitude` for radius); `users_roles.radius/point` for coverage. * **Active floor:** `users.last_sign_in_at >= now() - :activeDays` (30/60/90 presets); reject send if resolved count < minimum floor. * **Role:** `users_roles.role_id` (1 gopher / 2 requestor). * **Two-step send:** `POST /admin/broadcasts/preview` (returns opt-out-filtered recipient count) → `POST /admin/broadcasts/send` (reuses the `OOA_notif.js` consent + unsubscribe fan-out). * **Per-channel opt-out:** email = `users_roles.sub_ooa` (+ unsubscribe link); push = `users_roles.fcm_token` present; **SMS = GAP** (no per-user opt-out flag exists — add `users_roles.sub_sms` or an `sms_opt_outs` table + STOP webhook; interim carrier-only). * **Audit log (new):** `admin_broadcasts(admin_id, channels, filter_json, message, recipient_count, sent_count, failed_count, created_at)` (+ optional per-recipient `admin_broadcast_recipients`). Surface as "Sent history". ## Acceptance criteria 1. Users filterable by location (state/city/zip, + radius). 2. Active-user eligibility floor enforced; send blocked below the minimum floor. 3. Two-step compose → confirm with a resolved, opt-out-filtered recipient count. 4. Per-channel opt-out respected (email `sub_ooa`, push `fcm_token`; SMS pending an opt-out flag). 5. Every send writes a per-send audit-log row. ## Dependency SMS channel needs a per-user opt-out flag before it can claim per-user SMS consent (see spec).

Summary: Active Admin — Promo Code admin tool: fix 2 bugs (Value save, auto-expire), 3 UX consolidations, and add Category scoping + platform-subsidised "Add Money to Request" Type
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher admin managing Promo Codes, ## 🎯 I want the Promo Code admin tool to work reliably, present a cleaner UI, and support category scoping plus a new platform-subsidised promo type, ## ✅ So that I can configure codes correctly the first time, without working around bugs, and can run more targeted marketing campaigns including Gopher Rewards. --- ## 💡 Context / Background This ticket bundles seven distinct improvements to the existing Promo Code admin tool. They are split into bugs (must fix), UX consolidations (clean up the existing screen), and feature additions. All seven land on the same screen and are best shipped together, but each is independently scoped below for clarity. --- ## 📋 The 7 Improvements | # | Type | Change | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | UX | **Applies To** — remove the "Applies To" selector entirely. Only Requestors submit requests, so the field has a single possible value and is redundant; all codes are requestor-only. | | 2 | Feature | **Type** — add a new option for a **platform-subsidised promo** that adds money to the request budget. | | 3 | Bug | **Value** — fix the bug where the value field intermittently fails to save (both $ and % variants). | | 4 | UX | **Reduces tab merge** — combine "Reduces" and "Reduces On Age Restricted Fee" into a single tab with **multi-select checkboxes** (Gopher Fee, Instant Transfer Fee, Age-Restricted Fee) plus a **Select All** shortcut. A code can reduce one or more fees. | | 5 | UX | **Duration** — remove the "once" option (already asked at the top of the page). | | 6 | Feature | **Categories** — add ability to scope a promo code to specific request categories using checkboxes plus a Select All shortcut. | | 7 | Bug | **Auto-expire** — codes must become inactive precisely at their expiration timestamp. Doesn't work today. | --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior — Per Item ### Item 1 — Remove the "Applies To" selector * The "Applies To" selector is removed from the Promo Code admin screen entirely. Requestors are the only parties who submit requests, so the field has a single possible value and is redundant; every code is implicitly requestor-only. * This supersedes the original ask of only removing the "Gophers" option — since Requestors is the sole remaining target, the whole selector is dropped rather than left as a one-option field. **Dev note: remove the field; do not ship a single-option dropdown.** * Any existing codes that have "Gophers" set should be reviewed by admin; one-time migration is out of scope but those codes effectively become inert. ### Item 2 — New "Add Money to Request" Type * Add a new Type option to the existing Type selector (alongside the existing reductive types). * **Effect:** the Requestor's checkout total is reduced by the promo amount, while the **Gopher's payout is preserved in full**. The platform absorbs the difference. * This is the foundation for Gopher Rewards / marketplace-incentive campaigns where the platform pays to attract demand without shorting the Gopher. * The Value field, Duration, and Categories selectors all apply to this Type the same way they apply to existing types. * The accounting impact (platform-side ledger entry recording the subsidy per redemption) needs to be captured so it can be reconciled. ### Item 3 — Fix the Value save bug * The Value field must reliably persist whatever the admin entered (dollar amount or percentage), without requiring a second edit. * Both $ amount and % off variants must save and reload identically to what was entered. * Identify and fix the underlying cause — do not work around it with a client-side retry. ### Item 4 — Merge "Reduces" tabs into one multi-select * Today there are two tabs: "Reduces" and "Reduces On Age Restricted Fee." * Merge into a single tab listing the three fees a code can reduce: * Gopher Fee * Instant Transfer Fee * Age-Restricted Fee * Use **checkboxes** for multi-select — a code can reduce one OR MORE of these — plus a **Select All** shortcut that toggles all three on or off. At least one fee must be selected. * At redemption, the discount applies to the combined total of the selected fees. * Migrate existing codes: a code currently set against the Age-Restricted Fee loads with the Age-Restricted Fee box pre-checked; everything else with the appropriate box(es) checked. * **Note:** updated from the original single-select / radio design to multi-select checkboxes + Select All (product decision). See Implementation Considerations. ### Item 5 — Remove redundant Duration "once" * Remove the "once" option from the Duration selector. This option is already covered by a question asked at the top of the page, and having it in Duration creates redundant configuration. * Migrate existing codes: any code currently set to Duration = once should be migrated to the equivalent state via the top-of-page question. ### Item 6 — Category selection * Add a new field to scope a promo code to specific request categories. * Categories available: **Delivery**, **Ride Sharing**, **Service**, **Other**. * Use **checkboxes** for multi-select (a code can apply to one or more categories), plus a **Select All** shortcut that toggles every checkbox on or off. * At redemption, the code is only valid if the order's request type falls within the selected categories. If no categories are selected, the code is invalid (admin must explicitly choose at least one, or Select All). ### Item 7 — Fix auto-expire * When a code's expiration date / timestamp passes, the code must become inactive **precisely at that timestamp**, not on a deferred sweep. * The check must run at the moment of redemption (server-side validation) so the timing is exact regardless of any background job cadence. * Already-redeemed-before-expiration usages remain valid; only future redemptions are blocked. * Active/inactive state displayed in the admin UI should reflect the live evaluation (active until expiration timestamp, inactive thereafter). --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — Applies To selector removed** * **Given** an admin opens the Promo Code create / edit screen, * **When** they view the form, * **Then** there is no "Applies To" selector at all (and therefore no "Gophers" option); codes are requestor-only by default. **Scenario 2 — New Add Money to Request Type works** * **Given** an admin creates a promo code with the new Type and a value of $5, * **When** a Requestor redeems it on a request with a $20 budget, * **Then** the Requestor's checkout total is reduced by $5, and the Gopher's payout on the resulting order is unchanged from what it would have been at the original $20 budget. **Scenario 3 — Platform subsidy is captured in the ledger** * **Given** the new Type code is redeemed, * **When** the resulting transactions are recorded, * **Then** a platform-side ledger entry captures the subsidy amount so it can be reconciled in financial reporting. **Scenario 4 — Value field saves correctly** * **Given** an admin enters a dollar amount in the Value field, * **When** they save the code, * **Then** the code reloads with the exact value entered — no need to re-edit. **Scenario 5 — Value field works for percentages too** * **Given** an admin enters a percentage in the Value field, * **When** they save the code, * **Then** the code reloads with the exact percentage entered. **Scenario 6 — Reduces tabs are merged into one multi-select** * **Given** an admin opens the Promo Code edit screen, * **When** they view the Reduces section, * **Then** they see a single section with three fee checkboxes (Gopher Fee, Instant Transfer Fee, Age-Restricted Fee) plus a Select All shortcut — not two separate tabs — and can select one or more. At least one fee is required. **Scenario 7 — Existing Age-Restricted codes migrate cleanly** * **Given** an admin opens a code that was previously configured against the Age-Restricted Fee tab, * **When** the new merged UI loads it, * **Then** the Age-Restricted Fee checkbox is pre-checked with no data loss. **Scenario 8 — Duration "once" option is removed** * **Given** an admin opens the Promo Code create / edit screen, * **When** they view the Duration selector, * **Then** "once" is no longer an option. **Scenario 9 — Category multi-select with Select All works** * **Given** an admin is configuring a new code, * **When** they tick the Delivery and Ride Sharing checkboxes, * **Then** the code is scoped to those categories. Tapping Select All ticks all four (Delivery, Ride Sharing, Service, Other); tapping it again unticks all. **Scenario 10 — Category scoping enforced at redemption** * **Given** a code scoped to Delivery only, * **When** a Requestor attempts to redeem it on a Ride Sharing request, * **Then** redemption is rejected with a clear "not valid for this request type" message. **Scenario 11 — Auto-expire is precise** * **Given** a code's expiration timestamp is 5:00 PM today, * **When** a Requestor attempts redemption at 5:00:01 PM, * **Then** redemption is rejected with an "expired" message — no sweep-job delay. **Scenario 12 — Already-redeemed usages stay valid after expiration** * **Given** a Requestor redeemed a code before its expiration timestamp, * **When** that order is processed after the expiration timestamp, * **Then** the order continues to honour the discount — expiration affects only future redemptions. **Scenario 13 — Active / inactive display reflects live state** * **Given** the admin views a code in the Promo Code list view, * **When** the code's expiration timestamp passes, * **Then** the list view shows the code as inactive without requiring a page refresh or admin action. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * The new "Add Money to Request" Type **must preserve the Gopher's payout in full**. The discount is absorbed by the platform, not the Gopher. * Every redemption of the new Type must produce a ledger entry recording the platform's subsidy for that order. * Promo code expiration is evaluated **at redemption time, server-side**. No deferred sweeps. * Category selection requires at least one category to be selected (or Select All); a code with zero categories is invalid. * The Reduces tab merge does not change which fee(s) a given code reduces — existing codes migrate to the equivalent checkbox selection. A code may now reduce more than one fee; at least one fee is required. * The Value field fix must address the root cause, not be a client-side workaround. * The Applies To selector is removed entirely; codes are persisted as requestor-only. Existing codes with "Gophers" set become effectively inert (no migration of those codes is in scope). --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * The two bugs (Value save, auto-expire) likely live in separate code paths from the UI changes. Worth investigating early so any required backend changes are scoped before UI work begins. * The new "Add Money to Request" Type touches multiple subsystems: promo-code redemption, order pricing, Gopher payout calculation, and platform accounting. Recommend mapping each subsystem and identifying the single source of truth for "Gopher payout amount" before changing anything. * Auto-expire at redemption time is the right call for precision, but admin-side list views also need a way to display the current active/inactive state. The simplest implementation: compute active/inactive on the fly based on `expires_at <= now()` whenever the code is read. * For category selection, consider whether existing codes (created before this feature) default to "all categories" or to a specific subset. Recommended default: all categories (matches today's behaviour where there was no category restriction). * **(Updated) Reduces is multi-select** — checkboxes + Select All, not the single-select radio originally drafted. A code can reduce one or more fees and redemption discounts the combined total of the selected fees. Data model: `reducesFees: string[]` (legacy single-value `reducesFee` is normalized to an array on read). At least one fee is required. * **(Updated) Applies To selector removed entirely** — not left as a single-option ("Requestors") dropdown. Codes are persisted as requestor-only. * Recommend deploying behind a feature flag covering the new Type and the new Category selector. The bug fixes and UX consolidations can ship unflagged once tested. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Walk through every Scenario above explicitly — each maps to one of the 7 improvements. * For the Value bug: create and save dozens of codes with varying $ and % values and reload each. The bug is intermittent today, so volume matters. * For auto-expire: set a test code to expire in 60 seconds, wait, and confirm redemption fails. Repeat with millisecond precision boundaries to be sure. * For the new Type: confirm both the Requestor checkout total and the Gopher payout against an order baseline that's been recorded before promo application. * For the Reduces merge: open existing codes from both old tabs and confirm they load correctly under the new single multi-select section; confirm Select All toggles all three fees, that a code can reduce more than one fee, and that the redemption discount equals the combined total of the selected fees. * For the Duration removal: open existing codes with Duration = once and confirm they have been migrated to the equivalent top-of-page state. * Run on both the production-like staging environment and confirm against a Stripe test mode — the new Type's subsidy ledger entry must be visible in the test ledger. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * The new "Add Money to Request" Type is the foundation for **Gopher Rewards**, which is a forthcoming feature. Once this Type exists, marketing can run subsidised campaigns; the larger Gopher Rewards configuration is out of scope here. * Depends on the existing Promo Code redemption pipeline being modifiable to support the platform-subsidised payout path. * Out of scope: backfill / migration of existing codes that have "Gophers" set in Applies To. They become inert; admin can manually remove them if desired. * Out of scope: any Requestor-facing UI changes (e.g., showing the promo savings on checkout). This ticket is admin-tool only — once a code is configured, the existing Requestor redemption UI is assumed to consume it correctly.

Summary: Both apps — Add Deleted tab to Inbox with swipe-left-to-delete, permanent-delete confirmation, 90-day auto-purge, and admin-expiration auto-move
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a User of either app (Gopher Request / Gopher Go) managing my in-app Inbox, ## 🎯 I want to delete messages with a swipe-left gesture and review removed messages in a dedicated Deleted tab before they are permanently gone, ## ✅ So that I can keep my Inbox tidy with a familiar texting-app gesture while still having a brief safety window to recover or permanently remove messages on my own terms. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * The in-app Inbox should feel like a standard mobile texting experience. Today there is no way for a user to delete messages from the Inbox. * This ticket introduces a **two-stage delete** pattern: 1. **Swipe left on a message in the Inbox** moves it to a new **Deleted** tab. 2. **Delete from the Deleted tab** is the **permanent** delete — confirmed by a pop-up so an inadvertent tap can be aborted. * The **"silence"** feature commonly seen on similar UIs is **not** part of this scope. * Admin-sent messages that have an expiration date attached **auto-move from Inbox to Deleted** at the expiration date/time. They then follow the same rules as any other message in the Deleted tab. * This work applies to **both apps** — Gopher Request and Gopher Go. --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior ### Inbox tab * A user can **swipe left** on any message in the Inbox to move it to the Deleted tab. * No silence affordance is added. ### Deleted tab * A new **Deleted** tab is added to the Inbox view. * Messages in the Deleted tab can only be **permanently deleted** — there is no "restore to Inbox" affordance in this release. * Attempting to delete a message from the Deleted tab triggers a confirmation pop-up so an inadvertent swipe/tap can be aborted. * Messages in the Deleted tab are **automatically purged after 90 days** measured from when they entered the Deleted tab. ### Admin expiration handling * When an admin sends a message with an expiration date, that message **auto-moves from Inbox to Deleted at the expiration date/time**. * Once in the Deleted tab, the admin message follows the same rules as any other deleted message — it can be manually permanently deleted by the user, and it auto-purges after 90 days. --- ## 💰 Confirmation Pop-up (default copy) * **Title:** Delete permanently? * **Body:** This cannot be undone. * **Buttons:** Cancel (secondary) / Delete (primary destructive) * Pull final copy from Figma if defined there — the above is a sensible default that gives the user the abort path you asked for. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — Swipe-left moves a message from Inbox to Deleted** * **Given** a user is viewing the Inbox tab, * **When** the user swipes left on a message, * **Then** the message is removed from the Inbox and appears in the Deleted tab. **Scenario 2 — No restore from Deleted to Inbox** * **Given** a message is in the Deleted tab, * **When** the user views the message in the Deleted tab, * **Then** there is no "restore to Inbox" option — the only actions are read and permanent delete. **Scenario 3 — Permanent delete from Deleted requires confirmation** * **Given** a user is viewing the Deleted tab, * **When** the user attempts to delete a message from that tab, * **Then** a confirmation pop-up appears with the copy above and the user must tap Delete to proceed (Cancel aborts and leaves the message in place). **Scenario 4 — 90-day auto-purge from Deleted** * **Given** a message has been in the Deleted tab for 90 days, * **When** the auto-purge runs, * **Then** the message is permanently removed from the Deleted tab without further user action. **Scenario 5 — Admin-sent message with expiration auto-moves to Deleted** * **Given** an admin sent a message with an expiration date/time and the message is currently in the user's Inbox, * **When** the expiration date/time is reached, * **Then** the message automatically moves from Inbox to Deleted. **Scenario 6 — Admin-expired messages follow the same Deleted-tab rules** * **Given** an admin-sent message has been auto-moved to the Deleted tab, * **When** the user views the Deleted tab, * **Then** the message can be manually permanently deleted (with confirmation) and otherwise auto-purges 90 days after it entered the Deleted tab. **Scenario 7 — Swipe-left silence affordance is NOT present** * **Given** the feature has shipped, * **When** a user swipes left on a message in the Inbox, * **Then** no "silence" option appears — only the delete action. **Scenario 8 — Both apps covered** * **Given** the fix has shipped, * **When** a user opens either Gopher Request or Gopher Go, * **Then** the Deleted tab, swipe-left-to-delete, confirmation pop-up, 90-day purge, and admin-expiration auto-move all behave the same in both apps. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * Deletion is **two-stage**: swipe-left moves Inbox → Deleted; explicit delete from the Deleted tab permanently removes. * The permanent-delete action **must** be confirmed by a pop-up so accidental taps can be aborted. * Messages in the Deleted tab **auto-purge after 90 days** regardless of how they got there (user swipe or admin expiration). * No "restore to Inbox" affordance is in scope for this release. * No "silence" affordance is in scope for this release. * Admin-sent messages with expiration dates auto-move from Inbox to Deleted at their expiration time. Once in Deleted, they follow the same rules as any other deleted message. * The Deleted tab is part of the Inbox view in **both** apps — Gopher Request and Gopher Go. --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * The 90-day auto-purge requires a background job (or a check-on-fetch in the Inbox API) that evaluates `deleted_at` timestamps and permanently removes records older than 90 days. Each Deleted-tab record must carry a `deleted_at` timestamp. * Admin-expiration auto-move likewise requires either a scheduled job or an on-fetch check evaluating the admin message's `expires_at` and moving it. * The two background processes can share the same job runner. * The Deleted tab should still allow the user to **open and read** a message before deciding to permanently delete it. * The Figma reference for visual design and pop-up styling is included in the description — follow that strictly for spacing, copy, and button order. --- ## 🎨 Design Reference * **Figma:** https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=107-15594 --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Swipe-left on an Inbox message and confirm it appears in the Deleted tab and is gone from Inbox. * Delete a message from the Deleted tab and confirm the pop-up appears; tap Cancel and confirm the message remains; tap Delete and confirm the message is gone. * Place a message in Deleted, fast-forward (or test-data manipulate) the `deleted_at` timestamp to 90+ days ago, and confirm the auto-purge removes it. * Send a test admin message with a near-future expiration date, confirm it sits in Inbox until expiration, then verify it auto-moves to Deleted. * From the Deleted tab, manually delete an admin message and confirm the same confirmation flow runs. * Confirm no "silence" affordance exists on swipe-left. * Test on both iOS and Android. * Test on both apps — Gopher Request and Gopher Go. * Re-attach the two screenshots directly to this ticket (the existing `blob:` URLs do not render for other users). --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * The admin-message expiration date model must exist on the admin side and be readable by the apps. If that field is not currently exposed, that work is part of this scope. * The 90-day auto-purge is permanent — there is no recovery once purged. This is consistent with the permanent-delete confirmation behavior and the no-restore design. * Consider deploying behind a feature flag so the auto-purge job can be toggled if the threshold needs adjustment in production.

Summary: Gopher App - Expired Request - Email Update (1st Time Promo Code & Promo Code Already Used)
Description: ## Goal When a Requestor's order **expires**, they receive the expired-request email carrying a **"ReDo" promo** — unless they've already used it: * Has **not** used ReDo → email **with** the promo code. * **Has** used ReDo → same email **without** the promo code. ## Decisions (John, 2026-07-03) * **Shape:** an **update to the existing transactional expired email** (a conditional block) — not a separate drip send. Stays transactional (`support@`, no unsubscribe), dispatcher **type 17**. * **ReDo mechanics:** **100% of Gopher fees waived → $0 fees on the next request, redeemable once per account.** * **Timing:** "not in play until we start the Drip Campaign" — build now, ship behind an activation flag. **▶ Full developer handoff:** `docs/handoff/G40-104-expired-redo-promo.md` · impl detail: `Documentation/SMS:Emails/impl-expired-redo-promo-G40-104.md` ## ✅ Done (front-end) — `SMS:Emails/gopher-email-expired.html` Conditional **ReDo promo card** authored directly above the "Relist your request" CTA, using the email's own design tokens (mint card, navy/green): eyebrow → **"Your next request is fee-free."** → "Relist with code **ReDo** and we'll waive every Gopher fee — you pay **$0 in fees**. One-time, our treat." → dashed **ReDo** chip. Commented with the render rule (shown only when the requestor hasn't redeemed ReDo; suppressed after). Verified in-browser; screenshot shared. Expired email shows the **ReDo** code when the requestor has not used it; **omits** it once redeemed (once per account). 2. ReDo applies **100% off the Gopher fee** ($0 fees) on the next request. 3. Delivered as the transactional expired email (type 17), not a new drip send. 4. Not active until the drip campaign begins (activation flag).

Summary: Both apps — App-store review pre-prompt for engaged users (Request: ≥5 completed + opens History; Go: ≥7 completed in 7 days)
Description: ## Goal Nudge engaged, happy users to leave a store review at a positive moment, using the **platform-native** review APIs (iOS `SKStoreReviewController`, Android Play In-App Review `ReviewManager`). A **branded pre-prompt gate** is shown first (“Rate us / Not now”); only on **Rate us** does the app call the native API — so we ask in our own voice and keep the native prompt for users who opt in. Applies to **both apps** (Request + Go). > **Eligibility rewritten (John, 2026-07-02) — replaces the old 3-in-a-row + all-5-star logic:** > > * **Gopher Request (Requestor):** eligible when a user with **≥ 5 completed requests** opens **Request History**; the pre-prompt shows there. > * **Gopher Go (Gopher):** eligible after **≥ 7 completed requests within a rolling 7-day window** — the real trigger fires **post-completion** when that threshold is crossed. > **▶ Full developer handoff:** `docs/handoff/G40-107-review-prompt.md` ## ✅ Done (front-end, verified in-browser) * **Request web** (`Final/gopher-request.html`): branded `#reviewPromptOverlay` gate wired to open when **Request History** (`showSection('previous')`) opens and the user has **≥5 completed** requests; once per session. Copy: “Enjoying Gopher? … a quick App Store rating helps your neighbors find us.” * **Gopher Go** (`Final/gopher-go.html`): branded `#goReviewOverlay` gate (dark theme) gated on a **≥7-completed-this-week** eligibility stub (dev replaces with the server’s rolling-7-day count); once per session. Copy: “Enjoy earning with Gopher Go? …” * Both: **Rate us** swaps to a thank-you panel marking the native-API call seam; **Not now** dismisses. Demo helper `__previewReviewPrompt()`. Verified: gate fires only when eligible, once-guard holds, correct per-app copy + live counts, **zero console errors**; screenshots captured. ## 🔧 To build (developer / backend + native) * **Native call** on Rate us: iOS `SKStoreReviewController.requestReview()` (scene-based on iOS 14+); Android Play In-App Review `ReviewManager`. OS renders its own prompt + enforces its own rate limit (iOS ≤ 3 / 365 days). **Do not track** the outcome — the APIs don’t expose it. * **Server eligibility:** Request → lifetime completed-count ≥ 5; Go → rolling-7-day completed-count ≥ 7, computed post-completion, exposed as a `should_prompt_review` flag (replaces the Go stub). * **Trigger wiring:** Request → on History open when eligible; Go → **after an order completes** when the 7-in-7 threshold is crossed (the prototype uses history-open only because a static page has no live completion event). * **Feature flag** around the whole feature for rollback. ## Acceptance criteria 1. **Request:** a Requestor with ≥ 5 completed requests opens Request History → the branded pre-prompt appears (once). On **Rate us** the app calls the native review API. 2. **Go:** a Gopher reaches ≥ 7 completed requests within 7 days → after that completion the branded pre-prompt appears. On **Rate us** the app calls the native review API. 3. **Native only:** no custom prompt bypasses the native APIs; the OS shows its own UI and enforces its own frequency limit. 4. **No tracking:** the app does not record whether the user left a review. 5. **Feature-flagged:** the whole feature can be toggled off. _Superseded: the previous 3-consecutive-completions + only-5-star-ratings-given eligibility and its acceptance scenarios are obsolete._

Summary: Gopher Request — Send automated 48-hour check-in email to Requestor when a scheduled request is still un-accepted
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher Request operations system, ## 🎯 I want to send an automated 48-hour check-in email to a Requestor whose scheduled request is still un-accepted, ## ✅ So that the Requestor knows we are still working on finding them a Gopher, and — if they no longer need the service — has a one-tap path to cancel the request rather than letting it sit live indefinitely. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * A request that reaches the 48-hour mark un-accepted is, in practice, always a **scheduled** request — on-demand requests resolve (or expire) on a much shorter timeline. * This email is a customer-care touchpoint: it reassures the Requestor that the platform is still actively trying to match them, and gives them a clear off-ramp if they have moved on (booked elsewhere, no longer need the service, etc.). * The cancel path in the email uses the **existing deep link** into the Gopher Request app for that specific request, so the user lands directly on the request's cancel flow. --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior * **Trigger:** 48 hours after request **submission**, evaluated continuously. * **Gate:** the email is sent **only if** the request is still active and un-accepted at the 48-hour mark. * If the request has been accepted, completed, or cancelled before 48 hours have elapsed, **no email is sent**. * **Recipient:** the Requestor's email address on file for the account that submitted the request. * **Channel:** email only (no SMS, no in-app notification as part of this ticket). * **One-time:** each request triggers at most one 48-hour check-in email — no repeats. * **Cancel link:** uses the existing Gopher Request app deep link that opens the specific request and routes the user to its cancel flow. --- ## 📧 Email Content (draft — confirm against existing email template style) * **From:** the standard Gopher Request system address (e.g., `admin@gophergo.io` or whatever the existing email-from is for system messages). * **To:** Requestor's email on file. * **Subject:** Still need a Gopher? We're on it. **Body (draft):** Hi \[First Name\], We're still working on matching you with a Gopher for your scheduled request. Sometimes scheduled requests take a little longer to find the right fit. If you still need help, no action is needed — we'll keep working on it. If your plans have changed and you no longer need a Gopher, you can cancel your request here: \[**Open request in app**\] → _deep-link to the specific request's cancel flow in the Gopher Request app_ Thanks for using Gopher. _— The Gopher Team_ --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — Email sent at 48 hours when request is still un-accepted** * **Given** a scheduled request was submitted exactly 48 hours ago and is still in an active, un-accepted state, * **When** the 48-hour check-in job runs, * **Then** the check-in email is sent to the Requestor's email on file. **Scenario 2 — No email if accepted before 48 hours** * **Given** a request was accepted by a Gopher before the 48-hour mark, * **When** the 48-hour check-in job evaluates that request, * **Then** no email is sent. **Scenario 3 — No email if cancelled before 48 hours** * **Given** a request was cancelled before the 48-hour mark (by the Requestor or by an admin), * **When** the 48-hour check-in job evaluates that request, * **Then** no email is sent. **Scenario 4 — No email if completed before 48 hours** * **Given** a request was completed before the 48-hour mark, * **When** the 48-hour check-in job evaluates that request, * **Then** no email is sent. **Scenario 5 — One email per request, ever** * **Given** a request has already received its 48-hour check-in email, * **When** the job runs again for that request, * **Then** no additional email is sent — the check-in is a one-time send per request. **Scenario 6 — Cancel link deep-links to the correct request** * **Given** the Requestor receives the check-in email, * **When** the Requestor taps the cancel link on a device with Gopher Request installed, * **Then** the app opens to the specific request's cancel flow, not the home screen and not a different request. **Scenario 7 — Email is sent from the standard system sender and lands in inbox** * **Given** the email is generated, * **When** it is dispatched, * **Then** it is sent from the standard Gopher Request system email address and successfully delivers to the Requestor's inbox (passes SPF/DKIM, not flagged as spam in routine testing). --- ## 📐 Business Rules * The 48-hour timer is anchored to **request submission**, not to the start of broadcasting (in case those can differ). * The check-in email is sent **at most once** per request, regardless of subsequent state changes. * The email only sends if the request is **active and un-accepted** at the moment of evaluation. * The cancel link in the email **must** use the existing Gopher Request app deep link for that specific request — do not introduce a new web cancel flow. * The email is **email-only** — no SMS or in-app duplication is in scope for this ticket. * This is **not** part of a multi-step nurture sequence — it is a single check-in. (The original ticket's "Step 1" phrasing was an error.) --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * The 48-hour check requires either a scheduled job (e.g., hourly cron evaluating requests submitted \~48 hours ago) or per-request scheduled task created at submission time. Either approach is acceptable; the per-request scheduled task is more precise but adds operational overhead. * A `48h_checkin_sent_at` (or similar) flag on the request record is needed to enforce the one-time send rule. * The deep link should follow the existing format the app already supports for opening a specific request — reuse, don't reinvent. * If the Requestor's email on file is missing or invalid, log the failure and move on. Do not block the request. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Submit a test request, fast-forward (or test-data manipulate) `submitted_at` to 48+ hours ago, run the check-in job, and confirm the email is sent. * Repeat the above for a request that was accepted, cancelled, or completed before 48 hours — confirm no email is sent in each case. * Run the check-in job twice against the same request and confirm only one email is sent. * Tap the cancel link in the delivered email and confirm the Gopher Request app opens to that specific request's cancel flow. * Test on both iOS and Android device email clients (Gmail, Apple Mail, Outlook) to confirm the deep link behaves correctly on each. * Confirm the email passes basic deliverability (SPF/DKIM, not flagged as spam on standard inboxes). --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * This ticket depends on the existing deep-link mechanism that opens the Gopher Request app to a specific request's cancel flow. If that deep link does not exist yet, that is in scope as a prerequisite. * The system sender address and basic transactional email infrastructure are assumed to exist already (used elsewhere in the platform).

Summary: Gopher Go - Scheduled Request - Allow A Gopher To Cancel A Scheduled Request Before It Has Started
Description: Currently only the Requestor can cancel a scheduled request. Gophers must also be able to cancel a scheduled request before it has started. The standard cancellation flow and logging must apply when a Gopher initiates the cancellation, and the Requestor must be notified so they can take appropriate action. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher who has accepted a scheduled request that has not yet started, ## 🎯 I want to be able to cancel the scheduled request before it begins, ## ✅ So that the Requestor is notified promptly and can find a replacement Gopher or take other action in time. ## 💡 Context / Background * Scheduled requests are accepted in advance and have a defined start time. * Currently the cancellation option on a scheduled request is only available to the Requestor — Gophers have no way to cancel. * Circumstances may arise where a Gopher can no longer fulfill a scheduled request (e.g. an emergency, scheduling conflict) and needs the ability to cancel before the request starts. * When a Gopher cancels, the standard cancellation flow must apply — the cancellation is logged against the Gopher, the Requestor is notified, and the Gopher’s cancellation record is updated. * This mirrors the existing Gopher auto-cancel flow (G40-9) but for scheduled requests specifically, before the request has started. ## ❌ Current Behavior * The cancel option on a scheduled request is only available to the Requestor * Gophers have no way to cancel a scheduled request they can no longer fulfill * If a Gopher cannot attend, there is no in-app mechanism to release the request back to the marketplace or alert the Requestor ## ✅ Expected Behavior * A Gopher can cancel a scheduled request at any time before it has started * The standard cancellation flow is triggered — the Gopher is prompted to select a cancellation reason * The cancellation reason is logged against the Gopher’s account * The Requestor is immediately notified that their Gopher has cancelled and is presented with recovery options (consistent with G40-9) * The scheduled request is returned to an available or cancelled state as appropriate ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Gopher can cancel a scheduled request before it starts * **Given** a Gopher has accepted a scheduled request that has not yet started * **When** the Gopher taps the cancel option * **Then** the standard cancellation flow is triggered and the Gopher is prompted to select a reason ### Scenario 2 – Cancellation reason is logged * **Given** the Gopher has selected a cancellation reason * **When** the cancellation is confirmed * **Then** the cancellation and reason are logged against the Gopher’s account * **And** the original order is closed ### Scenario 3 – Requestor is notified and presented with recovery options * **Given** the Gopher has cancelled the scheduled request * **When** the cancellation is processed * **Then** the Requestor receives a notification that their Gopher has cancelled * **And** the Requestor is presented with recovery options consistent with the Gopher cancellation flow in G40-9 ### Scenario 4 – Gopher cannot cancel after the request has started * **Given** a Gopher has updated a scheduled request to In Progress * **When** the Gopher attempts to cancel * **Then** the cancel option is not available — cancellation is only permitted before the request starts ## ⚙️ Business Rules * A Gopher may cancel a scheduled request only before it has been updated to In Progress. * The standard cancellation flow must apply — a cancellation reason is always required. * The cancellation must be logged against the Gopher’s account in the same way as any other Gopher-initiated cancellation. * The Requestor must be notified immediately and presented with recovery options. * The original order must be closed upon cancellation. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * The cancel option must be surfaced in the Gopher Go UI for accepted scheduled requests that have not yet started. * The cancellation reason selection screen and logging must follow the same pattern as the existing Gopher cancellation flow. * The Requestor notification and recovery modal must be consistent with G40-9 (Auto-Repost Workflow When Gopher Cancels an Active Request). * Confirm the cancellation window: Gopher can cancel only while the request status is Accepted and before In Progress. ## 🧪 QA Notes * Accept a scheduled request as a Gopher and cancel before it starts — confirm the cancellation reason screen appears and the cancellation completes. * Confirm the cancellation is logged against the Gopher’s account. * Confirm the Requestor receives a notification and recovery options. * Update a scheduled request to In Progress and attempt to cancel — confirm the cancel option is not available. * Confirm the original order is closed after cancellation. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Active Admin — Capture Yes/No "Suggested Offer Used" on Delivery and Ride orders and surface in the Orders report + order detail view
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher operations team analysing pricing behaviour, ## 🎯 I want the Orders report and order detail view in the Admin Panel to record whether each Delivery or Ride request used the Suggested Offer Assistance pricing flow, ## ✅ So that we can validate — with real data — whether the suggested-pricing feature is materially influencing Requestor pricing decisions and whether to invest further in it. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * When a Requestor submits a Delivery or Ride request, they are shown the **Suggested Offer Assistance** modal containing a Low → Fair → Generous slider with a system-suggested amount. * From that modal, the Requestor can either tap **SUBMIT** — which submits the request at whatever value the slider is currently on — or tap **BACK** to exit and enter their own price through a different flow. * Today we have no way to distinguish, in our data, which Requestors submitted _through_ the Suggested Offer Assistance modal versus those who entered pricing through another path. * Without that signal, we cannot answer the strategic question: is the pricing assistant actually influencing Requestor behaviour? --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior * For every **Delivery** and **Ride Sharing** request submitted after this feature ships, capture a `suggested_offer_used` flag on the order record: * **Yes** — the Requestor submitted the request by tapping **SUBMIT** on the Suggested Offer Assistance modal (regardless of where they had moved the slider within the Low–Generous range). * **No** — the Requestor submitted the request through any other path (e.g., backed out of the assistance modal and entered a price elsewhere, or never opened the assistance modal). * Surface this value in two places in the Admin Panel: * As a **new column** in the report generated from the **Orders** view (filterable / sortable / exportable). * As a **"Suggested Offer Used: Yes/No"** field on the **Order # detail view**. * The flag is captured **going forward only** — existing orders submitted before this ships remain `null` / blank and are not back-filled. * Request types other than Delivery and Ride Sharing are out of scope for this release — the field should be `null` / blank for those. --- ## 📊 Data Model (sketch) * **Field name:** `suggested_offer_used` (or your existing naming convention equivalent). * **Allowed values:** `true`, `false`, `null`. * **Set to** `true` when: the request was submitted via the Suggested Offer Assistance modal's SUBMIT button. * **Set to** `false` when: a Delivery or Ride request was submitted through any other path. * **Set to** `null` when: the request is not a Delivery or Ride request, OR the order existed before this feature shipped (no backfill). * **Immutable:** value is written once at submission and never changes thereafter. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — Submit via Suggested Offer Assistance = Yes** * **Given** a Requestor is creating a Delivery or Ride request, * **When** they tap **SUBMIT** on the Suggested Offer Assistance modal (whether or not they moved the slider), * **Then** the order record's `suggested_offer_used` value is `true` and displays as **Yes** in the Admin Panel. **Scenario 2 — Back out of the modal then submit elsewhere = No** * **Given** a Requestor opens the Suggested Offer Assistance modal, * **When** they tap **BACK** and then submit the request through a different pricing path, * **Then** the order record's `suggested_offer_used` value is `false` and displays as **No** in the Admin Panel. **Scenario 3 — Never open the modal = No** * **Given** a Requestor creates a Delivery or Ride request and never opens the Suggested Offer Assistance modal, * **When** they submit the request, * **Then** the order record's `suggested_offer_used` value is `false` and displays as **No** in the Admin Panel. **Scenario 4 — Non-applicable request types are null** * **Given** a Requestor submits a request that is not Delivery or Ride Sharing, * **When** the order record is created, * **Then** `suggested_offer_used` is `null` / blank — the column displays empty for that row. **Scenario 5 — Historic orders are not backfilled** * **Given** the feature has shipped, * **When** an admin opens the Orders report or any order detail view for an order submitted before the feature shipped, * **Then** `suggested_offer_used` is `null` / blank for that order — no value has been inferred or backfilled. **Scenario 6 — Admin Panel column visibility and filter** * **Given** the feature has shipped, * **When** an admin generates the Orders report, * **Then** a new column named **Suggested Offer Used** is present and the report can be filtered, sorted, and exported on that column. **Scenario 7 — Admin Panel order detail visibility** * **Given** the feature has shipped, * **When** an admin opens any individual order's detail view, * **Then** a **Suggested Offer Used: Yes/No** field is visible (or blank for non-applicable orders). **Scenario 8 — Value is immutable after submission** * **Given** an order has been submitted with a `suggested_offer_used` value, * **When** any subsequent change is made to the order (status changes, completion, cancellation, etc.), * **Then** the `suggested_offer_used` value remains unchanged from what was set at submission. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * `suggested_offer_used = true` **only** when the request was submitted via the Suggested Offer Assistance modal's SUBMIT button. Slider position at submission is irrelevant — anywhere within Low–Generous still counts as Yes. * The flag applies **only** to Delivery and Ride Sharing requests in this release. All other request types: `null`. * **No backfill.** Orders submitted before this feature ships remain `null` and are never inferred. * The flag is set **once, at submission**, and is immutable thereafter. * The flag must be visible in **both** the Orders report (as a filterable column) **and** the order detail view (as a Yes/No field). --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * The submission path that triggers `true` is specifically the SUBMIT button on the Suggested Offer Assistance modal — that is the only signal needed; do not also try to detect slider movement, time on screen, etc. * Capture should happen server-side at the request submission API, not client-side only — the API call needs to receive an explicit indicator of which submission path was used. * If future request types are added to the suggested-pricing flow, the same field should be reused rather than introducing a parallel field per request type. * Recommend exposing this in any existing analytics or BI export pipeline that already pulls from the Orders table, so downstream reporting picks it up automatically. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Submit a Delivery request via the SUBMIT button on the Suggested Offer Assistance modal — confirm `suggested_offer_used = Yes` in both the Orders report column and the order detail view. * Submit a Delivery request after tapping BACK out of the modal — confirm `suggested_offer_used = No`. * Submit a Delivery request without ever opening the modal — confirm `suggested_offer_used = No`. * Repeat all three above for Ride Sharing. * Submit a non-Delivery, non-Ride request — confirm `suggested_offer_used` is blank in both views. * View an order created before this feature shipped — confirm the field is blank (no backfill). * Generate the Orders report and confirm the new column is present, filterable, sortable, and included in any export. * Take an order with `Yes` set and run it through status transitions (accepted, completed, cancelled) — confirm the value remains `Yes` throughout. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * This ticket depends on the existing Suggested Offer Assistance modal being live for Delivery and Ride Sharing. Reference screenshot of the modal is attached to this ticket. * The Orders report and order detail view in the Admin Panel are assumed to exist already — this ticket adds one column and one field, not a new view. * This is purely a capture-and-display ticket; no behavioural change to pricing or to the Requestor's experience is in scope.

Summary: AI - Machine Learning Enhancement to Suggested Pricing
Description: ## Goal Enhance the **suggested-pricing** algorithm (currently a static function of COGS only) to factor in demand/context signals. **Add:** Day of week · Time of day · Google-recognized holidays · for **"Gopher can purchase from anywhere"** requests, distance from pickup to drop-off. **Nature:** backend/pricing — **developer-only** (pricing logic fenced from AI edits). This ticket is groomed to a zero-discovery spec. **▶ Full spec:** `docs/handoff/G40-122-smart-pricing-ml-enhancement.md` ## Current algorithm (the seam) `controllers/order/create.js` → `get_smart_price` (\~lines 156-186). Takes only `service_cost` (sc): ``` base = 10.0; multiplier tiered by sc (0.10–0.20 for sc≥25; 0 below) suggested_offer = base + multiplier * sc ``` Only input is COGS. _(Incidental:_ `sc===50` falls through to multiplier 0 — use `>=50`; `sc<25` returns flat $10.) ## Near-term deterministic design (ship before the model) ``` core = base + multiplier(sc) * sc demandFactor = dowFactor * todFactor * holidayFactor // config lookup tables distanceComp = isShopAnywhere ? perMileRate * miles(pickup,dropoff) : 0 suggested_offer = round(core * demandFactor + distanceComp) ``` * **dow/tod** — tuned lookup tables (weekend/evening higher). * **holiday** — Google Calendar "US Holidays" (or holidays lib), cached yearly. * **distance** — Google Maps Distance Matrix (Maps already integrated, RFP Annex §3), pickup→dropoff, shop-anywhere type only. * **New inputs to** `get_smart_price`: `requested_at` (→ dow/tod), request type/category (→ isShopAnywhere), pickup+dropoff coords (→ miles). Today it only receives `service_cost`. ## ML path (AI-Inclusion epic G40-3) Log each suggestion (features) with the realized **accepted offer** + time-to-accept (sources: `orders`, `orders_cogs.original_offer/original_cost`; or a new `pricing_suggestions` log). Train sc/dow/tod/holiday/distance/geo/category → accepted-offer; serve behind the same endpoint. ## Acceptance criteria 1. Suggestion factors day-of-week, time-of-day, and US holidays (not just COGS). 2. "Purchase-from-anywhere" requests add a pickup→dropoff distance component. 3. Logic centralized in `get_smart_price`; client contract unchanged. 4. Suggestions + accepted offers logged for later model training.

Summary: Gopher Go - Account - Payout Account - Allowing Gopher To Accept Request With Invalid Payout
Description: ## **Summary** When a Gopher sets up a Stripe **payout** account, a debit card must be added to become “Stripe Verified.” If that card is **invalid/expired/unsupported** and the Gopher removes it, our system currently **deletes the Stripe account and creates a new one**, breaking scheduled transfers and forcing manual payouts. We must: 1. **Disallow removing a failing card** until a **new, valid card** is added, 2. **Pre-validate** card eligibility where possible, 3. **Keep payout status disabled** until a supported card is on file, 4. Surface a **clear UI alert/badge** guiding the Gopher to add a valid card. --- ## **Problem Details** * Current behavior allows a failing/unsupported debit card to be **removed** with no replacement. * This triggers unintended **Stripe connected account deletion/recreation**, which breaks **scheduled transfers** and requires **manual payouts** by Gopher Admin. * Gophers often add **unsupported cards** (e.g., **Cash App** / **DoorDash** cards) without being warned; they discover the issue only after **missing payouts** and contacting support. **Reported Example** * **User ID:** 73076 * **Order #:** 29682 * **Stripe Account ID:** `acct_1PrWp1FqyBu64OeY` **Reference (Stripe docs):** * Instant payouts & supported banks: <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://docs.stripe.com/payouts/instant-payouts-banks</custom> --- ## **Goals / Requirements** ### A. Card Validation & Payout State * ✅ **Pre-validation:** On card entry, attempt to determine if the card is eligible for payouts (brand/funding type, supported networks, BIN checks where Stripe exposes signals). * ✅ **If unsupported/invalid/expired:** * **Block activation** of payouts. * Keep **Payout Status = Disabled**. * Explain why and what card types are accepted. * ✅ **Do not allow the worker to take requests** while payout status is disabled. ### B. Prevent Card Removal Without Replacement * ✅ If the **only payout card** on file is failing/unsupported, **disallow “Remove Card”** until a **new valid card** is successfully added. * ✅ Replace “Remove” with a disabled state + tooltip/explainer: “Add a new eligible card to remove this one.” ### C. UI/UX Alerts * ✅ On **Account → Payout Account**, show **red badge**: * **“A new card must be added to receive payout.”** * ✅ If a card is unsupported, show inline error & guidance (e.g., “Prepaid wallets such as Cash App or DoorDash cards are not supported for payouts.”). * ✅ Keep the worker in a clear **Blocked** state for payouts until a valid card is added (with a learn-more link). ### D. Stripe Account Integrity * ✅ **Never delete/recreate** the connected Stripe account due to card removal. * ✅ Guardrails to **prevent account churn** on external account changes (listen for `external_account.deleted` and **block** backend flows that recreate connected accounts). ### E. Ops & Support (out of scope, need to create a ticket for this) * ✅ Log and surface in Admin: * Card eligibility failures, removal attempts blocked, payout status changes. * ✅ Bulk job to **flag existing Gophers** with unsupported cards; send notifications to update card. --- ## **Acceptance Criteria** 1. **Card Entry Guardrails** * Entering an unsupported or invalid card → **payout status remains Disabled**; user sees **explicit reason** and examples of accepted cards; **cannot start/accept requests** until fixed. 2. **Removal Lock** * If the only payout card is invalid/unsupported, “Remove” is **disabled** until a **new valid card** is added. * Attempting removal shows an **inline message** explaining the requirement. 3. **Red Badge & Messaging** * On **Account → Payout Account**, show **red badge**: “**A new card must be added to receive payout**” whenever payout status is Disabled due to card issues. 4. **No Account Recreation** * Removing/replacing cards **never** deletes and recreates the Stripe connected account. * Scheduled transfers remain intact; **no manual payouts** required due to this scenario. 5. **Unsupported Wallets** * Adding known unsupported wallet cards (e.g., **Cash App, DoorDash** cards) fails validation with **clear guidance**. 6. **Auditability** * Admin sees timeline events for: card added/failed/unsupported, removal attempts blocked, payout state transitions. --- ## **Technical Notes / Research Tasks** ### Stripe API Research (Engineering Spike) * Can we reliably **pre-check eligibility** for instant payouts to debit cards at entry time (brand/funding/BIN metadata)? * Confirm signals available on the attached **external account** (e.g., `card[funding]`, brand, network) and whether Stripe exposes **instant payout eligibility** flags pre-payout. * Determine recommended Stripe approach to **block unsupported cards** vs. allowing attach then holding payouts (`payouts_enabled`, **requirements**, or custom eligibility rules). * Define webhook listeners to maintain integrity: * `account.updated`, `external_account.created`, `external_account.deleted`, `payout.created`, `payout.failed`. ### Backend / Data * Add **payout status machine** (Enabled/Disabled/Needs-Card) with reasons. * Enforce **marketplace work gating** based on payout status. * Prevent any code path that **deletes/recreates** Stripe connected accounts on card changes. ### Mobile / Frontend * Payout screen: red badge, inline errors, disable “Remove” until new valid card is added, learn-more modal. * Block accepting/starting requests when payout disabled; show actionable message. ### Migrations / Cleanup * Report & notification to all Gophers currently with **unsupported/invalid/expired** cards; drive them to update. * Validate scheduled transfers are unaffected by card replacement flow. --- ## **Out of Scope (for this ticket)** * Changing payout **methods** beyond supported debit cards (e.g., bank accounts) unless later approved. * Retroactive payment reconciliation process (handled by Ops playbook). --- ## **QA Scenarios** * Add **Cash App/DoorDash** type card → validation blocks, payout stays Disabled, alerts shown. * Add **expired** or **invalid** card → blocked with clear message. * Try to **remove** failing card with no replacement → removal **disabled**; message instructs to add a new card. * Add **valid debit card** → payout status flips to Enabled, badge cleared, worker can accept requests. * Replace card without any account deletion; **scheduled transfers continue**. * Webhooks fire; Admin timeline shows correct events.

Summary: Gopher Request - More - Blocked Gophers - Allow Requestor To Block A Gopher From A Cancelled Request
Description: Currently, Requestors can only block a Gopher from within a completed request. If a Gopher cancels or a request is otherwise cancelled, the Requestor has no way to block that Gopher from future requests. The block option must be extended to cancelled requests so Requestors always have the ability to prevent an unwanted Gopher from being matched with them again. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Requestor whose request was cancelled by or with a Gopher, ## 🎯 I want to be able to block that Gopher directly from the cancelled request, ## ✅ So that I can prevent them from being matched with me on future requests, regardless of whether the request was completed or cancelled. ## 💡 Context / Background * The Blocked Gophers feature allows Requestors to prevent specific Gophers from appearing on or accepting their future requests. * Currently, the block option is only surfaced on completed requests — there is no way to block a Gopher from a cancelled request. * A Requestor may have a legitimate reason to block a Gopher after a cancellation — for example, if the Gopher cancelled at the last minute, behaved inappropriately in messaging, or if the Requestor simply does not want to work with that Gopher again. * The block action, underlying logic, and the Blocked Gophers list behavior remain unchanged — this ticket only extends the availability of the block option to cancelled request states. ## ❌ Current Behavior * The block Gopher option is only available on completed requests * If a request is cancelled, the Requestor has no in-app path to block the associated Gopher ## ✅ Expected Behavior * The block Gopher option is available on both completed and cancelled requests * When a Requestor blocks a Gopher from a cancelled request, the standard block flow applies and the Gopher is added to the Requestor’s Blocked Gophers list * The blocked Gopher will no longer appear on or be able to accept the Requestor’s future requests ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Block option is available on a cancelled request * **Given** a Requestor views a cancelled request that had a Gopher assigned * **When** the Requestor navigates to the request options * **Then** the block Gopher option is visible and accessible ### Scenario 2 – Blocking a Gopher from a cancelled request adds them to the Blocked Gophers list * **Given** a Requestor taps the block option on a cancelled request * **When** the block is confirmed * **Then** the Gopher is added to the Requestor’s Blocked Gophers list * **And** the blocked Gopher no longer appears on or can accept the Requestor’s future requests ### Scenario 3 – Block option is not shown when no Gopher was assigned * **Given** a Requestor views a cancelled request where no Gopher was ever assigned * **When** the Requestor navigates to the request options * **Then** the block Gopher option is not shown ### Scenario 4 – Existing block behavior on completed requests is unaffected * **Given** a Requestor views a completed request * **When** the Requestor uses the block option * **Then** the existing block behavior is unchanged ## ⚙️ Business Rules * The block option must appear on cancelled requests only when a Gopher was assigned to that request. * If no Gopher was assigned before cancellation, the block option must not be shown. * Blocking a Gopher from a cancelled request follows the same standard block flow as blocking from a completed request. * The Blocked Gophers list and its downstream effects (preventing the Gopher from appearing on or accepting the Requestor’s requests) are unchanged. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * The block option UI condition must be updated to check for request status — show on both completed and cancelled requests where a Gopher was assigned. * No changes to the underlying block logic, Blocked Gophers list, or matching exclusion logic are required. * Figma design reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=94-9921 ## 🧪 QA Notes * View a cancelled request where a Gopher was assigned — confirm the block option is visible. * Block a Gopher from a cancelled request — confirm they are added to the Blocked Gophers list. * Confirm the blocked Gopher no longer appears on or can accept the Requestor’s future requests. * View a cancelled request where no Gopher was assigned — confirm the block option is not shown. * Confirm the existing block behavior on completed requests is unchanged. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher App - Submitted Request - Editing A Live Request - Original Information Lost
Description: ## **Summary** When a **pending (submitted but not yet accepted)** request is edited, critical data is being lost or overwritten—specifically attached photos, scheduled dates, and addresses. Request details should **never change** unless the user explicitly edits that field. --- ## **Description** Editing a request currently triggers unwanted resets to existing data. This causes requests to expire incorrectly, lose context for Gophers already interested, and results in a bad customer experience. ### **Issues Identified:** #### ✅ **1. Attached photos are lost when editing a request** * If the user previously uploaded a picture, editing the request removes it * Customer must re-upload * Gophers lose context for the job #### ✅ **2. Scheduled date/time is overwritten** * When a scheduled request is edited (even for small text changes), the system changes the scheduled date * New date defaults to roughly **one hour after the time of editing** * This breaks scheduled requests, especially when they were originally days in the future * Causes requests to unintentionally **expire** * Gophers who were interested lose their submissions #### ✅ **3. Address fields sometimes reset** * Pickup or delivery addresses must be re-entered * Fails to preserve original data --- ## **Expected Behavior** When a **Pending Request** is edited: ✅ No information should change unless the user manually updates that specific field ✅ Photo attachments remain intact ✅ Scheduled date and time do not change unless user edits them ✅ Address fields persist ✅ No automatic overwriting of ANY request data ✅ System must maintain continuity so Gophers retain context and interest --- ## **Acceptance Criteria** ### **AC1 — Preserve Photos** * Editing a pending request must retain all previously attached photos * Photos only change if the user manually removes or replaces them ### **AC2 — Preserve Scheduled Date** * Editing other fields must NOT modify scheduled date/time * Scheduled date only updates if user manually selects a new date/time * Request must never auto-shift to “1 hour later” or any default time ### **AC3 — Preserve All Interactable Input within the Request** * All interactable elements within the request must remain unchanged * All interactable fields should only update when user edits those fields directly ### **AC4 — No Data Loss** * All existing fields remain intact unless touched by the user * No auto-clearing, no resetting, no defaulting ### **AC5 — No Auto-Expiration or Workflow Disruption** * Editing a pending scheduled request must NOT cause early expiration * Request should remain active with Gopher interest preserved ### **AC6 — QA Testing Must Confirm** * Multiple edit cycles retain data * Scheduled requests days in the future remain accurately scheduled after edits * No regression with Need ASAP requests * Photos persist on both iOS and Android --- ## **Technical Notes** * Review edit-request API to ensure full payload is sent and updated correctly * Validate that frontend is not unintentionally overwriting fields with null or default values * Confirm that scheduled date/time field is not being auto-updated with “now + 1h” * Ensure address persistence logic survives screen re-mounts or form rehydration * Consider disabling auto-save on field blur if it overwrites untouched fields

Summary: Gopher Go - Platform Stability Issue
Description: > 🔧 **DEV-READY HANDOFF — groomed 2026-07-02 (John Newbury).** No prototype build (native-lifecycle behavior); the core logic is already scaffolded + tested. No open questions. Full handoff: `docs/handoff/G40-139-available-tab-instant-refresh.md`. ## 🎯 The real issue (title is vague) The **Available tab is slow to show new requests** after a push. The feed must refresh **instantly (\~1–2s)** when (a) the app opens via a push notification, (b) it returns to the foreground, or (c) a new-request payload arrives while open — **no** manual pull-to-refresh, **no** full reload/flash, and **no** scroll-position loss. ## 🧩 Core logic already scaffolded + tested (owner) `G40-Build-Recap.md` → `wave2/g40-139/refreshDecider.js` (+ `useAvailableRefresh.jsx`): _refresh on push-foreground / app-foreground / in-app payload, debounced; hook wires Capacitor lifecycle; preserve scroll._ **Wire the FE to this; don't re-derive.** ## 📱 Developer work (native/FE runtime) 1. Mount `useAvailableRefresh` on the Available tab; drive `refreshDecider` on: **app-foreground-via-push** (iOS AppDelegate/SceneDelegate; Android `onResume`/foreground handler; Capacitor `App` resume + push `pushNotificationReceived`/`ActionPerformed`), **app-foreground-from-background**, and **in-app new-request payload** (foreground push, or a live socket event — confirm the channel is active + triggers the UI update). 2. **Debounce** overlapping triggers to one fetch; do an **incremental** update (no full reload) — preserve scroll, no flash. 3. Replace any polling-interval / tab-focus-only fetch causing the delay. ## 🖼️ Prototype No build — the static prototype has no push/lifecycle/backend. Visual reference only: the **“Available jobs”** frame in `_prototypes/Go/gopher-go-prototype.html`. ## ✅ Acceptance (from ticket) Open-via-push → request already visible (no manual refresh); app-open → real-time populate on notification; foreground-no-notification → immediate refetch; visible within **1–2s**; **no UI disruption or scroll loss**; iOS + Android. --- ## 📜 Original ticket (retained) When a Gopher receives a push for a new available request, the Available tab takes significant time to refresh and show it — in a time-sensitive marketplace, Gophers miss requests. The tab must update immediately on push-open, foreground, or in-app new-request notification. Likely caused by a polling interval / full reload rather than a foreground/notification-triggered fetch. (Full ACs, repro, and QA notes preserved in the handoff doc.)
