Summary: Both apps — Block sign-ups that match an admin-deactivated account on 2+ of Name/DOB/Address and route to support
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher trust & safety system protecting the platform from deactivated users returning under new credentials, ## 🎯 I want to block new sign-ups whose identity matches a previously admin-deactivated user on at least 2 of 3 identity fields (Name, DOB, Address), ## ✅ So that previously banned users cannot evade the ban simply by using a new Google Voice phone number and a fresh email address. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * The existing duplicate-prevention logic already blocks sign-ups that reuse a known phone number or email — those mechanisms are out of scope for this ticket and continue to operate as today. * The **evasion pattern this ticket targets**: deactivated users obtain a fresh Google Voice phone number and a new email, then attempt to re-create an account. Phone/email checks miss this because both values are new — but the underlying identity (real name, date of birth, address) is the same. * This ticket adds an **identity-matching layer** on top of the existing duplicate-prevention logic: at sign-up, compare the new applicant's Name, DOB, and Address against the pool of admin-deactivated accounts. If at least 2 of the 3 fields match a single deactivated account, hard-block the sign-up and route the user to support. --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior * At sign-up submission on **either app** (Gopher / Gopher Go), the system evaluates the applicant's Name, DOB, and Address against the pool of accounts that an admin has deactivated. * **Match threshold:** at least **2 of 3** fields must match against the **same** deactivated account (not 2 different fields across 2 different deactivated accounts). * If the threshold is met: * The sign-up is **hard-blocked at submission** — the new account is not created. * The applicant is shown a message directing them to **contact support@gophergo.io**. * The match event is **logged in the Admin Panel** for support visibility and audit. * Only an **admin manually overriding** the block can allow the applicant to proceed. * If the threshold is not met, sign-up continues normally through existing flows. * Phone number and email are **not** part of this match logic — they continue to be evaluated by the existing duplicate-prevention mechanisms. --- ## 🔍 Matching Rules | Field | Match precision | | --- | --- | | **Name** | **Exact** case-insensitive match on first name + last name. No fuzzy / typo tolerance. | | **DOB** | **Exact** match on YYYY-MM-DD. | | **Address** | **Full address including unit number** — normalised street, unit, city, state, zip. _Note: this is a defaulted decision — see Open Questions below._ | | **Matching pool** | Only accounts deactivated by an admin (admin-initiated bans for cause). Self-deleted accounts and inactive auto-deactivations are **not** in the pool. | | **Threshold** | At least **2 of 3** fields match against the **same** deactivated account. | | **Persistence** | The match rule applies **forever** — there is no time-based expiry. The block can only be lifted by an admin. | --- ## 💬 User-Facing Experience (draft — confirm copy) When the threshold is met at sign-up submission, display a blocking message: * **Title:** Account Cannot Be Created * **Body:** We're unable to create your account at this time. Please contact our support team at **support@gophergo.io** for assistance. * **Primary action:** Tap-to-email link that opens the user's mail client with `support@gophergo.io` pre-filled in the To field. The user must **not** be told _why_ they were blocked or which fields matched. Disclosure here would teach evaders exactly how to bypass the check. --- ## 🛡️ Admin Visibility & Audit * Every match-and-block event must be recorded in an admin-visible log with the following fields: * Timestamp of the sign-up attempt. * Applicant's submitted Name, DOB, Address, email, and phone number. * The matched **deactivated account ID** and the **specific fields that matched** (e.g., Name + DOB). * The applicant's IP address and device identifier where available. * The log must be queryable so support can quickly locate the relevant record when an applicant emails in. * Admins must have the ability to **manually allow** a previously blocked applicant to proceed — either by clearing the block on the matched deactivated account, or by approving the specific applicant. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — Two of three fields match → hard block** * **Given** an applicant submits sign-up details whose Name, DOB, and Address fields produce a 2-of-3 match against a single admin-deactivated account, * **When** the sign-up is submitted, * **Then** the account is not created, the applicant sees the blocking message, and a match event is logged in the Admin Panel. **Scenario 2 — All three fields match → hard block** * **Given** an applicant matches a deactivated account on all three of Name, DOB, and Address, * **When** the sign-up is submitted, * **Then** the same hard-block behaviour applies as Scenario 1. **Scenario 3 — Only one field matches → sign-up proceeds** * **Given** an applicant matches a deactivated account on only one field (e.g., shared household address but different name and DOB), * **When** the sign-up is submitted, * **Then** the sign-up proceeds normally through existing flows. **Scenario 4 — Matches split across two different deactivated accounts → sign-up proceeds** * **Given** an applicant matches deactivated account A on Name and deactivated account B on Address (1 of 3 against each, not 2 of 3 against any single account), * **When** the sign-up is submitted, * **Then** the sign-up proceeds normally — the 2-of-3 threshold must be met against the **same** deactivated account. **Scenario 5 — Self-deleted accounts do not participate in the match pool** * **Given** a user who self-deleted their account previously attempts to re-create an account with the same identity, * **When** the sign-up is submitted, * **Then** the sign-up proceeds normally — self-deletions are not in the matching pool. **Scenario 6 — Applicant is not told why they were blocked** * **Given** the blocking message is shown to the applicant, * **When** the applicant reads the message, * **Then** the message does not name which deactivated account, which fields matched, or any other detail that would teach evasion. **Scenario 7 — Admin can manually override** * **Given** an applicant has been blocked by this rule and contacted support, * **When** an admin investigates and decides to allow the applicant, * **Then** the admin can clear the block and the applicant can complete sign-up. **Scenario 8 — Audit log is created on every block** * **Given** any sign-up is blocked by this rule, * **When** the block fires, * **Then** the Admin Panel records a match event including timestamp, applicant identifiers, matched deactivated account ID, and which fields matched. **Scenario 9 — Both apps covered** * **Given** the feature has shipped, * **When** an applicant attempts sign-up on either Gopher or Gopher Go, * **Then** the same matching, blocking, and logging behaviour applies. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * The matching pool consists **only** of accounts that an admin has deactivated for cause. Self-deletions and inactivity-based deactivations are excluded. * The threshold is **2 of 3 fields against the same deactivated account.** Matches that span multiple deactivated accounts do not aggregate toward the threshold. * **Name** must match exactly (case-insensitive) on first + last. No fuzzy or typo-tolerant matching. * **DOB** must match exactly. * **Address** matching defaults to full address including unit number (see Open Questions). * Phone number and email are **not** part of this rule. The existing duplicate-prevention logic for those fields continues to operate independently. * The block is **hard** — only an admin can lift it. There is no automatic appeal or time-based unlock. * The blocking message must not disclose the reason or matched fields to the applicant. * The audit log must capture every match event for support and compliance. * This rule applies to **both** apps (Gopher and Gopher Go). --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * Matching should run **server-side** at the sign-up submission API, never client-side. A client-side check would be trivially bypassable. * Address normalisation is critical — "123 Main St Apt 4" and "123 Main Street, #4" should match. Use a standard address-normalisation library or service before comparison; do not rely on raw string equality. * Name normalisation should strip leading/trailing whitespace and lowercase before comparison. * The matching query should be indexed on the deactivated-account pool to keep sign-up latency acceptable. * Consider whether a banned user creating an account that matches but does NOT trigger the 2-of-3 threshold (e.g., changes their DOB by one year) should also create a lower-severity audit event for support pattern-recognition. Out of scope for this ticket but worth flagging. * Recommend deploying behind a feature flag so the block can be toggled off quickly if false-positive rates exceed support capacity. --- ## ⚠️ Open Question Still to Resolve * **Apartment unit handling.** The current default is to match on the full address **including unit number**. The trade-off: * **Including unit (current default):** fewer false positives in apartment buildings and shared housing, but easier to evade by changing the unit number. * **Excluding unit (street + city + zip only):** harder to evade, but creates false positives for unrelated residents at the same building / complex. Please confirm or override. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Create a test admin-deactivated account with known Name, DOB, and Address. * Attempt sign-up with all three matching — expect hard block + audit log + support message. * Attempt sign-up with two of three matching — expect hard block. * Attempt sign-up with one of three matching — expect normal sign-up to proceed. * Attempt sign-up where matches split across two different deactivated accounts — expect normal sign-up to proceed. * Create a self-deleted account with matching identity and attempt sign-up — expect normal sign-up to proceed. * Verify the blocking message does not reveal any matched fields or account identifiers. * Verify the audit log captures all required fields after each block. * Have an admin lift a block and verify the applicant can complete sign-up. * Test on both apps (Gopher and Gopher Go) and on both iOS and Android. * Test with address variations (different formatting, extra whitespace, mixed casing) to confirm normalisation works. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Depends on the existing admin deactivation flow producing a queryable record of deactivated accounts with the relevant identity fields. If those fields are not currently captured on deactivation, that work is in scope as a prerequisite. * Depends on an address-normalisation capability — if one does not exist in the codebase, picking and integrating one is in scope. * This rule sits alongside, not on top of, the existing phone and email duplicate-prevention logic. All three checks should run at sign-up; failing any one blocks the sign-up. * Consider a follow-up ticket to expose the audit log as a dashboard or report so support can review patterns over time.

Summary: BUG - Gopher App - Delivery Request - Gopher App - Delivery Request - Pricing Issue
Description: > ⛔ **CANCELED 2026-07-02 — the go-forward flow fully solves this (owner-confirmed).** The **$0-offer guard** (core bug + the absorbed G40-278) is already enforced in the new build's `stepGate()` — Payment to Gopher must be > $0 (Step 5) and Cost of Items must be > $0 when "purchase needed" is on (Step 2). The **Market-Suggested/Make-Your-Own** two-button screen is superseded by **Gopher iQ "Second Set of Eyes"** + the low-offer nudge, and the `pricing_selection_method` analytics is dropped with it. Full code trace in the comment. Nothing left to build. --- The delivery request pricing flow is not functioning as originally designed. Two compounding issues existed: (1) a Requestor could submit a request with $0 entered for both Cost of Items and Payment to Gopher (now guarded in the new flow), and (2) the pricing flow — the Market Suggested Offer vs. Make Your Own Offer choice and the Purchase Needed toggle — has been reworked into the Gopher iQ model in the new build. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Requestor creating a delivery request, ## 🎯 I want the pricing flow to correctly guide me and prevent $0 submissions. ## 🔍 Resolution (why canceled) * **$0 guard** — implemented in `gopher-request.html` `stepGate()`: Step 5 requires `payAmount > 0` (set mode); Step 2 requires `costOfItems > 0` when `itemsPurchased`. Continue/Review stays disabled otherwise, with a field pulse + toast. * **Purchase Needed toggle** — present; controls Cost of Items visibility/requirement. * **Market Suggested vs Make Your Own Offer** — replaced by Gopher iQ "Second Set of Eyes" suggested offer (`__openOfferSuggest`) + the low-offer notice (persuasive nudge below the iQ low-end). * `pricing_selection_method` analytics — dropped (tied to the removed two-button choice). ## 🧠 Notes * Duplicated by G40-278 ("$0 offer to worker"), which is already Canceled. * Original QA history: returned 2025-12-17 (pay/suggested-offer sync), approved 2025-12-22 in the old app. The go-forward Request flow supersedes that implementation.

Summary: Gopher Go - Request Broadcast - Twilio - SMS/Email Backup Update
Description: ### **As a** Gopher Go system broadcasting requests to available Gophers, ### **I want** backup SMS and email notifications to be **sent only when truly necessary and to the most relevant Gophers**, ### **So that** requests are fulfilled efficiently while significantly reducing unnecessary Twilio costs and notification spam. ‌ ## **💡 Context / Background** ‌ The current **Request Broadcast backup logic** (SMS + Email via Twilio) appears to be overly aggressive and inefficient: * Notifications may be using: * The Gopher’s **profile address**, and/or * The **current physical location** of the Gopher * Backup notifications are being sent **even when a request has already been accepted** * Extremely high SMS/email volumes are being sent (example: **144 emails**) for a single request * Twilio costs are increasing due to poor targeting and lack of caps ‌ ### **🔴 Real Example (Order #50376)** ‌ Despite the request being **accepted within minutes**, backup notifications were still triggered: ‌ **Order timeline:** | Date & Time | Notes | | --- | --- | | 2025-10-12 03:32 PM | **Order Created (Delivery-CBD/Other)** | | 2025-10-12 03:33 PM | **Order #50376 declined by Gopher#28008** | | 2025-10-12 03:36 PM | StripCardError:Your card has insufficient funds. | | 2025-10-12 03:36 PM | Assign Order Error for Gopher #15104: Error: User's bank denied transaction. | | 2025-10-12 03:36 PM | Gopher #15104 tryed to Claim Order But Error on claiming order User's bank denied transaction. | | 2025-10-12 03:38 PM | **OOA has attempted to broadcast a total of 1 SMS messages and 144 emails.** | * 03:32 PM — Order created * 03:33 PM — Order declined by one Gopher * 03:36 PM — Payment declined / assign errors * 03:38 PM — System sent **1 SMS + 144 emails** ‌ This should **NOT** have happened. ‌ 📎 _Screenshot reference:_ ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=fbb7fea0-b254-4bbf-b1bc-d424d3694414&&collection=&height=846&occurrenceKey=null&width=1878&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) ‌ ## **🔁 Required Updated Broadcast Logic** ‌ ### **🕒 Timing Rules** * Backup SMS + Email should trigger **ONLY IF**: * Request has been open for **more than 5 minutes** * **AND** no Gopher has accepted the request within the first 5 minutes ### **📍 Distance Targeting** * Only send to **Stripe-verified Gophers** * Adjust radius from: * ❌ 15 miles * ✅ **10 miles** ### **❌ Do NOT Send Backup If** * At least **one Gopher has accepted** within 5 minutes: * Submitted a bid * Accepted a “Select My Gopher” request * User has: * Unsubscribed from notifications * Replied **STOP** to SMS * Gopher is not Stripe verified ‌ ### **📊 Volume & Ranking Controls** * **Cap SMS sends to 50 max** * Rank eligible Gophers by: * Highest historical usage / engagement * Email volume should follow the same targeting rules (even if not capped the same way) ‌ ## **🔄 Request Type Considerations** ‌ Backup logic must apply consistently across: * **Requestor sets price** 🔗 <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://www.figma.com/design/H6THlatWvwT6ESI2j4MPTi/Final-Flows?node-id=152-6267&t=D39gakmlBKdloF6W-4</custom> * **Requestor asks for bids** 🔗 <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-1">https://www.figma.com/design/H6THlatWvwT6ESI2j4MPTi/Final-Flows?node-id=152-6348&t=D39gakmlBKdloF6W-4</custom> ‌ ## **✅ Acceptance Criteria** ‌ ### **Scenario 1 – Backup not sent if accepted** * **Given** a request is submitted, * **When** at least one Gopher accepts within 5 minutes, * **Then** NO backup SMS or Email should be sent. ‌ ### **Scenario 2 – Backup sent after 5 minutes** * **Given** a request has been open for more than 5 minutes, * **And** no Gopher has accepted, * **When** backup logic triggers, * **Then** an Email is sent only to eligible Gophers. ‌ ### **Scenario 3 – Distance & verification enforced** * **Given** backup notifications are sent, * **When** selecting recipients, * **Then** only Stripe-verified Gophers within **10 miles** are included. ‌ ### **Scenario 4 – Opt-out respected** * **Given** a Gopher has unsubscribed or replied STOP, * **When** backup notifications trigger, * **Then** they must NOT receive SMS or Email. ‌ ### **Scenario 5 – SMS volume capped** * **Given** more than 50 eligible Gophers exist, * **When** sending backup SMS, * **Then** only the top **50 ranked Gophers** receive SMS. ‌ ### **Scenario 6 – No duplicate or runaway sends** * **Given** backup notifications are triggered, * **When** logs are reviewed, * **Then** total SMS/Email volume must align with rules and never exceed caps. ‌ ## **⚙️ Business Rules** ‌ * Twilio usage must be **cost-controlled and intentional** * Backup notifications are a **fallback**, not default behavior * Acceptance within first 5 minutes cancels all backup sends * Stripe verification, distance, opt-out status are mandatory filters * Ranking logic must be deterministic and auditable ‌ ## **🔍 Example Comparison** ‌ | **Case** | **Current Behavior** | **Expected Behavior** | | --- | --- | --- | | Request accepted early | Backup still sent | Backup canceled | | Distance targeting | 15 miles | 10 miles | | SMS volume | 100+ | Max 50 | | Unsubscribed users | Still notified | Fully excluded | ‌ ## **🧠 Dependencies / Notes** ‌ * Review current broadcast logic and data sources: * Profile address vs live location * Acceptance state timing * Ensure Twilio STOP list and unsubscribe logic are enforced * Consider logging broadcast decisions for audit/debugging * This ticket focuses on **logic & cost reduction**, not UI changes ‌ ## **🧪 QA Notes** ‌ * Test requests that: * Are accepted within 5 minutes * Remain unaccepted >5 minutes * Verify: * No notifications sent in accepted case * Correct distance filtering * SMS cap enforced * STOP / unsubscribed users excluded * Validate logs match expected broadcast behavior * Confirm Twilio volume reduction in test environment * A Gopher can only receive notifications every 24 hours. This means that the same gopher can NOT receive multiple notifications from different requests within that time.

Summary: Gopher App - Submitted Request - Viewing Interested Gophers and Bids - Spacing Issue
Description: Experiencing issues with Customers viewing profiles and accidentally accepting the offer when intending to view a gophers profile. If there are no comments on the view profile and accept button are too close as you can see here in the red circle. The green is how it should look. ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=aee2c1c2-2146-46f6-9d2b-ee982877ba94&&collection=&height=852&occurrenceKey=null&width=393&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) Just move the View Profile link to the middle to allow more space. <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=1717-31976&t=89D8VXOqxFYR2cXQ-4</custom> # ✅ **Jira Ticket: Prevent Accidental Acceptance When Viewing Gopher Profiles** **Type:** Bug / UI Adjustment **Priority:** Medium–High (causing unintended request acceptance) **Component:** Request Offers List → Gopher Cards **Environment:** iOS & Android --- ## **Summary** Customers are accidentally tapping **Accept Offer** when they intended to tap **View Profile**, because the two actions are placed too close together when there are no comments on the offer card. This is causing unintentional request acceptance. The UI spacing does not match the intended layout shown in Figma. --- ## **Problem Description** When viewing offers from Gophers, the UI displays: * **View Profile** (small link) * **Accept Offer** (button) If a Gopher has no comments in their offer, the spacing collapses and the two elements become too close. This makes it extremely easy for customers to accidentally accept the offer instead of viewing the profile. Figma reference: 🔗 [https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=1717-31976&t=89D8VXOqxFYR2cXQ-4](https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=1717-31976&t=89D8VXOqxFYR2cXQ-4) User feedback and internal observation confirm unintended acceptances. --- ## **Expected Behavior** When there are **no comments**, the layout should still match the intended spacing: ✅ **View Profile** link centered horizontally ✅ Adequate separation from the **Accept Offer** button ✅ No accidental tap risk This is shown in the **green-circled** example. --- ## **Actual Behavior** ❌ View Profile and Accept Offer appear too close ❌ No padding/margin when comments section is empty ❌ Customers frequently tap the wrong action --- ## **Fix Required** **Move the "View Profile" link to the center of the card** (consistent with Figma) regardless of whether comments are present. Ensure: * Minimum vertical spacing above and below * Minimum margin requirement between View Profile and Accept Offer * Layout consistent on all screen sizes (Android devices especially vary) --- ## **Acceptance Criteria** ✅ View Profile is always centered ✅ Minimum spacing enforced between View Profile and Accept Offer (consistent with Figma) ✅ Behavior matches provided Figma reference ✅ Tested with: * Offers with comments * Offers with zero comments * Small-screen devices * Large-screen devices ✅ No accidental Accept Offer taps reported during QA --- ## **Notes for Developers** * Check conditionally-rendered comment containers—the missing comments should not collapse layout spacing. * Confirm Tap target spacing meets minimum platform accessibility requirements (Apple HIG, Material). * Padding must be hard-set, not dependent on comment text height.

Summary: Gopher Go - Viewing An Age-Restricted Delivery Request - Submitting A Counter-Offer - "Purchase Needed and ID Disclaimer Not functioning"
Description: We have a standard disclaimer for “Purchase Needed” requests, so the Gopher is aware to NOT accept the request if they do not have the funds to pay for the items. We need to ADD this same disclaimer when a Gopher submits a Counter-Offer. ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=817ec0b1-8010-4f65-9a3c-0bfef8240579&&collection=&height=852&occurrenceKey=null&width=393&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=6563-1484&t=KzsqC4L9ZqYcmF7w-4</custom> # ✅ **Jira Ticket: Add “Purchase Needed” Disclaimer When Gopher Submits a Counter-Offer** **Type:** Bug / Missing Logic **Priority:** High (risk of Gophers accepting jobs they cannot fund) **Component:** Gopher Offer Flow → Counter-Offer Modal **Environment:** iOS & Android --- ## **Summary** When a Request includes **Purchase Needed**, the app currently shows a standard disclaimer to inform Gophers that they should _not_ accept the request unless they have the funds to pay for the items upfront. However, this disclaimer is **missing** when a Gopher submits a **Counter-Offer**, which creates a risk that Gophers submit a price without understanding they must pay for the items first. We need to display the same disclaimer within the Counter-Offer flow. --- ## **Problem Description** * Requests with **Purchase Needed** show the disclaimer correctly on initial offer acceptance. * But if the Gopher chooses to **submit a Counter-Offer**, the disclaimer does **not** appear. * This creates confusion and risk, especially for deliveries involving item purchases. The Figma reference for the correct disclaimer behavior is available here: 🔗 **Figma** [https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=6563-1484&t=KzsqC4L9ZqYcmF7w-4](https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=6563-1484&t=KzsqC4L9ZqYcmF7w-4) --- ## **Expected Behavior** ✅ Whenever Purchase Needed = TRUE ✅ AND the Gopher selects **Submit Counter-Offer** → The same disclaimer modal must appear before the counter-offer is submitted. This ensures the Gopher acknowledges the financial requirement. --- ## **Actual Behavior** ❌ Counter-Offer can be submitted with **no disclaimer visible** ❌ Gophers may unknowingly commit to jobs they cannot afford --- ## **Required Update** **Add the same “Purchase Needed” disclaimer modal** that appears in standard acceptance flow into: **Gopher → Submit Counter-Offer → Confirmation Step** Requirements: * Modal must appear _before_ the counter-offer is finalized * Text must match existing Purchase Needed disclaimer word-for-word * Gopher must tap “Agree/Continue” before the counter-offer is submitted * This modal should only display when the request has **Purchase Needed = TRUE** * No duplicate modal if already shown once; only trigger once per session --- ## **Acceptance Criteria** ✅ Counter-offer submission now displays the Purchase Needed disclaimer ✅ Disclaimer uses identical language/style as existing modal ✅ Counter-offer cannot be submitted until the disclaimer is acknowledged ✅ Works on both iOS and Android ✅ QA tests: * Counter-offer with Purchase Needed ON * Counter-offer with Purchase Needed OFF (no disclaimer) * Acceptance of offer with Purchase Needed ON (unchanged) * Ensure no duplicate disclaimers appear --- ## **Notes for Developers** * Reuse the existing modal component—do _not_ create a second version. * Ensure logic is tied to backend flag `purchase_needed = true`. * Event tracking may be added later if needed.

Summary: Gopher App - Submitted Request - Gopher Accepts - Payment Authorization Decline - Customer Cannot Cancel Issue
Description: When a Requestor's payment authorization declines after a Gopher has accepted their request, the Requestor is left in a stuck state with no way to cancel. Additionally, if the Requestor updates their payment method and resubmits, the request is incorrectly broadcast back to the entire Gopher network rather than first giving the original Gopher the opportunity to re-accept. This ticket fixes both bugs and introduces a 1-minute priority re-acceptance window for the original Gopher. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Requestor whose payment method declined after a Gopher accepted their request, ## 🎯 I want to be able to either update my payment method and give my original Gopher first priority to re-accept, or cancel the request entirely, ## ✅ So that I am never stuck on a declined request waiting for it to expire, and the original Gopher is respected with first opportunity when I fix my payment. ## 💡 Context / Background * When a Requestor submits a request, a Gopher accepts it, and the payment authorization fails, the Requestor is currently stuck on the declined request with no actionable path forward. * There is no cancel option available during a payment decline state, forcing the Requestor to wait for the request to expire on its own. * If the Requestor does update their card and resubmit, the request incorrectly goes back out to the full Gopher network instead of first notifying the Gopher who originally accepted. * The correct behavior is: give the original Gopher a 1-minute exclusive priority window to re-accept before broadcasting to the full network. ## ⚠️ Issue Breakdown ### Bug 1 – No Cancel Option on Payment Decline * When a payment authorization declines, the Requestor has no way to cancel the request * The Requestor is stuck until the request expires with no actionable path * A cancel option must be available in the payment declined state ### Bug 2 – Card Update Rebroadcasts to Full Network * When the Requestor updates their payment method and resubmits, the request is broadcast to the entire Gopher network * The original Gopher who accepted receives no preferential notification or re-acceptance opportunity * The request should first be offered back to the original Gopher before being rebroadcast ## 🔀 Correct Flow After Payment Decline ### Path A – Requestor Updates Payment and Resubmits * Requestor is shown the payment declined state with the option to update their payment method * Requestor updates their card and resubmits the request * The original Gopher receives a banner notification alerting them the Requestor’s payment has been updated * Tapping the banner opens a popup modal offering the Gopher the opportunity to re-accept the request * The original Gopher has a 1-minute exclusive priority window to re-accept before the request is broadcast to the full Gopher network * If the Gopher re-accepts within 1 minute: the request is assigned to them and does not broadcast to the network * If the Gopher does not re-accept within 1 minute: the request broadcasts to the full Gopher network as a standard available request ### Path B – Requestor Cancels the Request * Requestor is shown the payment declined state with the option to cancel the request * If the Requestor chooses to cancel, the standard cancellation flow applies (reason required, logging, notifications) ## ❌ Current Behavior * When a payment declines, no cancel option is available — the Requestor is stuck until the request expires * When the Requestor updates their card and resubmits, the request broadcasts to the full network with no priority given to the original Gopher ## ✅ Expected Behavior * When a payment declines, the Requestor is shown two clear options: update payment or cancel * When the payment is updated and resubmitted, the original Gopher receives a priority banner notification and a 1-minute exclusive window to re-accept before the full network is notified * If the original Gopher does not re-accept within 1 minute, the request broadcasts to the full network ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Cancel option is available on payment decline * **Given** a Requestor’s payment authorization declines after a Gopher accepts their request * **When** the Requestor views the declined state * **Then** a cancel option is clearly available alongside the update payment option ### Scenario 2 – Original Gopher receives priority banner on payment update * **Given** the Requestor has updated their payment method and resubmitted * **When** the payment is successfully processed * **Then** the original Gopher receives a banner notification alerting them the payment has been updated * **And** tapping the banner opens a modal offering them the option to re-accept the request ### Scenario 3 – Original Gopher re-accepts within 1 minute * **Given** the original Gopher has received the priority notification * **When** the Gopher taps to re-accept within the 1-minute window * **Then** the request is assigned to them and the request is not broadcast to the full network ### Scenario 4 – Request broadcasts to full network after 1-minute window expires * **Given** the original Gopher has received the priority notification but does not re-accept within 1 minute * **When** the 1-minute priority window expires * **Then** the request is broadcast to the full Gopher network as a standard available request ### Scenario 5 – Requestor can cancel during payment decline state * **Given** the Requestor’s payment has declined and they do not want to update their card * **When** the Requestor taps Cancel * **Then** the standard cancellation flow is triggered and the request is cancelled ## ⚙️ Business Rules * When a payment declines after Gopher acceptance, the Requestor must always have two visible options: update payment or cancel. * When payment is successfully updated and resubmitted, the original Gopher receives a 1-minute exclusive priority window to re-accept before any other Gopher is notified. * The 1-minute priority window starts from the moment the updated payment is successfully processed. * If the original Gopher does not re-accept within 1 minute, the request broadcasts to the full network. * The cancel option during payment decline follows the standard cancellation flow. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * The payment declined state UI must be updated to surface both options (update payment and cancel) clearly. * The original Gopher’s account ID must be stored at the time of acceptance so they can be targeted for the priority notification on payment update. * The 1-minute priority timer must start on the backend the moment payment success is confirmed — the full network broadcast must be suppressed until the timer expires or the Gopher declines. * The re-acceptance modal must clearly communicate to the Gopher that they have been given priority and the time remaining in their window. * Figma – Payment declined state: https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=5588-893 * Figma – Priority re-acceptance modal: https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=7354-8687 ## 🧪 QA Notes * Trigger a payment decline after Gopher acceptance — confirm both update payment and cancel options are visible. * Update payment and resubmit — confirm the original Gopher receives a banner notification immediately. * Tap the banner — confirm the re-acceptance modal appears. * Re-accept within 1 minute — confirm the request is assigned to the original Gopher and not broadcast to the network. * Allow the 1-minute window to expire without re-accepting — confirm the request broadcasts to the full network. * Cancel from the declined state — confirm the standard cancellation flow triggers. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Both Accounts - Minimum Age To Sign Up Is 16
Description: Both apps currently allow users of any age to complete the sign-up flow. A minimum age of 16 must be enforced during account creation. Users who are under 16 must be blocked from creating an account with a clear, friendly message explaining the age requirement. ## 🧑‍💻 As a platform enforcing minimum age requirements, ## 🎯 I want to prevent any user under the age of 16 from completing account registration on either app, ## ✅ So that the platform complies with its minimum age policy and underage users cannot access the marketplace. ## 💡 Context / Background * The sign-up flow currently collects a date of birth but does not enforce a minimum age gate — users of any age can complete registration. * The minimum age to create an account on either app is 16. * When a user enters a date of birth that indicates they are under 16, account creation must be blocked immediately with a clear message. * This applies to both the Gopher App (Requestor) and Gopher Go (Gopher). ## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce 1. Open the Gopher App or Gopher Go. 2. Begin the sign-up flow. 3. Enter a date of birth that results in an age under 16. 4. Observe that the sign-up flow continues and the account is created without any age restriction error. ## ❌ Current Behavior * Users under 16 can complete the sign-up flow and create an account without any restriction * No age validation or minimum age gate is enforced at sign-up ## ✅ Expected Behavior * When a user enters a date of birth indicating they are under 16, account creation is blocked * A clear, friendly message is displayed explaining that users must be at least 16 to create an account * The user cannot proceed past the date of birth step if they are under 16 ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – User under 16 is blocked from signing up * **Given** a user enters a date of birth that makes them under 16 years old * **When** they attempt to proceed past the date of birth step * **Then** account creation is blocked and a message is displayed: "You must be at least 16 years old to create an account." * **And** the user cannot continue the sign-up flow ### Scenario 2 – User exactly 16 can sign up * **Given** a user enters a date of birth that makes them exactly 16 years old * **When** they proceed past the date of birth step * **Then** the sign-up flow continues normally ### Scenario 3 – User 17 or older can sign up * **Given** a user enters a date of birth that makes them 17 or older * **When** they proceed past the date of birth step * **Then** the sign-up flow continues normally with no age-related block ## ⚙️ Business Rules * The minimum age to create an account on either app is 16. * Age validation must be enforced on the backend as well as the frontend — frontend-only validation is not sufficient. * Age is calculated based on the user’s date of birth relative to today’s date — a user whose 16th birthday is today is eligible. * This applies to both the Gopher App and Gopher Go. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Confirm that date of birth is already collected during sign-up — if not, it must be added as a required field. * Age validation must be performed on the backend at the time the profile data is submitted, not just on the frontend, to prevent bypass. * Existing accounts created by users under 16 should be flagged for admin review — confirm with the team whether any remediation of existing under-age accounts is required. ## 🧪 QA Notes * Enter a DOB that makes the user 15 years old — confirm sign-up is blocked with the correct message. * Enter a DOB that makes the user exactly 16 today — confirm sign-up proceeds. * Enter a DOB that makes the user 17 or older — confirm sign-up proceeds normally. * Attempt to bypass the frontend validation via the API with an underage DOB — confirm the backend also rejects the request. * Test on both the Gopher App and Gopher Go. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher App - Favorite Gopher (MY Gopher) Recommendation View In Inbox Issue
Description: When a Requestor receives a MY Gopher recommendation inbox message, three issues are present: the View Profile link for recommended Gophers does not open the profile popup modal as intended, the SMS sent to the referred party is missing app download links, and on Android the inbox message cannot be scrolled to reveal all recommended Gophers at the bottom of the list. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Requestor who has received a MY Gopher recommendation in their inbox, ## 🎯 I want to be able to view each recommended Gopher’s profile, receive a working SMS with app links, and scroll to see all recommendations, ## ✅ So that I can fully evaluate each recommended Gopher and the referral experience works end-to-end. ## 💡 Context / Background * When a Gopher App user uses Refer App → Recommend MY Gopher, the recipient receives an inbox message with a list of one or more recommended Gophers. * Each recommended Gopher is displayed with their profile picture and a View Profile label to the left. * Tapping anywhere from the profile picture to the View Profile text should open the standard Gopher profile popup modal — the same format used when viewing bids, interested Gophers, and counter offers. * The referred party also receives an SMS notification about the recommendation. This SMS is missing the app download links. * On Android devices, the inbox message list cannot be scrolled, cutting off any Gophers at the bottom of the recommendation list. ## ⚠️ Issue Breakdown ### Bug 1 – View Profile Link Not Functioning * Tapping the recommended Gopher’s profile picture or the View Profile text in the inbox message does not open the profile popup modal * The tappable area must span from the profile picture through to the View Profile label * The profile popup modal that opens must match the format used for viewing bids, interested Gophers, and counter offers ### Bug 2 – SMS Missing App Download Links * The SMS sent to the referred party when a MY Gopher recommendation is made does not include links to download the apps * The SMS must include the following deep links: * **Gopher App (Requestor):** https://api.gophergo.io/api/v1/app/requester * **Gopher Go:** https://api.gophergo.io/api/v1/app/go ### Bug 3 – Android Scroll Issue (Bottom Gopher Not Visible) * On Android, the inbox message view containing recommended Gophers cannot be scrolled * When two or more Gophers are recommended, the bottom Gopher is cut off and inaccessible * The recommended Gopher list must be scrollable on Android so all recommendations are accessible ## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce ### Bug 1 – View Profile 1. Receive a MY Gopher recommendation inbox message with at least one recommended Gopher. 2. Open the inbox message. 3. Tap the recommended Gopher’s profile picture or the View Profile text. 4. Observe that the profile popup modal does not open. ### Bug 2 – SMS App Links 1. Have a Gopher App user send a MY Gopher recommendation via Refer App. 2. Check the SMS received by the referred party. 3. Observe that no app download links are included. ### Bug 3 – Android Scroll 1. On an Android device, open a MY Gopher recommendation inbox message with two or more recommended Gophers. 2. Attempt to scroll down to see the bottom recommended Gopher. 3. Observe the list does not scroll and the bottom Gopher is cut off. ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Tapping a recommended Gopher opens the profile popup modal * **Given** a Requestor has opened a MY Gopher recommendation inbox message * **When** they tap the recommended Gopher’s profile picture or the View Profile text * **Then** the Gopher’s profile popup modal opens in the standard format used for bids, interested Gophers, and counter offers ### Scenario 2 – Referral SMS includes app download links * **Given** a MY Gopher recommendation has been sent to a referred party * **When** the referred party receives the SMS * **Then** the SMS contains links to both the Gopher App (https://api.gophergo.io/api/v1/app/requester) and Gopher Go (https://api.gophergo.io/api/v1/app/go) ### Scenario 3 – Android inbox message is scrollable * **Given** an Android user opens a MY Gopher recommendation inbox message with multiple recommended Gophers * **When** they scroll down in the inbox message * **Then** all recommended Gophers are visible and accessible ## ⚙️ Business Rules * The tappable area on each recommended Gopher must span from the profile picture to the View Profile text. * The profile modal opened from the recommendation must match the exact format used elsewhere in the app for Gopher profile views. * The referral SMS must always include both app download links. * The recommendation list in the inbox message must be scrollable on both iOS and Android regardless of the number of Gophers listed. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Bug 1: Confirm whether the View Profile tap target is missing an onPress handler or whether the profile modal component is not being rendered in the inbox context. * Bug 2: Update the SMS template for MY Gopher referrals to include both app deep links. * Bug 3: The Android scroll issue is likely caused by a non-scrollable container wrapping the recommended Gopher list — ensure the list is wrapped in a ScrollView or FlatList with appropriate height constraints. * Figma design reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=105-15465 ## 🧪 QA Notes * Open a MY Gopher recommendation inbox message and tap a recommended Gopher’s profile picture — confirm the profile modal opens. * Tap the View Profile text — confirm the profile modal opens. * Confirm the profile modal matches the standard format used for bids and interested Gophers. * Send a MY Gopher recommendation and check the referred party’s SMS — confirm both app links are present and tappable. * On Android, open a recommendation message with 2+ Gophers — confirm the list scrolls and all Gophers are accessible. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher Go - Available Request View - Remove Customer Apt #
Description: The Gopher Go Available tab is exposing the customer’s apartment or unit number to Gophers before a request has been accepted. The platform already hides the physical street address numbers prior to acceptance for privacy. The apartment/unit number must follow the same rule and be hidden until the request is accepted. This applies to all request types. ## 🧑‍💻 As a platform protecting Requestor privacy, ## 🎯 I want the customer’s apartment or unit number to be hidden from Gophers on the Available tab until they have accepted the request, ## ✅ So that the Requestor’s specific unit details are not exposed to Gophers who have not been entrusted with fulfilling their request. ## 💡 Context / Background * The platform already hides the physical street address numbers (e.g. house number or building number) from Gophers on the Available tab until a request is accepted. * The apartment or unit number is a more specific piece of identifying information and must be subject to the same privacy restriction. * Currently, the apartment/unit number is visible to all Gophers browsing available requests before acceptance. * This applies to all request types across Gopher Go. ## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce 1. Log in to Gopher Go as a Gopher. 2. Navigate to the Available tab. 3. Open any available request where the Requestor has entered an apartment or unit number. 4. Observe that the apartment/unit number is visible before acceptance. ## ❌ Current Behavior * The customer’s apartment or unit number is visible to all Gophers on the Available tab before a request is accepted * The street address numbers are already correctly hidden, but the unit/apt number is not ## ✅ Expected Behavior * The apartment or unit number is hidden from Gophers on the Available tab before acceptance * Once a Gopher accepts the request, the full address including the apartment/unit number is revealed * This behavior is consistent across all request types ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Apt/unit number is hidden before acceptance * **Given** a Gopher is browsing available requests * **When** they view a request where the Requestor has entered an apartment or unit number * **Then** the apartment or unit number is not visible ### Scenario 2 – Full address including apt/unit is revealed after acceptance * **Given** a Gopher has accepted a request * **When** they view the request details * **Then** the full address including the apartment or unit number is displayed ### Scenario 3 – Applies to all request types * **Given** any request type (Delivery, Need A Ride, Service, etc.) where an apt/unit number is entered * **When** a Gopher views the request before accepting * **Then** the apt/unit number is hidden ## ⚙️ Business Rules * The apartment or unit number must be treated as private address information and hidden from Gophers until a request is accepted. * This rule applies consistently to all request types and all address fields — street number and unit/apt number are both hidden pre-acceptance. * The full address must be revealed immediately upon request acceptance. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Identify where the address is being constructed for display on the Available tab and confirm the unit/apt field is being excluded from the pre-acceptance masked address string. * The masking logic that already hides the street number should be extended to also strip the apartment or unit number from the pre-acceptance address display. * Confirm the full unmasked address (including unit/apt) is correctly surfaced once the request is accepted. ## 🧪 QA Notes * Create a request with an apartment or unit number and view it as a Gopher on the Available tab before accepting — confirm the apt/unit number is not visible. * Accept the request and confirm the full address including the apt/unit number is now visible. * Test across multiple request types — Delivery, Need A Ride, Service — to confirm consistent behavior. * Confirm the street address number is also still hidden before acceptance (regression check). * Test on both iOS and Android.

Description: ## Goal On the Gopher's **active request** screen, tapping **Pick-Up** or **Destination** opens a modal with **3 navigation options** — Google Maps (already integrated), Apple Maps, Waze — with a **set-default-platform** option, an **auto-prompt** when items are picked up, and a **purchase-from-anywhere countdown timer**. **▶ Full handoff:** `docs/handoff/G40-171-navigation-links.md` ## ✅ Done (front-end) — `_prototypes/Go/gopher-go-purchase-delivery-figma.html` New **"G40-171 · Navigation"** frame in the real accepted-lifecycle screen, built with the file's own tokens. Summary: Gopher Go - Account - Payout Issue With Zip Code
Description: When a Gopher goes to Account → Payout Account and provides their personal info for setting up their payout account, if the Gopher's Zip Code starts with a 0 (zero), they will receive the following errors and not be allowed to move forward. The states with ZIP codes starting with 0 are Connecticut, Massachusetts, Maine, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Rhode Island, and Vermont. ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=67f8a6e6-dc62-4dd1-8e03-b70c7fa2827d&&collection=&height=852&occurrenceKey=null&width=393&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=d70666ce-40b6-4746-8402-491b1f13c52d&&collection=&height=2556&occurrenceKey=null&width=1179&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) # ✅ **Jira Ticket: ZIP Codes Starting With “0” Not Accepted During Payout Account Setup** **Type:** Bug **Priority:** High (blocks Gophers from receiving payouts) **Component:** Account → Payout Account Setup (Stripe Integration) **Environment:** iOS & Android --- ## **Summary** Gophers cannot complete payout account setup if their ZIP code begins with **0** (zero). These ZIP codes trigger validation errors even when the entered ZIP is legitimate. As a result, Gophers from several Northeastern states are unable to activate their payout accounts. --- ## **Affected Users** Any Gopher whose ZIP code starts with **0**, including: * Connecticut * Massachusetts * Maine * New Hampshire * New Jersey * Rhode Island * Vermont This affects a large portion of Northeast-based workers. --- ## **Problem Description** When a Gopher navigates to: **Account → Payout Account → Add Payout Info** … and enters a ZIP code beginning with **0**, the system rejects it and shows an error message. Examples of invalidly rejected ZIPs: * 02108 (Boston, MA) * 06510 (New Haven, CT) * 03755 (NH) * 07030 (Hoboken, NJ) ZIP codes are **valid**, but our current validation rules treat leading zeros as invalid or strip the zero, causing a mismatch with Stripe’s required format. Gophers are unable to proceed to payout verification, preventing them from being paid. --- ## **Expected Behavior** ✅ ZIP codes starting with 0 must be accepted ✅ Leading zeros must be preserved when passed to Stripe ✅ Form validation must recognize ZIPs in all US states ✅ Gopher should be able to move forward in the payout account setup with no errors --- ## **Actual Behavior** ❌ ZIP codes with leading zeros trigger errors ❌ Input is blocked despite valid data ❌ Stripe onboarding cannot be completed ❌ Gophers from affected states are unable to set up payouts --- ## **Likely Cause** * ZIP field incorrectly typed as `number` instead of `string` * Leading zeros being trimmed before validation or before submission to Stripe * Regex validation that excludes `^0` * Client-side masking that autoremoves zeros * Incorrect formatting before sending to Stripe API --- ## **Fix Requirements** 1. **Treat ZIP code as a string**, not a number 2. **Preserve leading zeros** through: * Input field * Front-end validation * Submission payload * Stripe parameter formatting 3. Use a universal US ZIP regex: `^\d{5}(-\d{4})?$` 4. Validate only format, not state logic 5. Test on iOS + Android + Stripe sandbox onboarding --- ## **Acceptance Criteria** ✅ ZIP codes beginning with 0 are accepted with no errors ✅ Validation accepts all standard US ZIP formats (5-digit or ZIP+4) ✅ Data sent to Stripe retains leading zero ✅ Payout onboarding completes successfully for NE-based Gophers ✅ QA verifies with test ZIPs from: * Connecticut (06001–06999) * Massachusetts (01001–02791) * Maine (04001–04992) * New Hampshire (03031–03897) * New Jersey (07001–08989) * Rhode Island (02801–02940) * Vermont (05001–05907) --- ## **Notes for Developers** * Stripe **expects postal codes as strings**, not numeric. * React Native/Swift/Kotlin input components may default to numeric types that trim zeros. * Consider forcing `keyboardType="default"` for reliable string entry. * Add unit test to confirm leading zeros persist through the full pipeline.

Summary: Update & Refine Stripe API/Payment Workflow
Description: Gopher’s API and payment workflow needs to be updated and refined to allow for a cleaner and more robust payment process. Currently, there is a 7-day payment authorization window for payment transactions. Gopher’s payment workflow needs to be updated to handle scheduled requests, payment authorizations on those requests, and payments. See linked tasks. ‌ ‌ ### **As a** Gopher App user submitting and scheduling requests, ### **I want** a clean, reliable, and consistent payment workflow that correctly handles payment authorizations and transactions, ### **So that** my scheduled and on-demand requests can be processed smoothly without authorization errors or failed payments. ‌ ### **💡 Context / Background** ‌ * Gopher’s current payment system uses a **7-day payment authorization window**, which impacts how scheduled and delayed requests are handled. * The existing workflow does **not properly support scheduled requests**, authorization retries, or consistent payment capture logic. * The system needs to be **refined and updated** to ensure: * Correct pre-authorization on scheduled requests * Proper handling of payment authorization windows * Reliable payment capture during and after request completion * Additional related work is included in the **linked tasks** (API endpoints, payment logic, scheduling updates, etc.). ‌ ### **✅ Acceptance Criteria (Given / When / Then)** ‌ **Scenario 1 – Payment authorization for scheduled requests** * **Given** a user schedules a request to occur in the future, * **When** the scheduled time arrives, * **Then** the system must correctly perform or refresh the payment authorization according to Stripe rules and project requirements. ‌ **Scenario 2 – Updated authorization window handling** * **Given** the existing 7-day authorization window, * **When** a request is scheduled beyond that timeframe, * **Then** the authorization logic must handle re-authorizing or extending the authorization appropriately and safely. ‌ **Scenario 3 – Payment workflow stability** * **Given** a request is completed, * **When** payment capture occurs, * **Then** the workflow must behave consistently without errors, double charges, expired authorizations, or missed payments. ‌ **Scenario 4 – API reliability** * **Given** the updated workflow, * **When** API calls related to authorization, capture, or scheduling are triggered, * **Then** all responses must be accurate, stable, and follow the updated payment workflow rules. ‌ ### **⚙️ Business Rules** ‌ * Payment authorization must comply with Stripe’s authorization windows and refresh rules. * Scheduled requests require a **valid and active authorization** at the time the Gopher begins the work or when pricing updates occur. * Workflow must support: * Initial authorization * Re-authorization if needed * Capture upon request completion * Linked tasks may include updates to: * Backend payment services * Scheduling services * Database models * Notification logic * No duplicated authorizations or unintended charges may occur. ‌ ### **🧠 Dependencies / Notes** ‌ * Review full payment workflow in existing backend services (authorization, hold, capture). * Coordinate with linked tasks to ensure changes are not isolated or conflicting. * May require adjustments to: * Payment microservice * Scheduler service * API contract * Stripe integration logic * Thorough testing must be performed to avoid financial impact to users. ‌ ### **🧪 QA Notes:** ‌ * Test payment workflow for: * Normal immediate requests * Scheduled requests under 7 days * Scheduled requests over 7 days * Validate Stripe logs for authorization + capture accuracy. * Verify no duplicated usage of user payment method. * Confirm workflows work across different request categories.

Summary: Gopher App - Active Request - Age-Restricted - No Show Timer Issue
Description: When a Gopher arrives at the drop off location for an age-restricted delivery and the customer isn’t present, when the Gopher selects the “Tap here if customer is not present at drop off location. We'll notify them immediately via text and start the 10 minute timer,” the customer is supposed to receive a text and email stating they must show up with-in 10 minutes. This feature seems to be working intermittently. ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=53e0286a-4173-4428-9c27-94a98ce56051&&collection=&height=1083&occurrenceKey=null&width=393&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) When this feature isn’t working properly, the Gopher can potentially complete an order this way when not actually being at the drop off location and getting paid for a completed order with no chance of Gopher recouping the payout transfer. When the no-show timer is selected, the requestor is sent an email and SMS with instructions. ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=97b5f69c-19fa-4c03-b7e2-6f6d3a48ea47&&collection=&height=529&occurrenceKey=null&width=215&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) Once the 10 minute time expired, the screen allows the customer to confirm ID and Identity OR Requestor No-Show. ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=03af84f8-4e5e-42c8-8059-2f8744ac7129&&collection=&height=858&occurrenceKey=null&width=393&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) “The 10 minute timer for the Requestor has expired. You can still wait for the Requestor if you choose. If you choose Requestor No Show, the request will be completed and you will be paid for the total amount. DO NOT LEAVE THE AGE-RESTRICTED ITEMS! A GPS/time stamp will be logged at your exact location when you select either option to avoid dispute discrepancies (so please make sure you’re still at the drop off location when selecting).” ‌ DO NOT ALLOW A NO-SHOW TO GO INTO THE STANDARD PAYOUT FLOW. INCLUDE THIS WITH THE FRAUD EMAILS FOR ADMIN REVIEW. WE HAVE SEEN WORKERS USE THIS FEATURE FRAUDULENTLY <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=5188-12550</custom> # ✅ **Jira Ticket: Intermittent Failure of No-Show Timer Notifications + No-Show Payout Must Route to Fraud Review** **Type:** Bug / Compliance Risk **Priority:** **Critical** **Component:** Age-Restricted Delivery → No-Show Timer Logic / Notification System / Payout Flow **Environment:** iOS, Android, Backend API, Notification Service --- ## **Summary** When a Gopher is delivering an **age-restricted order** and the customer is not present, the Gopher can tap: **“Tap here if customer is not present at drop off location. We'll notify them immediately via text and start the 10 minute timer.”** This feature is intended to: 1. Trigger **immediate SMS + email** to the customer 2. Start a **10-minute timer** 3. After the timer, present the Gopher with two choices: * **Confirm ID and Identity** * **Requestor No-Show** However, the **notifications are firing inconsistently** (sometimes one, sometimes both, sometimes none), which allows the Gopher to complete an order as a “no-show” even if the customer was never notified. ### ✅ **New requirement:** **No age-restricted “Requestor No-Show” completion should enter the normal payout flow.** **It must be routed to the Fraud / Admin Review queue before payout is released.** This prevents fraudulent completions and ensures compliance with age-restricted delivery laws. Figma reference: 🔗 [https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=5188-12550](https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=5188-12550) --- ## **Detailed Description of the Bug** ### **Expected Flow** 1. Gopher taps “Customer Not Present – Start Timer” 2. **SMS** + **Email** immediately notify the requestor: * “You must show up within 10 minutes for ID verification.” 3. Timer counts down 10 minutes 4. Gopher sees expiration screen with messaging: > “The 10 minute timer for the Requestor has expired. > You can still wait for the Requestor if you choose. > If you choose Requestor No Show, the request will be completed and you will be paid for the total amount. > DO NOT LEAVE THE AGE-RESTRICTED ITEMS! > A GPS/time stamp will be logged at your exact location when you select either option.” 5. Gopher chooses: * Confirm ID, OR * **Requestor No-Show** ### **Actual Behavior** ❌ SMS sometimes fails ❌ Email sometimes fails ❌ Sometimes neither notification is sent ❌ Timer starts despite the customer being unaware ❌ Gopher can submit **No-Show** even when customer was never contacted ❌ The completion **incorrectly enters the standard payout flow** ❌ No fraud or admin review is triggered This exposes the system to: * Fraud * Misuse * Legal compliance violations * Financial loss (Gopher gets paid without delivering) --- ## **Impact** * High-risk compliance breach for alcohol/tobacco vaping deliveries * Financial loss due to invalid payouts * Customers unaware of required ID procedures * Support escalations and complaints * GPS/time validation becomes meaningless if customer is unaware --- ## **Required Fixes** ### ✅ **1. Notification Reliability Fix** * SMS and Email must ALWAYS send when the no-show timer is initiated * Add backend retry logic (Twilio + email provider) * Log notification status for auditing * Timer MUST NOT start unless backend confirms both messages were sent --- ### ✅ **2. Timer Logic Must Be Backend-Controlled** * Prevent client-side manipulation * Ensure accurate 10-minute countdown * Ensure customer notification went out before timer begins --- ### ✅ **3. No-Show Completion Must Route to Fraud/Admin Review** **Do NOT allow a Requestor No-Show (age-restricted) to enter standard payout flow.** Instead: **✅ Route this event into the Fraud/Admin Review queue** **✅ Block payout until manually approved** **✅ Include the following metadata for review:** * GPS coordinates at moment of no-show completion * Timestamp * Gopher ID * Customer notification logs (email + SMS success/failure) * Delivery request type * Photos (if provided) **Admin receives an alert via the same email system used for fraud notifications.** --- ### ✅ **4. Enhance Logging for Accuracy** Log the following server-side events: * `no_show_timer_started` * `notification_sent_sms` * `notification_sent_email` * `timer_completed` * `gps_timestamp_logged` * `id_confirm_selected` * `no_show_selected` * `no_show_routed_to_admin_review` --- ## **Acceptance Criteria** ✅ SMS + Email always sent before timer starts ✅ Timer does not begin unless notifications succeed ✅ Expiration screen appears exactly 10 minutes after backend timer triggers ✅ No-Show (age-restricted) **never** enters standard payout flow ✅ No-Show (age-restricted) automatically routes to Fraud/Admin Review ✅ Admin receives Fraud alert email ✅ Payout remains blocked until manual approval ✅ QA verifies across: * iOS * Android * Twilio * Backend Email Provider * Multiple network conditions --- ## **QA Test Cases** ### **Test 1: Both notifications succeed** * SMS + email sent * Timer starts * After 10 minutes → gopher sees correct options * No-Show → routed to Admin Review ### **Test 2: SMS fails** * Timer must **not** start * User cannot submit no-show ### **Test 3: Email fails** * Same as above ### **Test 4: Both fail intermittently** * Timer must not start * Block no-show completion ### **Test 5: Customer appears during timer** * Confirm ID → standard flow proceeds normally
