Summary: Gopher App - Available Gophers Calculation Update
Description: When a user submits an address while creating a request, the system must calculate and display an accurate count of eligible Gophers available for that request. The calculation must apply a strict set of qualification criteria and trigger a low-availability warning modal if fewer than 20 eligible Gophers are found. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Requestor entering details for a new request, ## 🎯 I want the app to show an accurate count of Gophers who are genuinely available and qualified for my request, ## ✅ So that I have a realistic expectation of how quickly my request can be fulfilled and am warned if availability is low in my area. ## 💡 Context / Background * The available Gopher headcount displayed during request creation is currently not filtered accurately enough. * It may include Gophers who are unverified, inactive, out of range, or whose work settings do not match the request category. * The calculation must be triggered when the Requestor submits their pick-up and/or drop-off address during request entry. * If the qualified Gopher count falls below 20, a low-availability modal must be shown to the Requestor. ## 📍 Eligible Gopher Criteria A Gopher is only counted as available if ALL of the following conditions are met: * **Stripe Payout Account Verified** — only Gophers with a verified Stripe payout account are eligible * **Within 15 Miles** — the Gopher’s GPS location or physical profile address must be within 15 miles of the pick-up and/or drop-off address * **Work Settings & Radius Match** — the Gopher’s work settings and service radius must match the category being requested * **Active Within Last 6 Months** — the Gopher must have logged in within the last 6 months ## ❌ Current Behavior * The available Gopher count does not apply all required qualification filters * Unverified, inactive, out-of-range, or category-mismatched Gophers may be included in the count * The displayed headcount may be inflated and does not reflect genuine availability * No low-availability warning is triggered when eligible Gophers are scarce ## ✅ Expected Behavior * When a Requestor submits an address during request creation, the system recalculates the eligible Gopher count using all four qualification criteria * Only Gophers meeting all criteria are counted * The accurate eligible headcount is displayed to the Requestor * If fewer than 20 eligible Gophers are found, a low-availability warning modal is displayed to the Requestor ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Eligible count is calculated on address submission * **Given** a Requestor submits a pick-up or drop-off address during request creation * **When** the address is submitted * **Then** the system recalculates the eligible Gopher count applying all four qualification criteria * **And** the accurate count is displayed to the Requestor ### Scenario 2 – Unqualified Gophers are excluded from the count * **Given** Gophers exist who are unverified, inactive, out of range, or whose work settings do not match the category * **When** the eligible count is calculated * **Then** those Gophers are excluded from the count ### Scenario 3 – Low-availability modal triggers when fewer than 20 eligible Gophers are found * **Given** the eligible Gopher count for the request is fewer than 20 * **When** the count is calculated * **Then** the low-availability warning modal is displayed to the Requestor ### Scenario 4 – No modal when 20 or more eligible Gophers are available * **Given** the eligible Gopher count is 20 or more * **When** the count is calculated * **Then** no low-availability modal is shown and the Requestor proceeds normally ### Scenario 5 – Count updates when address changes * **Given** a Requestor updates their pick-up or drop-off address after an initial calculation * **When** the new address is submitted * **Then** the eligible Gopher count is recalculated and updated accordingly ## ⚙️ Business Rules * All four eligibility criteria must be applied simultaneously — a Gopher must meet every condition to be counted. * Location is determined using the Gopher’s GPS location where available, falling back to their physical profile address. * The 15-mile proximity check applies to the pick-up and/or drop-off address submitted by the Requestor. * Work settings and service radius must match the specific category being requested, not just general availability. * A Gopher who has not logged in within the last 6 months is considered inactive and must be excluded. * The low-availability modal must trigger when the eligible count is fewer than 20, regardless of the total Gopher count in the system. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Calculation must be triggered on address submission during request creation, not on page load. * GPS location data for Gophers must be accessible at calculation time — confirm availability and fallback logic with the backend team. * Stripe verification status must be queryable as part of the eligibility filter. * Gopher work settings and service radius data must be structured to support category-level filtering. * Reference Figma for the low-availability modal design: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=15-3913 ## 🧪 QA Notes * Test with an address that has 20 or more eligible Gophers — confirm accurate count is displayed and no modal appears. * Test with an address that has fewer than 20 eligible Gophers — confirm the low-availability modal is triggered. * Verify unverified Gophers (no Stripe payout account) are excluded from the count. * Verify Gophers outside the 15-mile radius are excluded. * Verify Gophers whose work settings or service radius do not match the request category are excluded. * Verify Gophers who have not logged in within the last 6 months are excluded. * Test updating the address after an initial calculation — confirm the count recalculates correctly. * Test across multiple request categories to ensure work settings filtering applies correctly per category. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Both apps — Require OTP to change profile email, then notify old + new address with support escalation path
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a User of either app (Gopher / Gopher Go) updating the email address on my profile, ## 🎯 I want the change to be OTP-verified and confirmed by notification emails sent to both my old and new address, ## ✅ So that my email cannot be silently changed by anyone other than me, and if a change ever does happen without my knowledge, I have an immediate notification at my existing address with a clear path to recover the account. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * Email is the primary identifier for an account and the channel through which password resets and other security-critical messages flow. An attacker who silently changes the email locks the legitimate owner out. * The existing **standard email OTP** mechanism (already used elsewhere in the apps) is reused here — no new OTP component is built. * The dual-notification pattern (old + new address) is the standard industry approach to protect against account takeover: even if an attacker controls a session, the legitimate owner will see the notification at their existing address and can escalate immediately. --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior ### Email change flow 1. User initiates an email change from **My Profile** by entering a new email address. 2. **Pre-OTP validation:** * If the new email is the **same** as the current email on file, reject with **"No change detected"** and do not send an OTP. * If the new email is **already in use on another account**, reject with **"This email address is not available"** and do not send an OTP. * If the new email is **invalid format**, reject with a standard format-validation message and do not send an OTP. 3. **OTP send:** The system sends an OTP via the existing standard OTP flow to the **NEW email address only**. 4. **OTP entry:** The user enters the OTP in the app. * OTP retry limits, expiry, and resend behaviour follow the existing standard OTP rules — no bespoke rules apply on this surface. 5. **On successful OTP entry:** * The email on the user's account is updated to the new address. * **Two confirmation emails** are sent: * One to the **OLD** address. * One to the **NEW** address. * Both use the **standard email template** for the respective app (Gopher / Gopher Go). * The event is **logged in the Admin Panel audit trail**. 6. **On OTP failure** (exhausted attempts or expired): * The email is not changed. * The user is returned to the email-change entry point. * The failed attempt is logged in the Admin Panel audit trail. --- ## 📧 Confirmation Email Content (draft — confirm against existing template style) Both confirmation emails use the standard template for the respective app and contain: * **Subject:** Your email address was changed * **Body:** Hi \[First Name\], The email address on your Gopher account was just changed. * **From:** \[old email address\] * **To:** \[new email address\] * **When:** \[timestamp in user's local timezone\] * **Where:** \[device + approximate location, e.g., "iPhone, Raleigh, NC"\] If you made this change, no further action is needed. **If this wasn't you, please contact support@gophergo.io as soon as possible.** Thanks, _— The Gopher Team_ --- ## 📊 Notification Content Rules * Include: timestamp (local timezone), device, approximate location (city / region level only). * Do **not** include: IP address (not user-friendly and adds noise without value). * Do **not** include: a one-click reversal link in this release — the ticket specifies the support email as the recovery path. If a self-serve revert link is added in future, it would be a separate ticket. * The body must be identical in content for both the old and new address sends (single source of truth). --- ## 🛡️ Admin Visibility & Audit Log every email-change event in the Admin Panel with the following fields: * Timestamp of the attempt. * Account ID. * Old email and new email. * Event type: **Success**, **OTP failure (exhausted/expired)**, or **Duplicate-collision attempt**. * Device identifier and approximate location. The log enables security pattern review and gives support an immediate record when a user emails in about an unauthorised change. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — Happy path: OTP succeeds, email updates, both addresses notified** * **Given** a signed-in user enters a valid new email different from their current one and not in use on any other account, * **When** they submit the change and enter the correct OTP delivered to the new email, * **Then** the account's email is updated to the new address, a confirmation email is sent to both the old and new addresses, and the change is logged in the Admin Panel. **Scenario 2 — OTP sent to NEW email only (not OLD)** * **Given** a user has initiated an email change, * **When** the OTP is dispatched, * **Then** it is sent only to the new email address — the old address is not used for OTP. **Scenario 3 — Same-as-current rejected before OTP** * **Given** a user enters their current email as the "new" email, * **When** they submit, * **Then** the request is rejected with "No change detected" and no OTP is sent. **Scenario 4 — Duplicate collision rejected before OTP** * **Given** a user enters a new email that is already in use on another account, * **When** they submit, * **Then** the request is rejected with "This email address is not available," no OTP is sent, and the attempt is logged. **Scenario 5 — Invalid format rejected before OTP** * **Given** a user enters an email in an invalid format, * **When** they submit, * **Then** standard format validation rejects the input and no OTP is sent. **Scenario 6 — OTP failure does not change the email** * **Given** a user has been sent an OTP for an email change, * **When** the user fails OTP entry per existing standard OTP rules (attempts exhausted or expired), * **Then** the account email remains unchanged, no confirmation emails are sent, and the failed attempt is logged. **Scenario 7 — Old-address notification supports the "wasn't me" path** * **Given** a user receives a confirmation email at their old address, * **When** the user reads the email, * **Then** the body clearly directs them to email support@gophergo.io if the change was not initiated by them. **Scenario 8 — Notification contains timestamp + device + location** * **Given** the confirmation emails are dispatched, * **When** a user reads either confirmation, * **Then** the email contains the timestamp (in local time), device identifier, and approximate city/region of the change. **Scenario 9 — Standard template for the respective app** * **Given** the change happens on Gopher, * **When** the confirmation emails are dispatched, * **Then** they use the Gopher standard email template. The same rule applies for Gopher Go using the Gopher Go template. **Scenario 10 — Abandoned mid-flow** * **Given** a user starts an email change and never enters the OTP, * **When** the OTP expires per existing OTP rules, * **Then** the email on the account remains the original address — nothing partial is persisted. **Scenario 11 — Both apps covered** * **Given** the feature has shipped, * **When** a user changes their email on either Gopher or Gopher Go, * **Then** the same OTP, dual-notification, and audit behaviour applies. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * The new email address must pass three pre-OTP checks (different from current, not in use elsewhere, valid format) before any OTP is sent. * The OTP is sent to the **NEW** email address only — verifying the user controls the destination mailbox. * OTP retry limits, expiry, and resend behaviour are inherited from the existing standard OTP mechanism — no bespoke rules. * The email on file is updated **only** after successful OTP entry. No partial state is persisted on abandonment or OTP failure. * On success, confirmation emails go to **both** the old and new addresses, using the **standard email template** for the respective app. * The confirmation email includes timestamp, device, and approximate location. * The confirmation email **does not** include a one-click revert link in this release — support@gophergo.io is the only recovery path. * Every email-change event (success, OTP failure, duplicate collision) is logged in the Admin Panel audit trail. * This applies to **both** apps (Gopher and Gopher Go). --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * All checks must run server-side at the email-change API. Client-side validation alone is bypassable. * The pre-OTP duplicate-email check must run **before** sending the OTP. Sending an OTP first and rejecting after on collision both wastes a delivery and leaks account-existence information via delivery timing. * The two confirmation emails should be dispatched in parallel from the same job/transaction so neither can succeed without the other. * The audit log entry should be written in the same transaction as the email update to guarantee record integrity. * Reuse the existing standard OTP flow and standard email templates wherever they live in the codebase — do not introduce a new OTP service or template variant for this surface. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Initiate an email change with a valid new email — confirm OTP arrives at the new address only. * Enter the OTP correctly — confirm the email updates, both old and new addresses receive confirmation emails, and the event is in the Admin Panel audit log. * Repeat with an invalid OTP / expired OTP — confirm the email does not change and the failure is logged. * Submit the current email as the "new" email — confirm "No change detected" with no OTP sent. * Submit an email that is in use on another account — confirm rejection with no OTP sent and a logged event. * Submit an invalid-format email — confirm rejection with no OTP sent. * Abandon the flow after submitting the new email but before entering the OTP — confirm the account email is unchanged. * Verify the confirmation email body contains the From / To, timestamp, device, and approximate location. * Verify the "if this wasn't you" line directs the user to support@gophergo.io. * Run on both apps (Gopher and Gopher Go) and both iOS and Android. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Depends on the existing standard email OTP mechanism being usable for this flow. * Depends on the existing standard email templates for Gopher and Gopher Go. * Depends on the device + approximate-location signal being available at the email-change API. If only one of those is reliably captured today, it can ship with what's available and the rest added later. * Out of scope for this ticket: a self-serve "Revert this change" one-click link in the old-address notification. If desired in future, that would be a separate ticket given the additional flow (token issuance, expiry, single-use enforcement) it requires.

Summary: Gopher App - Cancel A Scheduled Request Email
Description: When a scheduled request that has not yet started is cancelled, the Gopher currently receives no notification. The standard cancellation flow must be applied to all scheduled request cancellations: the cancelling party must provide a reason, a post-cancellation email must be sent to both parties, the cancellation reason must be communicated to the Gopher out of respect, and if the cancellation occurs within 24 hours of the scheduled start time, the Gopher must be given the opportunity to rate the Requestor. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher whose scheduled request has been cancelled before it started, ## 🎯 I want to be notified of the cancellation, understand the reason, and have the opportunity to rate the Requestor if the cancellation was last-minute, ## ✅ So that I am treated with respect, kept informed, and can provide feedback when a Requestor cancels at short notice. ## 💡 Context / Background * Scheduled requests are accepted in advance and have a defined start time. A Gopher who accepts a scheduled request plans around it. * Currently, if a scheduled request is cancelled before it starts, the Gopher receives no notification, no reason, and no opportunity to respond. * The standard cancellation flow — required reason entry and post-cancellation email to both parties — must apply consistently to all scheduled request cancellations, regardless of who cancels. * The cancellation reason must be included in the Gopher’s notification and cancellation email heading as a courtesy. * If the cancellation occurs within 24 hours of the scheduled start time, the Gopher is given the opportunity to rate the Requestor — acknowledging that a last-minute cancellation directly impacts the Gopher. ## 🔀 Cancellation Flow ### Step 1 – Cancellation Reason Required * When either party (Requestor or Gopher) cancels a scheduled request before it has started, they must select a cancellation reason before the cancellation is confirmed * The cancellation cannot be submitted without a reason ### Step 2 – Post-Cancellation Email to Both Parties * Once the cancellation is confirmed, an email is sent to both the Requestor and the Gopher * The email heading for the Gopher’s notification includes the cancellation reason so they understand why the request was cancelled * The cancellation reason is communicated with respect — it is surfaced as a heading or clear label, not buried in the email body ### Step 3 – Late Cancellation Rating (Within 24 Hours of Start Time) * If the cancellation occurs within 24 hours of the scheduled request start time, the Gopher is presented with the standard rating screen to rate the Requestor * If the cancellation occurs more than 24 hours before the start time, no rating screen is shown ## ❌ Current Behavior * When a scheduled request is cancelled before it starts, the Gopher receives no notification * No cancellation reason is required from the cancelling party * No post-cancellation email is sent to either party * The Gopher is not given an opportunity to rate the Requestor regardless of timing ## ✅ Expected Behavior * A cancellation reason is always required before a scheduled request cancellation can be confirmed * A post-cancellation email is sent to both the Requestor and the Gopher * The Gopher’s email/notification includes the cancellation reason prominently in the heading * If the cancellation is within 24 hours of the start time, the Gopher is shown the rating screen to rate the Requestor * If the cancellation is more than 24 hours before the start time, no rating screen is shown ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Cancellation reason is required * **Given** either party is cancelling a scheduled request before it has started * **When** they attempt to confirm the cancellation * **Then** a cancellation reason must be selected before the cancellation can be confirmed ### Scenario 2 – Post-cancellation email is sent to both parties * **Given** a scheduled request has been cancelled * **When** the cancellation is confirmed * **Then** a cancellation email is sent to both the Requestor and the Gopher ### Scenario 3 – Gopher’s notification includes the cancellation reason in the heading * **Given** a cancellation email has been sent to the Gopher * **When** the Gopher receives the email or notification * **Then** the cancellation reason is displayed prominently in the heading ### Scenario 4 – Rating screen shown when cancellation is within 24 hours of start time * **Given** a scheduled request is cancelled within 24 hours of its start time * **When** the cancellation is confirmed * **Then** the Gopher is shown the standard rating screen to rate the Requestor ### Scenario 5 – No rating screen when cancellation is more than 24 hours before start time * **Given** a scheduled request is cancelled more than 24 hours before its start time * **When** the cancellation is confirmed * **Then** no rating screen is shown to the Gopher ## ⚙️ Business Rules * A cancellation reason is always required for scheduled request cancellations — cancellation cannot be confirmed without one. * A post-cancellation email must always be sent to both the Requestor and the Gopher. * The Gopher’s cancellation notification must include the cancellation reason prominently in the heading — not buried in the body. * The 24-hour window is calculated from the time of cancellation to the scheduled request start time. * The Gopher rating screen is only triggered when the cancellation falls within the 24-hour window. * This flow applies to both Requestor-initiated and Gopher-initiated cancellations of scheduled requests. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * The cancellation reason selection screen must be added to the scheduled request cancellation flow for both Requestors and Gophers. * The post-cancellation email template must be updated to include the cancellation reason in the heading for the Gopher-facing version. * The 24-hour check must compare the cancellation timestamp against the scheduled request start datetime. * The Gopher rating screen must use the same standard rating component used elsewhere in the platform. * Related ticket: G40-111 (Allow A Gopher To Cancel A Scheduled Request Before It Has Started) — the cancellation flow introduced here must apply to both Requestor and Gopher-initiated cancellations. * Figma – Cancellation reason screen: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=14-3540 * Figma – Post-cancellation email: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=14-3667 ## 🧪 QA Notes * Cancel a scheduled request as a Requestor without selecting a reason — confirm cancellation is blocked. * Cancel a scheduled request with a reason selected — confirm post-cancellation email is sent to both parties. * Verify the Gopher’s email/notification shows the cancellation reason prominently in the heading. * Cancel a scheduled request within 24 hours of the start time — confirm the Gopher is shown the rating screen. * Cancel a scheduled request more than 24 hours before the start time — confirm no rating screen is shown. * Test cancellation initiated by both the Requestor and the Gopher — confirm the same flow applies in both cases. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher Go - Completed Request - Age-Restricted Protocol & No Show Feature Used - Payout Delay
Description: When a Gopher completes an age-restricted request, a structured verification flow must be followed before payout is released. The flow branches based on whether the recipient has TrustShield and whether the customer is present. If the Requestor is a no-show after a 10-minute timer, the payout is paused for 24 hours and the order enters a Confirmation Pending state until resolved by auto-completion or admin action. Additional no-show safeguards require GPS proximity verification, Requestor timer acknowledgment, and a fraud alert on no-show submission. This ticket incorporates all requirements from G40-267. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher completing an age-restricted request, ## 🎯 I want a clear, structured verification flow that confirms the recipient’s identity before my payout is released, ## ✅ So that age-restricted deliveries are completed compliantly, fraudulent payouts are prevented, and I am fairly compensated even in no-show situations. ## 💡 Context / Background * Age-restricted requests require identity verification before a Gopher can complete the order and receive payout. * The verification flow branches based on whether the recipient has TrustShield (pre-verified identity) or requires on-site ID capture. * If the recipient is not present, the Gopher triggers a 10-minute wait timer before being able to log a no-show. * To prevent fraudulent no-show submissions, three additional safeguards apply when a Gopher attempts to submit a Requestor No Show: GPS proximity to the drop-off location must be checked, the Requestor must have acknowledged the timer, and a fraud alert must be triggered on submission. * The admin team must be notified by email whenever a no-show payout hold is triggered so they can monitor frequency and enforce best practices. * Admins can manually complete a Confirmation Pending order to expedite payout if needed. ## 🔀 Complete Flow ### Step 1 – Gopher Marks Request Completed * Gopher taps Update to Completed * A popup modal is displayed * If Continue is tapped: GPS location and timestamp are logged in the admin panel * If "Do Not Show Me Again" was previously selected: tapping Update – Completed automatically triggers the GPS/timestamp log without the popup ### Step 2A – TrustShield Path (Recipient is Pre-Verified) * The TrustShield verification screen is displayed * Gopher taps ID and Identity Confirmed * Gopher is taken to the ratings screen * Figma reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=24-11580 ### Step 2B – No TrustShield Path (On-Site ID Capture Required) * The active camera screen is displayed for ID capture * Gopher captures the recipient’s ID * Gopher taps ID and Identity Confirmed * Gopher is taken to the ratings screen * Figma reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=24-11713 ### Step 2C – Customer Not Present Path * Gopher taps Set Timer – Customer Not Present * A 10-minute countdown timer begins * Requestor receives a banner notification and text message alerting them the Gopher is waiting — the Requestor must acknowledge this notification * Figma reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=24-11657 ### Step 3 – After 10-Minute Timer Expires * Gopher is shown two options: Confirm ID and Identity or Requestor No Show * If Confirm ID and Identity is tapped: flow proceeds to the ratings screen as normal * If Requestor No Show is tapped, three checks are performed: * **GPS proximity check** — the system checks whether the Gopher’s current location is within 50 feet (\~15 meters) of the drop-off location’s lat/long. This check is non-blocking — the Gopher can still proceed. However, if the Gopher is outside the 50-foot radius, a warning notification is shown: "You appear to be outside the expected drop-off location. Submitting a no-show from this location will trigger a fraud alert and may affect your payout speed if a dispute arises." The Gopher must confirm to proceed. * **Requestor acknowledgment check** — the Requestor must have acknowledged the timer notification before the No Show can be submitted. If the Requestor has not acknowledged the timer, the Gopher is shown a message indicating the Requestor has not yet confirmed receipt of the wait notification. * **Fraud alert trigger** — when a Requestor No Show is submitted, a fraud alert notification is automatically triggered and flagged in the admin panel for review, regardless of GPS proximity. * Once all checks are passed or acknowledged, payout is paused for 24 hours and the order enters Confirmation Pending status * Figma reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=24-11685 ### Step 4 – Confirmation Pending Resolution * The order remains in Confirmation Pending status for up to 24 hours * After 24 hours with no action, the order auto-completes and payout is released * An admin can manually complete the order in the admin panel at any time to expedite the payout * An automated notification email is sent to admin@gophergo.io when a no-show payout hold is triggered ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – GPS and timestamp are logged on completion * **Given** a Gopher taps Completed on an age-restricted request * **When** Continue is tapped on the popup (or Do Not Show Me Again was previously selected) * **Then** the Gopher’s GPS location and timestamp are logged in the admin panel ### Scenario 2 – TrustShield path completes to ratings screen * **Given** the recipient has TrustShield * **When** the Gopher taps ID and Identity Confirmed * **Then** the Gopher is taken to the ratings screen and payout is released ### Scenario 3 – No TrustShield path requires ID capture before completion * **Given** the recipient does not have TrustShield * **When** the Gopher reaches the completion step * **Then** the active camera screen is displayed for ID capture * **And** once ID and Identity Confirmed is tapped, the Gopher proceeds to the ratings screen ### Scenario 4 – Customer Not Present triggers 10-minute timer and Requestor notification * **Given** the recipient is not present when the Gopher arrives * **When** the Gopher taps Set Timer – Customer Not Present * **Then** a 10-minute countdown timer begins and the Requestor receives a banner notification and text message requiring acknowledgment ### Scenario 5 – Gopher within 50 feet can submit No Show without warning * **Given** the 10-minute timer has expired and the Gopher’s GPS is within 50 feet of the drop-off location * **When** the Gopher taps Requestor No Show * **Then** no location warning is shown and the no-show submission proceeds ### Scenario 6 – Gopher outside 50 feet receives a warning before submitting No Show * **Given** the 10-minute timer has expired and the Gopher’s GPS is more than 50 feet from the drop-off location * **When** the Gopher taps Requestor No Show * **Then** a warning is shown: "You appear to be outside the expected drop-off location. Submitting a no-show from this location will trigger a fraud alert and may affect your payout speed if a dispute arises." * **And** the Gopher must confirm to proceed * **And** the no-show can still be submitted after confirmation ### Scenario 7 – Requestor No Show triggers fraud alert * **Given** a Gopher submits a Requestor No Show * **When** the no-show is confirmed * **Then** a fraud alert is automatically triggered and flagged in the admin panel for review ### Scenario 8 – Requestor No Show triggers 24-hour payout hold * **Given** the Gopher has confirmed the no-show submission * **When** the no-show is processed * **Then** the payout is paused for 24 hours, the order enters Confirmation Pending status, and an automated email is sent to admin@gophergo.io ### Scenario 9 – Confirmation Pending auto-completes after 24 hours * **Given** an order is in Confirmation Pending status * **When** 24 hours pass with no admin action * **Then** the order auto-completes and the payout is released ### Scenario 10 – Admin can manually complete a Confirmation Pending order * **Given** an order is in Confirmation Pending status * **When** an admin manually marks the order as complete * **Then** the order completes immediately and the payout is released ahead of the 24-hour window ## ⚙️ Business Rules * Identity verification is mandatory for all age-restricted request completions — payout cannot be released without it. * TrustShield recipients bypass on-site ID capture; non-TrustShield recipients require active camera ID capture. * GPS location and timestamp must be logged in the admin panel upon every age-restricted completion. * The Customer Not Present timer is exactly 10 minutes. The Requestor must be notified immediately when the timer starts and must acknowledge the notification. * The GPS proximity check at No Show submission uses a 50-foot (\~15 meter) radius from the drop-off lat/long. It is non-blocking but triggers a warning and fraud flag if the Gopher is outside the radius. * Every Requestor No Show submission triggers a fraud alert in the admin panel regardless of GPS proximity. * Tapping Requestor No Show triggers a mandatory 24-hour payout hold — this cannot be bypassed by the Gopher. * Every Requestor No Show event must trigger an automated notification to admin@gophergo.io for monitoring. * Confirmation Pending orders auto-complete after 24 hours if no admin action is taken. * Admins may manually complete a Confirmation Pending order at any time to expedite payout. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * TrustShield status must be queryable at the time of completion to determine which verification branch to trigger. * GPS and timestamp logging must be tied to the Continue action on the completion popup and to the Update – Completed action when Do Not Show Me Again is set. * The 10-minute timer must send a push notification and SMS to the Requestor at the moment it starts, and must track whether the Requestor has acknowledged the notification. * GPS proximity at No Show submission must be calculated against the drop-off location lat/long stored on the request record. The 50-foot radius (\~15 meters) accounts for large apartment complexes and multi-unit buildings. * The fraud alert on No Show submission must create a flagged record in the admin panel linked to the order and the Gopher’s account. * Automated email to admin@gophergo.io must fire on every Requestor No Show event. * Admin panel must expose a manual Complete action on all Confirmation Pending orders. * This ticket incorporates all requirements from G40-267 (No Show Update – Driver Must Be Near Drop-Off Location). G40-267 can be closed as a duplicate. * Figma – Full flow: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=22-11153 * Figma – Completion popup / GPS log: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=37-12942 * Figma – TrustShield screen: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=24-11580 * Figma – No TrustShield / ID capture screen: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=24-11713 * Figma – 10-minute timer screen: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=24-11657 * Figma – No Show / post-timer options: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=24-11685 * Figma – Ratings screen: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=24-11751 ## 🧪 QA Notes * Test TrustShield path — confirm verification screen appears, ID and Identity Confirmed leads to ratings screen, and GPS/timestamp is logged. * Test No TrustShield path — confirm active camera launches for ID capture, ID and Identity Confirmed leads to ratings screen. * Test Customer Not Present — confirm 10-minute timer starts and Requestor receives banner and SMS notification. * After timer expires, attempt No Show with Gopher GPS within 50 feet of drop-off — confirm no location warning is shown and submission proceeds. * After timer expires, attempt No Show with Gopher GPS more than 50 feet from drop-off — confirm the location warning appears with the correct copy and the Gopher must confirm before proceeding. * Submit a No Show — confirm a fraud alert is flagged in the admin panel linked to the order and Gopher account. * Submit a No Show — confirm payout is paused, order enters Confirmation Pending, and admin notification email is sent to admin@gophergo.io. * Test Confirmation Pending auto-completion — confirm order completes and payout releases after 24 hours. * Test admin manual completion of a Confirmation Pending order — confirm payout is released immediately. * Verify GPS and timestamp are correctly logged in the admin panel for all completion paths. * Verify Do Not Show Me Again suppresses the popup on subsequent completions and still logs GPS/timestamp. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher App — Generic "Network Error" appears when accepting a Standard Gopher who is already engaged on another request
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Requestor attempting to accept a Standard Gopher who has already engaged on another active request, ## 🎯 I want to see a clear, actionable explanation instead of a generic "Network Error," ## ✅ So that I understand why the acceptance failed and can either wait, message the Gopher, or select a different one. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * Standard Gophers (NOT Gopher Pros) can only complete **one** request at a time. * If a Standard Gopher has already accepted an I'll select my worker or Bid on another active request, and the Requestor attempts to accept that same Gopher on a new request, the system currently returns a generic **"Network Error."** * This is misleading — it implies a connectivity issue rather than a business rule conflict, and gives the Requestor no path forward. * Gopher Pros are exempt from this rule and can engage in more than one request at a time. --- ## 🚫 Current Behavior * Requestor taps to accept a Standard Gopher who is already engaged on another active request. * System returns a generic **"Network Error"** message. * Requestor has no way of knowing why the acceptance failed or what to do next. --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior * Replace the generic "Network Error" with the following message: > **"The Gopher you're attempting to accept is currently engaged in an active request. Only Gopher Pros can engage in more than one request at a time. You can message the Gopher to ask when they expect to finish or select an alternative Gopher."** * The modal should include two CTAs: * **Message Gopher** — opens the in-app chat thread with that Gopher. * **Select Alternative Gopher** — returns the Requestor to the Gopher selection flow. * The generic "Network Error" should only appear for true network failures going forward. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — Standard Gopher already engaged** * **Given** a Standard Gopher has accepted an I'll select my worker or Bid on a previous request and is currently engaged, * **When** the Requestor attempts to accept that same Gopher on a new request, * **Then** the system displays the new explanatory message (not "Network Error") with Message Gopher and Select Alternative Gopher options. **Scenario 2 — Gopher Pro is never blocked** * **Given** a Gopher Pro is currently engaged on one or more active requests, * **When** the Requestor attempts to accept that Gopher Pro on a new request, * **Then** acceptance succeeds and no warning is shown. **Scenario 3 — Standard Gopher completes mid-flow** * **Given** a Requestor sees the new message because the Standard Gopher is engaged, * **When** the Gopher completes their active request and the Requestor retries acceptance, * **Then** acceptance succeeds with no warning. **Scenario 4 — Message Gopher CTA from the modal** * **Given** the new message modal is displayed, * **When** the Requestor taps "Message Gopher," * **Then** the Requestor is taken directly to the in-app chat thread with that Gopher. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * The engaged-Gopher check **must run server-side** before the acceptance API confirms the assignment — not client-side only. * A Standard Gopher is considered "engaged" while they have any request in an Active or In-Progress status. * The check applies regardless of how the Requestor surfaced that Gopher (I'll select my worker, Bid, or otherwise). * Gopher Pros are exempt from the check at all times. * The generic "Network Error" should never appear for this scenario — only for true network failures. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Reproduce by having one test Standard Gopher accept an I'll select my worker / Bid on Request A, then have a second Requestor attempt to accept that same Gopher on Request B. * Confirm the new message appears, and the generic "Network Error" does not. * Re-test with a Gopher Pro account to confirm no block is triggered. * Test the Message Gopher CTA opens the correct in-app chat thread. * Test the Select Alternative Gopher CTA returns the Requestor to the Gopher selection flow. * Test on both iOS and Android. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * The original screenshot in the previous description used a `blob:` URL that does not render for other users. **Please re-attach the screenshot directly to this ticket** so it persists. * This bug is tied to the Standard vs. Gopher Pro business rule — any future change to single-request vs. multi-request eligibility will need to update this check as well.

Summary: Gopher Go — Prevent deletion of the last payout card on file to avoid Stripe account loss
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher managing my payout cards in Gopher Go, ## 🎯 I want the system to prevent me from deleting my only card on file until I've added a replacement, ## ✅ So that my Stripe account and full payout history are preserved and my future payouts are not disrupted. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * Currently, when a Gopher removes all cards on file, the Stripe account itself is deleted along with the entire payout history. * This is unacceptable — the Stripe account and history must persist for the lifetime of the Gopher's account. * The fix is to block deletion of the only card on file until a replacement card has been added. --- ## 🚫 Current Behavior * A Gopher with only one payout card on file is able to delete that card. * Doing so removes the last card from Stripe, which causes Stripe to delete the connected account. * The deletion of the Stripe account wipes the full payout history. --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior * A Gopher must always have at least one payout card on file. * If a Gopher attempts to delete their only card on file, the deletion is blocked and the following modal is displayed: **Modal copy (per Figma):** * **Title:** Attention! * **Body:** Stripe requires a card on file in order to maintain your account history. Please add the new card and then you can delete the old one. * **Primary button:** Back * This rule applies regardless of card health — even an expired, declined, or otherwise invalid card cannot be removed until a replacement has been added. * Once a new card is successfully added, the original card may be deleted without restriction. * The Stripe account and payout history must remain intact through this entire flow. --- ## 🎨 Design Consideration / Open Question The modal as designed only includes a **Back** button — there is no primary CTA that takes the Gopher directly to the Add New Card flow. Worth aligning with design on whether to: * Add a primary **Add New Card** CTA that routes the Gopher to the card-add flow, with **Back** as a secondary action, **or** * Keep the modal as-is and require the Gopher to navigate to Add New Card manually. Recommendation is the first option — it reduces friction and aligns the user's next action with what the modal copy is asking them to do. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — Block deletion of the only card** * **Given** a Gopher has exactly one payout card on file, * **When** the Gopher attempts to delete that card, * **Then** the deletion is blocked and the "Attention!" modal is displayed. **Scenario 2 — Add new card, then delete the original** * **Given** a Gopher has dismissed the "Attention!" modal and added a valid new card, * **When** the Gopher returns to delete the original card, * **Then** the original card is successfully removed and the new card is the active payout method. **Scenario 3 — Normal delete with multiple cards** * **Given** a Gopher has two or more payout cards on file, * **When** the Gopher deletes any card that is not the only card, * **Then** the deletion succeeds without showing the modal, and at least one card remains on file. **Scenario 4 — Stripe account preservation** * **Given** a Gopher has only one payout card on file, * **When** the deletion is blocked by the modal, * **Then** the Gopher's Stripe account and full payout history remain intact and accessible. **Scenario 5 — Bad card cannot be removed without replacement** * **Given** a Gopher's only card on file is expired, declined, or otherwise invalid, * **When** the Gopher attempts to remove that bad card, * **Then** the deletion is still blocked and the modal is displayed. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * A Gopher must always have at least one payout card on file in Stripe — the count must never drop to zero through user action. * The last-card check must run server-side before the Stripe detach API is called, not client-side only. * The rule applies regardless of card health — valid, expired, declined, and otherwise invalid cards are all subject to the same block. * Deleting the Stripe account or wiping payout history is never an acceptable side effect of a user action. * The replacement flow must add the new card to the same Stripe account, not create a new one. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Reproduce by attempting to delete the only card on a test Gopher account — confirm the "Attention!" modal appears and the card is not removed. * Confirm in the Stripe dashboard that the connected account and payout history are still present after the attempt. * Add a second card, delete the original, and confirm the new card becomes the active payout method. * Test with an expired or otherwise invalid card as the only card — confirm the block still applies. * Test on both iOS and Android. * Re-attach the modal screenshot directly to this ticket (the existing `blob:` URL does not render for other users). * **Figma reference:** https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=7046-28668 --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * This bug is closely related to the payout-failure flow tickets — if a payout fails because the only card is invalid, the resolution path depends on the Gopher being able to add a replacement card. The block here ensures the Gopher cannot accidentally orphan their Stripe account during that recovery flow. * Design alignment is needed on the "Add New Card" CTA question raised above before development begins.
