Most of this ticket is wiring the Gopher's message UI into the existing photo functionality.

Summary: Gopher Go - Cost Adjustment - Allow .25 (15 min) Increments
Description: The Cost Adjustment hours field in Gopher Go currently only accepts whole integers. This forces Gophers to either round up to a full hour (unfair to the Requestor) or absorb uncompensated time (unfair to the Gopher) when the actual time worked falls between integer values. The field must be updated to support 15-minute increments (0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, etc.) so adjustments can accurately reflect actual time worked. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher Go worker submitting a Cost Adjustment, ## 🎯 I want to be able to adjust hours worked in 15-minute increments, ## ✅ So that I am fairly compensated for all time worked and the Requestor only pays for the time actually received — without forcing either party into an inaccurate full-hour rounding. ## 💡 Context / Background * The Cost Adjustment flow allows Gophers to submit a time-based adjustment after completing a request. * Currently, the hours field only accepts whole integers (1, 2, 3, etc.), with no way to represent partial hours. * This creates an unfair situation for both parties: Gophers who work an extra 30 or 45 minutes cannot accurately claim that time, and Requestors who are charged a full extra hour feel overcharged. * The solution is to support quarter-hour (15-minute) increments, represented as decimal values: 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, 1.25, and so on. ## 🔢 Increment Reference * `0.25` — 15 minutes * `0.50` — 30 minutes * `0.75` — 45 minutes * `1.00` — 1 hour * `1.25` — 1 hour 15 minutes * ...and so on in 0.25 increments ## ❌ Current Behavior * The hours field in Cost Adjustment only accepts whole integers * There is no way to submit a partial hour (e.g. 0.25, 0.50, 1.75) * Gophers who work between integer hours must either over-report or under-report their time ## ✅ Expected Behavior * The hours field in Cost Adjustment accepts values in 0.25 increments * The UI presents the selection in a clear format (e.g. stepper, picker, or input that snaps to valid increments) * The corresponding cost adjustment is calculated accurately based on the decimal hour value selected * Integer values (whole hours) continue to work as before ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Gopher can select a 15-minute increment * **Given** a Gopher is submitting a Cost Adjustment * **When** they enter or select a time value * **Then** values of 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, 1.25, 1.50, 1.75, 2.00 (and so on) are all selectable ### Scenario 2 – Cost adjustment calculates correctly for partial hours * **Given** a Gopher selects a partial hour value (e.g. 0.50) * **When** the Cost Adjustment is submitted * **Then** the cost is calculated accurately based on the decimal value and the applicable hourly rate ### Scenario 3 – Whole hour values continue to work correctly * **Given** a Gopher selects a whole hour value (e.g. 1.00, 2.00) * **When** the Cost Adjustment is submitted * **Then** the behavior is identical to the previous integer-only implementation ### Scenario 4 – Values outside valid increments are not accepted * **Given** a Gopher attempts to enter a value that is not a 0.25 increment (e.g. 0.33, 1.1) * **When** the value is entered * **Then** the field snaps to or prompts for the nearest valid 0.25 increment ## ⚙️ Business Rules * The minimum increment for Cost Adjustment hours is 0.25 (15 minutes). * Valid values are multiples of 0.25 only (0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, 1.25, etc.). * Cost calculations must use the decimal hour value multiplied by the applicable hourly rate. * Non-increment values (e.g. 0.33, 1.1) must not be accepted. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Update the hours input field UI to support 0.25 increments — consider a stepper control, a picker/scroll wheel, or a text input with validation that snaps to the nearest valid increment. * Update the cost calculation logic on the backend to accept and correctly compute decimal hour values. * Ensure the Requestor-facing cost summary reflects the adjusted decimal hour value accurately. * Validate that the admin panel and any reporting that references Cost Adjustment hours also handles decimal values correctly. ## 🧪 QA Notes * Select 0.25 (15 min) — confirm the cost adjusts to 25% of the hourly rate. * Select 0.50 (30 min) — confirm the cost adjusts to 50% of the hourly rate. * Select 0.75 (45 min) — confirm the cost adjusts to 75% of the hourly rate. * Select 1.00 (1 hour) — confirm behavior matches the previous integer implementation. * Select 1.75 (1 hour 45 min) — confirm the cost calculates correctly. * Attempt to enter a non-increment value (e.g. 0.33) — confirm it is rejected or snapped to the nearest valid increment. * Verify the Requestor-facing cost summary reflects the correct decimal hour value. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher Go — "ID and Identity Confirmed" button is unresponsive on Android, forcing admin override at order completion
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher completing an order that requires on-site ID capture, ## 🎯 I want the "ID and Identity Confirmed" button to respond and complete the order from my device, ## ✅ So that the Requestor is the actual party confirming completion and admin intervention is not required. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * This bug surfaces on the **on-site ID capture path** at order completion (the path used when TrustShield is not available, where the Gopher captures the recipient's physical ID). * TrustShield path is **not affected** — in that flow the customer's selfie and ID are auto-displayed for visual comparison and this button is not part of that path. * The downstream impact is significant: because the Gopher is unable to complete the order, admin must complete it from the Admin Panel, which means the Gopher and Requestor are no longer the audit-of-record parties for completion. This is real dispute exposure. --- ## 🚫 Current Behavior * The Gopher reaches the ID & Identity verification step at order completion. * The Gopher captures the recipient's ID and taps **ID and Identity Confirmed**. * The button **simply does not respond** — there is no error, no spinner, and no state change. The Gopher is stuck on the verification screen. * The order is only completed when an admin overrides from the Admin Panel. --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior * Tapping **ID and Identity Confirmed** marks the order as complete on the Gopher's device. * The Gopher is routed to the ratings screen. * The completion is attributable to the Gopher and the Requestor in the audit log — admin override is not required. * If the underlying call fails for any reason, a clear, actionable error is surfaced to the Gopher — the button never silently fails. --- ## 🔍 Reproduction * **Reference user:** 103692 * **Reference order:** 49331 * **Device confirmed affected:** Samsung Galaxy A36 * **Scope:** Reproduced on other Android devices as well — this is not isolated to the Galaxy A36. iOS appears unaffected based on reports to date. **Steps:** 1. Sign in as the Gopher and open an active order that requires on-site ID capture at completion. 2. Proceed through the completion flow until the ID & Identity verification step. 3. Capture the recipient's physical ID per the flow. 4. Tap **ID and Identity Confirmed**. 5. Observe — the button does not respond. The Gopher remains on the verification screen with no error, no spinner, and no path forward without admin intervention. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — Happy-path on-site ID capture completion (Android)** * **Given** a Gopher on an Android device has reached the on-site ID capture verification step, * **When** the Gopher captures the ID and taps **ID and Identity Confirmed**, * **Then** the order is marked complete on the device and the Gopher is routed to the ratings screen. **Scenario 2 — Bug condition resolved on previously affected devices** * **Given** the Gopher is using a Samsung Galaxy A36 or any other previously affected Android device, * **When** the Gopher completes the on-site ID capture verification step, * **Then** the order completes from the Gopher's device without requiring admin intervention. **Scenario 3 — iOS regression check** * **Given** the Gopher is using an iOS device, * **When** the Gopher completes the on-site ID capture verification step, * **Then** the order completes successfully (no regression introduced by the Android fix). **Scenario 4 — TrustShield path regression check** * **Given** the Gopher is completing an order via the TrustShield path, * **When** the Gopher proceeds through completion, * **Then** behavior is unchanged — the TrustShield comparison flow continues to work as before. **Scenario 5 — Backend failure must surface to the Gopher** * **Given** the underlying completion API call fails for any reason, * **When** the Gopher taps **ID and Identity Confirmed**, * **Then** a clear, actionable error is displayed to the Gopher — the button must never silently no-op. **Scenario 6 — No admin override required** * **Given** the Gopher has tapped **ID and Identity Confirmed**, * **When** the order moves to completed status, * **Then** the completion action is attributable to the Gopher and the Requestor in the audit log, not to an admin override. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * Order completion must always be initiated and confirmed from the Gopher's device — admin-panel completion is for exception handling only, not a routine fallback. * The **ID and Identity Confirmed** button must never silently no-op. It must either succeed, surface a clear error, or transition to a recoverable state. * Every audit log entry for order completion must reflect the actual party that confirmed (Gopher / Requestor / admin), to preserve the integrity of dispute records. * The fix must apply across all supported Android devices and OS versions, not be patched only for the Samsung Galaxy A36. * The fix is scoped to the on-site ID capture path — the TrustShield path is not in scope but must be regression-tested. --- ## 🔎 Investigation Pointers * The button is unresponsive with **no error and no spinner** — this rules out a backend timeout or visible failure path. The fault is likely client-side. * High-probability areas to investigate first: * The button's `onPress`/`onClick` handler on Android — may be unbound, intercepted, or gated by an unresolved permission state (camera, storage). * Any pending camera-release or image-write promise from the prior ID capture step that never resolves and is blocking the next action. * Android-specific touch event handling on the verification screen overlay. * State machine for the verification step — the screen may be in a state where the button is rendered but not enabled. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Reproduce on the reference device (Samsung Galaxy A36) before and after the fix. * Test across a range of Android devices and OS versions to confirm the fix is platform-wide, not device-specific. * Run a regression on iOS to confirm no behavior change. * Run a regression on the TrustShield path to confirm no behavior change. * Confirm the audit log records the Gopher (not an admin) as the completion actor after the fix. * Force a simulated backend failure to confirm the new error-surface behavior works as expected. * Re-attach the original screenshot directly to this ticket (the existing `blob:` URL does not render for other users). --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * This bug sits inside the on-site ID capture flow defined in **G40-165** (Step 2B). Any structural changes to that flow should account for the fix landing here. * This is a **high-severity bug** — each occurrence requires admin intervention and degrades the audit trail used for dispute resolution. Recommend prioritising accordingly.

Summary: Gopher Go — Automatically reject a Gopher's Stripe account when their account is deactivated
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher Admin, ## 🎯 I want a Gopher's (worker) Stripe account automatically rejected when their Gopher account is deactivated, ## ✅ So that I do not have to manually go into the Gopher Stripe admin panel to reject the payout account, and the existing duplicate-Stripe-detection logic continues to fire when that user attempts to create a new Stripe account with a new number. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * Today, when a Gopher's account is deactivated by an admin, the admin then needs to log into the Gopher Stripe dashboard and manually reject the user's connected Stripe account. * Automating this serves two purposes: 1. **Removes manual work** — admin doesn't have to touch the Stripe dashboard at all. 2. **Preserves the existing duplicate-detection logic** — the current system identifies when a previously-rejected Stripe account holder tries to create a new Stripe account with a different number. If the rejection step is ever skipped manually, that detection misses. * This ticket simply automates the rejection action so it runs as part of the deactivation event. ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=external&localId=null&id=&&collection=&height=null&occurrenceKey=null&width=null&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=blob%3Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fmedia.staging.atl-paas.net%2F%3Ftype%3Dfile%26localId%3Dnull%26id%3D964f732c-8e3e-4586-ad80-293fcf65917f%26%26collection%3D%26height%3D297%26occurrenceKey%3Dnull%26width%3D1095%26__contextId%3Dnull%26__displayType%3Dnull%26__external%3Dfalse%26__fileMimeType%3Dnull%26__fileName%3Dnull%26__fileSize%3Dnull%26__mediaTraceId%3Dnull%26url%3Dnull) ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=external&localId=null&id=&&collection=&height=null&occurrenceKey=null&width=null&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=blob%3Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fmedia.staging.atl-paas.net%2F%3Ftype%3Dfile%26localId%3Dnull%26id%3De33b5659-26d7-45b1-9a21-8e04c6de9145%26%26collection%3D%26height%3D523%26occurrenceKey%3Dnull%26width%3D1513%26__contextId%3Dnull%26__displayType%3Dnull%26__external%3Dfalse%26__fileMimeType%3Dnull%26__fileName%3Dnull%26__fileSize%3Dnull%26__mediaTraceId%3Dnull%26url%3Dnull) --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior * When an admin deactivates a Gopher account, the system automatically calls Stripe to reject that Gopher's connected Stripe account — performing the same action the admin currently does manually in the Stripe dashboard. * No manual admin step in Stripe is required. * If the Stripe rejection call fails (Stripe API unreachable, account state issue, etc.), the deactivation event is logged as a partial success and surfaced to admin for manual retry. The Gopher account deactivation itself **does not** roll back. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — Deactivation triggers automatic Stripe rejection** * **Given** an admin deactivates a Gopher account, * **When** the deactivation is confirmed, * **Then** the system calls Stripe and rejects the Gopher's connected Stripe account without any further manual admin action. **Scenario 2 — Stripe account state matches manual rejection** * **Given** the automatic rejection has run successfully, * **When** an admin inspects the Stripe dashboard for that user, * **Then** the connected account state is identical to what would have been produced by the existing manual rejection flow. **Scenario 3 — Duplicate-detection logic remains intact** * **Given** a Gopher's account has been deactivated and their Stripe account auto-rejected, * **When** that user later attempts to create a new Stripe account with a different number, * **Then** the existing duplicate-detection logic fires as it does today — no regression introduced. **Scenario 4 — Stripe failure does not block deactivation** * **Given** the Stripe API is unreachable or the rejection call fails, * **When** the admin deactivates a Gopher account, * **Then** the Gopher account is still deactivated, the partial failure is logged, and the admin is notified to retry the Stripe rejection manually. **Scenario 5 — Re-activation is out of scope** * **Given** a previously deactivated Gopher is later re-activated by an admin, * **When** the re-activation occurs, * **Then** this ticket makes no claim about what happens to the Stripe account — re-activation handling is out of scope. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * Deactivation is the **trigger** — every admin deactivation of a Gopher account fires the Stripe rejection. * The Stripe rejection action must match the action currently performed manually in the Stripe dashboard — no new Stripe state should be introduced. * A Stripe failure must not block the Gopher deactivation from succeeding. * The existing duplicate-Stripe-detection logic must continue to fire after the auto-rejection — no behaviour change there. --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * The Stripe rejection should run **server-side** as part of the deactivation event handler, ideally in an async job so a slow Stripe response doesn't delay the admin's confirmation. * Log every auto-rejection attempt (success or failure) with the account ID, Stripe account ID, timestamp, and result for audit. * On failure, surface a retry action to admin so the manual fallback path stays available. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Deactivate a test Gopher account and confirm the connected Stripe account is rejected automatically, matching the state produced by the manual flow. * Confirm the deactivation completes successfully even when the Stripe call is forced to fail (e.g., simulate Stripe API error) and the failure is logged + surfaced to admin. * Confirm an existing duplicate-Stripe-detection test still passes after the auto-rejection.

Summary: Gopher Go — Cap payout card nickname at 25 characters and truncate long existing names at display to prevent card info being cut off
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher viewing my Payout Account screen, ## 🎯 I want card nicknames to be bounded so they don't push the rest of the card info off-screen, ## ✅ So that I can always see my card details (last 4 digits, expiry, etc.) regardless of how long a nickname I gave the card. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * When a Gopher names a payout card with a long nickname, the layout on the Payout Account screen breaks: the nickname expands and pushes other card info (last 4, expiry, etc.) off the bottom of the visible area. * The fix is to enforce a sensible maximum character count on the nickname input, and to handle any existing over-limit names gracefully at display time. --- ## 🚫 Current Behavior * The card nickname input accepts an arbitrary number of characters. * When the entered nickname is long, the Payout Account display does not constrain it, and other card details below get cut off / pushed out of view. --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior * The card nickname input is capped at **25 characters maximum**. Users cannot enter a 26th character. * For any **existing** card names already saved at more than 25 characters: do not mutate the stored value. Truncate at display with an ellipsis (e.g., `My really long card na…`) so the layout is preserved. * All other card info (last 4, expiry, etc.) remains fully visible regardless of nickname length. * The 25-character limit applies to **every** input surface where a card nickname is entered or edited. * Truncation-at-display applies to **every** read surface where the nickname is shown. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — New card nickname is capped at 25 characters** * **Given** a Gopher is naming a new payout card, * **When** they attempt to type a 26th character, * **Then** the 26th character is not accepted; the input stops at 25. **Scenario 2 — Long names truncate at display with ellipsis** * **Given** a Gopher's payout card was saved previously with a 50-character nickname, * **When** the Gopher opens the Payout Account screen, * **Then** the nickname is displayed truncated to fit (with ellipsis), and all other card info below it is visible. **Scenario 3 — Stored value is not mutated** * **Given** a Gopher has a card saved with a 50-character nickname, * **When** the truncation-at-display logic renders the nickname, * **Then** the underlying stored value remains the full 50 characters — only the rendered string is truncated. **Scenario 4 — Card info below the nickname is always fully visible** * **Given** any nickname length (within or beyond the 25-character limit), * **When** the Payout Account screen renders, * **Then** the last 4 digits and expiry date are fully visible — no cut-off at the bottom of the card display. **Scenario 5 — Consistent across all input and display surfaces** * **Given** any surface in the app where a card nickname can be entered or shown, * **When** that surface is used, * **Then** the 25-character input cap and the truncate-at-display rule both apply. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * Card nickname maximum length is **25 characters** on input. * Existing card nicknames that exceed 25 characters are **not** mutated — they're truncated at display only. * All card details below the nickname must remain fully visible regardless of nickname length. * The character limit and truncation rules apply uniformly across every surface where the nickname is entered or displayed. --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * Apply the 25-character limit at the input component level (e.g., `maxLength={25}` on the relevant text input). * For display, use a CSS or component-level truncation pattern (`text-overflow: ellipsis` on a fixed-width container, or a JS-side substring with appended ellipsis). CSS truncation is preferable because it adapts to varying screen widths. * Audit all surfaces that render the card nickname to ensure consistent treatment. Common surfaces: Payout Account screen, payout method selector during checkout / payout flows, any settings screen showing saved cards. * No backend changes are required if the limit is enforced at the UI input level. The stored field's max length on the server can remain at whatever it is today — over-limit values are simply never created going forward. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Try to enter 26+ characters in the card nickname field — confirm input stops at 25. * Manually set a test card's stored nickname to 50 characters (via direct DB / API) and view the Payout Account screen — confirm the display truncates with ellipsis and the rest of the card info is fully visible. * Edit that test card via the UI and confirm the editable input is populated with the full stored 50-character value (or the cap-applied state once edited). * Walk every other surface that shows the card nickname and confirm consistent truncation behaviour. * Test on both iOS and Android, both narrow and tall device aspect ratios. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * No backend or data migration required — this is a UI-layer fix only. * Out of scope: any validation on the _content_ of the nickname (profanity filtering, special character restrictions, etc.). Only length is bounded by this ticket. ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=external&localId=null&id=&&collection=&height=null&occurrenceKey=null&width=null&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=blob%3Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fmedia.staging.atl-paas.net%2F%3Ftype%3Dfile%26localId%3Dnull%26id%3D13d3adb6-a8ae-4997-92bb-a4cd2f1f160a%26%26collection%3D%26height%3D855%26occurrenceKey%3Dnull%26width%3D412%26__contextId%3Dnull%26__displayType%3Dnull%26__external%3Dfalse%26__fileMimeType%3Dnull%26__fileName%3Dnull%26__fileSize%3Dnull%26__mediaTraceId%3Dnull%26url%3Dnull)

Summary: Prepare Gopher apps for Google Play requirement: Support 16 KB memory page sizes (Request extension + plan update)
Description: ### **As a** mobile engineering team responsible for releasing Android builds, ### **I want** to ensure the Gopher apps meet Google Play’s requirement to support **16 KB memory page sizes**, ### **So that** we can continue releasing app updates after the enforcement date and avoid release blocks on Android. ‌ ### **💡Context / Background** ‌ Google Play has introduced a new requirement for all apps targeting **Android 15+**: ‌ * Apps **must support 16 KB memory page sizes**. * This requirement affects **all new releases** starting **October 31, 2025**. * Gopher’s latest production release **does NOT** currently support 16 KB memory page sizes. * If we do not comply by the enforcement date, **we will be unable to release new app updates** on Google Play. ‌ Timeline provided by Google: ‌ * **Warning sent:** September 10, 2025 * **Enforcement deadline:** October 31, 2025 * **Optional extension deadline:** May 30, 2026 (if extension is requested) ‌ The team intends to **request the extension** to allow more time for the necessary updates, configuration changes, and QA validation. ‌ ### **📝 What needs to happen** ‌ 1. **Request deadline extension** from Google Play to push compliance requirement to **May 30, 2026**. 2. Review/update Android build tooling to support **16 KB page sizes**, following Google’s documentation. 3. Validate app bundle compliance for future releases. 4. Test app in a 16 KB environment. ‌ ### **📎 Reference links from Google Play Console** ‌ * Prepare app for devices with 16 KB page sizes * Test app in a 16 KB environment * Transition to 16 KB page sizes using Android Studio * Technical requirement announcement * App bundle checker (Google Play Console) ‌ ### **✅ Acceptance Criteria** ‌ **Scenario 1 – Extension requested** * **Given** Google Play provides an option to request a deadline extension, * **When** the team submits the extension request, * **Then** the compliance deadline should be extended to **May 30, 2026**, * **And** confirmation of the extension must be documented. ‌ **Scenario 2 – Compliance plan documented** * **Given** the new requirement impacts future releases, * **When** engineering reviews the updates needed to support 16 KB page sizes, * **Then** a documented plan must exist for updating the build pipeline, architecture, and test environments. ‌ **Scenario 3 – Monitoring future releases** * **Given** app updates will need to support 16 KB page sizes, * **When** new bundles/APKs are built, * **Then** they must be checked in the Play Console to confirm compliance prior to submission. ‌ ### **⚙️ Business Rules** ‌ * App updates **cannot** be released to Play Store after Oct 31, 2025 unless 16 KB support is implemented _or_ the extension is granted. * Only Android builds with confirmed support will be accepted. * Extension **must** be requested prior to the enforcement date. * No impact to iOS builds. ‌ ### **🔍 Example** ‌ | **Requirement** | **Current State** | **Expected State** | | --- | --- | --- | | 16 KB memory page size support | ❌ Not supported | ✅ Supported in future releases | | Ability to submit updates after Oct 31, 2025 | ❌ Blocked without fix | ✅ Allowed with extension or compliance | | Extension request | Pending | Submitted + confirmed | ‌ ### **🧠 Dependencies / Notes** ‌ * Android engineering may need updates to: * NDK version * Build flags * Gradle configs * Memory page alignment settings * QA must test with a **16 KB emulator or test device**. * Google Play Console access required to submit extension. * Engineering must monitor support tools and relevant Google updates. ‌ ### **🧪 QA Notes:** ‌ * After changes are made, upload a test bundle to Google Play’s internal track to verify the 16 KB support flag. * Validate app behavior in 16 KB environment (startup, memory allocation, background tasks). * Confirm compliance message is cleared from Google Play Console.

Summary: Gopher App - Fix navigation loop when accessing Payment Method → default card → Back/Close in Gopher Request
Description: ### **As a** Gopher App user managing my payment methods, ### **I want** to be able to open my default payment method and return to the previous screen or main navigation without getting stuck, ### **So that** I can manage my payment information normally and navigate the app without being forced into an infinite loop. ‌ ### **💡Context / Background** ‌ * In the **Gopher Request (Gopher App)**, users attempting to **add or view a payment method** are getting trapped in an **infinite navigation loop**. * Steps to reproduce: 1. Log in 2. Go to **Account → Payment Method** 3. Tap the **default payment method** 4. Attempt to tap **Back** or **Close**, or navigate using the bottom menu * **Expected:** user returns to previous screen or main app section. * **Actual:** app becomes stuck in a looping state and cannot exit the payment method screen. * The loop breaks **ONLY** if the user: * Edits or saves changes to the payment method, **OR** * Deletes the existing method and re-adds it * This behavior is incorrect and confusing, and blocks normal navigation. * Issue has been **reproduced on both Android and iOS**. * There is a video attached showing the full behavior. ‌ 📎 _Video reference:_ ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=96193adb-3a52-4e4f-b525-d045ab4f1cf2&&collection=&height=850&occurrenceKey=null&width=428&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) ‌ ‌ ### **✅ Acceptance Criteria (Given / When / Then)** ‌ **Scenario 1 – Back button returns user correctly** * **Given** a user opens their default payment method, * **When** they tap **Back**, * **Then** they must be returned to the previous screen (**Payment Method list**), not stuck in a loop. ‌ **Scenario 2 – Close button exits correctly** * **Given** the default card details screen is open, * **When** the user taps **Close**, * **Then** the modal/screen must dismiss properly. ‌ **Scenario 3 – Bottom navigation works normally** * **Given** the user is viewing a payment method, * **When** they tap on any item in the bottom navigation (Home, Inbox, Profile, etc.), * **Then** the app must navigate to that screen normally without looping. ‌ **Scenario 4 – No dependency on saving/deleting** * **Given** the user does **not** edit or save the payment method, * **When** they attempt to exit, * **Then** navigation must still work without requiring changes, deletion, or re-adding the card. ‌ **Scenario 5 – Behavior consistent across platforms** * **Given** the fix is applied, * **When** tested on Android and iOS, * **Then** the navigation flow must work identically and correctly in both environments. ‌ ### **⚙️ Business Rules** ‌ * Payment Method detail view must behave like a standard modal/screen with working exit paths. * Navigation controllers/routes should not override or trap user navigation. * Avoid forcing updates/edits as a requirement to navigate away. * Applies specifically to **Gopher Request (Gopher App)** but verify shared components aren’t reused improperly in Gopher Go. ‌ ### **🔍 Example** ‌ | **Action** | **Current Behavior** | **Expected Behavior** | | --- | --- | --- | | Tap Back | App loops and stays stuck | Returns to Payment Method list | | Tap Close | Loop continues; screen doesn’t dismiss | Modal closes normally | | Tap bottom menu | User still trapped in loop | Navigates to selected tab | | No edits made | User stuck | User should leave freely | ‌ ### **🧠 Dependencies / Notes** ‌ * Possible causes to investigate: * Misconfigured navigation stack * Recursively triggered screen mounts * Modal not being dismissed properly * Incorrect React Navigation or native navigation routing * Shared component used for payment flow with unsupported behavior * The video evidence should help recreate the exact sequence. * Ensure there is no hidden Stripe verification or redirect logic interfering. ‌ ### **🧪 QA Notes:** ‌ * Reproduce loop on both **iOS** and **Android**. * Test exiting the payment method screen with: * Back button * Close button * Bottom navigation * Device back button (Android) * Test after adding new payment method * Test after viewing but **without** editing or saving * Confirm no infinite loops occur in any path.

menu items to avoid triggering OS buttons. * This behavior should **not** happen: * The app’s bottom menu should be fully visible and **clear of the system navigation area**. * Issue is confirmed with Summary: Both Apps - Inbox - Message UI/UX - Fix long message text not wrapping inside the message input box
Description: ### **As a** user sending messages in the Gopher Request and Gopher Go apps, ### **I want** the text I type in the message input box to **wrap correctly within the visible boundaries**, ### **So that** my message stays readable, does not overflow outside the UI, and behaves like a standard messaging input field. ‌ ### **💡Context / Background** ‌ * In both apps (**Gopher Request** and **Gopher Go**), when a user types a long message in the **Inbox conversation input field**, the text does **not wrap** inside the text box. * Instead, the text **runs past the boundary** of the input container, visually overflowing outside the box. * This breaks the UI, makes messages hard to review before sending, and does not match the expected behavior of modern messaging input fields. * Text should automatically wrap to additional lines and expand the box height as needed (or scroll within the field, depending on design). ‌ 📎 _Screenshot reference :_ ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=c3d7c86f-1e24-4f5e-99a3-0a3339f5b265&&collection=&height=860&occurrenceKey=null&width=439&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) width of the input field, * **Then** the text must **wrap to the next line** instead of overflowing the box. ‌ **Scenario 2 – Input box expands or scrolls properly** * **Given** a user continues typing beyond multiple lines, * **When** the message grows, * **Then** the input box must follow the app’s intended behavior: * Expand vertically _or_ * Allow scrolling within the input depending on design spec (confirm with UI team). **Scenario 3 – No text overflow on iOS and Android** * **Given** this issue occurs in both apps, * **When** tested on iOS and Android devices, * **Then** text must stay fully contained inside the message input box. ‌ **Scenario 4 – Emoji, symbols, and long words handled correctly** * **Given** the user types emojis, symbols, or long uninterrupted words (e.g., URLs), * **When** these exceed the input width, * **Then** they must wrap or be truncated correctly according to native text-wrapping rules. ‌ ### **⚙️ Business Rules** ‌ * Message input must behave like a standard multiline text field. * No text should overflow outside the bounding box under any circumstances. * Input must remain editable and scrollable for longer messages. * Applies to **Gopher Request** and **Gopher Go**. * No functional changes to message sending — purely UI/layout correction. ‌ ### **🔍 Examples** ‌ | **Behavior** | **Current (Bug)** | **Expected** | | --- | --- | --- | | Long sentence | Text exceeds boundaries | Text wraps within box | | Multiple lines | Box does not expand | Box expands or scrolls | | Emojis / symbols | Sometimes overflow | Stay inside text area | ‌ ### **🧠 Dependencies / Notes** ‌ * Likely related to: * Missing flexWrap, multiline, or text container sizing rules * Incorrect height/width constraints * Incorrect or outdated component shared between both apps * Check if a shared message composer component is used. * Validate behavior with keyboard open vs. closed. ‌ ### **🧪 QA Notes:** ‌ * Test on iOS and Android. * Type long sentences, long words, emojis, numbers, spacing variations. * Confirm: * Text wraps correctly * Box expands or scrolls without breaking layout * No visual overflow * Test across multiple device sizes. * Validate behavior in **Gopher Request** and **Gopher Go** independently.

Summary: Both apps — Remove WordPress dependency for link redirection (direct navigation), behind a feature flag, with future analytics path documented
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Product and engineering team, ## 🎯 I want the app to navigate users **directly** to the intended destination links without relying on WordPress as an intermediary, ## ✅ So that we simplify the flow, reduce unnecessary dependencies, and keep the door open to re-introducing analytics tracking in the future via a cleaner approach. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * Currently, the application uses **WordPress as a middleman** to redirect users to certain destination links. * The original intent appears to have been to: * Use WordPress redirects to **track analytics events**, and * Act as a form of **dynamic link handling**. * In practice: * These links **did not fully work as true dynamic links**, and * The WordPress dependency adds unnecessary complexity and latency to navigation. * The short-term goal is to **remove WordPress from the redirect flow** and **navigate users directly** to the intended destination (in-app deep link or external URL). * Analytics tracking can be re-enabled in the future via a cleaner solution — without reintroducing WordPress. * This ticket is **low priority** and focused on cleanup, simplification, and future-proofing. --- ## 🔍 Scope **In scope:** all redirects that exist purely to **bounce through WordPress and back out** to a final destination (in-app deep links, external URLs, etc.). **Out of scope:** actual WordPress-hosted content (e.g., blog posts, marketing pages where the WordPress URL itself is the destination). Those continue to be served from WordPress as today. Applies to **both apps** (Gopher Request and Gopher Go) wherever the redirect logic exists. --- ## 📊 Example | Current Flow | Desired Flow | | --- | --- | | App → WordPress → Destination | App → Destination | | Analytics via WP redirect | Analytics via future native / SDK solution | | Extra dependency, added latency | Reduced dependency, faster navigation | --- ## 🛠️ Implementation Phases **Phase 1 — Inventory (part of this ticket)** Before any code changes, produce an inventory of every WordPress redirect endpoint currently in use by either app. The inventory should capture for each redirect: * The WordPress URL pattern. * The final destination type (in-app deep link, external URL, etc.). * The source(s) in the codebase that link to it (push notification payloads, email templates, in-app menus, share sheets, etc.). * Whether the redirect is currently consumed for analytics anywhere. This inventory becomes the work backlog for Phase 2 and the verification checklist for QA. **Phase 2 — Replace each redirect** For every redirect identified in Phase 1, replace the WordPress-routed link with a direct link to the final destination. Coordinate any push notification payload, email template, or shared-link generator updates so existing in-flight links continue to resolve correctly during the transition. **Phase 3 — Deprecate the WordPress redirect endpoints** Once all clients are updated and a reasonable observation window confirms no traffic is hitting the old redirect endpoints, deprecate and remove them on the WordPress side. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — Inventory delivered** * **Given** Phase 1 is complete, * **When** the inventory document is reviewed, * **Then** every WordPress redirect endpoint currently in use is listed with its destination type, source(s) in the codebase, and current analytics usage. **Scenario 2 — Direct navigation for in-app deep links** * **Given** a user taps a link that used to route through WordPress to an in-app deep link, * **When** the navigation is triggered, * **Then** the app navigates directly to the in-app destination without passing through WordPress. **Scenario 3 — Direct navigation for external URLs** * **Given** a user taps a link that used to route through WordPress to an external URL, * **When** the navigation is triggered, * **Then** the app opens the external URL directly (browser or in-app browser per existing behaviour) without passing through WordPress. **Scenario 4 — Push notification deep links** * **Given** a push notification payload contains a link that previously routed through WordPress, * **When** the user taps the notification, * **Then** the app navigates directly to the intended destination. **Scenario 5 — Email and shared-link generators updated** * **Given** the email templates and any shared-link generators are reviewed, * **When** a recipient clicks a link generated after this change, * **Then** the link routes directly to the destination, not through WordPress. **Scenario 6 — Actual WordPress-hosted content still works** * **Given** a link points to actual WordPress-hosted content (blog post, marketing page), * **When** the user taps it, * **Then** behaviour is unchanged — it continues to load from WordPress. **Scenario 7 — Feature-flagged rollback** * **Given** the new direct-link behaviour is behind a feature flag, * **When** the flag is disabled, * **Then** the app falls back to the previous WordPress-routed behaviour for the duration the flag is off. **Scenario 8 — No analytics regression beyond the known WP-redirect events** * **Given** analytics from the WordPress redirect step are intentionally going away, * **When** other analytics events are reviewed post-change, * **Then** no unrelated analytics are lost — only the WP-redirect-derived events are missing, as expected. **Scenario 9 — Both apps covered** * **Given** shared redirect logic exists across apps, * **When** the change ships, * **Then** Gopher Request and Gopher Go both navigate directly without WordPress for affected links. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * User navigation experience must be **faster and simpler** — latency from the removed hop should be measurably reduced (or at least never worse). * **No regression** to existing user flows — every link that worked before this change must still resolve correctly. * WordPress-derived analytics removal is **temporary and intentional**, not a loss of capability. Re-enablement is out of scope for this ticket. * The solution should be compatible with future marketing-driven tracking needs. * Applies to **both** apps (Gopher Request and Gopher Go) wherever shared redirect logic exists. * Actual WordPress-hosted content (blog posts, marketing pages) is **out of scope** — only the bounce-through-WordPress redirects are removed. * All new direct-link behaviour ships **behind a feature flag** for phased rollback. --- ## 🔎 Implementation Considerations * The inventory in Phase 1 is the critical first step — without it, the work is open-ended and easy to miss endpoints. * Server-side and client-side may both need updates: links generated server-side (push notification payloads, email templates) need their URL builders updated; client-side link handlers need to recognise the new direct format. * The feature flag should gate the **link-generation** side, not just the link-handling side. Otherwise old WP-routed links generated before the flip will still work, but the system is in a mixed state. * Plan for a transition window where both old (WP-routed) and new (direct) links coexist — in-flight push notifications and emails sent before the change will still arrive at users. * Recommend documenting whichever future analytics approach is chosen (native events, Universal Links + App Links, Branch / AppsFlyer / similar SDK) in a follow-up ticket so the architecture decision is recorded. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Walk through every redirect in the Phase 1 inventory and verify direct navigation works after the change. * Confirm no broken redirects or dead links for any of the inventoried endpoints. * Test all the source paths: in-app menus, push notifications (cold start, warm start, foregrounded), email links, share-sheet links. * Confirm WordPress-hosted blog/marketing content still loads correctly (out-of-scope regression check). * Validate behaviour on both iOS and Android. * Toggle the feature flag off and confirm fallback to WordPress-routed behaviour still works for the duration the flag is off. * Compare measured navigation latency before and after on a representative set of links — should be the same or faster. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * **Phase 1 inventory is a prerequisite for Phase 2.** Do not start the replacement work without it. * Confirm whether any current WordPress-redirect-derived analytics are still actively consumed downstream (dashboards, marketing reports, attribution). If anything is, document what is being lost so stakeholders are aware. * **Future analytics path:** Google fully sunset Firebase Dynamic Links on August 25, 2025 — it is not available as a replacement. Concrete alternatives to consider when analytics is re-enabled (out of scope for this ticket): * Native iOS **Universal Links** + Android **App Links** — OS-level deep linking, no third-party dependency. * Marketing attribution SDKs like **Branch** or **AppsFlyer** — if cross-platform attribution and campaign reporting are needed. * In-app analytics events fired at navigation time — simplest option if only basic event counts are required. * This ticket is **removal and preparation**, not full analytics implementation. Any analytics re-introduction should be its own ticket once marketing has decided the requirements.

Summary: Gopher App - Remove cost adjustment disclaimer after approval when final total is confirmed
Description: ### **As a** Gopher App user reviewing a request with a cost adjustment, ### **I want** the cost adjustment disclaimer to be removed once the adjustment is approved and reflected in the total, ### **So that** the displayed total clearly matches what will be charged to my bank without unnecessary or confusing messaging. ‌ ### **💡Context / Background** ‌ * Cost adjustments are typically **initiated and approved only once** in nearly all cases. * Currently, after a cost adjustment is approved, a **disclaimer remains visible at the bottom of the screen**, even though: * The adjusted amount is finalized, and * The **Total** shown already reflects the final charge. * This disclaimer can create confusion, as the customer’s bank will be charged exactly the amount shown in the updated **Total**. * This behavior is also applicable when: * A cost adjustment is approved that is **less than 20%**, * In these cases, the adjustment is already covered within the original authorization, and the disclaimer is no longer relevant. The UX can be simplified by removing the disclaimer once the adjustment is approved and the total is final. ‌ ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=43b27e26-46fb-49c4-8983-98db95625679&&collection=&height=512&occurrenceKey=null&width=438&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) ‌ ### **✅ Acceptance Criteria** ‌ **Scenario 1 – Disclaimer removed after cost adjustment approval** * **Given** a cost adjustment has been approved, * **When** the updated total is displayed, * **Then** the cost adjustment disclaimer at the bottom must be **removed**. ‌ **Scenario 2 – Total reflects final charge** * **Given** a cost adjustment is approved, * **When** the user views the request summary, * **Then** the **Total** amount must reflect the final charge that matches the customer’s bank transaction. ‌ **Scenario 3 – Applies to < 20% cost adjustments** * **Given** a cost adjustment approved that is **less than 20%**, * **When** the total is updated within the original authorization, * **Then** the disclaimer must also be removed, as no additional authorization is required. ‌ **Scenario 4 – No disclaimer shown once final state is reached** * **Given** the request is in a finalized state with an approved cost adjustment, * **When** the screen is displayed, * **Then** no warning or disclaimer related to cost adjustments should be shown. ‌ ### **⚙️ Business Rules** ‌ * Disclaimers are only relevant **before** a cost adjustment is approved. * Once approved, the total amount becomes the **source of truth**. * The UI should reflect the final, accurate charge without redundant warnings. * Applies to all request types that support cost adjustments. ‌ ### **🔍 Example** ‌ | **State** | **Current Behavior** | **Expected Behavior** | | --- | --- | --- | | Cost adjustment pending | Disclaimer shown | Disclaimer shown | | Cost adjustment approved | Disclaimer still visible | Disclaimer removed | | Adjustment < 20% approved | Disclaimer visible | Disclaimer removed | ‌ ### **🧠 Dependencies / Notes** ‌ * Confirm where the disclaimer visibility is controlled (frontend state vs backend flag). * Ensure disclaimer logic correctly differentiates between: * Pending adjustments * Approved adjustments * Verify no impact to scenarios where multiple adjustments could theoretically occur (even if rare). ‌ ### **🧪 QA Notes** ‌ * Test cost adjustment flows with: * Adjustment < 20% * Adjustment ≥ 20% * Verify disclaimer visibility before approval. * Confirm disclaimer disappears immediately after approval. * Validate Total matches final charged amount. * Test on both Gopher Request and Gopher Go apps if applicable.

Summary: BE - Both Apps - Simplify Sign-Up Process
Description: **UPDATE - When a user enters profile info up to the point of needing to enter the email OTP, IF the OTP is not entered during that session, AND/OR the email was the incorrect email, they are unable to update their email. The back button will take them to the SMS sign in.** **What should be happening is the back button takes the user to the profile info so the user can update their email address.** ## 🧑‍💻 As a backend system supporting user onboarding, ## 🎯 I want to assign user IDs early, persist onboarding progress, and enforce email verification before allowing access to the app, ## ✅ So that all users have a verified email and a consistent account state before entering the marketplace. ## 💡 Context / Background * The signup flow is being reorganized on the frontend (G40-7) to introduce a final email verification step and temporarily remove Sourcing Info. * To support this, the backend must generate and persist a user record immediately after phone OTP, track onboarding progress and account status, enforce email verification before Home access, support both new users and existing unverified users, and persist partial signup state across sessions. * This ticket focuses only on backend logic, APIs, and data handling. ## ⚙️ Backend Scope ### 1. User ID Assignment & Account State * Generate a user ID immediately after SMS/OTP verification * Save all subsequent profile data under this ID * Introduce or enforce an account status flag: `incomplete`, `email_verified`, `active` * Keep account in incomplete state until email OTP verification succeeds ### 2. Email Confirmation Enforcement * Add backend enforcement so users cannot reach Home unless email is verified * For existing users with unverified email: return a response that forces redirect to Email Verification * Implement/confirm: email OTP generation, OTP validation, and OTP resend logic * **Admin requirement:** Provide an email OTP link accessible from the Admin Panel and a "Did not receive?" / resend option via backend endpoint ### 3. Step-by-Step Auto-Save Support * Each Continue → step must persist partial profile data and update onboarding progress state * Allow users to close app, background app, and resume from last completed step ### 4. Remove Sourcing Info (Backend-Safe) * Do not delete any backend fields or dependencies * Allow signup to complete without sourcing info * Ensure backend does not block or error when sourcing data is missing ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### User ID & State * User ID created immediately after phone OTP * Account status remains incomplete until email verified * Profile data persists under same user ID ### Email Enforcement * Backend blocks Home access for unverified users * Existing users are flagged and redirected to email verification * Email OTP validation and resend endpoints work correctly ### Progress Persistence * Each signup step saves data incrementally * Signup resumes from last completed step after app restart ### Sourcing Info * Backend does not require sourcing info for signup completion * No regressions or errors due to skipped step ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * This is a foundational onboarding change. * Coordinate with frontend (G40-7) on status flags and redirect responses. * Analytics events are out of scope for this ticket. * Phase 2 (App Demo) will build on this state model. * Figma reference: https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=6158-28302 * **Related tickets:** G40-7 is the frontend counterpart to this ticket and must be implemented in parallel. G40-271 captures the bugs and regressions introduced when this sign-up enhancement was deployed in March 2026 — the issues in G40-271 are rooted in the backend account state and AWS sync logic scoped here. All three must be reviewed and resolved together.

Summary: Gopher App - Edit Request - Duplicate Issue
Description: **UPDATE - This feature has a bug. What is happening is IF a Requestor has a (Delivery - Convenience Store) request and selected “Edit,” and changes the delivery type to (Delivery - Age-Restricted) a new Order will be created and now the Requestors has 2 requests submitted.** **This should not happen. An EDIT ALWAYS keeps the same order number. The new info will be saved and a new “Updated Order Confirmation Email” will be sent.** <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://www.figma.com/design/H6THlatWvwT6ESI2j4MPTi/Final-Flows?node-id=159-6910&t=Z6fGIwPZPvrZmKuR-4</custom> ## **🧑‍💻 As a** Gopher Request user editing an existing request, ## **🎯 I want** to update my request and resubmit it without creating a duplicate, ## **✅ So that** my original request is correctly updated and rebroadcast without causing confusion or extra orders. ‌ ## **💡 Context / Background** ‌ * A Requestor submitted **Order #51334**, a scheduled **“Need a Ride”** request. * When using the **Edit** option to add special instructions (for 4 people): * The system created a **new request (Order #51335)** instead of updating the original. * This behavior results in: * Duplicate requests * Confusion for Gophers * Incorrect rebroadcasting * Based on the increasing number of duplicate requests, this appears to be an issue with the **Edit Request** functionality, likely treating edits as new submissions. ‌ ## **❌ Current Behavior** ‌ * Editing a request generates a **new order ID**. * The original request remains active. * Both requests may be broadcast simultaneously. ‌ ## **✅ Expected Behavior** ‌ * Editing a request updates the **existing order record**. * The updated request **continues using the same order ID**. * The request **remains active or returns to the matching state**, as appropriate. * Only **one active request** exists after an edit. ‌ ## **🔁 Steps to Reproduce** ‌ 1. Create a scheduled request (e.g., “Need a Ride”). 2. Submit the request successfully. 3. Navigate to the request details. 4. Tap **Edit**. 5. Modify request details (e.g., add special instructions). 6. Submit changes. 7. Observe a new request/order ID is created. ‌ ## **✅ Acceptance Criteria** ‌ ### **Scenario 1 – Edit updates existing request** * **Given** a Requestor edits an existing request * **When** the changes are submitted * **Then** the original request is updated * **And** no new order ID is created ‌ ### **Scenario 2 – Edited request continues matching without creating a new order** * **Given **a Requestor edits an existing request * **When **the changes are submitted * **Then **the system updates the original request record * **And **the original order ID is preserved * **And **the request continues through the normal matching flow ‌ ### **Scenario 3 – No duplicate active requests** * **Given** a request has been edited * **When** viewing active requests * **Then** only one active request is present ‌ ### **Scenario 4 – Scheduled requests handled correctly** * **Given** a scheduled request is edited * **When** the scheduled details are updated * **Then** the original scheduled request is modified * **And** no additional scheduled request is created ‌ ### **Scenario 5 – Request history integrity** * **Given** a request has been edited * **When** reviewing request history * **Then** edits are reflected on the original request record ‌ ## **⚙️ Business Rules** ‌ * Editing a request must **never create a new order**. * The existing request ID must be preserved. * Rebroadcasting must reference the same request. * Applies to all editable request types. ‌ ## **🧠 Dependencies / Notes** ‌ * Investigate whether the **Edit** flow reuses the Create Request endpoint. * Confirm backend behavior around request cloning vs updating. * Ensure idempotency for edit submissions. * Check edge cases for scheduled vs immediate requests. ‌ ## **🧪 QA Notes** ‌ * Test editing requests multiple times. * Validate no duplicate requests are created. * Verify scheduled request edits behave correctly. * Confirm correct behavior across iOS and Android. * Check logs for duplicate creation attempts.

Summary: Gopher Go — "Need A Ride" request details are missing rider count, special instructions, and trip distance on the Gopher view
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher Go user viewing an available "Need A Ride" request, ## 🎯 I want to see all of the information relevant to the price offered and the job needed — including rider count, special instructions, and trip distance — ## ✅ So that I can accept the request with confidence that I can perform everything required for the trip. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * When a "Need A Ride" request is submitted, the Requestor provides **Number of Riders** (required) and may provide **Special Instructions** (optional). The system also derives **Trip Distance** from the pickup → drop-off route. * None of these three values currently appear on the Gopher's request details view. * Without this information, the Gopher cannot confidently assess whether they can perform the trip (vehicle capacity, task constraints, effort vs. payout). --- ## 🚫 Current Behavior * A Gopher viewing an available "Need A Ride" request does **not** see: * Number of Riders * Special Instructions (when provided) * Trip Distance (in miles) * The Gopher must accept blind on these dimensions or message the Requestor to ask, which adds friction. --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior * The Gopher's request details view for "Need A Ride" must display all three values: * **Number of Riders** — always displayed (required at submission). * **Special Instructions** — displayed as full text when provided; the row is **omitted entirely** when not provided (not shown as an empty field). * **Trip Distance** — always displayed in **miles**, derived from the pickup → drop-off route. --- ## 📊 Missing-Fields Summary | Field | In Requestor flow? | In Gopher view today? | Should show? | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Number of Riders | Yes (required at submit) | No | Yes — always | | Special Instructions | Yes (optional) | No | Yes, when provided (full text, omit row when empty) | | Trip Distance (mi) | Derived from pickup → drop-off | No | Yes — always, in miles | --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 — All three fields visible on the Gopher request details view** * **Given** a "Need A Ride" request has been submitted with rider count, special instructions, and a valid pickup/drop-off, * **When** a Gopher views the request details before accepting, * **Then** Number of Riders, Special Instructions (full text), and Trip Distance (in miles) are all displayed. **Scenario 2 — Special Instructions omitted when not provided** * **Given** a "Need A Ride" request was submitted without Special Instructions, * **When** a Gopher views the request details, * **Then** the Special Instructions row is omitted entirely (not shown as an empty field). **Scenario 3 — Trip distance displays in miles** * **Given** a "Need A Ride" request with valid pickup and drop-off addresses, * **When** a Gopher views the request details, * **Then** Trip Distance is shown in miles, calculated from the pickup → drop-off route. **Scenario 4 — Number of Riders always displays** * **Given** Number of Riders is a required field at submission, * **When** a Gopher views the request details, * **Then** Number of Riders is always populated with the value submitted (1 or more). **Scenario 5 — Special Instructions display in full** * **Given** a "Need A Ride" request was submitted with a long Special Instructions value, * **When** a Gopher views the request details, * **Then** the full text of Special Instructions is displayed without truncation or a "see more" affordance. **Scenario 6 — Other request types unaffected** * **Given** a Delivery or Service request is being viewed by a Gopher, * **When** the Gopher views request details, * **Then** behavior for those request types is unchanged — no regression. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * The Gopher's request details view must surface every field that materially affects the Gopher's ability to perform the request — vehicle capacity (riders), task constraints (special instructions), and effort (distance). * Trip Distance is always displayed in **miles**, regardless of user locale. * Special Instructions are always displayed in **full**, with no truncation or "see more" affordance. * Optional fields with no value provided must be **omitted from the view entirely** — not shown as empty rows. * Trip Distance is derived from the pickup → drop-off route and is read-only. * This fix is scoped to the "Need A Ride" request type — Delivery and Service request types are not in scope but must be regression-tested. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Submit a "Need A Ride" request with all optional fields populated and confirm all three values appear on the Gopher view. * Submit a "Need A Ride" request with no Special Instructions and confirm the row is omitted, not shown empty. * Submit a "Need A Ride" request with a long Special Instructions value and confirm the full text displays without truncation. * Validate Trip Distance against a known pickup → drop-off route to confirm calculation accuracy. * Test on both iOS and Android. * Run regression on Delivery and Service request views to confirm no unintended changes. * Re-attach the "current state" and "should look" screenshots directly to this ticket (the existing `blob:` URLs do not render for other users) — or add a Figma link if a design exists. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * This bug is a data-passing gap between the Requestor submit flow and the Gopher request details view — the values exist in the request payload but are not being read or rendered on the Gopher side. * The fix may require both API and UI changes depending on whether the Gopher request details endpoint already includes these fields in its response.

Summary: [Research] Both Apps - Android - Motorola Edge Device Compatibility Issue
