Summary: Gopher GO – Cost Adjustment Validation – Confirm Lowered Price Before Applying
Description: ## **🧑‍💻 As a** Gopher Go user adjusting the cost of a service, ## **🎯 I want** to be warned when I lower the original service cost, ## **✅ So that** I can confirm the change is intentional and avoid accidental price reductions. ‌ ## **💡 Context / Background** ‌ * Gopher GO users are currently able to adjust the cost of a service to a **lower amount** without any confirmation. * This can result in: * Accidental price reductions * Confusion or disputes with Gophers * Unintended financial impact * To prevent mistakes, the system should prompt the user to **confirm intent** when a cost adjustment results in a lower price than the original amount. ‌ This validation should be implemented as a **new confirmation screen**, not a system alert, and should clearly guide the user to either proceed or revise the adjustment. ‌ ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=fcf6614e-752d-43e2-a9a2-3f7437933f68&&collection=&height=852&occurrenceKey=null&width=393&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null) <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=7354-8063&t=GOZZjysUayShUjWU-4</custom> ‌ ## **🛠️ Proposed Behavior** ‌ * When a Gopher Go user adjusts the service cost to a **lower amount**: * Display a **confirmation screen (modal or full screen)**. * The screen contains: * A clear warning message explaining the price reduction * Two actions: * **Continue** * **Edit Adjustment** ## **🔁 Navigation Logic** * **Continue** * Confirms the adjusted lower price * Navigates the user to the **Request Details** screen showing the updated request summary * **Edit Adjustment** * Returns the user to the **cost adjustment screen** * Allows them to modify the adjusted amount ## **❌ Current Behavior** ‌ * Lower price adjustments are applied immediately. * No confirmation or validation is shown. * Accidental changes cannot be easily caught before submission. ‌ ## **✅ Expected Behavior** ‌ * Lower price adjustments require explicit confirmation. * Users are clearly informed of the impact of the change. * Navigation paths are intuitive and prevent mistakes. ‌ ## **✅ Acceptance Criteria** ‌ ### **Scenario 1 – Detect lower cost adjustment** * **Given** a Gopher GO user edits the service cost * **When** the adjusted amount is lower than the original price * **Then** the system must trigger the cost adjustment confirmation screen ‌ ### **Scenario 2 – Show confirmation screen** * **Given** a lower cost adjustment is detected * **When** the confirmation screen is displayed * **Then** it must show: * A warning message about reducing the service cost * A **Continue** button * An **Edit Adjustment** button ### **Scenario 3 – Continue with adjustment** * **Given** the confirmation screen is shown * **When** the Gopher GO user taps **Continue** * **Then** the adjusted cost is applied * **And** the user is navigated to the **Request Details** screen ‌ ### **Scenario 4 – Edit adjustment** * **Given** the confirmation screen is shown * **When** the Gopher GO user taps **Edit Adjustment** * **Then** the user is returned to the **cost adjustment screen** * **And** the previously entered value remains editable ‌ ### **Scenario 5 – No validation for increased cost** * **Given** a Gopher GO user adjusts the cost to a higher amount * **When** the adjustment is submitted * **Then** no confirmation screen is shown ‌ ## **⚙️ Business Rules** ‌ * Validation applies **only when the adjusted cost is lower than the original cost**. * Confirmation must occur **before** applying the change. * The confirmation screen must not be dismissible without choosing an action. * Applies to all request types that support cost adjustments. * No backend pricing logic should change as part of this ticket. ‌ ## **🧪 QA Notes** ‌ * Test lowering cost from multiple entry points. * Verify navigation paths for both buttons. * Ensure cost value persists correctly when returning to edit. * Confirm no confirmation appears for increased costs. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Admin Panel - App Notifications / Inbox Message - Bulk Message Sending Error
Description: The admin panel has lost the ability to send SMS , Inbox messages and push notifications to multiple users simultaneously. Two compounding issues exist: (1) selecting multiple users via comma-separated IDs and attempting to send results in an error, and (2) sending to large volumes of users causes major platform disruption. Both must be resolved so admins can reliably send push notifications, inbox messages, and SMS messages to any number of users without errors or server impact. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Admin Panel user, ## 🎯 I want to be able to send push notifications, inbox messages, and SMS messages to any number of selected users without errors or platform disruption, ## ✅ So that I can reliably communicate specific and targeted messages to individual users or large user groups at any time. ## 💡 Context / Background * The admin panel previously supported sending push notifications and SMS messages to multiple users by entering their user IDs separated by commas. * This functionality has regressed — users can be selected but attempting to send results in an error. * A separate but related issue exists where sending to a large volume of users causes a major disruption to the platform, indicating the bulk send logic is not properly queued or rate-limited on the backend. * The platform must support bulk sends of push notifications, inbox messages, and SMS messages to any number of users without negative server impact. ## ❌ Current Behavior * Entering comma-separated user IDs and attempting to send a push notification or SMS results in an error — the message is not delivered * Users can be selected in the admin panel but the send action fails * Sending to a large number of users causes major platform disruption * There is no rate-limiting, queuing, or batching in place to handle high-volume sends safely ## ✅ Expected Behavior * Admins can select multiple users via comma-separated IDs and successfully send a push notification, inbox message, or SMS to all selected users * No error is thrown during the send process regardless of the number of recipients * Bulk sends of any volume are processed without causing server disruption or platform degradation * Messages are queued and dispatched in batches on the backend to protect server stability ## ⚠️ Issue Breakdown ### Issue 1 – Multi-User Send Error * Selecting multiple users via comma-separated IDs and attempting to send any message type returns an error * This is a regression — the feature previously worked and must be restored * Affects: push notifications, inbox messages, and SMS ### Issue 2 – Bulk Volume Causes Platform Disruption * Sending to a large number of users simultaneously overwhelms the server and causes major platform disruption * The backend send logic must be re-architected to use a queue-based or batch processing approach * This is a critical scalability blocker — the platform must handle bulk sends of any size safely ## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce ### Issue 1 – Multi-User Send Error 1. Navigate to Admin Panel → App Notifications or Inbox Message. 2. Enter multiple user IDs separated by commas. 3. Compose a push notification, inbox message, or SMS. 4. Attempt to send. 5. Observe the error message and confirm the message was not delivered. ### Issue 2 – Bulk Volume Platform Disruption 1. Navigate to Admin Panel → App Notifications or Inbox Message. 2. Select a large volume of users. 3. Attempt to send a push notification, inbox message, or SMS. 4. Observe platform degradation or disruption. ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Multi-user send succeeds without error * **Given** an admin enters multiple comma-separated user IDs and composes a message * **When** the admin sends the message * **Then** the message is successfully delivered to all selected users * **And** no error is thrown ### Scenario 2 – All three message types work for multi-user sends * **Given** an admin selects multiple users * **When** the admin sends a push notification, inbox message, or SMS * **Then** all three message types are successfully delivered to all selected users without error ### Scenario 3 – Large volume bulk send does not disrupt the platform * **Given** an admin sends a message to a large number of users * **When** the send is triggered * **Then** messages are queued and dispatched in batches * **And** no platform degradation, errors, or service disruption occurs * **And** all recipients receive the message ### Scenario 4 – Single user send is unaffected by the fix * **Given** an admin sends a message to a single user * **When** the message is sent * **Then** the message is delivered successfully with no change to the existing single-user send behavior ## ⚙️ Business Rules * The admin panel must support sending push notifications, inbox messages, and SMS to any number of users without error. * Bulk sends must never cause platform disruption regardless of recipient volume. * Backend bulk send processing must use a queue-based or batch approach to protect server stability. * Single-user send behavior must remain unchanged. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Identify the regression that broke multi-user comma-separated ID sending and restore the original behavior. * Re-architect the bulk send backend to use a message queue (e.g. SQS, Redis queue, or equivalent) so large sends are processed asynchronously in batches rather than synchronously in a single request. * Implement rate limiting and/or batch size caps on the notification dispatch layer to prevent server overload. * Ensure the fix applies to all three message types: push notification, inbox message, and SMS. * Consider adding a send progress indicator in the admin panel for large bulk sends so admins can confirm the send is processing. ## 🧪 QA Notes * Test sending a push notification, inbox message, and SMS to 2–5 comma-separated user IDs — confirm successful delivery with no error. * Test sending to a large volume of users (e.g. 100, 500, 1000+) — confirm messages are delivered and no platform disruption occurs. * Test all three message types for both small and large recipient lists. * Test single-user send — confirm behavior is unchanged. * Monitor server health and platform stability during large bulk send tests. * Verify all recipients receive the message when sent in bulk.

Summary: Twilio SMS + Email backup escalation — exclude Gophers with no completed request in the last 6 months (with 3-month new-Gopher carve-out)
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher operations system escalating a stalled request via Twilio SMS and Email backup, ## 🎯 I want to exclude Gophers who have not completed any request in the last 6 months from receiving the escalation, ## ✅ So that the escalation only reaches Gophers likely to act — reducing Twilio cost, recipient noise, and the rate of escalations that fail to convert because they hit dormant accounts. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * The Twilio SMS + Email **backup** communication is an **escalation channel** — it fires only when a submitted request has had **no activity for 5 minutes**. * ⏱️ **Timer anchor (per G40-44):** the 5-minute window starts **AFTER the last broadcast notification has been sent** — i.e., after the final tier of the \[G40-44\] broadcast cadence has been notified — **not** at request submission. While the broadcast cadence is still sending notifications to tiers, the 5-minute inactivity clock has **not** started. * The current escalation logic identifies a candidate list of nearby/qualified Gophers and sends them an SMS and Email in addition to (or in place of) the standard push. * This ticket adds a **dormancy filter** on top of that existing candidate list: any candidate Gopher with **no completed request in the last 6 months** is removed from the SMS + Email send. * Rationale: dormant Gophers are statistically unlikely to act on an escalation. Excluding them reduces Twilio spend, recipient fatigue, and stale-broadcast noise without changing the underlying candidate selection. --- ## 🔁 Where this filter inserts 1. Request is submitted; the **\[G40-44\] broadcast cadence** notifies worker tiers in sequence. 2. The **last broadcast notification** is sent (final tier reached). 3. **5 minutes elapse with no activity**, timed from that last-notification moment (**not** from submission). 4. Existing escalation logic identifies the candidate list of nearby/qualified Gophers (e.g., 50 Gophers). 5. **NEW — dormancy filter:** remove any candidate Gopher who (a) registered more than 3 months ago AND (b) has no completed request in the last 6 months. (e.g., 15 removed.) 6. Twilio sends SMS and Email to the remaining filtered list (e.g., 35 Gophers). --- ## 🧮 Worked Example * Existing selection logic identifies **50** candidate Gophers for an escalation. * Of those, **15** have no completed request in the last 6 months **and** registered more than 3 months ago. * Dormancy filter excludes those 15. * Final escalation list: **35** Gophers receive the SMS + Email backup. --- ## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 0 — Timer starts after last broadcast notification** * **Given** a request whose broadcast cadence (G40-44) is still notifying worker tiers, * **When** the final tier's notification has just been sent, * **Then** the 5-minute inactivity countdown starts at that moment — not at submission — and the escalation only fires if 5 minutes then pass with no activity. **Scenario 1 — Dormant Gopher excluded** * **Given** a Gopher registered more than 3 months ago and has no completed request in the last 6 months, * **When** a 5-minute-inactivity escalation fires and the recipient list is finalised, * **Then** that Gopher is excluded from both the SMS and the Email send. **Scenario 2 — Brand-new Gopher (within first 3 months) included** * **Given** a Gopher registered less than 3 months ago and has no completed requests yet, * **When** an escalation fires, * **Then** that Gopher is included — the dormancy filter only applies after the Gopher has been registered for 3 months. **Scenario 3 — Gopher between 3 and 6 months with no completions** * **Given** a Gopher registered between 3 and 6 months ago and has no completed requests yet, * **When** an escalation fires, * **Then** that Gopher is **excluded** — they are past the 3-month carve-out and have no qualifying activity in the 6-month window. **Scenario 4 — Recently-active Gopher included** * **Given** a Gopher has at least one completed request within the last 6 months, * **When** an escalation fires, * **Then** that Gopher is included regardless of when they originally registered. **Scenario 5 — Auto-reactivation on next completion** * **Given** a previously excluded Gopher completes a new request, * **When** the next escalation occurs, * **Then** the Gopher is automatically re-included — no manual reactivation is required. **Scenario 6 — Cancelled and refunded orders do not reset the clock** * **Given** a Gopher's only recent activity is a cancelled, refunded, expired, or admin-overridden order, * **When** the dormancy filter evaluates their record, * **Then** that activity does not count toward the 6-month window and the Gopher remains excluded. **Scenario 7 — Worked example math** * **Given** the existing selection logic returns 50 candidates and 15 are dormant per this rule, * **When** the new filter is applied, * **Then** exactly 35 Gophers receive the SMS + Email backup. **Scenario 8 — Existing selection logic unchanged** * **Given** the existing escalation candidate-selection logic was producing a candidate list of N Gophers before this change, * **When** the new filter is applied, * **Then** the underlying selection logic still produces the same N candidates — the filter only narrows that list, never expands or reorders it. --- ## 📐 Business Rules * ⏱️ **Timer anchor:** the 5-minute inactivity window is measured from when the **last broadcast notification was sent** (final tier of the \[G40-44\] cadence), **not** from request submission. If the cadence is still sending notifications, the 5-minute clock has not started. * The dormancy filter only runs on the **5-minute inactivity escalation path** — it does not affect push, marketing, transactional, or admin-triggered sends. * The 6-month window is rolling — measured from the escalation timestamp, not a fixed calendar date. * **"Completed"** means a request reached the successful Completed status. Cancelled, refunded, expired, and admin-overridden orders do **not** count toward the activity window. * Gophers who registered **less than 3 months ago** are exempt from the filter — they have not had enough time on the platform to accumulate a completion history. * Exclusion is automatic and reversible — the moment an excluded Gopher completes a new request, they re-enter the eligible pool for future escalations. * The filter is **additive** to existing escalation logic — it does not change which Gophers are considered candidates, only which of those candidates are sent to. * The filter must be applied to both the SMS and Email channels uniformly — a Gopher excluded from SMS is also excluded from Email for the same escalation. --- ## 📊 Observability * Each escalation should log: total candidates identified by the upstream selection logic, count excluded by the new dormancy filter, and final send count. * These counts should be retrievable in the admin panel or via an internal metrics endpoint to validate the filter is operating as expected and to track Twilio cost reduction over time. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Seed test Gophers with a known mix of registration dates and completed-request dates: * Registered 2 months ago, no completions — expect **included** (within 3-month carve-out). * Registered 4 months ago, no completions — expect **excluded** (past carve-out, no qualifying activity). * Registered 1 year ago, completed a request 5 months ago — expect **included**. * Registered 1 year ago, completed a request 7 months ago — expect **excluded**. * Registered 1 year ago, only cancelled/refunded orders in last 6 months — expect **excluded**. * Submit a test request, let the broadcast cadence finish sending its last tier notification, then allow it to sit idle for 5 minutes from that point, and verify the SMS and Email recipient lists match the expected filtered set. * Complete a request as a previously excluded Gopher and confirm they are re-included in the next escalation. * Verify the observability counts are written correctly for at least one production-scale escalation. * Confirm the underlying recipient-selection logic was not modified — its output count should be identical to pre-change for the same input. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * **Relates to \[G40-44\] (Broadcast Cadence).** The "last notification sent" event that starts this 5-minute timer is the final-tier notification defined in G40-44. If G40-44's cadence changes, revisit this timer anchor. * This filter depends on access to two data points per Gopher: registration date and most-recent successful completion date. Both should already exist in the Gopher record; if either is not currently exposed to the escalation service, that integration work is in scope. * Recommend deploying behind a feature flag so the filter can be toggled off quickly if it over-restricts in production.

Summary: Gopher App – Request Again must carry over original order's address + photos/media
Description: > 🔄 **RE-SCOPED 2026-07-02.** The original “Request Again behaves like Edit / errors on submit” bug **and** the forward/back-compat rules are **already solved by design in the new build** (`gopher-request.html` → `raFast` / `__startRequestAgainFast`): it builds a brand-new request via `resetFlowState()` + selective prefill, lands on Review, never references the prior order ID, silently ignores unknown old fields, and leaves new fields blank for validation. Code trace is in the comments. **The only remaining go-forward work is what this ticket now covers: carry the original order's ADDRESSES _and_ PHOTOS/MEDIA into the pre-filled Request Again.** --- ## 🎯 Requirement When a user taps **Request Again** on a completed order, the new pre-filled request must carry over from the original order: 1. **Pickup & drop-off address(es)** — every stop, in the same order. 2. **Photos / media attachments.** …as **editable** pre-filled values on the NEW request (the user may change or remove them before submitting). ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria **AC1 — Address carry-over.** Given a completed Delivery/Restaurant order with pickup + drop-off addresses, when the user taps Request Again, then the new request pre-fills all pickup and drop-off stops in the same order, the user can edit them, and submission succeeds. _(Fixes the Jan-23 QA defect where the drop-off address failed to load — order #496.)_ **AC2 — Media carry-over.** Given a completed order that included photos/media, when the user taps Request Again, then those photos are attached to the new request (shown, removable) and ride through on submit. _(Fixes the Jan-23 QA defect where the image did not carry over — compare orders #493 vs #494.)_ **AC3 — Copies, never linked.** The carried-over address/media are **copies** on the new order; editing or removing them must never touch the original completed order, which remains immutable. **AC4 — Graceful when absent.** If the original order had no media (or an address type the current flow doesn't use), the corresponding field is simply left blank — no error. (Consistent with the already-implemented S6/S7 compat behavior.) ## 🛠️ Where this plugs in (go-forward) * **Data / backend:** the completed-order (history) record must **persist the original order's addresses and media** so Request Again can read them. _(In today's prototype the history record —_ `DASH_DATA.previousRequests` — stores only date/id/category/details/worker/amount/rating/breakdown; it has no address or media fields, which is exactly why raFast doesn't yet carry them.) * **Front-end:** extend `__startRequestAgainFast(prev, selected)` (`gopher-request.html:14320`) to map `prev` pickup/drop-off stops into `state.pickupStops` / `state.dropoffStops` — the `__startDealRequest` bridge already does exactly this pattern — and to attach `prev` media. **NOTE:** the flow `state` currently has **no** media/photos field at all; production must add one. ## ✅ Already handled — do NOT rebuild (verified in the new build) * New order, new order ID, no edit, no linkage to the prior order (orig. S1/S2/S5). * No “Update it” / edit copy anywhere (orig. S3). * Submits without error on valid input (orig. S4). * Obsolete cached fields silently ignored (orig. S6) and new required fields left blank + validated (orig. S7) — both inherent to the selective-prefill + land-on-Review pattern. --- ## 📋 Original bug context (historical — for reference) Reported as: “Request Again” behaved like Edit Request (UI said “Update it”), referenced the previous order ID, and errored on submit instead of creating a new order. Repro: Account → Request History → Completed → Request Again → submit. Core behavior was QA-approved in STAGE/QA on 2026-01-29 (new order ID generated, original unchanged, no linkage, iOS + Android). The two carry-over defects above were raised in the 2026-01-23 QA return and are what remains.

Summary: Both Apps - Implement mandatory app update for future major release versions
Description: **As a** user running an outdated major version of the app, **I want** to be clearly prompted to update, **So that** I can continue using a stable, compatible version of the app without encountering bugs or broken functionality caused by version mismatches. --- ## 💡 Context / Background * Users are not currently required to upgrade to the latest version of the app. * This results in multiple app versions in circulation, inconsistent behavior, already-fixed bugs appearing to still exist, and increased support and QA complexity. * To stabilize behavior and ensure compatibility, a **force-update mechanism** is needed for **future major release versions** (defined as an increment to the first version number, e.g. 3.x → 4.0). * Minor and patch versions (e.g. 4.0 → 4.1, 4.1.0 → 4.1.1) are **not** subject to forced updates unless explicitly configured. * Applies to both **Gopher Request** and **Gopher Go** apps. --- ## 🛠️ Proposed Solution ### Backend * Introduce a version-check endpoint that receives the device's installed app version, compares it against the **minimum required version** stored in the database, and returns whether the version is **Allowed** or **Blocked**. * Minimum required version must be configurable per platform (iOS / Android) **without requiring an app redeployment**. * Backend is the source of truth for version enforcement. ### Frontend * On app launch (and on resume from background), call the version validation endpoint. * If the backend returns **Blocked**: * Display a **full-screen, non-dismissible modal**. * Block access to all app functionality. * Show clear messaging explaining an update is required. * Include a primary CTA: **Update App** — deep-linked to the correct App Store (iOS App Store or Google Play). * If the backend returns **Allowed**, the user proceeds normally. * Define fallback behavior for network failure during version check (e.g. allow entry but retry on next launch). --- ## ❌ Current Behavior * Users can continue using outdated versions indefinitely. * Incompatible versions coexist in production. * Unexpected bugs and behavior occur due to version mismatches. --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior * Users on outdated major versions are blocked from using the app until they update. * Only compatible versions are allowed to interact with the system. --- ## 🔁 Acceptance Criteria **Scenario 1 – Version validation on app launch** * **Given** the app is launched * **When** the app sends its current version to the backend * **Then** the backend validates it against the platform-specific minimum required version and returns Allowed or Blocked **Scenario 2 – Force update required** * **Given** the user's app version is below the required major version * **When** the backend responds with Blocked * **Then** a full-screen, non-dismissible update modal is displayed * **And** the user cannot access any app functionality **Scenario 3 – Redirect to App Store** * **Given** the force update modal is displayed * **When** the user taps **Update App** * **Then** they are deep-linked to the correct App Store for their platform (iOS or Android) **Scenario 4 – App usage allowed** * **Given** the user's app version meets or exceeds the minimum required version * **When** the app completes version validation * **Then** the user proceeds normally into the app with no interruption **Scenario 5 – Platform-specific enforcement** * **Given** the user is on iOS or Android * **When** version validation occurs * **Then** enforcement uses the minimum version configured specifically for that platform **Scenario 6 – Network failure during version check** * **Given** the app launches with no or poor network connectivity * **When** the version check endpoint cannot be reached * **Then** the app applies the defined fallback behavior (to be specified by the team before development begins) --- ## ⚙️ Business Rules * Forced updates apply to **major version increments only** unless explicitly overridden in the backend config. * The update modal must **not** be dismissible under any circumstance. * Version requirements must be configurable per platform without an app redeployment. * Backend is the single source of truth — the app must not make local version decisions. * Applies to both **Gopher Request** and **Gopher Go**. --- ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Backend must expose a reliable, low-latency version-check endpoint. * Frontend must perform version validation early in the app lifecycle, before any navigation. * Fallback behavior for network failure must be defined and agreed upon before development begins. * Modal copy must be clear and user-friendly — coordinate with design/copy team. --- ## 🧪 QA Notes * Test with app versions below, equal to, and above the required major version. * Verify the modal blocks all navigation and cannot be dismissed. * Confirm the Update App CTA deep-links correctly on both iOS and Android. * Test on both platforms with good, poor, and no network connectivity. * Validate that backend version config changes take effect without an app release.

Summary: Gopher Go – Standard Gophers Lose Active Requests After App Restart
Description: > ⛔ **CANCELED 2026-07-02 — not reproducible / mis-framed.** A code investigation of the legacy backend found **no tier-based cause** — the active/available-orders path has zero Standard-vs-Pro logic, and reported by a former junior dev, not by real workers. Full analysis + the exact endpoint, the 3 possible per-order causes, and the one-line fix are in the comments. Re-open only if a worker actually reproduces active-request loss. --- ## 🧑‍💻 As a Standard Gopher working on an active request, ## 🎯 I want my in-progress requests to persist after closing and reopening the app, ## ✅ So that I can complete jobs normally and Requestors are not blocked from closing or resolving requests. ## 💡 Context / Background * During development and testing of **ticket G40-58**, a bug was reported affecting **Standard Gophers**: when a request reaches **“In Progress”**, closing and reopening the app made the active request disappear. * _(Investigation update — see comments: the code shows no tier-based behavior; this path re-fetches the gopher's active orders by_ `gopher_id` regardless of app session or tier.) ## ❌ Reported Behavior * Standard Gopher accepts a request → status **In Progress** → closes/reopens app → active request no longer visible → job cannot be completed → Requestor cannot close. ## ✅ Expected Behavior * Active requests persist across app restarts; all Gopher tiers see identical in-progress behavior; requests remain actionable until completion or cancellation. ## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce (as reported) 1. Log in as a Standard Gopher. 2. Accept a request. 3. Confirm **In Progress**. 4. Close the app. 5. Reopen. 6. Observe the active request is missing. ## 🧠 Notes * Originally discovered while working on G40-58; parity rule was: Pro vs Standard differences apply only **before** acceptance (early notifications, multi-job), never once a request is in progress. The code review confirms in-progress retrieval is already tier-agnostic.

Summary: Admin Panel / Go App – Research: Requestor Unable to Complete Request (Infinite Loop on Completion)
Description: ## **🧑‍💻 As a** support and engineering team, ## **🎯 I want** to investigate why some Requestors are unable to complete or update their requests in the app, ## **✅ So that** requests can be closed normally without requiring admin intervention and users do not experience blocking loops. ‌ ## **💡 Context / Background** ‌ * Two reported cases were identified where: * The Requestor **could not complete or update their request in the app** * Support had to rely on the **Admin Panel** to verify request status and manually complete the request * While the Admin Panel allows completion on behalf of the user, this: * Creates a poor user experience * Increases support load * Masks an underlying issue in the app flow * This appears to be a **bug**, not expected behavior, and requires investigation. ‌ ## **🐞 User-Reported Behavior (Exact Feedback)** ‌ > “I’ve done two runs for you guys. Both times, I go and update my request status, everything is fine, but I go to complete it, I get the picture ID, I click complete, it kicks me back to the screen where I click update request. > I click complete, I capture the ID, I hit complete, it kicks me back to the screen where I hit update request… in a giant loop.” ‌ This indicates: ‌ * The completion action is not persisting * The request state may not be transitioning correctly * The UI repeatedly returns the user to the previous step ‌ ## **❌ Current Behavior** ‌ * Requestor attempts to complete a request in the app * The app: * Prompts for required completion steps (e.g., picture ID) * Appears to accept the action * Then returns the user to the **Update Request** screen * The user is stuck in an **infinite loop** * Request cannot be completed from the app * Support must intervene via the Admin Panel ‌ ## **✅ Expected Behavior** ‌ * Requestor can complete the request successfully in the app * Completion steps persist after submission * Request transitions to **Completed** state * Admin intervention is not required for normal request completion ‌ ## **🔁 Steps to Reproduce** ## **(based on report)** ‌ 1. Requestor opens an active request. 2. Taps **Update Request**. 3. Selects **Complete**. 4. Captures and submits required picture ID. 5. Taps **Complete**. 6. App navigates back to **Update Request** instead of completing. 7. Loop repeats indefinitely. ‌ ## **🔍 Scope of This Ticket (Research)** ‌ * Identify whether the issue is caused by: * Frontend state handling * Backend request status transitions * Validation failures not surfaced to the user * Version mismatch or partial update * Review Admin Panel vs App request state discrepancies. * Determine whether this affects: * Specific request types * Specific app versions * Specific platforms (iOS / Android) * References : <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://admin.gophergo.io/booking/53628</custom> and <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-1">https://admin.gophergo.io/booking/53623</custom> (requests 53628 and 53623 respectively) ## **✅ Acceptance Criteria** ‌ ### **Scenario 1 – Identify root cause** * **Given** a request that cannot be completed in the app * **When** engineering reviews logs, request state, and UI flow * **Then** the root cause of the completion loop is identified ‌ ### **Scenario 2 – Confirm admin vs app state mismatch** * **Given** a request stuck in the completion loop * **When** comparing Admin Panel data with app state * **Then** any inconsistencies are documented ‌ ### **Scenario 3 – Reproduce or rule out** * **Given** the reported behavior * **When** testing similar request flows * **Then** the issue is either reproducible or clearly scoped to specific conditions ‌ ### **Scenario 4 – Actionable follow-up** * **Given** the investigation is complete * **When** findings are documented * **Then** a follow-up bug ticket is created (if needed) with clear fix scope ‌ ## **⚙️ Business Rules** ‌ * Requestors must be able to complete their own requests without support. * Admin Panel should be a fallback, not the primary resolution path. * Request completion must be idempotent and state-safe. ‌ ## **🧠 Dependencies / Notes** ‌ * Requires access to: * App logs * Backend request lifecycle logs * Admin Panel state * Coordinate with support to identify: * Request IDs * App versions * Platform used * This ticket is **investigation-only**; fixes should be logged separately. ‌ ## **🧪 QA Notes** ‌ * Attempt to reproduce with: * Different request types * Different app versions * Validate completion flow end-to-end. * Confirm no loops exist after investigation/fix.

Summary: BUG - Gopher Request - Expired Request Still Showing Active Could Not Accept A Bid
Description: ## **🧑‍💻 As a** Requestor accepting a Gopher’s bid, ## **🎯 I want** to successfully accept a bid and proceed normally, ## **✅ So that** I can connect with the Gopher and continue the request flow without the app breaking. ‌ ## **💡 Context / Background** ‌ A support case reported that a Requestor encountered a **white screen** when attempting to accept a bid. ‌ **Details:** ‌ * Requestor ID: **116470** * Gopher ID: **35670** * Order ID: **52823** * Request expiration date: **Feb 7** * Issue reported on: **Feb 10** ‌ The request had already passed its expiration date. ‌ A recent enhancement was released to **prevent requests from expiring when a bid is pending**, which may be related to this behavior. This suggests a potential **regression or edge case** involving request expiration + bid acceptance. ‌ ## **❌ Current Behavior** ‌ * Requestor attempts to accept a Gopher’s bid. * The app displays a **white screen**. * User cannot proceed or complete the action. * Multiple attempts and workarounds fail. ‌ ## **✅ Expected Behavior** ‌ * Requestor can accept a bid normally. * If the request is in a special state (expired / pending acceptance), the app should: * Handle the state correctly, or * Show a clear error message * The app should never display a blank/white screen. ‌ ## **🔁 Steps to Reproduce (Suspected Flow)** ‌ 1. Create a request that reaches or passes its expiration time. 2. Ensure a Gopher bid exists on the request. 3. Attempt to accept the bid after the original expiration date. 4. Observe the white screen. ‌ ## **🔍 Scope of Investigation** ‌ * Validate request lifecycle state for expired requests with pending bids. * Review recent enhancement: * “Do not let a request expire with pending offers” * Identify whether: * Frontend is not handling a new state * Backend is returning an unexpected state/response * Navigation fails when request is in an invalid or new status * Confirm whether this affects: * Only expired requests * Only bid acceptance * Both iOS and Android ## **✅ Acceptance Criteria** ‌ ### **Scenario 1 – Accepting bid does not crash app** * **Given** a request has a pending bid * **When** the Requestor attempts to accept the bid * **Then** the app does not display a white screen * **And** the user can continue the flow normally ‌ ### **Scenario 2 – Expired request edge case handled** * **Given** a request has passed its expiration date but has a pending bid * **When** the Requestor attempts to accept the bid * **Then** the system handles the request state correctly * **And** the user receives a valid next step or message ‌ ### **Scenario 3 – No regression from expiration enhancement** * **Given** the new “do not expire with pending offers” enhancement * **When** users interact with affected requests * **Then** no blank or broken screens occur ‌ ## **⚙️ Business Rules** ‌ * The app must never present a blank/white screen. * Expired or edge-case states must be handled gracefully. * Request lifecycle logic must remain consistent after recent enhancements. ‌ ## **🧠 Dependencies / Notes** ‌ * Likely related to recent request expiration enhancement. * Requires log review for order **52823**. * Coordinate with backend and mobile teams. * May require follow-up fix ticket after root cause is confirmed. ‌ ## **🧪 QA Notes** ‌ * Test: * Expired requests with bids * Non-expired requests with bids * iOS and Android * Validate navigation and state transitions.

Summary: Infrastructure – Elastic Beanstalk Platform Upgrade & EC2-Classic → VPC Migration
Description: ‌ ## **🧑‍💻 As a(n)** engineer / platform / DevOps team, ## **🎯I want** to upgrade our Elastic Beanstalk environment to a supported platform branch and migrate from EC2-Classic to VPC, ## **✅ So that** we can continue making environment changes, receive security updates, and avoid deployment failures. ‌ ## **💡 Context / Background** ‌ While attempting to update environment variables, AWS is blocking changes and displaying warnings indicating that the environment is running on **retired infrastructure**. ‌ Key issues identified: ‌ 1️⃣ **Retired Elastic Beanstalk Platform** * The environment uses a **retired platform branch** * Retired branches: * No longer receive maintenance or security updates * Are not supported by AWS * AWS recommends upgrading immediately. Reference: <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/platforms-glossary.html</custom> ‌ 2️⃣ **Environment Created in EC2-Classic** * The environment was originally created using **EC2-Classic** * AWS now supports **VPC-only networking** * When attempting to update environment variables: * Elastic Beanstalk tries to implicitly migrate networking * The update fails This is likely the **root cause of deployment and configuration update failures**. ‌ ## **❌ Current Behavior** ‌ * Updating environment variables fails. * Infrastructure attempts to migrate automatically and errors out. * Platform branch is unsupported and not receiving updates. * Deployment and configuration changes are becoming risky/unreliable. ‌ ## **✅ Expected Behavior** ‌ * Environment runs on a **supported Elastic Beanstalk platform branch**. * Environment is fully migrated to **VPC networking**. * Environment variables and configuration changes can be applied normally. * Deployments succeed without platform or networking conflicts. ‌ ## **🔍 Scope of Work** ‌ This ticket includes **research, planning, and migration execution**. ‌ ### **Phase 1 – Assessment** * Identify: * Current platform branch * Current runtime versions * Current EC2-Classic configuration * Document: * Dependencies and risks * Downtime considerations * Required AWS resources (VPC, subnets, security groups) ### **Phase 2 – Migration Strategy** * Plan migration to: * Supported Elastic Beanstalk platform * VPC networking * Determine safest approach: * Blue/Green deployment (recommended) * New environment creation + cutover ### **Phase 3 – Implementation** * Create new EB environment in VPC. * Configure networking and security groups. * Deploy application to new environment. * Validate functionality. * Cut over traffic (DNS swap). ‌ ## **✅ Acceptance Criteria** ‌ ### **Scenario 1 – Platform branch upgraded** * **Given** the new environment is created * **When** the application is deployed * **Then** the environment runs on a supported Elastic Beanstalk platform ‌ ### **Scenario 2 – Environment migrated to VPC** * **Given** the migration is complete * **When** reviewing networking configuration * **Then** the environment runs fully inside a VPC ‌ ### **Scenario 3 – Configuration updates succeed** * **Given** the new environment is active * **When** updating environment variables * **Then** the changes apply successfully without errors ‌ ### **Scenario 4 – Successful deployment** * **Given** traffic is routed to the new environment * **When** users access the application * **Then** the app behaves as before with no regression ‌ ## **⚙️ Business Rules** ‌ * Must move off retired platform immediately. * Must use VPC networking (AWS requirement). * Prefer **zero-downtime migration**. * Old environment should remain available until cutover validation is complete. ‌ ## **🧠 Dependencies / Notes** ‌ * Requires AWS access and DevOps coordination. * Recommend Blue/Green deployment to minimize risk. * Verify: * Environment variables * S3 / RDS / external service connectivity * SSL / DNS configuration * Old environment should be decommissioned only after validation. ‌ ## **🧪 QA Notes** ‌ * Validate: * App loads and core flows work * Environment variables apply successfully * Deployments succeed * Monitor logs after cutover.

Summary: BUG - Both Apps - Previous messaging enhancement removed privacy and terms regulation for blocking phone numbers and $ amounts in messaging.
Description: A previous messaging enhancement regressed the content filtering rules that block phone numbers and dollar amounts from being shared in in-app messaging. These rules must be restored. When a user attempts to send a message containing a phone number or dollar amount, the flagged characters are replaced with an equal number of `#` characters — the message is still sent, but the sensitive content is masked. Additionally, any message where filtering is triggered must be permanently tagged as **Flagged** in the admin panel for compliance review and reporting. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher App or Gopher Go user sending a message, ## 🎯 I want phone numbers and dollar amounts to be automatically masked in messages, ## ✅ So that the platform remains compliant with privacy and terms of service regulations, off-platform transactions are prevented, and admins can identify and act on repeat violators. ## 💡 Context / Background * The Gopher platform restricts the sharing of phone numbers and dollar amounts in in-app messaging to protect users and prevent off-platform transactions. * This content filtering was previously in place and functioning correctly. * A recent messaging enhancement removed or bypassed this filtering logic, causing a regression. * The masking behavior replaces each flagged character with a `#` — preserving message length while obscuring the sensitive content. * All in-app messages are stored in the admin panel under **Messages**, each with a unique Message ID (e.g. Messages/64437), along with fields for Order ID, Title, From, To, Message content, and Created At. * A new **Flagged** field must be added to each Message ID record. Any message that triggers content filtering — even if the user edits and resends — must be permanently tagged **Yes** in this field. * The Flagged field must also be visible and filterable when admins run message reports, enabling identification of serial violators. * This applies to both the Gopher App and Gopher Go. ## ❌ Current Behavior * Phone numbers and dollar amounts can be sent in messages without any filtering or masking * The content filtering rules introduced previously are no longer active * Users can freely exchange phone numbers and negotiate dollar amounts outside of the platform's payment flow * No Flagged field exists on Message ID records in the admin panel * Admins have no way to identify or report on messages that contained blocked content ## ✅ Expected Behavior * When a message containing a **phone number** is sent, each digit/character of the phone number is replaced with a `#` character on a 1:1 basis * When a message containing a **dollar amount** is sent, the dollar sign and numeric characters are replaced with `#` characters on a 1:1 basis * The rest of the message is delivered as written — only the flagged content is masked * Masking applies in real time before the message is delivered to the recipient * Any message that triggers content filtering is permanently tagged **Flagged: Yes** on its Message ID record in the admin panel — regardless of whether the user edits or resends * The **Flagged** field is visible in the Message ID detail view and filterable/reportable in the admin Messages report * This behavior applies across all messaging flows in both apps ## 🗒️ Masking Examples * User sends: `Call me at 555-867-5309` Recipient sees: `Call me at ###-###-####` Admin panel Message ID: **Flagged = Yes** * User sends: `I'll do it for $50` Recipient sees: `I'll do it for ###` Admin panel Message ID: **Flagged = Yes** * User sends: `Just let me know when you can fit this in` Recipient sees: `Just let me know when you can fit this in` Admin panel Message ID: **Flagged = No (not set)** ## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce 1. Open a conversation in either app. 2. Send a message containing a phone number (e.g. "Call me at 555-867-5309"). 3. Observe the phone number appears unmasked in the delivered message. 4. Send a message containing a dollar amount (e.g. "I'll do it for $50"). 5. Observe the dollar amount appears unmasked in the delivered message. 6. Navigate to the admin panel Messages section and locate the Message ID for either message. 7. Observe there is no Flagged field on the record. ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Phone number is masked * **Given** a user sends a message containing a phone number * **When** the message is delivered * **Then** each character of the phone number is replaced with a `#` on a 1:1 basis * **And** the remainder of the message is delivered as written * **And** the Message ID in the admin panel is tagged Flagged: Yes ### Scenario 2 – Dollar amount is masked * **Given** a user sends a message containing a dollar amount * **When** the message is delivered * **Then** the dollar sign and numeric characters are replaced with `#` characters on a 1:1 basis * **And** the remainder of the message is delivered as written * **And** the Message ID in the admin panel is tagged Flagged: Yes ### Scenario 3 – Message with no flagged content is unaffected * **Given** a user sends a message with no phone number or dollar amount * **When** the message is delivered * **Then** the message is delivered exactly as written with no modifications * **And** the Message ID is not tagged as Flagged ### Scenario 4 – Message containing both phone number and dollar amount * **Given** a user sends a message containing both a phone number and a dollar amount * **When** the message is delivered * **Then** both the phone number and the dollar amount are independently masked * **And** the rest of the message is delivered as written * **And** the Message ID is tagged Flagged: Yes ### Scenario 5 – Flagged tag is permanent regardless of edits or resends * **Given** a message triggered content filtering and was tagged Flagged: Yes * **When** the user edits and resends the message without the blocked content * **Then** the Message ID retains the Flagged: Yes tag * **And** the tag is never removed or reset ### Scenario 6 – Flagged messages are visible and filterable in admin reporting * **Given** an admin runs a message report in the admin panel * **When** the report is generated * **Then** the Flagged column is visible in the report results * **And** the admin can filter results by Flagged: Yes to identify users with repeated violations ## ⚙️ Business Rules * Phone numbers and dollar amounts must never be transmitted unmasked through the in-app messaging system. * Flagged characters are replaced with `#` on a strict 1:1 character basis. * Only the flagged content is masked — surrounding text is never altered. * Masking must occur before the message is delivered to the recipient. * Any message that triggers content filtering must be permanently tagged **Flagged: Yes** on the Message ID record in the admin panel. * The Flagged tag is permanent and cannot be removed, even if the user edits or resends the message. * The Flagged field must be available as a column and filter in admin message reports. * This rule applies to all messaging flows in both the Gopher App and Gopher Go. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Identify the messaging enhancement that introduced this regression and determine what change removed the filtering logic. * Restore or reimplement the content filtering rules for phone numbers and dollar amounts. * Confirm filtering is applied server-side (not just client-side) to prevent bypass. * Ensure the regex or detection logic handles common phone number formats (e.g. with dashes, spaces, parentheses) and dollar amount formats (e.g. $50, $1,000, $9.99). * Add a **Flagged** boolean field to the Message ID data model in the admin panel. Default value: No. Set to Yes automatically when filtering is triggered. * Expose the Flagged field in the admin Messages report as a visible column and filterable attribute. * Reference admin panel Message ID structure: ID#, Order ID, Title, From, To, Messages, Created At, Flagged. ## 🧪 QA Notes * Test sending a message with a phone number in multiple formats (dashes, spaces, parentheses) — confirm all characters are masked 1:1 and Message ID is tagged Flagged: Yes. * Test sending a message with a dollar amount in multiple formats ($50, $1,000, $9.99) — confirm masking applies correctly and Message ID is tagged Flagged: Yes. * Test sending a message with both a phone number and a dollar amount — confirm both are independently masked and the Message ID is tagged Flagged: Yes. * Test sending a message with no flagged content — confirm it is delivered unmodified and Message ID is not tagged. * After a message is flagged, have the user edit and resend without blocked content — confirm Flagged: Yes tag persists on the Message ID. * In the admin panel, run a message report and confirm the Flagged column is visible and filterable. * Filter the report by Flagged: Yes and confirm only messages that triggered filtering are returned. * Verify masking is applied before the message reaches the recipient. * Test across all messaging flows in both the Gopher App and Gopher Go. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: BUG - Admin Panel - Deleted/Deactivated Date Issue
Description: When running the User report in the admin panel, the Deleted/Deactivated date field incorrectly displays the account’s Created date instead of the actual date the account was deleted or deactivated. This makes it impossible to accurately track user churn, attrition, or account lifecycle in reporting. ## 🧑‍💻 As a admin running the User report, ## 🎯 I want the Deleted/Deactivated date field to show the actual date the account was deleted or deactivated, ## ✅ So that I can accurately track user churn and attrition over time. ## 💡 Context / Background * The User report in the admin panel includes a Deleted/Deactivated date field intended to track when an account was removed or disabled. * This date is used to measure user churn and attrition over time. * Currently, the field is incorrectly populated with the account’s Created date rather than the date the account was actually deleted or deactivated. * This means all attrition reporting is currently inaccurate — deleted accounts appear as if they were deleted on the same day they were created. ## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce 1. In the admin panel, navigate to Reports → User report. 2. Filter or locate accounts with a Deleted or Deactivated status. 3. Observe the Deleted/Deactivated date column. 4. Confirm the date shown matches the account’s Created date rather than the actual deletion or deactivation date. ## ❌ Current Behavior * The Deleted/Deactivated date field in the User report displays the account’s Created date * The actual date the account was deleted or deactivated is not being recorded or displayed * Attrition and churn reporting is inaccurate as a result ## ✅ Expected Behavior * The Deleted/Deactivated date field in the User report displays the actual date the account was deleted or deactivated * The Created date and Deleted/Deactivated date are stored and displayed as separate, distinct values * Attrition and churn reports accurately reflect when users left the platform ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Deleted/Deactivated date shows the correct date * **Given** an account has been deleted or deactivated * **When** an admin views the User report * **Then** the Deleted/Deactivated date field shows the actual date the account was deleted or deactivated * **And** the date is different from the Created date unless the account was deleted on the same day it was created ### Scenario 2 – Created date is unaffected * **Given** an account has been deleted or deactivated * **When** an admin views the User report * **Then** the Created date field still shows the original account creation date and is unchanged ### Scenario 3 – Active accounts show no Deleted/Deactivated date * **Given** an account is active and has not been deleted or deactivated * **When** an admin views the User report * **Then** the Deleted/Deactivated date field is empty or null for that account ## ⚙️ Business Rules * The Deleted/Deactivated date must always reflect the timestamp of the delete or deactivate action, not the account creation timestamp. * Created date and Deleted/Deactivated date must be stored as separate fields in the data model. * Active accounts must have a null or empty Deleted/Deactivated date. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Identify whether the Deleted/Deactivated date is stored as a separate field or is being incorrectly defaulted to the Created date at the report query layer. * If the deletion/deactivation timestamp is not currently being recorded when an account is deleted or deactivated, a new field (e.g. deleted_at or deactivated_at) must be added to the user record and populated at the time of the action. * Existing deleted/deactivated accounts with incorrect dates will need to be assessed — if the correct timestamps are not recoverable from logs, those records may need to remain as-is with a note that historical data prior to this fix may be inaccurate. ## 🧪 QA Notes * Delete or deactivate a test account and immediately check the User report — confirm the Deleted/Deactivated date reflects today’s date (the actual action date). * Confirm the Created date for the same account is unchanged. * Check an active account in the User report — confirm the Deleted/Deactivated date field is empty or null. * Verify the fix applies to both deleted and deactivated account states.

Summary: BUG - Gopher App - Duplicate Issue - If User Edits Request To A Different Category, A New Request Is Generated
Description: When a user edits an existing request — even if they change the subcategory — the original order number must be preserved. A new request must **never** be generated as a result of an edit. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher App user editing an existing request, ## 🎯 I want my edited request to update in place and retain its original order number, ## ✅ So that I do not end up with duplicate orders or lose track of my original request. ## 💡 Context / Background * Users are able to edit a pending/active request from within the app. * Editing within the **same subcategory** works correctly — the order number is retained and no duplicate is created. * However, if the user changes to a **different subcategory** during an edit, the system incorrectly generates a **new request with a new order number**, resulting in a duplicate. * Example: a user edits a _Delivery – General Errand_ request and changes it to _Delivery – Other Age-Restricted_. Instead of updating the existing order, a duplicate request is created. ## ❌ Current Behavior * Editing a request and changing the subcategory causes the system to generate a **new order with a new order number** * The original order remains open, resulting in a **duplicate request** * Editing within the same subcategory does **not** trigger this issue — the bug is isolated to cross-subcategory edits ## ✅ Expected Behavior * Any edit to a request — regardless of whether the subcategory changes — must **update the existing order in place** * The **original order number is always retained** * No new order or duplicate is ever created as a result of an edit * The edit flow behaves consistently whether the subcategory stays the same or changes ## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce 1. Create a request under any subcategory (e.g. _Delivery – General Errand_). 2. Navigate to the request and tap **Edit**. 3. Change the subcategory to a different one (e.g. _Delivery – Other Age-Restricted_). 4. Submit the edited request. 5. Observe that a new order number is generated and a duplicate request exists. ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Edit within the same subcategory * **Given** a user edits a request without changing the subcategory * **When** the edited request is submitted * **Then** the original order is updated in place * **And** the order number remains unchanged * **And** no duplicate request is created ### Scenario 2 – Edit with a subcategory change * **Given** a user edits a request and changes it to a different subcategory * **When** the edited request is submitted * **Then** the original order is updated in place with the new subcategory * **And** the order number remains unchanged * **And** no new order or duplicate is generated ### Scenario 3 – No duplicate in request history * **Given** a user has submitted an edited request with a subcategory change * **When** the user views their request history * **Then** only one order exists for that request * **And** the order reflects the updated subcategory ## ⚙️ Business Rules * An edit to an existing request must **always update the original order** — never create a new one. * The order number is immutable once assigned and must persist through any edits, including subcategory changes. * Subcategory changes are treated as field-level updates, not new request creation events. * Edit behavior must be consistent across all category and subcategory combinations. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Investigate whether a subcategory change triggers a new request creation event on the frontend or backend. * Confirm the edit flow uses an **Update Request** endpoint, not a **Create Request** endpoint, for all edits regardless of subcategory. * Ensure the original order ID is passed through the entire edit flow and is not reset upon subcategory selection. * Verify fix is consistent across all category and subcategory combinations. ## 🧪 QA Notes * Test editing a request without changing the subcategory — confirm order number is retained. * Test editing a request and changing to a different subcategory — confirm order number is retained and no duplicate is created. * Test across multiple category and subcategory combinations. * Verify request history shows only one order after an edit. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher App - Saving An Order Info So Users Don't Have To Start Over (and learn user behaviors)
Description: During order creation, users currently lose all entered data if they exit the app, switch screens, or are interrupted before submitting. This ticket introduces a Draft Order system that auto-saves order progress at every step, assigns a draft order number immediately when an order is started, and allows users to seamlessly resume where they left off. Draft order data is visible to the user in their order history, surfaced in a new admin panel tab, and used to build behavioral analytics around user drop-off and completion patterns. This feature is part of the new UI/UX version. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Requestor creating an order in the Gopher App, ## 🎯 I want my order progress to be automatically saved as I move through each step so I can resume it if I leave the app or get interrupted, ## ✅ So that I never have to start an order from scratch again, and the platform can better understand how users interact with the request creation flow. ## 💡 Context / Background * Users currently lose all order creation progress if they leave the app, are interrupted, or navigate away before submitting. This creates friction and results in abandoned orders that are never completed. * The Draft Order system addresses this by saving order data incrementally as the user progresses through each screen. * A draft order number is assigned as soon as the user begins creating an order, before submission. * Draft orders are surfaced to the user in their order history so they can find and resume them easily. * Draft order data is also captured in a new admin panel tab and report, enabling the team to analyze where users drop off in the creation flow and understand behavioral patterns on the platform. * This feature is part of the new UI/UX version. ## 🔀 Complete Flow ### Step 1 - Draft Order Created on First Interaction * As soon as a user begins creating a request, a draft order number is assigned * The draft order is immediately recorded in the user's order history and in the admin panel Draft Orders tab ### Step 2 - Auto-Save on Each Step * Each time the user taps Next or transitions between screens during order creation, the data entered on that screen is saved to the draft * Progress is preserved even if the user exits the app, backgrounds it, or navigates away before submitting ### Step 3 - Resume from Dashboard * If the user leaves the app or navigates away at any point, tapping the Request button on the bottom dashboard nav shows the user their pending draft order(s) * The user can select a draft and resume from the exact step where they left off * Multiple drafts are supported - if a user has more than one pending draft, all are shown ### Step 4 - Draft Converts to Order on Submission * When the user completes all steps and submits the request, the draft order is converted to a live order * The draft order record is updated with the final submitted status ### Step 5 - Cancelled Draft Orders are Retained * If a user cancels a draft order, the draft is retained in the log with a final status of Cancelled * The data entered up to the point of cancellation is preserved for analytics purposes ## 📄 Draft Orders - User-Facing * Draft orders appear in the user's Order History tab, clearly labeled as Draft * Tapping the Request button on the dashboard when a draft exists shows the user their pending draft(s) first * The user can resume a draft or start a new request ## 📊 Draft Orders - Admin Panel * A new Draft Orders tab is added to the admin panel * The Draft Orders report mirrors the existing Orders report but includes two additional columns: Pending (draft not yet submitted) and Cancelled (draft cancelled before submission) * Draft order records are also visible in individual user profiles in the admin panel * Draft data is retained permanently for behavioral analytics, even after the draft is converted or cancelled ## ❌ Current Behavior * No order progress is saved during creation - if the user exits the app or navigates away, all entered data is lost * Users must start the entire order creation flow from scratch after any interruption * No draft order tracking exists in the user-facing UI or admin panel ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 - Draft order number is assigned on first step * **Given** a user begins creating a request * **When** the first step of the order creation flow is initiated * **Then** a draft order number is assigned and the draft is recorded in the system ### Scenario 2 - Progress is saved on each Next tap * **Given** a user is progressing through order creation * **When** the user taps Next or transitions to the next screen * **Then** all data entered on the current screen is saved to the draft ### Scenario 3 - User can resume draft after leaving the app * **Given** a user has a pending draft and has left the app * **When** the user taps the Request button on the dashboard * **Then** the user's pending draft(s) are shown and they can resume from the step where they left off ### Scenario 4 - Submitted draft converts to a live order * **Given** a user completes all order creation steps and submits * **When** the order is submitted * **Then** the draft is converted to a live order and no longer appears as a pending draft ### Scenario 5 - Cancelled draft is retained with Cancelled status * **Given** a user cancels a draft order * **When** the cancellation is confirmed * **Then** the draft record is retained with a final status of Cancelled and all data is preserved for analytics ### Scenario 6 - Draft orders appear in user Order History * **Given** a user has one or more pending draft orders * **When** the user views their Order History * **Then** the drafts are clearly visible and labeled as Draft ### Scenario 7 - Admin panel Draft Orders tab shows all draft records * **Given** draft orders exist on the platform * **When** an admin navigates to the Draft Orders tab * **Then** all draft orders are listed with Pending and Cancelled columns visible ## ⚙️ Business Rules * A draft order number is assigned at the start of every order creation session. * Progress is saved incrementally at every Next tap or screen transition - no manual save action is required from the user. * Draft orders are accessible from the Request button on the dashboard and from the user's Order History. * A draft is converted to a live order only upon final submission. * Cancelled drafts are never deleted - they are retained with a Cancelled status for analytics. * Draft order data is visible in individual user profiles in the admin panel. * The admin panel Draft Orders report mirrors the Orders report and includes Pending and Cancelled status columns. * This feature is part of the new UI/UX version and should be scoped and implemented accordingly. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * A draft order data model must be created with fields for: draft order number, user ID, category/subcategory, all order creation fields captured per step, current step, status (Pending / Converted / Cancelled), created timestamp, last updated timestamp. * The draft must be saved to the backend on each Next action - local device storage alone is not sufficient as the user must be able to resume on any device. * The Request button on the dashboard must check for existing pending drafts and surface them before launching a new creation flow. * The admin panel requires a new Draft Orders tab and report, plus a Draft Orders section in individual user profiles. * Draft order analytics will enable the team to identify drop-off points in the creation flow by measuring which step users most commonly abandon - the last saved step on cancelled or stale drafts is the key metric. * This feature is part of the new UI/UX version - implementation must align with the new design system and flow. * Figma design reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=102-13675 ## 🧪 QA Notes * Start creating an order and tap Next through several steps - confirm a draft order number is assigned and data is saved at each step. * Exit the app mid-creation, reopen, and tap the Request button - confirm the pending draft is shown and the flow resumes from the last saved step. * Complete and submit an order - confirm the draft converts to a live order and is no longer listed as a pending draft. * Cancel a draft mid-creation - confirm it is retained in the log with Cancelled status. * Check the user's Order History - confirm drafts are visible and clearly labeled. * Check the admin panel Draft Orders tab - confirm all drafts appear with Pending and Cancelled columns. * Check the user's profile in the admin panel - confirm their draft orders are visible. * Create multiple drafts without submitting - confirm all appear when the Request button is tapped. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: BUG - Both Apps - Sign-Up Issue With Existing Users
Description: Following the sign-up process enhancement deployed to the App Stores in March 2026, multiple issues have emerged affecting existing users with unconfirmed email addresses, admin panel email management, and AWS authentication sync. These issues span both the Gopher App and Gopher Go. ## 🧑‍💻 As a returning user, admin, or support team member, ## 🎯 I want existing user accounts to be correctly recognized and manageable across the app and admin panel, ## ✅ So that users are not forced into unwanted new account creation, email updates are properly synced, and confirmation flows work as intended. ## 💡 Context / Background * In March 2026, a sign-up process enhancement was deployed to both app stores. * This enhancement introduced regressions affecting existing users with unconfirmed email addresses. * A new user category was added in AWS that is not linked to the admin panel, creating a sync disconnect. * The issues affect both the user-facing apps and the admin panel's ability to manage accounts. ## ❌ Current Behavior * Existing users with unconfirmed email addresses are being **forced to create new accounts**, even if they have existing order history * These users should instead be prompted to **update their email address and confirm via OTP** — this flow is not triggering correctly * A new AWS category introduced during the March 2026 deployment is **not linked to the admin panel** — email changes made in the admin panel are no longer recognized by the app * When an admin manually updates a user’s email address in the admin panel, the change is **not saved in a way the app recognizes** * The **Send Confirmation Email** button in the admin panel is not functioning correctly following the March 2026 deployment * If a user begins sign-up, reaches the email OTP screen, and **does not complete the session** (OTP expires or session is abandoned), the next time they log in via SMS they are immediately shown the email OTP screen again * On the email OTP screen, tapping the **back arrow (upper left)** simply refreshes the same OTP page — it does not navigate back * The user has no way to update their email address or resend the OTP if the email on file is incorrect — they are completely stuck ## ✅ Expected Behavior * Existing users with unconfirmed emails are **never forced into new account creation** — their existing account and order history must be preserved * These users are prompted to **update and confirm their email via OTP** within the existing account flow * The new AWS category is **fully linked to the admin panel** so that email updates made by admins are recognized by the app * Admin panel email updates are **saved and synced correctly** so the app recognizes the change immediately * The **Send Confirmation Email** button functions correctly and sends the confirmation email to the user * When a user re-logs in via SMS and is shown the email OTP screen, the **back arrow navigates back to the Confirmation screen** where they can update their email address * From the Confirmation screen, the user can **correct their email address and trigger a new OTP** to be sent ## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce ### Issue 1 – Existing user forced into new account creation 1. Identify an existing user with an unconfirmed email address and order history. 2. Attempt to log in or resume the account on either app. 3. Observe that the user is routed to new account creation instead of an email update/OTP confirmation flow. ### Issue 2 – Admin panel email update not recognized by app 1. In the admin panel, manually update a user's email address. 2. Attempt to log in with the updated email on either app. 3. Observe the app does not recognize the updated email. ### Issue 3 – Send Confirmation Email button not working 1. In the admin panel, navigate to a user account. 2. Click the Send Confirmation Email button. 3. Observe the email is not sent or the button produces no action. ### Issue 4 – User stuck on email OTP screen after incomplete session 1. Begin sign-up and proceed all the way to the email OTP screen. 2. Do not complete the OTP entry — exit the app or allow the session to expire. 3. Log back in using SMS. 4. Observe the email OTP screen is shown immediately. 5. Tap the back arrow (upper left). 6. Observe the same OTP page refreshes instead of navigating back. 7. Observe there is no way to update the email address or request a new OTP. ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Existing user with unconfirmed email is not forced into new account creation * **Given** an existing user with an unconfirmed email address and order history attempts to access their account * **When** the app recognizes the existing account * **Then** the user is prompted to update and confirm their email via OTP * **And** their existing account and order history are preserved * **And** no new account is created ### Scenario 2 – OTP email confirmation flow works correctly * **Given** the user is prompted to confirm their email via OTP * **When** the user enters the correct OTP * **Then** the email is confirmed and the user gains full access to their account ### Scenario 3 – Admin panel email update is recognized by the app * **Given** an admin has updated a user's email address in the admin panel * **When** the user attempts to log in with the updated email * **Then** the app recognizes the updated email and allows login ### Scenario 4 – Send Confirmation Email button works correctly * **Given** an admin clicks the Send Confirmation Email button for a user * **When** the action is triggered * **Then** a confirmation email is successfully sent to the user * **And** the user receives the email and can complete confirmation ### Scenario 5 – AWS category is linked to the admin panel * **Given** the new AWS user category exists * **When** an email is updated via the admin panel * **Then** the change is reflected in AWS and recognized by the app ### Scenario 6 – Back arrow on email OTP screen navigates to Confirmation screen * **Given** a user is on the email OTP screen after logging in via SMS * **When** the user taps the back arrow (upper left) * **Then** the user is taken back to the Confirmation screen * **And** the OTP page does not refresh ### Scenario 7 – User can update email and resend OTP from Confirmation screen * **Given** a user has navigated back to the Confirmation screen from the OTP screen * **When** the user updates their email address and re-submits * **Then** a new OTP is sent to the updated email address * **And** the user can complete email confirmation successfully ## ⚙️ Business Rules * Existing users must never be forced into new account creation regardless of email confirmation status. * Users with unconfirmed emails must be routed to an email update and OTP confirmation flow within their existing account. * Email updates made in the admin panel must be synced to AWS and recognized by the app. * The Send Confirmation Email button must function correctly at all times post sign-up enhancement. * All AWS user categories must be linked to and manageable from the admin panel. * The back arrow on the email OTP screen must always navigate back to the Confirmation screen — never refresh the OTP page. * Users must always have a path to correct their email address and request a new OTP if needed. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Root cause is tied to the sign-up process enhancement deployed to the App Stores in March 2026 — regression introduced at that point. * Investigate the new AWS user category added during the March 2026 deployment and confirm it is properly linked to the admin panel. * Confirm the admin panel email update flow writes changes to the correct AWS attribute so the app can recognize them. * Review and fix the Send Confirmation Email trigger in the admin panel to ensure it fires correctly post-deployment. * Fix back arrow navigation on the email OTP screen so it routes to the Confirmation screen rather than refreshing in place. * Applies to both the Gopher App and Gopher Go. * **Related tickets:** This bug is a direct result of the sign-up enhancement work defined in G40-7 (Frontend — Simplify Sign-Up Process) and G40-242 (Backend — Simplify Sign-Up Process). G40-7 and G40-242 define the intended front-end and back-end behavior; G40-271 captures the regressions introduced when that work was deployed.
