Summary: Admin Panel - Create an Email OTP field just like we have for SMS
Description: The admin panel currently has an OTP report that covers SMS-based one-time passcodes. With the introduction of email OTP verification, admins need an equivalent report for email OTPs to assist users with recovery. This ticket renames the existing OTP report to SMS OTP and creates a new Email OTP report that is an exact replica of the SMS OTP report. ## 🧑‍💻 As a admin panel user assisting a user with OTP recovery, ## 🎯 I want to be able to look up both SMS OTPs and Email OTPs for a user in the admin panel, ## ✅ So that I can quickly assist users who are not receiving or are having issues with either type of OTP. ## 💡 Context / Background * The admin panel currently has an OTP report used by the support team to look up and assist users with SMS-based OTP issues. * With email OTP now in use for account verification, admins require the same lookup capability for email OTPs. * The implementation is straightforward: rename the existing report to clarify it covers SMS OTPs, and create an identical Email OTP report for email-based OTP lookups. ## 🛠️ Scope of Changes ### Change 1 - Rename Existing OTP Report * The existing OTP report in the admin panel must be renamed from OTP to SMS OTP * All references to this report throughout the admin panel must be updated to SMS OTP * No changes to the report’s functionality, columns, or data ### Change 2 - Create Email OTP Report * A new Email OTP report must be created in the admin panel * The Email OTP report must be an exact replica of the SMS OTP report in structure, columns, filtering, and functionality * The Email OTP report surfaces email-based OTP records instead of SMS-based OTP records ## ❌ Current Behavior * The admin panel has a single OTP report covering SMS OTPs, with no label distinguishing it from email OTPs * There is no Email OTP report or lookup capability in the admin panel ## ✅ Expected Behavior * The existing OTP report is renamed to SMS OTP throughout the admin panel * A new Email OTP report is available in the admin panel, mirroring the SMS OTP report in structure and functionality * Admins can look up email OTP records for any user to assist with email verification issues ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 - Existing OTP report is renamed to SMS OTP * **Given** an admin navigates to the OTP report * **When** the report loads * **Then** the report is labeled SMS OTP and all references throughout the admin panel reflect this rename * **And** the report’s data, columns, and functionality are unchanged ### Scenario 2 - Email OTP report is available and mirrors SMS OTP * **Given** an admin navigates to the Email OTP report * **When** the report loads * **Then** the report displays email OTP records with the same structure, columns, and filtering as the SMS OTP report ### Scenario 3 - Admin can look up a user’s email OTP records * **Given** an admin is assisting a user with an email OTP issue * **When** the admin searches for the user in the Email OTP report * **Then** the user’s email OTP records are returned and visible ## ⚙️ Business Rules * The existing OTP report must be renamed to SMS OTP with no changes to its data or functionality. * The Email OTP report must be an exact structural replica of the SMS OTP report, populated with email OTP data. * Both reports must be clearly distinguishable by name in the admin panel navigation. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * The Email OTP report must be connected to the email OTP data source — confirm with the backend team that email OTP records are being stored in a queryable format equivalent to SMS OTP records. * The rename of the existing report to SMS OTP should be a label-only change — no data migration or structural change required. * Related ticket: G40-271 (Sign-Up Regression) — email OTP issues reported there make this admin lookup capability a priority for the support team. ## 🧪 QA Notes * Navigate to the admin panel OTP report — confirm it is now labeled SMS OTP. * Confirm the SMS OTP report data and functionality are unchanged. * Navigate to the Email OTP report — confirm it exists and mirrors the SMS OTP report structure. * Search for a user in the Email OTP report — confirm their email OTP records are returned. * Confirm both reports are accessible and clearly labeled in the admin panel navigation.

Summary: Gopher App - Address Entered To Recognize Current Time Zones
Description: The app currently determines time zone based solely on the user's device location. When a request involves an address in a different time zone, all scheduled times must be derived from and displayed relative to the time zone of the request address — not the user's device. This affects both how times are stored and how they are displayed to Requestors and Gophers across both apps. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Requestor scheduling a request at an address in a different time zone, or a Gopher viewing a scheduled request, ## 🎯 I want all scheduled times to reflect the correct time zone for the request location, displayed accurately in my own local time, ## ✅ So that neither the Requestor nor the Gopher is confused about when a scheduled request is supposed to occur, regardless of where each party is located. ## 💡 Context / Background * The app currently uses the user's device time zone as the reference for all scheduling and time display. * When a Requestor creates a scheduled request for an address in a different time zone, the scheduled time is incorrectly interpreted against the Requestor's device time zone rather than the address's time zone. * This causes scheduling confusion for both parties, particularly when a Gopher is in a different time zone from the request address. * The fix requires deriving the request time zone from the address, storing the canonical time in UTC, and displaying it converted to each party's local time zone. ## 📍 Time Zone Trigger Rules * **Standard requests** — the time zone is derived from the pick-up address entered by the Requestor * **"Gopher can pick up anywhere" selected** — when this option is chosen, no specific pick-up address is provided, so the drop-off address becomes the time zone trigger ## 🕒 How Times Must Be Displayed * **Requestor** — sees the scheduled time in the time zone of the request address. Example: a request scheduled for 2:00 PM at a pick-up address in Chicago is shown to the Requestor as 2:00 PM CT. * **Gopher (Gopher Go)** — sees the scheduled time converted to their own local time zone. Example: a Gopher in New York sees the same Chicago 2:00 PM CT request as 3:00 PM ET. * A time zone label must always be shown alongside the scheduled time so both parties know which time zone is being referenced. ## ❌ Current Behavior * All scheduled times are based on the device’s local time zone, regardless of the request address * A request scheduled at an address in a different time zone displays the wrong local time to the Gopher * No time zone label is shown alongside scheduled times ## ✅ Expected Behavior * When a pick-up or drop-off address is entered in a different time zone, the app determines the time zone from that address * The scheduled time is stored in UTC and displayed to each user converted to their relevant local time zone * The Requestor sees the time in the request address time zone; the Gopher sees it converted to their own local time * A time zone label is displayed alongside every scheduled time ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 - Pick-up address determines the request time zone * **Given** a Requestor enters a pick-up address in a time zone different from their device * **When** the Requestor schedules a future time for the request * **Then** the time picker reflects the time zone of the pick-up address * **And** the time zone label is shown alongside the scheduled time ### Scenario 2 - Drop-off address is the trigger when Gopher can pick up anywhere * **Given** a Requestor selects "Gopher can pick up anywhere" and enters a drop-off address in a different time zone * **When** the Requestor schedules a future time * **Then** the time zone is derived from the drop-off address ### Scenario 3 - Gopher sees scheduled time in their own local time zone * **Given** a scheduled request exists with a pick-up address in a different time zone from the Gopher * **When** the Gopher views the request in Gopher Go * **Then** the scheduled time is displayed converted to the Gopher’s local time zone with a time zone label ### Scenario 4 - Same time zone request is unaffected * **Given** a Requestor enters an address in the same time zone as their device * **When** they schedule a request * **Then** the behavior is identical to the current experience with no change ## ⚙️ Business Rules * The request time zone is always derived from the pick-up address. If no pick-up address is provided (Gopher can pick up anywhere), the drop-off address is used. * Scheduled times must be stored in UTC on the backend. * Times must be displayed to each user converted to their relevant local time zone — the Requestor sees the request address time zone; the Gopher sees their own device time zone. * A time zone abbreviation or label must always be shown alongside any displayed scheduled time. * This applies to both the Gopher App and Gopher Go. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Use the Google Time Zone API or equivalent to resolve the IANA time zone identifier from the pick-up or drop-off lat/long at the time the address is entered. * Store the resolved IANA time zone on the request record alongside the UTC scheduled time so it can be used for accurate display on both sides. * All existing scheduled request timestamps must be audited — if they are currently stored in local time rather than UTC, a migration plan is required. * The time picker UI on the Requestor side must reflect the request address time zone, not the device time zone, when they differ. * The Gopher Go app must convert the UTC scheduled time to the Gopher’s device time zone for display. ## 🧪 QA Notes * Create a scheduled request with a pick-up address in a different time zone — confirm the time picker reflects that address’s time zone and the label is shown. * Select "Gopher can pick up anywhere" and enter a drop-off address in a different time zone — confirm the time zone is derived from the drop-off address. * As a Gopher in a different time zone, view the scheduled request in Gopher Go — confirm the time is correctly converted to the Gopher’s local time zone with a label. * Create a request with an address in the same time zone as the device — confirm no change in behavior. * Test with addresses spanning multiple US time zones (ET, CT, MT, PT) to cover all offset scenarios. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher App - Regression Error - Flow Is Allowing Pick-Up and Drop-Off Address To Be The Same
Description: The app is currently allowing users to submit a request where the pick-up and drop-off addresses are identical. This is a regression — this validation previously existed and must be restored. When a user enters the same address for both fields, a friendly in-app reminder must appear and prevent submission until the addresses are corrected. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher App user creating a request, ## 🎯 I want to be clearly notified if my pick-up and drop-off addresses are the same, ## ✅ So that I can correct the error before submitting and avoid a request that cannot be fulfilled. ## 💡 Context / Background * Any request that involves a pick-up and drop-off location requires two distinct addresses. * Having the same address for both fields is logically invalid and cannot be fulfilled by a Gopher. * This validation was previously in place but has regressed — the app is now allowing identical addresses to pass through without any warning or error. * A friendly, non-disruptive reminder popup must be shown to guide the user to fix the issue rather than a hard error block. ## ❌ Current Behavior * The app allows a user to enter the same address for both pick-up and drop-off with no warning * No validation or error message is triggered * The request can proceed to submission with identical addresses ## ✅ Expected Behavior * If a user enters the same address for both pick-up and drop-off, a **friendly reminder popup** is displayed * The popup message clearly communicates that pick-up and drop-off addresses must be different * The user is returned to the address fields to make a correction * Submission is blocked until the two addresses are distinct * This validation applies to all request types that include pick-up and drop-off fields ## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce 1. Begin creating any request that includes pick-up and drop-off address fields. 2. Enter the same address in both the pick-up and drop-off fields. 3. Proceed to submit the request. 4. Observe that no warning or validation error appears and the request is allowed to proceed. ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Same address entered for pick-up and drop-off * **Given** a user has entered the same address for both pick-up and drop-off * **When** the user attempts to proceed or submit * **Then** a friendly reminder popup is displayed * **And** the popup informs the user that pick-up and drop-off addresses must be different * **And** submission is blocked until the addresses are corrected ### Scenario 2 – Different addresses entered for pick-up and drop-off * **Given** a user has entered different addresses for pick-up and drop-off * **When** the user attempts to proceed or submit * **Then** no popup or validation error appears * **And** the request proceeds normally ### Scenario 3 – User corrects addresses after reminder * **Given** the reminder popup has been shown * **When** the user updates one of the addresses to be different * **Then** the validation clears and the user can proceed with submission ## ⚙️ Business Rules * Pick-up and drop-off addresses must never be identical for any request type. * Validation must trigger before submission is allowed to proceed. * The user-facing message must be friendly and instructional, not a hard error block. * This rule applies across all request types and flows that include pick-up and drop-off fields. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Reference Figma design for the reminder popup UI: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=103-14608 * Identify at which point in the previous build this validation existed and where the regression was introduced. * Validation should ideally trigger on address field blur or on submission attempt — confirm preferred UX trigger with design. * Ensure address comparison is normalized (e.g. case-insensitive, trimmed whitespace) to catch identical addresses entered with slight formatting differences. ## 🧪 QA Notes * Test entering the exact same address in both pick-up and drop-off fields — confirm reminder popup appears and blocks submission. * Test entering different addresses — confirm no popup and request proceeds normally. * Test correcting the address after the popup appears — confirm validation clears and submission is allowed. * Test with slight formatting variations of the same address (different casing, extra spaces) — confirm the validation still catches them as identical. * Test across all request types that include pick-up and drop-off fields. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: BUG - Both Apps - Refer App - Email Contacts - No Contacts Populate
Description: When a user attempts to refer a friend via email contacts in the Refer App flow, no contacts are populated. The SMS contacts referral flow uses the same underlying contacts access logic and is working correctly, which isolates the bug to how email addresses are being read or filtered from the device contacts. The email contacts flow must be fixed to match the behavior of the working SMS contacts flow. ## 🧑‍💻 As a user accessing the Refer App feature in either app, ## 🎯 I want my device email contacts to populate when I choose to refer by email, ## ✅ So that I can easily select contacts to refer without having to manually type email addresses. ## 💡 Context / Background * The Refer App feature allows users to refer friends via SMS or email using their device contacts. * The SMS contacts flow correctly reads and displays contacts from the device. * The email contacts flow uses the same contacts access logic but no contacts are being returned — the list appears empty. * The most likely cause is that the contacts query is not correctly identifying or filtering for email addresses from the device contacts data, while the SMS flow correctly filters for phone numbers. * This affects both the Gopher App and Gopher Go. ## ❌ Current Behavior * When a user selects the email referral option and accesses their contacts, no contacts are displayed * The contacts list appears blank even when the user has contacts with email addresses on their device * The SMS contacts flow works correctly using the same contacts access logic ## ✅ Expected Behavior * When a user selects the email referral option, their device contacts with email addresses are populated in the contacts list * Only contacts that have at least one email address on file are shown * The behavior mirrors the SMS contacts flow, which correctly filters for contacts with phone numbers * If a contact has multiple email addresses, all available addresses are shown for selection ## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce 1. Open the Gopher App or Gopher Go. 2. Navigate to Refer App. 3. Select the option to refer by email. 4. Tap to access email contacts. 5. Observe that no contacts are displayed, even though the device has contacts with email addresses. ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – Email contacts populate when referral by email is selected * **Given** a user has contacts with email addresses on their device * **When** the user selects the email referral option in the Refer App flow * **Then** their contacts with email addresses are displayed in the contacts list ### Scenario 2 – Only contacts with email addresses are shown * **Given** the user’s device has contacts both with and without email addresses * **When** the email contacts list loads * **Then** only contacts with at least one email address are shown ### Scenario 3 – SMS contacts flow is unaffected * **Given** the email contacts bug has been fixed * **When** the user uses the SMS referral option * **Then** the SMS contacts flow continues to work correctly and is unaffected by the fix ### Scenario 4 – Empty state shown when no contacts have email addresses * **Given** a user has no contacts with email addresses on their device * **When** the email contacts list loads * **Then** a friendly empty state message is shown rather than a blank screen ## ⚙️ Business Rules * The email contacts list must only display contacts that have at least one email address. * The fix must not alter or regress the SMS contacts flow. * Contacts access permissions must be requested if not already granted before the contacts list is shown. * This applies to both the Gopher App and Gopher Go. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Compare the contacts query logic used in the SMS flow (which works) against the email flow (which doesn’t) — the fix is likely a filter or field mapping correction to target email address fields rather than phone number fields. * Confirm the contacts permission scope includes access to email address fields on both iOS and Android. * On iOS, email addresses are stored under the emailAddresses property of CNContact. Confirm this field is being read correctly. * On Android, email addresses are stored under ContactsContract.CommonDataKinds.Email. Confirm this is being queried. * Related ticket: G40-212 (Refer App Enhancement and Bug Fix) — this bug affects the email referral flow updated in that ticket. ## 🧪 QA Notes * On a device with contacts that have email addresses, open Refer App and select refer by email — confirm contacts populate. * Verify only contacts with email addresses appear — contacts without emails should be excluded. * Select an email contact and confirm the referral email is sent to the correct address. * Test the SMS contacts flow — confirm it is unaffected and continues to work correctly. * Test on a device with no contacts that have email addresses — confirm a friendly empty state is shown. * Test on both the Gopher App and Gopher Go. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Both Apps - Convert Intercom And Inbox
Description: Intercom is currently used for in-app customer support messaging in both the Gopher App and Gopher Go. When a support agent replies to a user through Intercom’s in-app messenger (not email-based threads), the user receives no dashboard notification or inbox alert within the app. This is not a replacement of Intercom — Intercom remains the messaging platform. The fix is to surface Intercom message notifications in the app’s existing inbox/notification system so users are alerted when a new Intercom reply is waiting for them. ## 🧑‍💻 As a Gopher App or Gopher Go user who has an active Intercom support conversation, ## 🎯 I want to receive an in-app inbox or dashboard notification when a support agent replies to my message, ## ✅ So that I never miss a support reply and can respond promptly without having to manually check Intercom. ## 💡 Context / Background * Intercom is used as the in-app support messaging platform across both apps and has accumulated 3 years of customer conversation history. * This history is a valuable asset and will be leveraged for a future AI chatbot. Intercom is not being replaced. * Currently, when a support agent sends a reply through Intercom’s in-app messenger, the user is not notified via the app’s inbox or dashboard. The message sits unread unless the user happens to open Intercom manually. * This is specifically for Intercom’s in-app messenger conversations, not Intercom threads that have already moved to email. * The solution is to use Intercom’s webhook or notification API to trigger an in-app inbox alert when a new reply is sent to the user through the in-app messenger. ## ❌ Current Behavior * When a support agent replies to a user via Intercom’s in-app messenger, no dashboard alert or inbox notification is shown to the user in the app * Users must manually open Intercom to check for new replies * Response rates and resolution times are impacted because users are unaware of new replies ## ✅ Expected Behavior * When a support agent sends a new reply through Intercom’s in-app messenger, the user receives an in-app inbox notification or dashboard alert * The notification indicates a new message from support is waiting * Tapping the notification takes the user directly to the Intercom conversation * Intercom remains the messaging platform — no changes to how messages are stored, managed, or sent * This does not apply to Intercom conversations that have transitioned to email threads ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 – User receives in-app notification when Intercom reply is sent * **Given** a user has an active in-app Intercom conversation * **When** a support agent sends a reply through Intercom’s in-app messenger * **Then** the user receives an in-app inbox or dashboard notification alerting them to the new message ### Scenario 2 – Tapping the notification opens the Intercom conversation * **Given** the user has received an in-app notification for a new Intercom reply * **When** the user taps the notification * **Then** the user is taken directly to the relevant Intercom conversation ### Scenario 3 – Email-transitioned conversations do not trigger in-app notifications * **Given** an Intercom conversation has transitioned to an email thread * **When** a reply is sent on that thread * **Then** no in-app notification is triggered — the user is notified via email only as before ### Scenario 4 – Notification clears once the user views the message * **Given** the user has an unread Intercom notification in their inbox * **When** the user opens and reads the Intercom message * **Then** the notification is marked as read and cleared from the inbox ## ⚙️ Business Rules * Intercom remains the messaging platform — no messages are to be migrated, replaced, or duplicated. * Notifications apply only to in-app Intercom messenger conversations, not email-transitioned threads. * The notification must deep-link directly to the relevant Intercom conversation. * This applies to both the Gopher App and Gopher Go. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Use Intercom’s webhook integration to listen for the conversation.reply event and trigger an in-app notification when a new reply is sent to a user. * Alternatively, Intercom’s Mobile Push Notifications SDK can be used to deliver push alerts natively when a new in-app message is received — evaluate which approach best fits the current integration. * The notification payload must include the conversation ID so a deep link to the Intercom thread can be constructed. * Confirm with the Intercom integration that conversations transitioned to email can be identified and excluded from triggering in-app notifications. * Intercom’s 3 years of conversation history is not in scope for this ticket but will be leveraged in a future AI chatbot initiative — ensure no changes made here affect the historical data. * Intercom webhook reference: https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/webhooks/ * Intercom Mobile Push reference: https://developers.intercom.com/installing-intercom/docs/ios-push-notifications ## 🧪 QA Notes * Have a support agent send a reply via Intercom in-app messenger — confirm the user receives an in-app inbox or dashboard notification. * Tap the notification — confirm it deep-links directly to the Intercom conversation. * Send a reply on an email-transitioned Intercom thread — confirm no in-app notification is triggered. * Open and read the Intercom message — confirm the notification clears from the inbox. * Verify Intercom conversation history and existing functionality are unaffected. * Test on both the Gopher App and Gopher Go. * Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Customer rating screen — star-conditional options: Favorite/Recommend on 4–5★, Block on ≤3★
Description: ## 🧑‍💻 As a Requestor rating a Gopher after confirming a completed request, ## 🎯 I want the rating screen to surface different follow-up options depending on the star rating I give, ## ✅ So that high-rated Gophers can be favorited and recommended, and low-rated Gophers can be excluded from my future requests. ## 💡 Context Extends the post-confirmation rating screen on the **customer** surfaces (Connect / Request / Request App). Relates to G40-39 (parent — non-AR completion → photo → rating) and G40-65 (completion confirmation modal). Builds on the existing "Favorite Gopher Feature" and "Refer A Favorite Gopher" Confluence specs, which define the favorite/recommend behaviors but not the star-conditional branching on the rating screen itself. ## ✅ Acceptance Criteria ### Scenario 1 — High rating (4–5 stars) * **Given** the Requestor is on the rating screen after confirming a completed request * **When** they select a 4- or 5-star rating * **Then** the screen shows **"Add as MY Gopher"** and **"Recommend \[name\] for similar jobs"** options (selected by default per design) * **And** an optional comment field is available ### Scenario 2 — Low rating (3 stars or fewer) * **Given** the Requestor is on the rating screen * **When** they select a rating of 3 stars or fewer * **Then** the favorite/recommend options are replaced by **"Do not send requests to \[name\] again"** (block path) * **And** an optional comment field is available ### Scenario 3 — Switching across the boundary * **Given** the Requestor changes their star selection across the 3/4-star boundary * **When** the rating crosses from ≤3 to ≥4 (or vice versa) * **Then** the option set swaps in real time to match the new rating ### Scenario 4 — Favorite action * **Given** the Requestor selects "Add as MY Gopher" * **When** the rating is submitted * **Then** the Favorite Gopher recognition fires per the "Favorite Gopher Feature" spec (worker-facing congrats handled in Gopher Go) ## ⚙️ Business Rules * Applies to the customer surfaces only (Connect, Request, Request App). Worker-facing congrats modal is Gopher Go scope. * The 4–5★ vs ≤3★ branch is determined by the currently-selected star value and updates live. * "Do not send requests again" routes to the existing block-requester behavior. ## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes * Design reference: rating-screen + cancelled-variant frames (attached in handoff). * Relates to: G40-39 (parent), G40-65; "Favorite Gopher Feature", "Refer A Favorite Gopher" (Confluence).

Summary: Scale-hardening pass — remediate vibe-coded front-end debt before/at framework rebuild
Description: ## Context The current front end (`Code/Final` + the Request/Go prototypes) is an **AI-generated, single-file, no-build static prototype** — the right blueprint for UX sign-off, but it carries **scale-blocking tech debt** that must be remediated when the app is rebuilt into a real framework for production. This umbrella ticket tracks that debt so it's burned down deliberately. ## Scope / checklist * **Assets:** replace base64-inlined images/fonts with real files served from a CDN/asset pipeline (URL refs, cache headers, responsive `srcset`, WebP/AVIF). Base64 is a prototype convenience — \~33% larger, defeats caching/parallelism, bloats files + diffs. Confirmed structural in the mobile simulators (base64 `srcdoc` screens) and throughout `Code/Final`. * **CSS:** consolidate duplicated/inline style blocks into a tokenized system (design tokens + shared stylesheets); remove dead rules. NOTE the Go prototype stores CSS in **fragmented per-screen JS string blocks** — a known drift source (caused the footer-consistency bug) to eliminate. * **JS:** modularize single-file inline scripts behind a build step (bundler); remove global leakage; add linting/CI. * **Architecture:** single-file HTML pages → componentized framework with a real state layer + backend. (Per repo `AGENTS.md`, payments/auth/persistence/matching/security remain human-dev scope.) * **Tooling:** stand up the asset + build/CI pipeline so the above stay fixed. * **PRE-LIVE FLAG AUDIT:** audit and **DISABLE all** `DEMO_*` flags before any live prototype or reskin of the existing app — currently `DEMO_SKIP_PHOTO_GATE` (photo gate) and `DEMO_SHOW_CARD_DISMISS` (card "×"). These are demo-only affordances gated behind loud `DEMO_*` constants; none may reach production. Grep for `/DEMO_/` and confirm each is off/removed. ## Acceptance criteria * No base64-inlined assets in the production build; assets served as cacheable CDN files w/ modern formats. * CSS consolidated into shared tokenized stylesheet(s); no per-screen duplicated blocks. * JS bundled/modularized behind a build step with linting in CI. * Prototype single-file pages rebuilt as framework components with a state layer. * Documented asset/build pipeline enforced by CI. * All `DEMO_*` flags audited and disabled; none present in the production build. ## Notes Umbrella tech-debt tracker for the post-UX scale-hardening pass; expect to split into sub-tasks per area (assets / CSS / JS / framework / flags) once the rebuild starts. Relates to the reskin-readiness audits **G40-301** (banner) and **G40-302** (pop-up modal).

Summary: Gopher Request — Request-specific deep link into a specific request's cancel flow (replace deprecated Firebase Dynamic Links)
Description: ## 🎯 Goal Provide a deep link that carries a **specific request id** and, when tapped, opens the Gopher Request app directly on **that request's cancel flow** (not the home screen, not a different request). ## 💡 Why this is its own ticket Split out of **G40-108** (48-hour check-in email). Grounding finding: **no request-specific deep link exists anywhere in the backend today.** Every SMS/email link is a single static Firebase Dynamic Link — `https://gopherrequestapp.page.link/amTC` (requester) / `https://gophergoapp.page.link/H2PN` (gopher) — that opens the app generically and carries no order id (see `middleware/crons.js:389,557`, `controllers/order/cost_adjustment.js:195`, `controllers/order/order_bids.js:808`). G40-108 ships v1 with the existing generic app-open link; this ticket is the **prerequisite** for its acceptance **Scenario 6** (and would upgrade the check-in email to true one-tap cancel). ## ⚠️ Platform constraint — Firebase Dynamic Links is deprecated Google has **deprecated Firebase Dynamic Links (shutdown 2025)**. Do **not** extend FDL. This ticket should establish the **replacement** deep-link mechanism (iOS Universal Links / Android App Links, or an equivalent) for the whole platform — the request-specific cancel link is the first consumer. ## ✅ Expected behavior * A link of the form "open request `<id>` → cancel flow" can be generated backend-side. * Tapping it with the app installed routes to that specific request's cancel screen. * Fallback (app not installed) behaves sanely (store / web landing). * Reusable: other per-request notifications (bids, counter-offers, cost adjustments) can adopt the same request-scoped link. ## 🔗 Consumers / follow-on * **G40-108** — 48h check-in email (blocked-by this for Scenario 6). * Candidate migrations off the generic FDL: cost-adjustment SMS, confirm-reminder SMS, bid/counter-offer notifications. ## 🧠 Notes Scope covers both (a) backend link generation carrying the order id and (b) app-side route handling that parses it and lands on the cancel flow. Verify on iOS + Android across Gmail / Apple Mail / Outlook.

Summary: Pop-up Modal Standards — establish + implement modal style guides (Request/Connect and the 2 native apps) BEFORE dev handoff
Description: ## Goal Establish a canonical **pop-up / modal style guide** and reusable modal component, then implement it across the new-flow surfaces **before anything is handed to the new developer**. Every modal in the product should come from this standard — not from old Figma. ## Why (important fork) The majority of the old Figma designs depict the **OLD UX**. We are **not** carrying any old-app Figma designs into the new build. Modal/pop-up UI must be defined fresh here and implemented in the prototypes so the developer builds against a single, consistent, already-realized standard instead of reverse-engineering inconsistent one-off modals or stale Figma frames. ## Two style guides **Guide A — Request + Connect** (customer & business request surfaces) * Source of truth: `Final/gopher-request.html` (`.gr-modal`) and `Final/gopher-connect.html` (`.gc-modal`). **Guide B — The 2 native apps** (Gopher requester App + Gopher Go worker App) * Source of truth: `_prototypes/Go/gopher-go-worker.html` and the requester app shell. Each guide is derived from the **current new-UX prototypes**, harmonized — never from old Figma. ## Scope — what the standard must define (per guide) 1. **Anatomy:** scrim/overlay, container, close affordance, icon/illustration slot, eyebrow, title, body, primary CTA, secondary/text action. 2. **Variants:** info · confirm · success · warning/destructive · input. 3. **Sizing & responsive** behavior (mobile-first; safe-area on native). 4. **Typography** scale + brand fonts. 5. **Color tokens** (Midnight Blue #002461, Shamrock #33D975, Sand #FBF3E4, + accent), including destructive. 6. **Button hierarchy** (primary filled / secondary text) + placement. 7. **Motion** (enter/exit) + scrim behavior. 8. **Accessibility:** focus trap, ARIA roles, Esc-to-close, scrim-dismiss rules, min tap targets. 9. **Voice/tone** ("neighbor" voice) + copy patterns. 10. **Reusable component:** one shared modal component per guide, injected via the existing component-marker pattern, so every modal is one implementation. ## Deliverables * Written standard (one doc per guide). * Reusable modal component implemented in each surface's prototype. * Existing ad-hoc modals migrated to the standard (inventory + convert). ## Acceptance * Both guides documented and approved. * A reusable modal component exists and is used by all modals in Request, Connect, and both apps. * No modal derives its visual design from old Figma. * **This ticket is a HARD BLOCKER:** no groomed ticket is handed to the developer until the modal standards are built and implemented. Tickets whose UI includes a modal (e.g. G40-137's "Counter-Offer Update") consume this standard rather than any Figma frame. ## Note on existing handoffs Groomed tickets that referenced a Figma modal (notably **G40-137**) are updated to point their modal UI at this standard; the old Figma node is retained only as intent/copy reference, not as visual design.
